glossary.pronumque: prōnus — leaning forward; inclined, prone, disposed (toward) (n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.; here n. nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.propinquae: propinquus — neighbouring, close by (f. nom. pl.; the form is also f. gen. or dat. sg.)
glossary.prosiluit: prōsiliō — leapt forward, sprang out (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.pudibunda: pudibundus — shamefaced, covered in shame (n. nom./acc. pl.; the form is also f. nom. or abl. sg.; here n. acc. pl.)
glossary.puerile: puerīlis — of boyhood, boyish (n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.pulsabant: pulsō — were beating, were striking (3 pl. imperf.; frequentative of pellō)
glossary.pulso: pulsō — I beat, batter, pound (1 sg. pres. act.; the form is also m./n. dat. or abl. sg. of pulsus 'driven, struck' (part. of pellō) and of the noun pulsus 'a beating' — here the verb)
glossary.pulvereamque: pulvereus — dusty, of dust (adj., f. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.purpureasque: purpureus — purple, crimson (adj., f. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.pylos: Pylos — Pylos, Neleus' city on the west coast of the Peloponnese (f. nom. sg., Greek)
glossary.quales: quālis — such as, of the kind that (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; correlative with tālis; here acc. pl.)
glossary.quandocumque: quandōcumque — whenever; at some time or other, sooner or later (adv./conj.)
glossary.radiantia: radiō — shining, gleaming, giving off rays (pres. act. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.)
glossary.rapere: rapiō — to seize, snatch away, carry off by force, abduct (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.rapiam: rapiō — I will tear away, snatch out by force (1 sg. fut.; the form is also 1 sg. pres. subj.; future in these lines)
glossary.raptaeque: rapiō — seized, dragged off (perf. pass. part., f. dat. or gen. sg., also f. nom. pl.; here dat. sg., of the person the thing is put on) + -que 'and'
glossary.raptas: rapiō — snatched, caught up, carried off (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl.)
glossary.recursus: recursus — a running back, return journey (m. 4th decl., acc. pl.; the form is also nom. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.redito: redeō — come back, you shall return (2 sg. future imperative in -tō, the solemn form used in requests, laws and prayers; also 3 sg. fut. imperative)
glossary.redituram: redeō — about to return, going to come back (fut. act. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.refringit: refringō — breaks open, bursts, smashes down (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.regales: rēgālis — royal, of a king (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; here f. nom. pl.)
glossary.reges: rēx — kings (m. acc. pl.; the form is also nom. pl., and 2 sg. fut. of regō 'rule' — here the noun, acc. pl.)
glossary.regionibus: regiō — regions, districts, territories (f. dat. or abl. pl.)
glossary.reliqui: relinquō — I left behind, I abandoned (1 sg. perf.; the form is also m./n. gen. sg. or m. nom. pl. of reliquus 'remaining, left over' — here the verb)
glossary.remige: rēmex — oarsman, rower (m. abl. sg.; often collective, 'oarage, rowing', paired with vēlum 'sail')
glossary.remittas: remittō — you should send back, may release (2 sg. pres. subj.; in a request or indirect command)
glossary.remotam: removeō — removed, set apart, out of the way, remote (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.removente: removeō — removing, driving away, keeping off (pres. act. part., m./f./n. abl. sg.)
glossary.repellit: repellō — drives back, thrusts away, overturns (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.repetisse: repetō — to have gone back to, to have attacked again (perf. act. inf., syncopated from repetīvisse/repetiisse); with a person's body as object, to assault sexually again
glossary.repetiti: repetō — sought again, come round again, recurring (perf. pass. part., m. gen. sg.; the form is also m. nom. pl.)
glossary.rerumque: rēs — of things, of affairs, of the state (f. gen. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.reserato: reserō — unbarred, unlocked, opened up (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg., also dat.; here n. abl. sg. in an ablative absolute)
glossary.restet: restō — may remain, may be left over (3 sg. pres. subj.)
glossary.retinentia: retineō — holding on to, still keeping (pres. act. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; here acc. pl.)
glossary.reverti: revertor — to return, to go back (pres. inf.; the verb is deponent in the present system, so the -ī form is its active-meaning infinitive. The same spelling is also 1 sg. perf. act. 'I returned', since the perfect is active — here the infinitive)
glossary.revertitur: revertor — returns, comes back (3 sg. pres.; deponent in the present system, active in meaning)
glossary.rigent: rigeō — stand stiff, are rigid, stand hard and unyielding (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.ritibus: rītus — rites, ritual observances, the customary usages of a cult (m. 4th decl., dat. or abl. pl.)
glossary.sacrum: sacrum — a rite, a sacred observance, a sacrifice (n. acc. sg. of the noun; the form is also m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg. of the adj. sacer 'holy, consecrated' — here the noun)
glossary.saevi: saevus — savage, cruel, brutal (m./n. gen. sg.; the form is also m. nom. pl., and the sg. imperative of saeviō 'rage' — here gen. sg.)
glossary.saevitiam: saevitia — savagery, brutality, ferocity (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.saevo: saevus — savage, fierce, cruel (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; here n. abl. sg.; the form is also 1 sg. pres. of saeviō 'I rage')
glossary.salire: saliō — to leap, jump, twitch convulsively (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.salutent: salūtō — (that they) greet, send greetings to (3 pl. pres. subj.; in an indirect command)
glossary.sceleris: scelus — of the crime, of the outrage, of the foul deed (n. gen. sg.)
glossary.secessit: sēcēdō — withdrew, went apart, retired (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.sepulcrum: sepulcrum — tomb, grave, burial monument (n. acc. sg.; the form is also nom. sg.)
glossary.sermo: sermō — talk, conversation, discussion (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.signataque: signō — marked, stained, stamped (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg., also n. nom./acc. pl.; here f. nom. sg., with est forming the perfect passive 'has been marked') + -que 'and'
glossary.similesque: similis — like, matching, of the same kind (m./f. nom. or acc. pl.; takes gen. or dat.; here acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.singultibus: singultus — sobs, catches of the breath (m. 4th decl., dat. or abl. pl.; here abl.)
glossary.sitae: situs — situated, lying, placed (perf. pass. part. of sinō used as an adjective, f. nom. pl.; the form is also f. gen. or dat. sg.)
glossary.sithoniae: Sīthonius — Sithonian, i.e. Thracian (adj., f. nom. pl.; from Sithonia in Thrace; the form is also f. gen. or dat. sg.)
glossary.solemus: soleō — we are accustomed, we usually (do) (1 pl. pres.; takes an infinitive)
glossary.solido: solidus — solid, whole, unbroken (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; here n. abl. sg.; the form is also 1 sg. pres. of solidō 'make firm')
glossary.sollicitae: sollicitus — anxious, troubled, worn with worry (f. gen. or dat. sg., also f. nom. pl.; here gen. sg.)
glossary.sollicitare: sollicitō — to work upon, tempt, bribe, stir up (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.sontem: sōns — guilty, criminal, deserving punishment (adj., m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.sparsis: spargō — scattered, spattered, flung loose (perf. pass. part., m./f./n. dat. or abl. pl.; here m. abl. pl.)
glossary.sparte: Spartē — Sparta, the chief city of Laconia (f. nom. sg., the Greek form of Latin Sparta; the form is also abl. sg.)
glossary.spondere: spondeō — to promise solemnly, pledge, guarantee (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.stabulorum: stabulum — of the stalls, steading, farm buildings (n. gen. pl.)
glossary.stimulatus: stimulō — goaded, spurred on, driven (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.stravere: sternō — spread, laid out, made up (a bed) (3 pl. perf., the -ēre ending for -ērunt)
glossary.stridunt: strīdō — hiss, sizzle, shriek (3 pl. pres.; the verb also has a 2nd-conjugation form strīdeō)
glossary.structa: struō — built, constructed, piled up (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; the form is also f. nom. or abl. sg.; here n. nom. pl.)
glossary.subii: subeō — I went under, I made my way beneath (1 sg. perf.)
glossary.subnixa: subnīxus — propped on, resting upon, supported by (+ abl.) (perf. part. of subnītor used adjectivally, f. nom. sg.)
glossary.subvectaque: subvehō — carried up, brought over (by water) (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; the form is also f. nom. or abl. sg.; here n. nom. pl.) + -que 'and'
glossary.successisse: succēdō — to have turned out well, to have prospered (perf. act. inf.; used impersonally with a dative of the person for whom it went well)
glossary.supponat: suppōnō — should set beneath, should put (fire) under (3 sg. pres. subj.)
glossary.supposuique: suppōnō — I set beneath, I thrust under (1 sg. perf.) + -que 'and'
glossary.suppressit: supprimō — checked, held back, reined in (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.supremumque: suprēmus — last, final (n. acc. sg., here adverbial/internal accusative, 'for the last time'; the form is also m. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.suspendit: suspendō — hung up, set up (a warp on the loom) (3 sg.; the present and perfect of this verb are identical in form, so the tense is fixed only by context — perfect in these lines; uncertain)
glossary.tacitaque: tacitus — silent, unspoken, kept to oneself (f. nom. or abl. sg., also n. nom./acc. pl.; here f. abl. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.tartareas: Tartareus — of Tartarus, infernal, belonging to the underworld (adj., f. acc. pl.)
glossary.tellusque: tellūs — earth, land, ground (f. nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.tenebor: teneō — I shall be held, kept, shut in (1 sg. fut. pass.)
glossary.terea: Tēreus — Tereus, king of Thrace, husband of Procne (m. acc. sg.; the Greek accusative Tērea, not Latin -eum)
glossary.tereo: Tēreus — Tereus (m. abl. sg.; the form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.tereu: Tēreus — Tereus (m. voc. sg., the Greek vocative in -eu)
glossary.tereus: Tēreus — Tereus, the Thracian king who marries Procne (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.terrebant: terreō — were terrifying, were menacing (3 pl. imperf.)
glossary.terribilis: terribilis — terrifying, dreadful to look at (adj., m./f. nom. sg.; the form is also gen. sg.)
glossary.testari: testor — to bear witness to, to attest, to declare (pres. inf. of the deponent, active in meaning)
glossary.testarique: testor — to call to witness, to invoke as witnesses (pres. inf. of the deponent, active in meaning) + -que 'and'
glossary.thalamique: thalamus — of the bedchamber, of the bridal chamber (m. gen. sg.; the form is also nom. pl.) + -que 'and'

glossary.expetit: expetō, expetere — seeks eagerly, strives for (3rd sing. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.explevit: expleō, explēre, explēvī — filled up, completed (3rd sing. perf. ind. act.)
glossary.exspectato: exspectō, exspectāre, -āvī, -ātum — expected, awaited (perf. pass. part., abl. sing. neut.)
glossary.exstincta: exstinguō, exstinguere, exstīnxī, exstīnctum — extinguished, quenched, put out (perf. pass. part., nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.exta: exta, -ōrum n. pl. — entrails, vitals of a victim, inspected for omens (nom. pl.)
glossary.extulerat: efferō, efferre, extulī, ēlātum — had raised up, had brought forth (3rd sing. pluperf. ind. act.)
glossary.facerem: faciō, facere — I was making, performing, offering (1st sing. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.facietque: faciō, facere — and will make, will cause (3rd sing. fut. ind. act. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.facinusque: facinus, -oris n. — and deed, especially a crime, outrage (acc. sing. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.fatebar: fateor, fatērī, fassus sum — I was admitting, confessing (1st sing. imperf. indic., deponent)
glossary.faterer: fateor, fatērī, fassus sum — I might confess, admit (1st sing. imperf. subj., deponent)
glossary.fatur: for, fārī, fātus sum — speaks, says (3rd sing. pres. indic., deponent; defective verb, mainly poetic)
glossary.faventum: faveō, favēre — of those favouring, wishing well (gen. pl. pres. act. part., poetic -um for -ium; used as a noun)
glossary.fecundique: fēcundus, -a, -um — fruitful, fertile (gen. sing. masc./neut., with -que 'and'; also nom. pl. masc.)
glossary.feliciter: fēlīciter (adv. of fēlīx) — happily, favourably, with good luck (adverb)
glossary.feracis: ferāx, ferācis — fertile, productive (often + gen.) (gen. sing., all genders; also poetic acc. pl. for ferācēs)
glossary.ferinae: ferīnus, -a, -um — of wild beasts, of game (gen./dat. sing. fem.)
glossary.feriuntque: feriō, ferīre — and they strike, smite (3rd pl. pres. indic. act., with -que 'and')
glossary.ferrem: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātus — I would bear, carry, bring (1st sing. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.fictor: fictor, -ōris m. — shaper, moulder; feigner, inventor of a fiction (nom. sing.)
glossary.fictus: fingō, fingere, fīnxī, fictus — feigned, made-up, counterfeit (nom. sing. masc., perf. pass. part.)
glossary.fidelius: fidēlis, -e — more faithfully (comparative adverb); also the comparative adj. 'more faithful' (nom./acc. sing. neut.)
glossary.fideque: fidēs, fideī f. — faith, trust, loyalty, pledge (abl. sing., with -que 'and'); not to be confused with fīde, imperative of fīdō 'trust!'
glossary.fidere: fīdō, fīdere, fīsus sum — to trust, rely on (+ dat./abl.) (pres. act. inf.; semi-deponent)
glossary.finivit: fīniō, fīnīre — brought to an end, finished (3rd sing. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.firmissimus: firmus, -a, -um — strongest, most steadfast (nom. sing. masc., superlative)
glossary.flabat: flō, flāre — was blowing (3rd sing. imperf. indic. act.; of wind)
glossary.flebile: flēbilis, -e — tearful, lamentable, to be wept over (nom./acc. sing. neut.)
glossary.flentes: fleō, flēre — weeping (nom./acc. pl. masc./fem., pres. act. part.)
glossary.flexerat: flectō, flectere, flexī, flexus — had bent, turned, directed (3rd sing. pluperf. indic. act.)
glossary.florentemque: flōreō, flōrēre — and blooming, flowering, bright with (+ abl.) (acc. sing. masc./fem., pres. act. part., with -que 'and')
glossary.florentis: flōreō, flōrēre — blooming, flowering (gen. sing., pres. act. part.; also poetic acc. pl. for flōrentēs)
glossary.foedusque: foedus, foederis n. — treaty, compact, pact (acc. sing., with -que 'and'); distinct from the adjective foedus, -a, -um 'foul, hideous'
glossary.formosius: formōsus, -a, -um — more beautiful (nom./acc. sing. neut., comparative); the same form serves as the comparative adverb 'more beautifully'
glossary.fortunaque: fortūna, -ae f. — fortune, chance, luck (nom. sing., with -que 'and'; the form is also abl. sing.)
glossary.fovebam: foveō, fovēre, fōvī, fōtus — I was cherishing, keeping warm, nursing (1st sing. imperf. indic. act.)
glossary.fraterque: frāter, frātris m. — and (his) brother (nom. sing., with -que 'and')
glossary.fraudo: fraudō, fraudāre — I cheat, defraud (someone of something, + abl.) (1st sing. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.fugiuntque: fugiō, fugere — and they flee, run away from (3rd pl. pres. indic. act., with -que 'and')
glossary.fulgore: fulgor, -ōris m. — flash, gleam, lightning-flash (abl. sing.)
glossary.fulva: fulvus, -a, -um — tawny, yellowish-brown (nom./abl. sing. fem.; also nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.fundit: fundō, fundere, fūdī, fūsus — pours, pours out (3rd sing. pres. indic. act.; the same verb also means 'rout, scatter'; distinct from fundō, fundāre 'to found')
glossary.funeribus: fūnus, fūneris n. — funeral rites, burial; death (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.gerebant: gerō, gerere, gessī, gestus — they were bearing, carrying, displaying (3rd pl. imperf. indic. act.)
glossary.gerentes: gerō, gerere — bearing, carrying (nom./acc. pl. masc./fem., pres. act. part.)
glossary.gerere: gerō, gerere, gessī, gestus — to bear, carry on, wage (war) (pres. act. inf.; also 2nd sing. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.gladii: gladius, -ī m. — sword (gen. sing.; also nom. pl.)
glossary.gnato: gnātus, -ī m. (= nātus) — son (dat./abl. sing.; archaic gn- spelling of nātus)
glossary.gnosiacas: Gnōsiacus, -a, -um — of Knossos, Cretan (acc. pl. fem.; from Gnōsus/Knossos, chief city of Crete)
glossary.gradibus: gradus, -ūs m. — step, stair; pace (dat./abl. pl., 4th decl.)
glossary.graniferumque: grānifer, -fera, -ferum — and grain-bearing, carrying grain (acc. sing. neut., with -que 'and')
glossary.graviore: gravis, -e — heavier, more grievous, more severe (abl. sing., comparative)
glossary.gregibus: grex, gregis m. — flock, herd (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.gyaros: Gyaros, -ī f. — Gyaros, a small island of the Cyclades (nom. sing., Greek declension)
glossary.habitus: habeō, habēre, habuī, habitus — held, regarded, considered (nom. sing. masc., perf. pass. part.); the same form is also the noun habitus, -ūs m. 'condition, bearing, dress' (nom. sing.)
glossary.haurit: hauriō, haurīre — drains, drinks up, draws (3rd sing. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.honorum: honor (honōs), honōris m. — honour, distinction, office (gen. pl.)
glossary.horruerant: horreō, horrēre, horruī — had bristled, had shuddered (3rd pl. pluperf. indic. act.)
glossary.hymetti: Hymettus, -ī m. — Hymettus, the mountain south-east of Athens, famous for its honey and marble (gen. sing.)
glossary.iaculabile: iaculābilis, -e — that can be hurled, fit for throwing (nom./acc. sing. neut.)
glossary.ignavos: ignāvus, -a, -um — sluggish, idle, listless (acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.ignoro: ignōrō, ignōrāre — I do not know, am unacquainted with (1st sing. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.immo: immō — on the contrary, no indeed, rather (adverb correcting or strengthening what precedes)
glossary.imperiumque: imperium, -ī n. — command, sovereignty, empire (nom./acc. sing., with -que 'and')
glossary.implevit: impleō, implēre, implēvī, implētus — filled, filled up (3rd sing. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.inclusit: inclūdō, inclūdere, inclūsī, inclūsus — shut in, enclosed, confined (3rd sing. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.incultos: incultus, -a, -um — untilled, uncultivated, wild (acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.incurrere: incurrō, incurrere — to run at, charge, rush upon (+ dat.) (pres. act. inf.; the form can also be 3rd pl. perf. indic. for incurrērunt)
glossary.indefletaeque: indēflētus, -a, -um — and unwept, unmourned (nom. pl. fem., with -que 'and'; a rare poetic compound)
glossary.indulgent: indulgeō, indulgēre — they give way to, yield to, indulge (+ dat.) (3rd pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.ineo: ineō, inīre — I enter, go into (1st sing. pres. indic. act.; compound of eō)
glossary.inesset: īnsum, inesse — would be in, be present in (+ dat.) (3rd sing. imperf. subj.)
glossary.inexcusabile: inexcūsābilis, -e — admitting no excuse, leaving nothing to complain of (nom./acc. sing. neut.)
glossary.ingrate: ingrātus, -a, -um — ungrateful, thankless one (voc. sing. masc.); the same form is also the adverb ingrātē 'ungratefully'
glossary.ingrediorque: ingredior, ingredī, ingressus sum — and I enter, step into (1st sing. pres. indic., deponent, with -que 'and')
glossary.inhaeret: inhaereō, inhaerēre — clings to, sticks fast in (+ dat.) (3rd sing. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.inhumata: inhumātus, -a, -um — unburied (nom./acc. pl. neut.; also nom./abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.iniquae: inīquus, -a, -um — unfair, hostile, ill-disposed (gen./dat. sing. fem.; also nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.inluxisse: illūcēscō (inlūcēscō), illūcēscere, illūxī — to have dawned, grown light (perf. act. inf.; inl- is the older spelling of ill-)
glossary.inmoriuntur: immorior (inmorior), immorī — they die in, die upon (+ dat.) (3rd pl. pres. indic., deponent; inm- for imm-)
glossary.inmutatque: immūtō (inmūtō), immūtāre — and changes, alters (3rd sing. pres. indic. act., with -que 'and'; inm- for imm-)
glossary.insidiosa: īnsidiōsus, -a, -um — treacherous, full of snares, deceitful (nom./acc. pl. neut.; also nom./abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.intervenit: interveniō, intervenīre, intervēnī — comes between, intervenes, breaks in on (+ dat.) (3rd sing. pres. indic. act.; the form is also 3rd sing. perf.)
glossary.invidiosior: invidiōsus, -a, -um — more apt to arouse ill-will, more resented, more hateful (nom. sing. masc./fem., comparative)
glossary.invisi: invīsus, -a, -um — hated, loathed (gen. sing. masc./neut.; also nom. pl. masc.); the same letters can be 1st sing. perf. of invīsō 'I visited, went to see'
glossary.invitumque: invītus, -a, -um — and unwilling, against his will (acc. sing. masc., with -que 'and')
glossary.irasci: īrāscor, īrāscī — to grow angry, be enraged (pres. inf., deponent)
glossary.isthmon: Isthmus, -ī m. — the Isthmus, the neck of land at Corinth joining the Peloponnese to mainland Greece (acc. sing., Greek form Isthmon)
glossary.iubebat: iubeō, iubēre, iussī, iussus — was bidding, ordering, urging (3rd sing. imperf. indic. act.)
glossary.iugalia: iugālis, -e — of marriage, nuptial; of the yoke (nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.iuvenumque: iuvenis, -is m./f. — young man, youth (gen. pl., with -que 'and')
glossary.iuvere: iuvō, iuvāre, iūvī — they helped, aided (3rd pl. perf. indic. act., poetic -ēre for -ērunt); the form can also be pres. pass. inf. 'to be helped'
glossary.iuves: iuvō, iuvāre — may you help, aid, support (2nd sing. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.iuvit: iuvō, iuvāre, iūvī — helped, aided; pleased (3rd sing. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.iuxta: iuxtā — close by, near at hand (adverb); also a preposition + acc. 'next to, beside'
glossary.lacriment: lacrimō, lacrimāre — they may weep, shed tears (3rd pl. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.laesum: laedō, laedere, laesī, laesus — injured, wronged, outraged (acc. sing. masc./neut., perf. pass. part.)
glossary.laetatur: laetor, laetārī — rejoices, is glad (+ abl.) (3rd sing. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.laetis: laetus, -a, -um — joyful, glad (dat./abl. pl.; as a noun in the neuter, 'joys, glad things')
glossary.lanaeque: lāna, -ae f. — wool, fleece (nom. pl., with -que 'and'; the form is also gen./dat. sing.)
glossary.languor: languor, -ōris m. — faintness, listlessness, sickly weakness (nom. sing.)
glossary.laqueo: laqueus, -ī m. — noose, halter, snare (abl. sing.); the same letters can be 1st sing. pres. of laqueō 'I ensnare'
glossary.lassaque: lassus, -a, -um — and weary, worn out (nom./acc. pl. neut., with -que 'and'; also nom./abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.latebat: lateō, latēre — was hidden, lay concealed, escaped notice (3rd sing. imperf. indic. act.)
glossary.latentis: lateō, latēre — hidden, lurking (gen. sing., pres. act. part.; also poetic acc. pl. for latentēs)
glossary.latronis: latrō, latrōnis m. — brigand, robber, highwayman (gen. sing.)
glossary.lecti: lectus, -ī m. — bed, couch, marriage-bed (gen. sing.); the same form is also legō's perf. pass. part. lēctus 'chosen, gathered' (gen. sing. masc./neut., nom. pl. masc.)
glossary.lelegeia: Lelegēius, -a, -um — of the Leleges, an ancient people of Greece and Asia Minor (acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.lues: luēs, luis f. — plague, pestilence, contagion (nom. sing.); the same letters can be 2nd sing. fut. of luō 'you will pay, atone for'
glossary.lutea: lūteus, -a, -um — saffron-yellow, golden (nom./abl. sing. fem.; also nom./acc. pl. neut.); distinct from lŭteus 'of mud, of clay'
glossary.lyctia: Lyctius, -a, -um — of Lyctos, a city of Crete; hence Cretan (nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.maciem: maciēs, -ēī f. — leanness, thinness, wasting (acc. sing., 5th decl.)
glossary.magnaeque: magnus, -a, -um — great, large (gen./dat. sing. fem., with -que 'and'; also nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.maiorem: maior, maius (comp. of magnus) — greater, larger (acc. sing. masc./fem.)
glossary.maiusque: maior, maius (comp. of magnus) — and greater, larger (nom./acc. sing. neut., with -que 'and')
glossary.mandatam: mandō, mandāre, mandāvī, mandātus — entrusted, commissioned, committed (acc. sing. fem., perf. pass. part.)
glossary.marathon: Marathōn, -ōnis f. — Marathon, a plain and deme on the east coast of Attica (nom. sing., Greek declension)
glossary.marmoreamque: marmoreus, -a, -um — and of marble, marble-white (acc. sing. fem., with -que 'and')
glossary.matrumque: māter, mātris f. — mother (gen. pl., with -que 'and')
glossary.mecumque: mēcum (mē + cum) — and with me (abl. of ego with postposed cum, plus -que 'and')
glossary.medendi: medeor, medērī — of healing, of curing (+ dat.) (gen. sing. of the gerund, from a deponent verb)
glossary.medentes: medeor, medērī — healers, physicians; those healing (nom./acc. pl., pres. part. of a deponent verb, used as a noun)
glossary.meditataque: meditor, meditārī, meditātus sum — and rehearsed, thought out beforehand (nom./acc. pl. neut., perf. part. of a deponent verb, so active in sense, with -que 'and')
glossary.meminit: meminī, meminisse — remembers, bears in mind (+ gen. or acc.) (3rd sing. perf. indic.; a defective verb whose perfect has present meaning)
glossary.memorare: memorō, memorāre — to recount, relate, mention (pres. act. inf.; also 2nd sing. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.memorata: memorō, memorāre, memorāvī, memorātus — things said, related, recounted (nom./acc. pl. neut., perf. pass. part.; also nom./abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.miliaque: mīlia, mīlium n. pl. — and thousands (of, + gen.) (nom./acc. pl., with -que 'and'; plural of mīlle)
glossary.militiae: mīlitia, -ae f. — military service, campaign, warfare (gen./dat. sing.; also nom. pl.)
glossary.minari: minor, minārī, minātus sum — to threaten, make threats (pres. inf., deponent)
glossary.minorque: minor, minus (comp. of parvus) — and the younger, the lesser (nom. sing. masc./fem., with -que 'and'); the same letters are also 1st sing. pres. of minor 'I threaten'
glossary.minos: Mīnōs, Mīnōis m. — Minos, king of Crete, son of Jupiter and Europa (nom. sing., Greek declension)
glossary.mirandum: mīror, mīrārī — a thing to be wondered at, a marvel (acc. sing. neut. gerundive used as a noun)
glossary.miror: mīror, mīrārī — I wonder at, marvel, am amazed (1st sing. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.miserarum: miser, -era, -erum — wretched, pitiable, unhappy (gen. pl. fem.)
glossary.miseris: miser, -era, -erum — wretched, pitiable (dat./abl. pl.; often as a noun, 'the wretched')
glossary.miseros: miser, -era, -erum — wretched, pitiable, unhappy (acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.monitusque: monitus, -ūs m. — and warnings, admonitions (acc. pl., 4th decl., with -que 'and'); the same letters are also moneō's perf. pass. part. 'warned' (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.morbi: morbus, -ī m. — disease, sickness (gen. sing.; also nom. pl.)
glossary.morer: moror, morārī — I may delay, hold up, detain (1st sing. pres. subj., deponent)
glossary.mores: mōs, mōris m. — (pl.) character, habits, ways, morals (nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.moriturus: morior, morī, mortuus sum — about to die, doomed to die (nom. sing. masc., fut. act. part.)
glossary.mortisque: mors, mortis f. — death (gen. sing., with -que 'and')
glossary.movebere: moveō, movēre — you will be moved, stirred, affected (2nd sing. fut. indic. pass., poetic -re for -ris)
glossary.muneraque: mūnus, mūneris n. — and gifts, presents; duties (nom./acc. pl., with -que 'and')
glossary.muneribus: mūnus, mūneris n. — gift, present; duty, service (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.muneribusque: mūnus, mūneris n. — and with gifts, offerings (dat./abl. pl., with -que 'and')
glossary.mutatus: mūtō, mūtāre, mūtāvī, mūtātus — changed, altered (nom. sing. masc., perf. pass. part.)
glossary.myconum: Mycōnus (Mycōnos), -ī f. — Myconos, an island of the Cyclades (acc. sing.)
glossary.myrmidonasque: Myrmidones, -um m. pl. — and the Myrmidons, the people of Aegina, later followers of Achilles (acc. pl., Greek form -as, with -que 'and')
glossary.nactasque: nancīscor, nancīscī, nactus sum — and having obtained, come by, got (acc. pl. fem., perf. part. of a deponent verb, so active in sense, with -que 'and')
glossary.nascuntur: nāscor, nāscī, nātus sum — they are born, come into being, spring up (3rd pl. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.nebulis: nebula, -ae f. — mist, cloud, fog (abl. pl.)
glossary.nereius: Nērēius, -a, -um — of Nereus, descended from Nereus the sea-god (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.nexis: nectō, nectere, nexuī, nexus — bound, fastened, linked together (dat./abl. pl., perf. pass. part.)
glossary.nigrumque: niger, nigra, nigrum — and black, dark (acc. sing. masc. or nom./acc. sing. neut., with -que 'and')
glossary.nitente: nītor, nītī, nīxus sum — leaning, resting, propped (on, + abl.) (abl. sing., pres. part. of a deponent verb); identical in form to niteō's participle nitēns 'shining, gleaming'
glossary.nitidaeque: nitidus, -a, -um — and shining, glossy, sleek (gen./dat. sing. fem., with -que 'and'; also nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.nodus: nōdus, -ī m. — knot, knob (in wood) (nom. sing.)
glossary.noscoque: nōscō, nōscere, nōvī, nōtus — and I recognise, come to know (1st sing. pres. indic. act., with -que 'and')
glossary.nuruumque: nurus, -ūs f. — and daughters-in-law, young married women (gen. pl., 4th decl., with -que 'and')
glossary.obliquantem: oblīquō, oblīquāre — turning aside, slanting, averting (acc. sing. masc./fem., pres. act. part.)
glossary.obsuntque: obsum, obesse — and they are harmful, do damage to (+ dat.) (3rd pl. pres. indic., with -que 'and')
glossary.obvia: obvius, -a, -um — in the way, meeting, coming to meet (+ dat.) (nom./abl. sing. fem.; also nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.occumbere: occumbō, occumbere — to fall in death, meet one's end (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.occurrunt: occurrō, occurrere — they run to meet, come up to (+ dat.) (3rd pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.odissem: ōdī, ōdisse — I should hate, loathe (1st sing. pluperf. subj.; a defective verb whose perfect stem carries present meaning, so this reads as an imperfect)
glossary.oenopiam: Oenōpia, -ae f. — Oenopia, the old name of the island of Aegina (acc. sing.)
glossary.offensaque: offendō, offendere, offendī, offēnsus — and offended, hurt, affronted (nom./abl. sing. fem., perf. pass. part., with -que 'and'); the same form is also the noun offēnsa, -ae f. 'affront, offence'
glossary.oliaros: Oliaros, -ī f. — Oliaros, an island of the Cyclades west of Paros (nom. sing., Greek declension)
glossary.operata: operor, operārī, operātus sum — having devoted herself to, busied with (+ dat.), esp. in religious service (nom./abl. sing. fem., perf. part. of a deponent verb, so active in sense)
glossary.opis: ops, opis f. — help, aid, resources (gen. sing.; the nom. sing. is scarcely used, and the plural opēs means 'wealth, power')
glossary.oportuit: oportet, oportēre, oportuit — it was fitting, one ought to have (3rd sing. perf. indic.; impersonal verb)
glossary.optime: bonus, -a, -um (superl. optimus) — best, most excellent (voc. sing. masc.); the same letters are also the adverb optimē 'best, very well'
glossary.orabam: ōrō, ōrāre — I was begging, entreating, praying for (1st sing. imperf. indic. act.)
glossary.orithyiae: Ōrīthyia, -ae f. — Orithyia, daughter of Erechtheus of Athens, carried off by Boreas (gen./dat. sing.)
glossary.ortum: orior, orīrī, ortus sum — sprung from, arisen, born (acc. sing. masc./neut., perf. part. of a deponent verb, so active in sense); the same form is also the noun ortus, -ūs m. 'rising, origin' (acc. sing.)
glossary.oviumque: ovis, ovis f. — and of sheep (gen. pl., with -que 'and')
glossary.pacaverat: pācō, pācāre — had subdued, brought to peace (3rd sing. pluperf. indic. act.)
glossary.pallante: Pallās, Pallantis m. — Pallas, son of Pandion and brother of Aegeus, an Athenian prince (abl. sing.); distinct from Pallās, Palladis f., the goddess Athena
glossary.parcum: parcus, -a, -um — thrifty, sparing, frugal (nom./acc. sing. neut.; also acc. sing. masc.)
glossary.pares: pār, paris — equal, matched, a match for (+ dat.) (nom./acc. pl. masc./fem.); the same letters are also 2nd sing. pres. subj. of parō 'you may prepare'
glossary.paron: Paros, -ī f. — Paros, an island of the Cyclades famed for its marble (acc. sing., Greek form Paron)
glossary.partior: partior, partīrī, partītus sum — I divide, share out, distribute (1st sing. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.parvamque: parvus, -a, -um — and small, little (acc. sing. fem., with -que 'and')

glossary.phoce: Phōcus, -ī m. — Phocus, son of Aeacus by the sea-nymph Psamathe, half-brother of Telamon and Peleus (voc. sing.)
glossary.phocus: Phōcus, -ī m. — Phocus, son of Aeacus by the sea-nymph Psamathe, half-brother of Telamon and Peleus (nom. sing.)

glossary.prodidit: prōdō, prōdere — betrayed; gave up, handed down (3rd sing. perfect indicative active)

glossary.properus: properus, -a, -um — hurrying, in haste, quick (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.prosiliunt: prōsiliō, prōsilīre — they leap forth, spring up (3rd pl. present indicative active)
glossary.provida: prōvidus, -a, -um — foreseeing, provident, prophetic (nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.pudicam: pudīcus, -a, -um — chaste, modest, virtuous (acc. sing. fem.)

glossary.regemque: rēx, rēgis m. — king (acc. sing. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.repetam: repetō, repetere — I shall go back over, recount from the start (1st sing. future indicative active; the identical form is also present subjunctive)

glossary.requiris: requīrō, requīrere — you seek, ask after, miss (2nd sing. present indicative active)
glossary.requiro: requīrō, requīrere — I seek, ask after, miss (1st sing. present indicative active)
glossary.reservet: reservō, reservāre — keeps back, saves up (3rd sing. present subjunctive active)
glossary.restantem: restō, restāre — resisting, holding out, standing firm (present active participle, acc. sing.)
glossary.retexuit: retexō, retexere — unwove, unravelled, undid (3rd sing. perfect indicative active)

glossary.rugosoque: rūgōsus, -a, -um — wrinkled, furrowed, ridged (abl. sing. masc./neut. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.salutis: salūs, salūtis f. — safety, deliverance; health, well-being (gen. sing.)

glossary.scythicis: Scythicus, -a, -um — Scythian, of Scythia, the lands north of the Black Sea (abl. pl.)
glossary.secundo: secundus, -a, -um — favourable, auspicious; following, second (abl. sing. masc./neut.). Distinct from secundō, secundāre 'to favour'
glossary.secures: secūris, -is f. — axe, sacrificial axe (nom. pl.; the same form is acc. pl.). Not the adjective sēcūrus

glossary.semianimes: sēmianimis, -e — half-alive, half-dead (acc. pl. masc./fem.; the same form is nom. pl.)
glossary.senumque: senex, senis m. — old man (gen. pl. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.sequentur: sequor, sequī — they will follow, accompany (3rd pl. future indicative, deponent)
glossary.servantes: servō, servāre — keeping, guarding, preserving (present active participle, acc. pl. masc./fem.; the same form is nom. pl.)

glossary.servor: servō, servāre — I am kept, guarded, reserved (1st sing. present indicative passive)
glossary.silvisque: silva, -ae f. — wood, forest (dat./abl. pl. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.sinis: Sinis, -is m. — Sinis, the pine-bending brigand of the Isthmus of Corinth, killed by Theseus (nom. sing.). Distinct from sinis, 2nd sing. of sinō 'allow'
glossary.sintque: sum, esse — let them be, may they be (3rd pl. present subjunctive + enclitic -que 'and')

glossary.somni: somnus, -ī m. — sleep (gen. sing.; the same form is nom. pl.). Distinct from somnium, -ī n. 'dream', gen. sing. somniī

glossary.sospite: sospes, sospitis — safe, unharmed, having come through unhurt (abl. sing.)
glossary.sparsisque: spargō, spargere — scattered, strewn, sprinkled (perfect passive participle, dat./abl. pl., + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.sparsuras: spargō, spargere — about to scatter, going to strew (future active participle, acc. pl. fem.)
glossary.spectari: spectō, spectāre — to be looked at, be seen (present passive infinitive)
glossary.speque: spēs, speī f. — hope (abl. sing. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.sperabam: spērō, spērāre — I was hoping, kept hoping (1st sing. imperfect indicative active)
glossary.spirarunt: spīrō, spīrāre — they breathed, blew (3rd pl. perfect indicative active, syncopated for spīrāvērunt)
glossary.spissa: spissus, -a, -um — thick, dense, close-packed (abl. sing. fem.; the same form is nom. sing. fem. and nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.stabunt: stō, stāre — they will stand, stand firm (3rd pl. future indicative active; with an ablative of price, stāre means 'to cost')
glossary.statuo: statuō, statuere — I decide, determine; I set up (1st sing. present indicative active)
glossary.status: status, -ūs m. — state, condition, position (nom. sing., 4th decl.). Distinct from status, the perfect participle of sistō 'set up'
glossary.strage: strāgēs, -is f. — slaughter, carnage; a heap of the fallen (abl. sing.)
glossary.stratum: strātum, -ī n. — bed-covering, bedding, couch (acc. sing.); also strātus, the perfect passive participle of sternō 'lay low, strew' (nom./acc. sing. neut.). Both uses occur in this text
glossary.studiosus: studiōsus, -a, -um — eager for, devoted to, fond of (+ gen.) (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.subiectos: subiciō, subicere — placed underneath, set below (perfect passive participle, acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.sublimia: sublīmis, -e — lofty, high, raised aloft (nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.sufficit: sufficiō, sufficere — suffices, is enough (3rd sing. present indicative active)
glossary.sulco: sulcus, -ī m. — furrow (abl. sing.; the same form is dat. sing.). Distinct from sulcō, sulcāre 'to furrow'
glossary.sumimus: sūmō, sūmere — we take, take up (1st pl. present indicative active)
glossary.sumpta: sūmō, sūmere — taken up, assumed (perfect passive participle, nom./acc. pl. neut.; the same form is nom. sing. fem. and abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.superabit: superō, superāre — will surpass, outstrip, overcome (3rd sing. future indicative active)
glossary.supple: suppleō, supplēre — fill up, make complete, replenish (2nd sing. present imperative active)
glossary.supremo: suprēmus, -a, -um — highest; last, final (abl. sing. masc./neut.; superlative of superus)
glossary.suscipimus: suscipiō, suscipere — we undertake, take upon ourselves (1st pl. present indicative active)
glossary.tabent: tābeō, tābēre — they waste away, rot, melt away (3rd pl. present indicative active)
glossary.tactusque: tangō, tangere — touched, affected, moved (perfect passive participle, nom. sing. masc., + enclitic -que 'and'). Distinct from tactus, -ūs m. 'touch', spelled alike
glossary.taedia: taedium, -ī n. — weariness, disgust, loathing (nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.tantaeque: tantus, -a, -um — so great, so large (gen. sing. fem. + enclitic -que 'and'; the same form is dat. sing. fem. and nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.telamon: Telamōn, -ōnis m. — Telamon, son of Aeacus, brother of Peleus, father of Ajax (nom. sing.)
glossary.telamonque: Telamōn, -ōnis m. — Telamon, son of Aeacus, brother of Peleus, father of Ajax (nom. sing. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.temptamenta: temptāmentum, -ī n. — trial, test, attempt (nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.tenax: tenāx, tenācis — holding fast, tenacious, clinging (often + gen.) (nom. sing.)
glossary.teneat: teneō, tenēre — holds, keeps, occupies (3rd sing. present subjunctive active)
glossary.tenebroso: tenebrōsus, -a, -um — dark, gloomy, shadowy (abl. sing. masc./neut.)
glossary.tenos: Tēnos, -ī f. — Tenos, one of the Cyclades in the Aegean (nom. sing., Greek form)
glossary.ternis: ternī, -ae, -a — three each, three at a time, threefold (distributive numeral, dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.thalamosque: thalamus, -ī m. — bedchamber, marriage-chamber; marriage (acc. pl. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.theseu: Thēseus, -eī m. — Theseus, son of Aegeus, hero and king of Athens (voc. sing.)
glossary.theseus: Thēseus, -eī m. — Theseus, son of Aegeus, hero and king of Athens (nom. sing.)
glossary.thymo: thymum, -ī n. — thyme (abl. sing.; the same form is dat. sing.)
glossary.timemus: timeō, timēre — we fear, are afraid of (1st pl. present indicative active)
glossary.timori: timor, timōris m. — fear, dread (dat. sing.)
glossary.tirynthius: Tīrynthius, -a, -um — Tirynthian, of Tiryns in the Argolid; as a noun, the hero of Tiryns, i.e. Hercules (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.titulos: titulus, -ī m. — inscription, title; mark of honour, distinction (acc. pl.)
glossary.tonitruque: tonitrus, -ūs m. (also tonitruum, -ī n.) — thunder, thunderclap (abl. sing. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.torosa: torōsus, -a, -um — muscular, brawny, bulging with muscle (nom./acc. pl. neut.; the same form is nom./abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.torrentur: torreō, torrēre — they are scorched, parched, burned (3rd pl. present indicative passive)
glossary.totius: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire, all (gen. sing., all genders)
glossary.tremiscere: tremīscō, tremīscere — to begin to tremble, start shaking (present active infinitive, inceptive)
glossary.tribusque: trēs, tria — three (dat./abl. pl. + enclitic -que 'and'). Distinct from tribus, -ūs f. 'tribe', spelled alike
glossary.tristes: trīstis, -e — sad, grim, gloomy, harsh (nom. pl. masc./fem.; the same form is acc. pl.)
glossary.tristique: trīstis, -e — sad, grim, gloomy, harsh (abl. sing. + enclitic -que 'and'; the same form is dat. sing.)
glossary.tulerit: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — he/she brought, bore, won (3rd sing. perfect subjunctive active; the identical form is also future perfect indicative)
glossary.tulerunt: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — they brought, bore, carried (3rd pl. perfect indicative active)
glossary.ubicumque: ubicumque — wherever, in whatever place (indeclinable relative adverb)

glossary.ultroque: ultrō — of one's own accord, voluntarily, unprompted; besides (indeclinable adverb + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.ursi: ursus, -ī m. — bear (nom. pl.; the same form is gen. sing.)
glossary.utilius: ūtilis, -e — more useful, more advantageous (comparative, nom./acc. sing. neut.; the same form serves as the comparative adverb 'more usefully')
glossary.vacuos: vacuus, -a, -um — empty, vacant, free of (+ abl.) (acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.vagantur: vagor, vagārī — they wander, roam, drift (3rd pl. present indicative, deponent)
glossary.valebant: valeō, valēre — they were strong, were able, had the strength (3rd pl. imperfect indicative active)
glossary.velata: vēlō, vēlāre — veiled, covered, clothed (perfect passive participle, nom. sing. fem.; the same form is nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.velimus: volō, velle — we should wish, may we wish (1st pl. present subjunctive active). From volō 'wish', not volō, volāre 'fly'
glossary.veniendi: veniō, venīre — of coming, of arriving (gerund, gen. sing.)
glossary.venientia: veniō, venīre — coming, approaching (present active participle, nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.versantes: versō, versāre — turning, rolling, twisting about (present active participle, acc. pl. masc./fem.; the same form is nom. pl.)
glossary.veterumque: vetus, veteris — old, former, of long standing (gen. pl. + enclitic -que 'and')

glossary.videbis: videō, vidēre — you will see (2nd sing. future indicative active)
glossary.vigilans: vigilō, vigilāre — waking, awake, keeping watch (present active participle, nom. sing.)
glossary.viis: via, -ae f. — road, way, street (abl. pl.; the same form is dat. pl.)

glossary.vinctorum: vinciō, vincīre, vīnxī, vīnctum — bound, tied, fettered (perfect passive participle, gen. pl. masc./neut.). From vinciō 'bind'; the participle of vincō 'conquer' is victus
glossary.vinum: vīnum, -ī n. — wine (acc. sing.; the same form is nom. sing.)
glossary.vitiantur: vitiō, vitiāre — they are spoiled, tainted, corrupted (3rd pl. present indicative passive)
glossary.vittis: vitta, -ae f. — fillet, ribbon, sacrificial headband (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.vocesque: vōx, vōcis f. — voice; word, utterance (acc. pl. + enclitic -que 'and'; the same form is nom. pl.)
glossary.voles: volō, velle — you will wish, you will want (2nd sing. future indicative active). From volō 'wish', not volō, volāre 'fly'

glossary.captare: captō, captāre — try to catch, snap at (pres. act. inf.)

glossary.devovitque: dēvoveō, dēvovēre, dēvōvī — curse, damn (3rd sing. perf. ind. act. + enclitic -que “and”)

glossary.dicebat: dīcō, dīcere — say, call (3rd sing. imperf. ind. act.)
