glossary.insequeris: īnsequor, īnsequī — you pursue, you press the charge against (2nd sing. pres. ind.; deponent — passive in form, active in sense; the future would be īnsequēris, with a long e)
glossary.insilit: īnsiliō, īnsilīre — leaps into, springs onto (3rd sing. pres. ind. act.; takes the dat. or in + acc.)
glossary.instruit: īnstruō, īnstruere, īnstrūxī — equips, fits out; also instructs (3rd sing. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.intendensque: intendō, intendere — and stretching out, straining (pres. act. part., nom. sing. fem. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.intresque: intrō, intrāre — and may you enter (2nd sing. pres. subj. act. + enclitic -que “and”; subjunctive of wish)
glossary.invitum: invītus, -a, -um — unwilling, against his will (acc. sing. masc.)
glossary.iterata: iterō, iterāre — repeated, retraced, gone over a second time (perf. pass. part., nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.iubeo: iubeō, iubēre, iussī — I bid, order, tell (1st sing. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.iudice: iūdex, iūdicis m./f. — judge (abl. sing.; common gender, so it serves for a woman too)
glossary.iunctam: iungō, iungere, iūnxī, iūnctum — joined, coupled (perf. pass. part., acc. sing. fem.)
glossary.iunonia: Iūnōnius, -a, -um — of Juno, sacred to Juno (nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.iurabat: iūrō, iūrāre — was swearing, would swear (3rd sing. imperf. ind. act.)
glossary.iustissimus: iūstus, -a, -um — most just, entirely fair (superlative, nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.iuvenaliter: iuvenāliter — in youthful fashion, with a young man’s energy (adv.)
glossary.laceraret: lacerō, lacerāre — might tear, might mangle (3rd sing. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.lacrimans: lacrimō, lacrimāre — weeping, in tears (pres. act. part., nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.laelapa: Laelaps, -apis m. — Laelaps (“Storm-wind”), Cephalus’ hound (Greek acc. sing.)
glossary.laeter: laetor, laetārī — am I to rejoice? (1st sing. pres. subj.; deponent — passive in form, active in sense)
glossary.laiades: Lāiadēs, -ae m. — the son of Laius, i.e. Oedipus (nom. sing.)
glossary.lapillo: lapillus, -ī m. — little stone, pebble (abl. sing.)
glossary.lapsum: lāpsus, -ūs m. — a fall, a slipping (acc. sing.); or lābor, lābī, lāpsus — having slipped, having fallen (perf. part. of the deponent, acc. sing. masc., active in sense)
glossary.laudabat: laudō, laudāre — was praising, kept praising (3rd sing. imperf. ind. act.)
glossary.lebinthos: Lebinthos, -ī f. — Lebinthos, an island of the Sporades (nom. sing., Greek -os for -us)
glossary.lenis: lēnis, -e — gentle, soft, mild (nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.letoia: Lētōius, -a, -um — of Leto (Latona), Leto’s (nom. sing. fem.; prōlēs Lētōia means Apollo)
glossary.librat: lībrō, lībrāre — balances, poises, swings for a throw (3rd sing. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.libravit: lībrō, lībrāre, lībrāvī — balanced, poised (3rd sing. perf. ind. act.)
glossary.ligo: ligō, ligāre — I bind, bind up, tie (1st sing. pres. ind. act.; not the noun ligō, ligōnis m. “mattock”)
glossary.lino: līnum, -ī n. — flax, linen thread, string (abl. sing.; not the verb linō “smear”)
glossary.liquit: linquō, linquere, līquī — left, left behind (3rd sing. perf. ind. act.; not from liquō “melt, strain”)
glossary.longumque: longus, -a, -um — and long (acc. sing. neut. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.lucifero: Lūcifer, -erī m. — Lucifer, the Morning Star (the planet Venus before dawn) (abl. sing.)
glossary.lusuque: lūsus, -ūs m. — and play, sport, playing about (abl. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.manentem: maneō, manēre, mānsī — remaining, lasting, still holding (pres. act. part., acc. sing. fem.)
glossary.martis: Mārs, Mārtis m. — Mars, god of war; by metonymy war, fighting (gen. sing.)
glossary.mavors: Māvors, -ortis m. — Mavors, the older poetic name of Mars; by metonymy war (nom. sing.)
glossary.medere: medeor, medērī — heal!, remedy! (2nd sing. pres. imperative; deponent, so the imperative ends in -re and is not a passive infinitive; takes the dat.)
glossary.meliore: melior, melius — better (comparative of bonus, abl. sing. masc.)
glossary.meminisse: meminī, meminisse — to remember (perf. inf.; a defective verb, perfect in form but present in sense; takes the gen.)
glossary.memorabat: memorō, memorāre — was recounting, was relating (3rd sing. imperf. ind. act.)
glossary.mentitus: mentior, mentīrī, mentītus — having lied, having feigned, pretending (perf. part., nom. sing. masc.; deponent, so active in sense)
glossary.meosque: meus, -a, -um — and my, my own (acc. pl. masc. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.merentem: mereō, merēre (also dep. mereor, merērī) — deserving it, earning what she gets (pres. act. part., acc. sing. fem.)
glossary.meriti: meritum, -ī n. — service, deserving deed, favour earned (gen. sing.; the noun, not the perf. part. of mereor)
glossary.minima: minimus, -a, -um — smallest, least (superlative of parvus, abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.minoide: Mīnōis, -idos f. — the daughter of Minos, i.e. Ariadne (abl. sing., Greek patronymic)
glossary.misi: mittō, mittere, mīsī — I sent, I hurled, I let fly (1st sing. perf. ind. act.)
glossary.moneo: moneō, monēre — I warn, advise, remind (1st sing. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.monstrum: mōnstrum, -ī n. — monster, monstrosity, unnatural thing (acc. sing.)
glossary.morantia: moror, morārī — delaying, holding back (pres. act. part., acc. pl. neut.; deponent, active in sense)
glossary.moraque: mora, -ae f. — and delay (abl. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.motaque: moveō, movēre, mōvī, mōtum — and stirred, set moving (perf. pass. part., abl. sing. fem. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.multiplicique: multiplex, -icis — and manifold, with many windings (abl. sing. fem. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.narratur: nārrō, nārrāre — is told, is related (3rd sing. pres. ind. pass.)
glossary.natalis: nātālis, -e — of one’s birth, native (gen. sing. masc.; the adjective, not the noun nātālis, -is m. “birthday”)
glossary.naturamque: nātūra, -ae f. — and nature (acc. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.nefanda: nefāndus, -a, -um — unspeakable, abominable, not to be uttered (abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.negetur: negō, negāre — may be denied, may be refused (3rd sing. pres. subj. pass.)
glossary.nise: Nīsus, -ī m. — Nisus, king of Megara, father of Scylla (voc. sing.)
glossary.niseia: Nīsēius, -a, -um — of Nisus, Nisus’ (nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.nisus: Nīsus, -ī m. — Nisus, king of Megara, father of Scylla (nom. sing.; not the noun nīsus, -ūs m. “effort” nor the perf. part. of nītor)
glossary.nitidos: nitidus, -a, -um — shining, bright, gleaming (acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.nixique: Nīxus, -ī m. — and of the Kneeler, the constellation Engonasin, identified with Hercules; the name means “the one straining on his knee” (gen. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.noctisque: nox, noctis f. — and of night (gen. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.nodo: nōdus, -ī m. — knot; also a joint or pivot (abl. sing.)
glossary.nodosa: nōdōsus, -a, -um — knotted, full of knots (nom. pl. neut.)
glossary.noster: noster, nostra, nostrum — our (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.nostroque: noster, nostra, nostrum — and our (dat. or abl. sing. masc./neut. — the forms are identical; + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.notatas: notō, notāre — marked, noticed, observed (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. fem.)
glossary.novat: novō, novāre — makes new, alters, remakes (3rd sing. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.novenis: novēnī, -ae, -a — nine each, in nines (distributive numeral, abl. pl. masc.)
glossary.novoque: novus, -a, -um — and new, fresh (abl. sing. masc. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.nudaverat: nūdō, nūdāre, nūdāvī — had laid bare, had uncovered (3rd sing. pluperf. ind. act.)
glossary.nullius: nūllus, -a, -um — of no, of none (gen. sing. fem.)
glossary.oblite: oblīvīscor, oblīvīscī, oblītus — you who have forgotten (perf. part., voc. sing. masc.; deponent, so active in sense; takes the gen.)
glossary.obstaret: obstō, obstāre — might stand in the way of, might block (3rd sing. imperf. subj. act.; takes the dat.)
glossary.obstruat: obstruō, obstruere — let him block, may he bar (3rd sing. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.occurrensque: occurrō, occurrere — and running to meet, meeting (pres. act. part., nom. sing. masc. + enclitic -que “and”; takes the dat.)
glossary.odere: ōdī, ōdisse — they hate (3rd pl. perf. ind.; -ēre for -ērunt, and the verb is perfect in form but present in sense)
glossary.odoratas: odōrātus, -a, -um — fragrant, sweet-smelling (acc. pl. fem.; the adjective, not the perf. part. of odōror “smell out”)
glossary.opprobrium: opprobrium, -ī n. — disgrace, reproach, a standing scandal (nom. sing.)
glossary.optima: optimus, -a, -um — best, dearest (superlative of bonus, voc. sing. fem.)
glossary.orientis: orior, orīrī — rising (pres. act. part., gen. sing. fem.; deponent, active in sense; not the noun oriēns “the east”)
glossary.orionis: Ōrīōn, -ōnis m. — Orion, the hunter set among the stars (gen. sing.)
glossary.ostro: ostrum, -ī n. — purple, purple dye from the murex (abl. sing.)
glossary.parem: pār, paris — an equal, a match (acc. sing. masc./fem., the adjective used as a noun; not the pres. subj. of parō)
glossary.parosque: Paros, -ī f. — and Paros, an island of the Cyclades (nom. sing., Greek -os for -us, + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.pasiphaen: Pāsiphaē, -ēs f. — Pasiphae, wife of Minos and mother of the Minotaur (Greek acc. sing.)
glossary.pastum: pāscō, pāscere, pāvī, pāstum — fed, fattened, pastured (perf. pass. part., acc. sing. neut.; not the noun pāstus, -ūs m. “fodder”)
glossary.patebat: pateō, patēre — was lying open, was plain for all to see (3rd sing. imperf. ind. act.)
glossary.pateret: pateō, patēre — might lie open, might be available (3rd sing. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.paterno: paternus, -a, -um — of a father, paternal (abl. sing. masc.)
glossary.patiare: patior, patī, passus — you allow, you suffer (2nd sing. pres. subj.; deponent, active in sense; -re for -ris)
glossary.patriae: patria, -ae f. — native land, fatherland (dat. sing.); or patrius, -a, -um — of a father, a father’s (nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.patrique: pater, patris m. — and to a father (dat. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.pavere: paveō, pavēre, pāvī — they dreaded, were terrified at (3rd pl. perf. ind. act.; -ēre for -ērunt, not the pres. inf.)
glossary.pecorumque: pecus, pecoris n. — and of the flocks, of the herds (gen. pl. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.pelago: pelagus, -ī n. — the sea, the open sea (abl. sing.; a Greek loan, 2nd decl. but neuter)
glossary.pennarum: penna, -ae f. — of the feathers, of the wings (gen. pl.)
glossary.percipit: percipiō, percipere — catches, takes hold of, gets a grip on (3rd sing. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.perdix: perdīx, -īcis m./f. — partridge; also Perdix, the nephew of Daedalus turned into that bird (nom. sing.)
glossary.pereant: pereō, perīre — let them perish, may they be lost (3rd pl. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.perempto: perimō, perimere, perēmī, peremptum — killed, done away with (perf. pass. part., abl. sing. masc.)
glossary.perenni: perennis, -e — everlasting, unfailing, year-round (abl. sing. neut.)
glossary.pereo: pereō, perīre — I am dying, I perish (1st sing. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.pericla: perīculum, -ī n. — dangers, perils (acc. pl.; perīcla is the syncopated poetic form of perīcula)
glossary.perimat: perimō, perimere — let him destroy, may he kill (3rd sing. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.petebatur: petō, petere, petīvī — was being sought, was being asked for (3rd sing. imperf. ind. pass.)
glossary.phrygius: Phrygius, -a, -um — Phrygian, of Phrygia in Asia Minor (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.plagarum: plaga, -ae f. — hunting-net, snare (gen. pl.; not plāga “blow” or plaga “region, tract”)
glossary.plausit: plaudō, plaudere — clapped, beat, flapped (3rd sing. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.plures: plūrēs, plūra — more, a good many (compar. of multus; acc. pl. fem.)
glossary.ponentem: pōnō, pōnere — laying, placing (pres. act. part., acc. sing. masc.)
glossary.ponitque: pōnō, pōnere — lays, sets down (3rd sing. pres. act. ind. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.pontusque: pontus, -ī m. — sea, open sea (nom. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.porrecta: porrigō, porrigere — held out, proffered (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. neut., used as a noun: the things held out; the form is also nom./abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.porta: porta, -ae f. — gate, city-gate (abl. sing.; the same letters are also 2nd sing. pres. of portō “you carry”)
glossary.posceret: poscō, poscere — should demand, should ask for (3rd sing. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.poscor: poscō, poscere — I am called on, am asked for (1st sing. pres. pass. ind.; keeps an acc. of the thing demanded)
glossary.positarum: pōnō, pōnere — set out, laid in place (perf. pass. part., gen. pl. fem.)
glossary.possideat: possideō, possidēre — let him possess, though he possess (3rd sing. pres. subj. act., concessive)
glossary.poteramus: possum, posse — we were able, we could (1st pl. imperf. ind.)
glossary.praebuit: praebeō, praebēre — offered, lent, presented (3rd sing. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.praecepta: praeceptum, -ī n. — instructions, precepts, teaching (acc. pl.)
glossary.praecipitata: praecipitō, praecipitāre — flung headlong, cast down (perf. pass. part., nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.praedaque: praeda, -ae f. — booty, spoil, prize (abl. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.praeferret: praeferō, praeferre — would set before, would prefer (3rd sing. imperf. subj. act.; the thing preferred in acc., the thing outranked in dat.)
glossary.praelate: praeferō, praeferre — preferred, set above (perf. pass. part., voc. sing. masc.)
glossary.praeposuisse: praepōnō, praepōnere — to have preferred, to have set before (perf. act. inf.)
glossary.praestare: praestō, praestāre — to furnish, provide, make good (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.praetemptatque: praetemptō, praetemptāre — tries out beforehand, tests (3rd sing. pres. act. ind. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.prioribus: prior, prius — earlier, former (compar. adj.; abl. pl. masc.)
glossary.priorum: prior, prius — of earlier men, of those before (compar. adj. used as a noun; gen. pl. masc.)
glossary.prodita: prōdō, prōdere — betrayed, given up to the enemy (perf. pass. part., voc. pl. neut.; the form is also nom./acc. pl. neut. and nom./abl. sing. fem.)
glossary.produxit: prōdūcō, prōdūcere — brought forth, led out (3rd sing. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.progenuit: prōgignō, prōgignere — begot, fathered (3rd sing. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.progressaque: prōgredior, prōgredī — having gone forth, having advanced (perf. part., nom. sing. fem. + enclitic -que “and”; deponent, so active in sense)
glossary.prohibes: prohibeō, prohibēre — you keep off, you bar, you shut out (2nd sing. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.properare: properō, properāre — to hurry, to make haste (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.propter: propter — close to, hard by; also on account of (prep. + acc.)
glossary.pulcherrime: pulcher, pulchra, pulchrum — fairest, most beautiful (superl. pulcherrimus, voc. sing. masc.; the same letters can be the superl. adverb “most beautifully”)
glossary.puppes: puppis, -is f. — sterns, and so ships (acc. pl.)
glossary.puppim: puppis, -is f. — stern, and so ship (acc. sing., Greek-style -im)
glossary.puppimque: puppis, -is f. — stern, and so ship (acc. sing., Greek-style -im, + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.purpureusque: purpureus, -a, -um — clad in purple, purple-bright (nom. sing. masc. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.quatit: quatiō, quatere — shakes, beats, flails (3rd sing. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.ratibus: ratis, -is f. — rafts, ships, vessels (abl. pl.)
glossary.recedit: recēdō, recēdere — draws back, falls away, recedes (3rd sing. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.recludere: reclūdō, reclūdere — to unbar, throw open (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.recordor: recordor, recordārī — I remember, I call to mind (1st sing. pres. ind.; deponent, so active in sense)
glossary.recurvam: recurvus, -a, -um — curved back, hooked (acc. sing. fem.)
glossary.redeuntibus: redeō, redīre — returning, coming home (pres. act. part., dat. pl. masc.)
glossary.refecta: reficiō, reficere — restored, brought round again (perf. pass. part., nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.reficisque: reficiō, reficere — you restore, you revive (2nd sing. pres. act. ind. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.refluitque: refluō, refluere — flows back (3rd sing. pres. act. ind. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.regebat: regō, regere — was guiding, was controlling (3rd sing. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.regione: regiō, -ōnis f. — region, quarter, direction (abl. sing.)
glossary.relecto: relegō, relegere — traversed again, gathered back up (perf. pass. part., abl. sing. neut.; from re- + legō, not relēgō, relēgāre “banish”)
glossary.relictae: relinquō, relinquere — left behind (perf. pass. part., nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.relinquis: relinquō, relinquere — you leave behind, you abandon (2nd sing. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.remanente: remaneō, remanēre — remaining, staying behind (pres. act. part., abl. sing.)
glossary.remigioque: rēmigium, -ī n. — oarage, the gear of oars; of a bird, its wings as oars (abl. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.renidenti: renīdeō, renīdēre — beaming, smiling, shining (pres. act. part., abl. sing.)
glossary.repetebam: repetō, repetere — I kept seeking again, I would go back to (1st sing. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.repetenda: repetō, repetere — to be given again, to be repeated (gerundive, acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.requies: requiēs, -ētis f. — rest, respite, relief (nom. sing.)
glossary.requiram: requīrō, requīrere — am I to look for, shall I seek (1st sing. pres. subj. act., deliberative; identical in form to the fut. act. ind.)
glossary.reserabit: reserō, reserāre — will unbar, will throw open (3rd sing. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.resonantia: resonō, resonāre — resounding, echoing (pres. act. part., acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.retegente: retegō, retegere — uncovering, laying bare (pres. act. part., abl. sing.)
glossary.retinacula: retināculum, -ī n. — mooring-cables, holdfasts, tethers (acc. pl.)
glossary.rettuleram: referō, referre — I had brought back, I had turned back (1st sing. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.revertar: revertor, revertī — am I to return, where shall I go back to (1st sing. pres. subj., deliberative; identical in form to the fut. ind.; semi-deponent, passive in form but active in sense)
glossary.revocataque: revocō, revocāre — called back, recalled (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. neut. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.rigidi: rigidus, -a, -um — stiff, unbending, harsh (gen. sing. masc.)
glossary.rogarem: rogō, rogāre — I would ask, I would beg (1st sing. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.rurigenae: rūrigena, -ae m. — country-dwellers, country folk (nom. pl. of a 1st-decl. masc. noun; the form is also gen./dat. sing.)
glossary.sacraque: sacer, sacra, sacrum — sacred, holy (abl. sing. fem. + enclitic -que “and”; the same letters can be nom./acc. pl. neut., or the noun sacra “sacred rites”)
glossary.saecli: saeculum, -ī n. — age, generation (gen. sing.; syncopated for saeculī)
glossary.samos: Samos, -ī f. — Samos, Aegean island sacred to Juno (nom. sing.; Greek 2nd decl., fem. despite the -os)
glossary.sanae: sānus, -a, -um — sound, sane, in one’s right mind (gen. sing. fem.)
glossary.sat: sat — enough, sufficiently (indecl.; shortened form of satis)
glossary.sceleratum: scelerātus, -a, -um — guilt-stained, criminal (acc. sing. masc.; a perf. pass. part. of scelerō used as an adjective)
glossary.scissaque: scindō, scindere — torn open, rent (perf. pass. part., abl. sing. fem. + enclitic -que “and”; the form is also nom. sing. fem. and nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.segnior: segnis, -e — slower, more sluggish (compar., nom. sing. masc./fem.)
glossary.seniles: senīlis, -e — of an old man, aged (nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.sepulti: sepeliō, sepelīre — of the buried man (perf. pass. part. used as a noun, gen. sing. masc.; the form is also nom. pl. masc.)
glossary.sequenti: sequor, sequī — following, coming next (pres. act. part., abl. sing.; deponent, so active in sense)
glossary.sequentis: sequor, sequī — of the one following, of the pursuer (pres. act. part., gen. sing.; the form can also be acc. pl. = sequentēs; deponent, so active in sense)
glossary.sexta: sextus, -a, -um — sixth (nom. pl. neut.; not the fem. nom. sing., which the same letters also give)
glossary.sinuaverat: sinuō, sinuāre — had bent into a curve, had drawn round (3rd sing. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.socialis: sociālis, -e — of partnership, conjugal, binding two together (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.solebam: soleō, solēre — I used to, I was in the habit of (1st sing. imperf. ind.; semi-deponent, takes an inf.)
glossary.solitus: soleō, solēre — accustomed, wont (perf. part., nom. sing. masc.; semi-deponent, so active in sense — with a form of sum it makes the perfect)
glossary.solvi: solvō, solvere — to be loosed, to be cast off (pres. pass. inf.; the same letters are also 1st sing. perf. act. ind., “I loosed”)
glossary.spatiumque: spatium, -ī n. — open space, stretch of ground (acc. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.speratque: spērō, spērāre — hopes (3rd sing. pres. act. ind. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.spinas: spīna, -ae f. — spines, backbone, fish-bones (acc. pl.)
glossary.splendidus: splendidus, -a, -um — gleaming, shining, bright (nom. sing. masc.)
glossary.spoliat: spoliō, spoliāre — strips, robs, despoils (3rd sing. pres. act. ind.; the person robbed in acc., the thing taken in abl.)
glossary.spoliis: spolium, -ī n. — spoils, arms stripped from a beaten foe (abl. pl.)
glossary.strepitum: strepitus, -ūs m. — noise, rustling, clatter (acc. sing.)
glossary.strictumque: stringō, stringere — drawn, unsheathed (perf. pass. part., acc. sing. masc. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.suasit: suādeō, suādēre — urged, prompted, advised (3rd sing. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.subducere: subdūcō, subdūcere — to draw away, to slip out from under (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.succensa: succendō, succendere — set alight, inflamed (perf. pass. part., nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.summoveant: summoveō, summovēre — may they drive off, let them banish (3rd pl. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.sumptam: sūmō, sūmere — taken, lifted, picked up (perf. pass. part., acc. sing. fem.)
glossary.superata: superō, superāre — overcome, conquered (perf. pass. part., nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.superosque: superī, -ōrum m. pl. — the gods above (from superus, -a, -um “upper”; acc. pl. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.sustinuisse: sustineō, sustinēre — to have held up, to have borne up (perf. act. inf.)
glossary.susurra: susurrus, -a, -um — whispering, murmuring (abl. sing. fem., agreeing with lingua; an adjective, distinct from the noun susurrus, -ī m. “a whisper”)
glossary.syrtis: Syrtis, -is f. — the Syrtis, the treacherous shoal-gulf off the North African coast, byword for a deadly shore (nom. sing.)
glossary.tabuerant: tābēscō, tābēscere — had melted away, had wasted away (3rd pl. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.taciturna: taciturnus, -a, -um — silent, saying nothing (nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.tangeret: tangō, tangere — might touch, should touch (3rd sing. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.telumque: tēlum, -ī n. — weapon, missile, javelin (acc. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.tenenti: teneō, tenēre — to one holding, to one who has hold (pres. act. part., dat. sing.)
glossary.tenentibus: teneō, tenēre — holding, upholding, maintaining (pres. act. part., abl. pl. neut.; the form is also dat. pl.)
glossary.tenentis: teneō, tenēre — of the one holding (pres. act. part., gen. sing.; the form can also be acc. pl. = tenentēs)
glossary.teneram: tener, tenera, tenerum — tender, young, delicate (acc. sing. fem.)
glossary.testataque: testor, testārī — having borne witness to, having proclaimed (perf. part., nom. sing. fem. + enclitic -que “and”; deponent, so active in sense — with est it forms the perf. ind.)
glossary.thalamis: thalamus, -ī m. — marriage-chamber, marriage-bed (dat. pl.; the form is also abl. pl.)
glossary.tollor: tollō, tollere — I raise myself, I am carried up (1st sing. pres. pass. ind., reflexive in sense)
glossary.tonso: tondeō, tondēre — shorn, clipped, cut off (perf. pass. part., abl. sing. masc.)
glossary.torserat: torqueō, torquēre — had hurled, had whirled (3rd sing. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.torvum: torvus, -a, -um — grim, fierce, savage of eye (acc. sing. masc.)
glossary.tractare: tractō, tractāre — to handle, to be dealing with (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.tradit: trādō, trādere — hands over, imparts, passes on (3rd sing. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.trahar: trahō, trahere — I shall be dragged (1st sing. fut. pass. ind.; the same letters are also pres. pass. subj.)
glossary.trahebant: trahō, trahere — were dragging, were drawing on (3rd pl. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.trahentem: trahō, trahere — drawing out, pulling (pres. act. part., acc. sing. masc./fem.)
glossary.transibat: trānseō, trānsīre — was crossing, was clearing (3rd sing. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.tremuere: tremō, tremere — trembled, shook (3rd pl. perf. act. ind.; syncopated for tremuērunt)
glossary.turbatque: turbō, turbāre — throws into confusion, muddles (3rd sing. pres. act. ind. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.turbatusque: turbō, turbāre — disturbed, shaken, thrown off balance (perf. pass. part., nom. sing. masc. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.unica: ūnicus, -a, -um — one and only, sole of its kind (nom. sing. fem.)
glossary.urebant: ūrō, ūrere — were burning, kept scorching (3rd pl. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.urimur: ūrō, ūrere — we are burned, we are scorched (1st pl. pres. pass. ind.)
glossary.vano: vānus, -a, -um — empty, groundless, false (abl. sing. neut.)
glossary.vanos: vānus, -a, -um — empty, futile, catching nothing (acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.vastat: vāstō, vāstāre — lays waste, ravages (3rd sing. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.velavit: vēlō, vēlāre — covered, clothed, veiled (3rd sing. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.velocis: vēlōx, vēlōcis — swift, rapid (gen. sing.; the form is also acc. pl. masc./fem.)
glossary.venatum: vēnor, vēnārī — to hunt (supine in -um, expressing purpose after a verb of motion; not the perf. part. nor the noun vēnātus, -ūs m.)
glossary.venias: veniō, venīre — may you come, come (2nd sing. pres. subj. act., jussive)
glossary.venimus: veniō, venīre — we came (1st pl. perf. act. ind., vēnimus; the same letters spell the pres. ind. venīmus, “we come”)
glossary.veniret: veniō, venīre — were to come, should come (3rd sing. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.venturas: veniō, venīre — about to come, oncoming (fut. act. part., acc. pl. fem.)
glossary.veras: vērus, -a, -um — real, true, genuine (acc. pl. fem.)
glossary.vere: vērē — truly, rightly, in very truth (adv.; the same letters are also vēre, abl. sing. of vēr, vēris n. “spring”)
glossary.vertebar: vertō, vertere — I was turning myself, I was turning (1st sing. imperf. pass. ind., reflexive in sense)
glossary.viarum: via, -ae f. — ways, roads, passages (gen. pl.)
glossary.vicisti: vincō, vincere — you have conquered, you won (2nd sing. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.victorque: victor, -ōris m. — victor, in triumph (nom. sing. + enclitic -que “and”; often in apposition, “as victor”)
glossary.viderit: videō, vidēre — she shall have seen, she has seen for herself (3rd sing. fut. perf. act. ind.; identical in form to the perf. subj.)
glossary.vinxit: vinciō, vincīre — bound, fastened together (3rd sing. perf. act. ind.; from vinciō “bind”, not vincō “conquer”, whose perfect is vīcit)
glossary.vocabat: vocō, vocāre — was calling, kept calling (3rd sing. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.vocalibus: vōcālis, -e — sounding, voiceful, that give out a note (dat. pl. masc.)
glossary.vola: volō, volāre — fly! (2nd sing. pres. act. imper.; not the noun vola, -ae f. “hollow of the hand”, nor a form of volō, velle “wish”)
glossary.volandi: volō, volāre — of flying (gerund, gen. sing.)
glossary.volatile: volātilis, -e — winged, flying, swift-flying (acc. sing. neut.)
glossary.volitat: volitō, volitāre — flits, flutters about (3rd sing. pres. act. ind.; frequentative of volō, volāre)
glossary.votique: vōtum, -ī n. — prayer, wish, vow (gen. sing. + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.vulneret: vulnerō, vulnerāre — should wound (3rd sing. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.abditus: abdo, abdere, abdidi, abditum — hidden away, put out of sight (perf. pass. part., nom. m. sg.; with fuerat forms a pluperfect passive)
glossary.abscisa: abscido, abscidere, abscidi, abscisum — cut off, lopped (perf. pass. part., abl. f. sg. agreeing with arbore, the tree)
glossary.absens: absum, abesse, afui — absent, far away (pres. part. of absum, nom. m. sg.)
glossary.abstulerat: aufero, auferre, abstuli, ablatum — take away, carry off (3rd sg. pluperf. act. indic.)
glossary.acarnanum: Acarnanes, -um m. pl. — the Acarnanians, people of Acarnania in western Greece (gen. pl.; the river Achelous is their river)
glossary.acastus: Acastus, -i m. — Acastus, son of Pelias, Argonaut and one of the Calydonian hunters (nom. sg.)
glossary.accipite: accipio, accipere, accepi, acceptum — receive, accept (2nd pl. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.acerno: acernus, -a, -um — of maple wood, maple- (adj., dat. m. sg. with trunco)
glossary.acerris: acerra, -ae f. — casket of incense, incense-box (abl. pl.)
glossary.acheloe: Achelous, -i m. — Achelous, god of the greatest river of Greece, on the Aetolian border (Greek voc. sg. in -e)
glossary.achelous: Achelous, -i m. — Achelous, god of the greatest river of Greece, on the Aetolian border (nom. sg.)
glossary.achillis: Achilles, -is m. — Achilles, son of Peleus, greatest of the Greeks at Troy (gen. sg.)
glossary.actoridaeque: Actorides, -ae m. — son of Actor; in the plural the matched twin Actoridae, Cteatus and Eurytus (patronymic, nom. pl.; -que = and)
glossary.addendum: addo, addere, addidi, additum — add, heap on (gerundive, nom. n. sg. with scelus, in the passive periphrastic addendum est, “must be added”)
glossary.ademi: adimo, adimere, ademi, ademptum — take away, strip from (1st sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.adfectibus: adfectus (affectus), -us m. — feeling, emotion, impulse (abl. pl.; the edition prints adf- for aff-)
glossary.adfer: adfero (affero), adferre, attuli, adlatum — bring, bring to (2nd sg. pres. imperative act., irregular short form; the edition prints adf- for aff-)
glossary.adflatibus: adflatus (afflatus), -us m. — a breathing on, blast of hot breath (abl. pl.; the edition prints adf- for aff-)
glossary.adfusaeque: adfundo (affundo), adfundere, adfudi, adfusum — pour upon; in the passive part. used reflexively, having flung themselves down beside (perf. pass. part., nom. f. pl.; -que = and)
glossary.adimunt: adimo, adimere, ademi, ademptum — take away, strip off, take from (+ dat. of the person) (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.; in one use the plural verb agrees by sense with the collective pars, “some of them”)
glossary.adpositas: adpono (appono), adponere, adposui, adpositum — set beside, put in place (perf. pass. part., acc. f. pl. with mensas; the edition prints adp- for app-)
glossary.adsuerant: adsuesco (assuesco), adsuescere, adsuevi, adsuetum — grow accustomed; in the perfect stem, be accustomed (3rd pl. pluperf. act. indic., syncopated for adsueverant; the pluperfect here has imperfect force, “were in the habit of”)
glossary.adversos: adversus, -a, -um — facing, turned toward one, front (adj., acc. m. pl. with armos, the shoulders fronting him)
glossary.aegre: aegre — with difficulty, ill (adv.; with ferre, “to take badly, resent”)
glossary.aequantur: aequo, aequare, aequavi, aequatum — make level, match, put on a par (3rd pl. pres. pass. indic., “are matched with,” governing the dative)
glossary.aerata: aeratus, -a, -um — fitted with bronze, bronze-tipped (adj., abl. f. sg. with cuspide; from aes, aeris, “bronze,” not from aer, “air”)
glossary.aetnaea: Aetnaeus, -a, -um — of Etna, Sicilian (adj., nom. f. sg. with tellus)
glossary.age: ago, agere, egi, actum — come on!, go on! (2nd sg. pres. imperative act. used as an interjection urging on another imperative, not in its literal sense “drive”)
glossary.agricolis: agricola, -ae m. — farmer, tiller (abl. pl. after ab; 1st decl. but masculine)
glossary.alcmenae: Alcmena (Alcmene), -ae f. — Alcmena, mother of Hercules by Jupiter (gen. sg., depending on nurum, her daughter-in-law)
glossary.althaea: Althaea, -ae f. — Althaea, wife of Oeneus and mother of Meleager (nom. sg.)
glossary.ambitiosus: ambitiosus, -a, -um — going the rounds, ranging from one to the next (adj., nom. m. sg. with honor; from ambio, “go round,” not “ambitious” in the modern sense)
glossary.ampycides: Ampycides, -ae m. — son of Ampyx, i.e. the seer Mopsus (Greek patronymic, nom. sg.)
glossary.ampycidesque: Ampycides, -ae m. — son of Ampyx, i.e. the seer Mopsus (Greek patronymic, nom. sg.; -que = and)
glossary.amyclis: Amyclae, -arum f. pl. — Amyclae, an ancient Laconian town near Sparta (abl. pl., place from which)
glossary.amyntore: Amyntor, -oris m. — Amyntor, king of the Dolopians, father of Phoenix (abl. sg., ablative of origin with cretus)
glossary.ancaei: Ancaeus, -i m. — Ancaeus, the Arcadian axeman gored by the boar (gen. sg.)
glossary.ancaeo: Ancaeus, -i m. — Ancaeus, the Arcadian axeman gored by the boar (abl. sg. after cum in one use; dat. sg. with nocuit in the other)
glossary.ancaeus: Ancaeus, -i m. — Ancaeus, the Arcadian axeman gored by the boar (nom. sg.)
glossary.ancipitemque: anceps, ancipitis — two-headed, double-bladed (adj., acc. f. sg. with securim; -que = and)
glossary.antiquis: antiquus, -a, -um — old, ancient (adj., abl. f. pl. with Amyclis)
glossary.aphareia: Aphareius, -a, -um — of Aphareus, king of Messene and father of Lynceus and Idas (adj., nom. f. sg. with proles)
glossary.aprum: aper, apri m. — wild boar (acc. sg.)
glossary.arborea: arboreus, -a, -um — of a tree, belonging to a tree (adj., abl. f. sg. with radice)
glossary.armos: armus, -i m. — shoulder, foreleg of an animal (acc. pl.)
glossary.arsisses: ardeo, ardere, arsi, arsum — burn, be aflame (2nd sg. pluperf. subj. act.; with utinam, an unfulfilled wish about the past)
glossary.audentem: audeo, audere, ausus sum — dare, venture (semi-deponent; pres. part., acc. m. sg. used substantivally, “the man making the attempt”)
glossary.auratis: auratus, -a, -um — gilded, gold-embroidered (adj., abl. f. pl. with vestibus, in the exchange construction with mutavit)
glossary.bacaque: baca (bacca), -ae f. — berry, olive (nom. sg.; -que = and)
glossary.bellatricemque: bellatrix, -icis f. — warrior-woman; used adjectivally, warlike (acc. sg. with Minervam; -que = and)
glossary.bipennifer: bipennifer, -fera, -ferum — bearing a double axe (adj., nom. m. sg.)
glossary.cadat: cado, cadere, cecidi, casum — fall, die (3rd sg. pres. subj. act.; in a quod-clause stating the ground of his grief)
glossary.caeneus: Caeneus, -ei m. — Caeneus, born the girl Caenis and made a man by Neptune (nom. sg.)
glossary.calydonides: Calydonis, -idis f. — Calydonian woman, of Calydon (Greek feminine form, nom. pl. with matres)
glossary.calydonis: Calydon, -onis f. — Calydon, the Aetolian city ruled by Oeneus (gen. sg.; not the Greek feminine adjective Calydonis, -idis, “Calydonian woman”)
glossary.calydonius: Calydonius, -a, -um — Calydonian, of Calydon (adj., nom. m. sg. with heros, i.e. Meleager)
glossary.candidioribus: candidus, -a, -um — dazzling white, gleaming (comparative, abl. m. pl. with equis; nive is the ablative of comparison)
glossary.canisve: canis, canis m./f. — dog (nom. sg.; -ve = or)
glossary.canitiem: canities, -ei f. — white hair, grey hairs (acc. sg.)
glossary.cannae: canna, -ae f. — cane, small reed (nom. pl., with parvae; one of the plants that hold the bottom of the hollow)
glossary.carior: carus, -a, -um — dear, beloved (comparative, nom. m. sg. used as a vocative, with me as ablative of comparison: “dearer to me than myself”)
glossary.cecropida: Cecropides, -ae m. — descendant of Cecrops, i.e. Athenian; here Theseus (Greek voc. sg. of a patronymic in -ides)
glossary.cererem: Ceres, Cereris f. — Ceres, goddess of the harvest; by metonymy the grain itself (acc. sg.; here the standing crop, not the goddess)
glossary.cernitis: cerno, cernere, crevi, cretum — see, make out, distinguish (2nd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.cessasse: cesso, cessare, cessavi, cessatum — be idle, stand neglected (perf. act. inf., syncopated for cessavisse, in indirect statement after ferunt)
glossary.choreas: chorea, -ae f. — a round dance (acc. pl.; a Greek loanword)
glossary.cinis: cinis, cineris m. — ash, ashes (nom. sg., predicative with vos: “will you lie as a little ash”)
glossary.coacervatos: coacervo, coacervare, coacervavi, coacervatum — heap up, pile together (perf. pass. part., acc. m. pl. with luctus, 4th decl. acc. pl.)
glossary.cocalus: Cocalus, -i m. — Cocalus, king of Sicily, who sheltered Daedalus (nom. sg.)
glossary.coeptus: coepi, coepisse, coeptum — begun, set going (perf. pass. part. of the defective coepi, nom. m. sg. with honor)
glossary.coloque: colo, colere, colui, cultum — worship, honour, tend (1st sg. pres. act. indic.; -que = and, paired with the preceding -que in “both … and”)
glossary.coluique: colo, colere, colui, cultum — worship, honour, tend (1st sg. perf. act. indic.; the first of a -que … -que pair, “both … and”)
glossary.committe: committo, committere, commisi, commissum — entrust, commit (2nd sg. pres. imperative act.; with the reflexive te, “entrust yourself to”; the negative command is formed with nec plus the imperative, a poetic idiom)
glossary.complexae: complector, complecti, complexus sum — embrace, clasp (deponent, so active in sense; perf. part., nom. f. pl., “having embraced”)
glossary.concava: concavus, -a, -um — hollow, hollowed out (adj., nom. f. sg. with vallis)
glossary.concedite: concedo, concedere, concessi, concessum — yield, give way, leave the field (2nd pl. pres. imperative act., with dative of the thing yielded to)
glossary.conchae: concha, -ae f. — shell, mussel-shell (nom. pl., subject of lacunabant)
glossary.condit: condo, condere, condidi, conditum — bury, plunge, sink a weapon home (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.; not from condio, “season”)
glossary.coniecit: conicio, conicere, conieci, coniectum — hurl, fling (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.coniungere: coniungo, coniungere, coniunxi, coniunctum — join, clasp together (pres. act. inf., complementary with petunt)
glossary.conlectus: colligo (conligo), colligere, collegi, collectum — gather, draw together (perf. pass. part., nom. m. sg. with crinis; the edition prints conl- for coll-)
glossary.consanguineas: consanguineus, -a, -um — of the same blood, kindred (adj., acc. f. pl. with umbras)
glossary.consilioque: consilium, -i n. — advice, counsel (abl. sg., governed by utor which takes the ablative; -que = and)
glossary.consiste: consisto, consistere, constiti — halt, stand still, take a stand (2nd sg. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.consorti: consors, consortis — sharing the same lot, kindred, of a brother (adj., abl. sg. with sanguine; i-stem ablative in -i, not a dative)
glossary.conspicui: conspicuus, -a, -um — conspicuous, striking to look at (adj., nom. m. pl.)
glossary.continuam: continuus, -a, -um — unbroken, continuous (adj., acc. f. sg. with humum)
glossary.contorta: contorqueo, contorquere, contorsi, contortum — hurl with a twist, whirl (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg. with cuspis)
glossary.convaluit: convalesco, convalescere, convalui — gather strength, grow strong (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.; inceptive verb, so the perfect means “had come to full strength”)
glossary.corneaque: corneus, -a, -um — of horn, horny (adj., acc. n. pl. with ora, here “beaks”; from cornu, “horn,” not the homograph corneus from cornus, “of cornel wood”; -que = and)
glossary.coronantur: corono, coronare, coronavi, coronatum — wreathe, garland (3rd pl. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.creator: creator, -oris m. — begetter, father (nom. sg.; here Peleus)
glossary.crescentes: cresco, crescere, crevi, cretum — grow, spring up (pres. part., acc. f. pl. with segetes)
glossary.cruentat: cruento, cruentare, cruentavi, cruentatum — stain with blood, bloody (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.cupiuntque: cupio, cupere, cupivi, cupitum — desire, long for (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.; -que = and)
glossary.currant: curro, currere, cucurri, cursum — run (3rd pl. pres. subj. act.; after dum, “so long as, until,” with subjunctive of anticipation)
glossary.daedalon: Daedalus, -i m. — Daedalus, the Athenian craftsman who built the labyrinth and the wings (Greek acc. sg. in -on)
glossary.dapibusque: daps, dapis f. — feast, banquet fare (abl. pl., in an ablative absolute with remotis; -que = and)
glossary.datam: do, dare, dedi, datum — give (perf. pass. part., acc. f. sg. with animam)
glossary.decipiat: decipio, decipere, decepi, deceptum — deceive, lead astray (3rd sg. pres. subj. act.; jussive in a prohibition introduced by nec)
glossary.dedero: do, dare, dedi, datum — give (1st sg. fut. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.deficiunt: deficio, deficere, defeci, defectum — fail, give out (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.despexitque: despicio, despicere, despexi, despectum — look down at, look down from above (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.; here the literal sense, not “despise”; -que = and)
glossary.destrinxit: destringo, destringere, destrinxi, destrictum — graze, skim, scrape along (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.devexaque: devexus, -a, -um — sloping downward, shelving (either nom. f. sg. with silva, “the wood, sloping away, looks out over the fields,” or acc. n. pl. with arva, “looks out over the sloping fields”; the word order allows both; -que = and)
glossary.dicemur: dico, dicere, dixi, dictum — say; in the passive, be called (1st pl. fut. pass. indic., with the predicate nominative inultae)
glossary.dicto: dico, dicere, dixi, dictum — speak, utter (perf. pass. part., abl. n. sg. with carmine in an ablative absolute; not the noun dictum, “saying”)
glossary.diduxit: diduco, diducere, diduxi, diductum — draw apart, split, separate (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.digitoque: digitus, -i m. — finger (abl. sg. of means; -que = and)
glossary.dignabitur: dignor, dignari, dignatus sum — think worthy, deign to accept (deponent, 3rd sg. fut. indic.; the person thought worthy stands in the accusative)
glossary.dilectae: diligo, diligere, dilexi, dilectum — love, hold dear (perf. pass. part. used as an adjective, dat. f. sg. agreeing with huic, “from her, my beloved”)
glossary.direxit: dirigo, dirigere, direxi, directum — aim, direct, level at (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.; also spelled derexit)
glossary.diri: dirus, -a, -um — dreadful, ghastly, ill-omened (adj., gen. n. sg. with facti)
glossary.discrimina: discrimen, -inis n. — separating interval, distinction between things (acc. n. pl.)
glossary.discubuere: discumbo, discumbere, discubui, discubitum — recline at table, take one's place at a banquet (3rd pl. perf. act. indic. in the poetic -ere for -erunt)
glossary.displicet: displiceo, displicere, displicui — be displeasing, not please (+ dat.) (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.distent: disto, distare — stand apart, differ (3rd pl. pres. subj. act. in an indirect question after quantum; the verb has no perfect forms)
glossary.doce: doceo, docere, docui, doctum — teach, tell, inform (2nd sg. pres. imperative act.)
glossary.dolorque: dolor, -oris m. — pain, grief (nom. sg.; -que = and)
glossary.domoque: domus, -us f. — house, home (abl. sg., governed by utor which takes the ablative; -que = and)
glossary.dryasque: Dryas, -antis m. — Dryas, one of the heroes at the Calydonian hunt (nom. sg., Greek form; -que = and)
glossary.echinadas: Echinades, -um f. pl. — the Echinades, the islands off the mouth of the Achelous (Greek acc. pl. in -as)
glossary.echionio: Echionius, -a, -um — of Echion, here the huntsman Echion (adj., abl. m. sg. with lacerto; the same adjective elsewhere means “Theban,” from the Echion who helped found Thebes)
glossary.editus: edo, edere, edidi, editum — bring forth; here bring to light, name aloud (perf. pass. part., nom. m. sg.; with est it forms the perfect passive)
glossary.enaesimus: Enaesimus, -i m. — Enaesimus, son of Hippocoon, killed by the boar (nom. sg.)
glossary.epiros: Epiros (Epirus), -i f. — Epirus, the region of north-western Greece famed for its cattle (nom. sg.; Greek spelling -os for Latin -us)
glossary.erechtheas: Erechtheus, -a, -um — of Erechtheus, i.e. Athenian (adj., acc. f. pl. with arces)
glossary.eueninae: Eueninus, -a, -um — of the Euenus, the Aetolian river beside Calydon (adj., nom. f. pl. with matres)
glossary.eundi: eo, ire, ii (ivi), itum — go, press on (gerund, gen. sg., dependent on studio)
glossary.eurytidae: Eurytides, -ae m. — son of Eurytus, i.e. the hunter Hippasus (patronymic; gen. sg. with femur, though the identical dat. sg. read as a dative of disadvantage gives the same sense)
glossary.eurytion: Eurytion, -onis m. — Eurytion, one of the heroes at the Calydonian hunt (nom. sg., Greek form)
glossary.excepi: excipio, excipere, excepi, exceptum — catch, take up, receive (1st sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.excitus: excio (excieo), excire, excivi, excitum — rouse out, startle from cover (perf. pass. part., nom. m. sg.)
glossary.exclamant: exclamo, exclamare, exclamavi, exclamatum — cry out, shout (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.excussis: excutio, excutere, excussi, excussum — shake out, strike out, dash together (perf. pass. part., abl. f. pl. with nubibus in an ablative absolute)
glossary.exhortantur: exhortor, exhortari, exhortatus sum — urge on, encourage (deponent, 3rd pl. pres. indic.; with se here reciprocal, “urge one another on”)
glossary.exsatiata: exsatio, exsatiare, exsatiavi, exsatiatum — glut, sate to the full (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg., agreeing with Latonia)
glossary.exspectant: exspecto, exspectare, exspectavi, exspectatum — await, wait for (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.exstinctos: exstinguo, exstinguere, exstinxi, exstinctum — put out, quench, kill (perf. pass. part., acc. m. pl. with fratres)
glossary.exstinctus: exstinguo, exstinguere, exstinxi, exstinctum — put out, quench, kill (perf. pass. part., nom. m. sg.; with est it forms the perfect passive)
glossary.exuvias: exuviae, -arum f. pl. — spoils, the hide stripped from a beast (acc. pl.; the noun exists only in the plural)
glossary.facioque: facio, facere, feci, factum — do, make, commit (1st sg. pres. act. indic.; -que = and)
glossary.fatalia: fatalis, -e — of fate, destined, fateful (adj., acc. n. pl. with stamina)
glossary.fatigatum: fatigo, fatigare, fatigavi, fatigatum — weary, wear out (perf. pass. part., acc. m. sg. with Daedalon)
glossary.fecissent: facio, facere, feci, factum — do, make, inflict (3rd pl. pluperf. subj. act.; the apodosis of a past contrary-to-fact condition with nisi)
glossary.fecitque: facio, facere, feci, factum — do, make, cause (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.; -que = and)
glossary.femineis: femineus, -a, -um — of a woman, a woman's (adj., dat. n. pl. with an understood tela, governed by praestent, “surpass”)
glossary.feret: fero, ferre, tuli, latum — carry, carry off (3rd sg. fut. act. indic.; with impune, “will get off unpunished”)
glossary.feror: fero, ferre, tuli, latum — bear; in the passive, be borne along, rush (1st sg. pres. pass. indic.; of a river in spate, “as great as I ever run”)
glossary.feroxque: ferox, ferocis — fierce, high-spirited (adj., nom. m. sg.; -que = and)
glossary.fervida: fervidus, -a, -um — boiling, seething, scalding (adj., nom. f. sg. with spuma)
glossary.fidensque: fido, fidere, fisus sum — trust in, rely on (semi-deponent, governing the dative or ablative; pres. part., nom. m. sg.; -que = and)
glossary.flagrantem: flagro, flagrare, flagravi, flagratum — blaze, be on fire (pres. part., acc. m. sg. with ramum)
glossary.flammam: flamma, -ae f. — flame, fire (acc. sg. after in, of motion into)
glossary.fleturi: fleo, flere, flevi, fletum — weep, weep for (fut. act. part., gen. m. sg. with coloni: the farmer who is going to weep)
glossary.foventque: foveo, fovere, fovi, fotum — keep warm, cherish, caress (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.; -que = and)
glossary.fragmina: fragmen, -inis n. — a broken piece, splinter of wood (acc. n. pl.)
glossary.fragorem: fragor, -oris m. — crash, crashing noise (acc. sg.)
glossary.frangunt: frango, frangere, fregi, fractum — break, break down (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.fraternaque: fraternus, -a, -um — of a brother, a brother's (adj., acc. n. pl. with fata; -que = and)
glossary.fraterni: fraternus, -a, -um — of a brother, my brothers' (adj., nom. m. pl. used as a vocative with manes)
glossary.fratresque: frater, fratris m. — brother (acc. pl.; -que = and)
glossary.frendens: frendo, frendere — gnash the teeth, grind in rage (pres. act. part., nom. m. sg.)
glossary.frondentis: frondeo, frondere — be leafy, be in leaf (pres. part., gen. f. sg. with olivae; not the acc. pl. in -is, which is spelled the same)
glossary.frondosus: frondosus, -a, -um — leafy, thick with foliage (adj., nom. m. sg. with ramus)
glossary.fruetur: fruor, frui, fructus (fruitus) sum — enjoy, have the benefit of (+ abl.) (deponent, 3rd sg. fut. indic.)
glossary.fugerat: fugio, fugere, fugi, fugitum — flee; here transitive, flee from, run away from (3rd sg. pluperf. act. ind., with an acc. object)
glossary.functus: fungor, fungi, functus sum — perform, discharge, go through with (perf. part. of a deponent, so active in sense: having done his part; nom. m. sg., governing an abl.)
glossary.fundunt: fundo, fundere, fudi, fusum — pour, pour out (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.funereum: funereus, -a, -um — funereal, belonging to death, deadly (acc. m. sg.)
glossary.funus: funus, funeris n. — death, corpse, funeral rite (nom. sg.; the neuter nom. and acc. are identical, and here it is the subject of an understood “is to be added”)
glossary.furenti: furo, furere — rage, be frenzied (pres. act. part., dat. m. sg., used as a noun of the maddened beast; dative because the verb it goes with takes one)
glossary.futuro: sum, esse, fui, futurus — be (fut. act. part., abl. n. sg., in an abl. absolute: about to be, destined to be)
glossary.gelidaeque: gelidus, -a, -um — icy, chill (nom. f. pl., + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.gemunt: gemo, gemere, gemui, gemitum — groan, moan aloud (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.glomerataque: glomero, glomerare, glomeravi, glomeratum — wind into a ball, clot, congeal (perf. pass. part., nom. n. pl., + enclitic -que)
glossary.gorgenque: Gorge, Gorges f. — Gorge, daughter of Oeneus and Althaea, sister of Meleager (Greek acc. sg. in -en, + enclitic -que)
glossary.grandaevumque: grandaevus, -a, -um — of great age, aged (acc. m. sg., + enclitic -que)
glossary.gravidi: gravidus, -a, -um — laden, heavy with fruit (nom. m. pl., agreeing with a 4th-decl. nom. pl. in -us)
glossary.habebatur: habeo, habere, habui, habitum — have, hold; in the passive, be reckoned, be considered (3rd sg. imperf. pass. ind.)
glossary.hae: hic, haec, hoc — this, these (nom. f. pl.)
glossary.haesura: haereo, haerere, haesi, haesurus — stick fast, cling (fut. act. part., nom. f. sg.; with a form of videor it means seemed about to lodge)
glossary.hastilibus: hastile, -is n. — spear-shaft, spear (dat. pl., governed by similis, like; the dat. and abl. pl. of this 3rd-decl. neuter are identical)
glossary.hausitque: haurio, haurire, hausi, haustum — drain, drink up; of a weapon, drive through, pierce (3rd sg. perf. act. ind., + enclitic -que)
glossary.haustos: haurio, haurire, hausi, haustum — draw up, scoop up, gather up (perf. pass. part., acc. m. pl.)
glossary.herbida: herbidus, -a, -um — grassy, rich in pasture (nom. f. sg., agreeing with a Greek f. place-name)
glossary.hippalmon: Hippalmos, -i m. — Hippalmus, one of the hunters at Calydon (Greek acc. sg. in -on)
glossary.hippasus: Hippasus, -i m. — Hippasus, one of the hunters at Calydon (nom. sg.)
glossary.hippocoon: Hippocoon, -ontis m. — Hippocoon, a Spartan of Amyclae who sent his sons to the hunt (nom. sg.)
glossary.hippocoonte: Hippocoon, -ontis m. — Hippocoon, a Spartan of Amyclae, father of Enaesimus (abl. sg., of parentage with a participle meaning sprung from)
glossary.hippodamas: Hippodamas, -antis m. — Hippodamas, father of Perimele (nom. sg., Greek 3rd decl.)
glossary.hippothousque: Hippothous, -i m. — Hippothous, one of the hunters at Calydon (nom. sg., + enclitic -que)
glossary.honorant: honoro, honorare, honoravi, honoratum — honour, do honour to (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.honoris: honos (honor), honoris m. — honour, distinction, the credit of a deed (gen. sg., objective, depending on a noun of robbing; the trap is that it looks like a nom. pl.)
glossary.horrea: horreum, -i n. — granary, storehouse (nom. n. pl., subject of its verb)
glossary.horrent: horreo, horrere, horrui — bristle, stand stiff and rough (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.hostemque: hostis, -is m. — enemy, foe (acc. sg., + enclitic -que)
glossary.hyanteo: Hyanteus, -a, -um — Hyantean, i.e. Boeotian, from the Hyantes, the old inhabitants of Boeotia (abl. m. sg.)
glossary.hyleusque: Hyleus, -ei m. — Hyleus, one of the hunters at Calydon (nom. sg., + enclitic -que)
glossary.iacebitis: iaceo, iacere, iacui — lie, lie prostrate (2nd pl. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.iaceret: iaceo, iacere, iacui — lie, lie prostrate (3rd sg. imperf. act. subj., in a circumstantial cum-clause)
glossary.iaciuntque: iacio, iacere, ieci, iactum — throw, hurl (3rd pl. pres. act. ind., + enclitic -que; not to be confused with iaceo, iacere, to lie)
glossary.iactis: iacio, iacere, ieci, iactum — throw, hurl (perf. pass. part., dat. n. pl., used as a noun of the weapons already thrown; dative because the verb it goes with takes one)
glossary.iaculis: iaculum, -i n. — javelin, throwing-spear (dat. pl., governed by pervius, passable for)
glossary.iaculoque: iaculum, -i n. — javelin, throwing-spear (abl. sg. of respect with an adj. of distinction, + enclitic -que)
glossary.idas: Idas, -ae m. — Idas, son of Aphareus and brother of Lynceus, one of the hunters (nom. sg., Greek 1st decl.)
glossary.ignavo: ignavus, -a, -um — spiritless, unmanly, inglorious (abl. n. sg.; said with contempt of a death without a wound, no honourable end but a coward's)
glossary.ignoscite: ignosco, ignoscere, ignovi, ignotum — pardon, forgive (+ dat.) (2nd pl. pres. act. imperative)
glossary.impietate: impietas, -atis f. — impiety, unnatural conduct, breach of duty to kin (abl. sg. of respect)
glossary.impiger: impiger, impigra, impigrum — tireless, unflagging, quick to act (nom. m. sg.)
glossary.imploravere: imploro, implorare, imploravi, imploratum — beg for, call on for help (3rd pl. perf. act. ind.; poetic -ere for -erunt)
glossary.impresso: imprimo, imprimere, impressi, impressum — press on, press into (perf. pass. part., abl. m. sg.: with the thumb pressed down)
glossary.incautus: incautus, -a, -um — heedless, off his guard (nom. m. sg.)
glossary.inclite: inclitus (inclutus), -a, -um — famed, renowned (voc. m. sg., addressing the hero directly)
glossary.increvit: incresco, increscere, increvi — grow upon, swell, increase (3rd sg. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.incursu: incursus, -us m. — charge, onset, running attack (abl. sg.)
glossary.indis: Indus, -a, -um — Indian, of India (abl. m. pl.; the adjective, not the noun Indi, and of tusks it means an elephant's)
glossary.inferias: inferiae, -arum f. pl. — offerings to the dead, funeral dues (acc. pl.; the noun exists only in the plural)
glossary.infestae: infestus, -a, -um — hostile, dangerous, bent on harm (gen. f. sg., agreeing with a goddess's name; the trap is that it looks like a nom. pl.)
glossary.ingeniumque: ingenium, -i n. — natural talent, creative power (acc. n. sg., + enclitic -que)
glossary.inhonoratae: inhonoratus, -a, -um — unhonoured, passed over without honour (nom. f. pl., the goddess speaking of herself in the plural)
glossary.inimicos: inimicus, -a, -um — hostile, unfriendly, an enemy's (acc. m. pl.; a transferred epithet, the fires being hostile to the man they will burn)
glossary.inmanemque: inmanis (the usual spelling is immanis), -e — monstrous, enormous, savage (acc. m. sg., + enclitic -que; the edition keeps the unassimilated inm-)
glossary.inmanis: inmanis (the usual spelling is immanis), -e — monstrous, savage, uncontrollable (nom. m. sg.; the edition keeps the unassimilated inm-)
glossary.inmemores: inmemor (the usual spelling is immemor), -oris — forgetful of, heedless of (+ gen.) (nom. f. pl. in both uses in this text: of mourning sisters heedless of decency, and of nymphs heedless of a god owed his due; the edition keeps the unassimilated inm-)
glossary.inritat: inrito (the usual spelling is irrito), inritare, inritavi, inritatum — provoke, goad, stir up (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.; the edition keeps the unassimilated inr-)
glossary.insiluit: insilio, insilire, insilui — leap on, spring up into (3rd sg. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.institerat: insisto, insistere, institi — take one's stand on, plant oneself on (3rd sg. pluperf. act. ind.; the perfect stem institi is shared with insto, to stand over, so the sense decides — here he had planted himself on his toes)
glossary.instruxere: instruo, instruere, instruxi, instructum — set out, furnish, lay (a table) (3rd pl. perf. act. ind.; poetic -ere for -erunt)
glossary.intercipe: intercipio, intercipere, intercepi, interceptum — intercept, snatch away before it arrives (2nd sg. pres. act. imperative)
glossary.intercipit: intercipio, intercipere, intercepi, interceptum — intercept, cut off, steal in transit (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.intumui: intumesco, intumescere, intumui — swell up, rise in flood (1st sg. perf. act. ind., the river-god speaking of himself)
glossary.inultae: inultus, -a, -um — unavenged, left without revenge (nom. f. pl., the goddess speaking of herself in the plural)
glossary.inveniebantur: invenio, invenire, inveni, inventum — find, come upon (3rd pl. imperf. pass. ind.: were still to be found)
glossary.invidere: invideo, invidere, invidi, invisum — envy, begrudge (3rd pl. perf. act. ind., poetic -ere for -erunt; the form is identical to the pres. act. infinitive, but here it is the perfect indicative, parallel to the finite verb beside it)
glossary.iolao: Iolaus, -i m. — Iolaus, nephew and comrade-in-arms of Hercules (abl. sg., after cum)
glossary.iuncique: iuncus, -i m. — rush, reed (nom. m. pl., + enclitic -que)
glossary.iuvencos: iuvencus, -i m. — bullock, young ox (acc. pl.)
glossary.ixionides: Ixionides, -ae m. — the son of Ixion, i.e. Pirithous (nom. sg., Greek patronymic of the 1st decl.)
glossary.ixionis: Ixion, -onis m. — Ixion, Lapith king and father of Pirithous (gen. sg.)
glossary.lacunabant: lacuno, lacunare, lacunavi, lacunatum — panel, work into sunken coffers (of a ceiling) (3rd pl. imperf. act. ind.; a rare verb)
glossary.lacunae: lacuna, -ae f. — hollow, dip, standing pool (gen. sg., depending on a neuter plural meaning the lowest parts; the trap is that it looks like a nom. pl. or dat. sg.)
glossary.laetior: laetus, -a, -um, compar. laetior, laetius — glad, delighted; more delighted (nom. f. sg. of the comparative, answered by quam)
glossary.laetissimus: laetus, -a, -um, superl. laetissimus — glad, delighted; overjoyed (nom. m. sg. of the superlative, with an abl. of cause)
glossary.laetitiae: laetitia, -ae f. — joy, gladness (dat. sg., predicative — the double-dative construction, is a joy to someone)
glossary.lamentabile: lamentabilis, -e — lamentable, calling for mourning (acc. n. sg.)
glossary.languescuntque: languesco, languescere, langui — grow faint, slacken, sink (3rd pl. pres. act. ind., + enclitic -que)
glossary.latentes: lateo, latere, latui — lie hidden, be concealed (pres. act. part., acc. f. pl.: hidden, secret)
glossary.latoidos: Latois, Latoidos f. — the daughter of Latona, i.e. Diana (Greek gen. sg. in -idos)
glossary.latrantes: latro, latrare, latravi, latratum — bark, bay (pres. act. part., acc. m. pl., used as a noun of the baying hounds)
glossary.latrantis: latro, latrare, latravi, latratum — bark, bay (pres. act. part., gen. m. sg., used as a noun of a hound; the trap is that it looks like an acc. pl.)
glossary.laude: laus, laudis f. — praise, glory, a deed that earns credit (abl. sg. of cause: thanks to that glory)
glossary.lecta: lego, legere, legi, lectum — gather, pick out, choose (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg., agreeing with a f. noun of the 4th decl.: a picked, hand-chosen band)
glossary.lelex: Lelex, Lelegis m. — Lelex, a hero of Naryx, one of the Calydonian hunters and later a grey-haired guest at the river-god's table (nom. sg. in both of its uses in this text)
glossary.leniat: lenio, lenire, lenivi, lenitum — soften, soothe, appease (3rd sg. pres. act. subj., in a purpose clause)
glossary.letiferos: letifer, letifera, letiferum — death-bringing, deadly (acc. m. pl.)
glossary.leucippusque: Leucippus, -i m. — Leucippus, one of the hunters at Calydon (nom. sg., + enclitic -que)
glossary.libasse: libo, libare, libavi, libatum — pour a libation, offer as first-fruits (perf. act. infinitive, syncopated for libavisse, in indirect statement)
glossary.librato: libro, librare, libravi, libratum — poise, balance, aim by weight (perf. pass. part., abl. n. sg., in an abl. absolute: well-poised, well-aimed)
glossary.linguis: lingua, -ae f. — tongue (abl. pl. of means)
glossary.liquentibus: liquens, liquentis (pres. part. of liqueo/liquor used as an adj.) — flowing, liquid, clear (abl. f. pl.)
glossary.liquerunt: linquo, linquere, liqui, lictum — leave, abandon, fail (3rd pl. perf. act. ind.; from linquo, not from liqueo, to be liquid — here the sinews failed him)
glossary.lugebitis: lugeo, lugere, luxi, luctum — mourn, grieve for (2nd pl. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.lyaeo: Lyaeus, -i m. — Lyaeus, the Releaser, a cult title of Bacchus (dat. sg.)
glossary.lynceus: Lynceus, -ei m. — Lynceus, son of Aphareus and brother of Idas, proverbial for keen sight (nom. sg.)
glossary.mactassent: macto, mactare, mactavi, mactatum — sacrifice, slaughter as an offering (3rd pl. pluperf. act. subj., syncopated for mactavissent)
glossary.maeret: maereo, maerere — grieve, be in mourning (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.magniloquo: magniloquus, -a, -um — big-talking, boastful, full of large words (abl. n. sg.; a hostile word, the narrator marking the boast as bluster)
glossary.maiores: magnus, -a, -um, compar. maior, maius — greater, bigger (acc. m. pl., agreeing with the noun for bulls; not the noun maiores, ancestors, and not a nom. pl. here)
glossary.mavortius: Mavortius, -a, -um — of Mars, warlike; used as a noun, the son of Mars, i.e. Meleager (nom. m. sg.)
glossary.meleagron: Meleagros, -i m. — Meleager, son of Oeneus, prince of Calydon (Greek acc. sg. in -on)
glossary.meleagros: Meleagros, -i m. — Meleager, son of Oeneus, prince of Calydon (nom. sg., Greek nom. in -os)
glossary.memoraverat: memoro, memorare, memoravi, memoratum — recount, declare, utter (3rd sg. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.menso: metior, metiri, mensus sum — measure, measure out, traverse (perf. part. of a deponent, so active in sense: having measured off; abl. m. sg. in an abl. absolute)
glossary.mensum: mensis, -is m. — month (gen. pl., the alternative shorter form for mensium; not the participle mensum from metior)
glossary.mersaeque: mergo, mergere, mersi, mersum — plunge, sink, drown (perf. pass. part., dat. f. sg., of the drowning girl to whom help is asked; + enclitic -que)
glossary.merum: merum, -i n. — unmixed wine, wine neat (acc. sg.; the noun, not the adjective merus)
glossary.metit: meto, metere, messui, messum — reap, mow down (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.minanti: minor, minari, minatus sum — threaten (deponent) (pres. part., dat. m. sg., governed by similis, like: like one threatening something cruel)
glossary.minervam: Minerva, -ae f. — Minerva, goddess of war and of crafts (acc. sg.)
glossary.mirantes: miror, mirari, miratus sum — wonder at, gaze at in amazement (deponent) (pres. part., nom. m. pl., active in sense)
glossary.mirere: miror, mirari, miratus sum — wonder at, be surprised at (deponent) (2nd sg. pres. subj., the alternative ending -re for -ris; in a quo minus purpose clause, so that you may wonder less)
glossary.misereri: misereor, misereri, miseritus sum — feel pity, take pity (+ gen.) (pres. infinitive of a deponent, so active in sense despite the passive ending; in indirect statement)
glossary.missisque: mitto, mittere, misi, missum — send, let fly, throw (perf. pass. part., abl. f. pl. in an abl. absolute with the numeral, two having been thrown; + enclitic -que)
glossary.mittentis: mitto, mittere, misi, missum — send, throw (pres. act. part., gen. m. sg., used as a noun of the thrower; the trap is that it looks like an acc. pl.)

glossary.deflent: dēfleō — they weep for, bewail (pres. 3 pl.)

glossary.delata: dēferō — carried down, brought (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.)

glossary.dilecta: dīligō — beloved, cherished (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.)

glossary.medullis: medulla, -ae, f. — marrow; the inmost part, the core (dat. or abl. pl.)
glossary.memoris: memor, memoris — mindful, remembering (+ gen.); grateful (m./f./n. gen. sg.)

glossary.miserandus: miseror, miserārī, miserātus sum — pity, lament; gerundive miserandus, -a, -um — pitiable, deserving pity (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.molle: mollis, molle — soft, yielding, tender (n. nom. or acc. sg.)

glossary.moturaque: moveō, movēre, mōvī, mōtum — move, stir, sway (fut. act. part., f. nom. sg., “going to move”); plus -que “and”
glossary.myrteta: myrtētum, -ī, n. — myrtle grove, myrtle thicket (nom. or acc. pl.)
glossary.nemeaea: Nemeaeus, -a, -um — Nemean, of Nemea (f. nom. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)

glossary.nescioquam: nescioquis, nescioqua, nescioquod (also written nescio quis) — someone or other, some unnamed one (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.nitere: niteō, nitēre, nituī — shine, glisten, be sleek (pres. act. infin.); or nītor, nītī, nīsus (nīxus) sum — lean on, strive (2nd sg. pres. imper., deponent)
glossary.nixosque: Nīxī, -ōrum, m. pl. — the Nixi, the kneeling birth-gods invoked in labor (acc. pl.); plus -que “and”

glossary.nostrasque: noster, nostra, nostrum — our; in poetry often simply “my” (f. acc. pl.); plus -que “and”
glossary.notat: notō, notāre, notāvī, notātum — mark, note; write down; brand, censure (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.notatam: notō, notāre, notāvī, notātum — mark; brand, stigmatize, censure (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg., “marked, branded”)
glossary.nutrici: nūtrīx, nūtrīcis, f. — nurse, wet-nurse, foster-mother (dat. sg.)
glossary.obest: obsum, obesse, obfuī — be in the way, hinder, harm (+ dat.) (3rd sg. pres. indic.)
glossary.oblectamina: oblectāmen, oblectāminis, n. — delight, amusement, plaything (nom. or acc. pl.)
glossary.obligor: obligō, obligāre, obligāvī, obligātum — bind, put under obligation (1st sg. pres. pass. indic., “I am bound, I am obliged”)
glossary.obscena: obscēnus, -a, -um — foul, filthy, indecent; ill-omened (n. nom./acc. pl.; also f. nom. sg.)
glossary.obscenae: obscēnus, -a, -um — foul, filthy, indecent; ill-omened (f. nom. or voc. pl.; also f. gen. or dat. sg.)
glossary.obscenas: obscēnus, -a, -um — foul, filthy, indecent; ill-omened (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.oceanus: Ōceanus, -ī, m. — Ocean, the Titan god of the sea encircling the world (nom. sg.)
glossary.oechalidum: Oechalis, Oechalidis, f. — woman of Oechalia, Oechalian (gen. pl.)
glossary.oetaeas: Oetaeus, -a, -um — of Oeta, Oetaean (the Thessalian mountain of Hercules’ pyre) (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.officiis: officium, -ī, n. — service, duty, kind office (dat. or abl. pl.)
glossary.ostendi: ostendō, ostendere, ostendī, ostentum — show, display, point out (1st sg. perf. indic. act.; the same form is also the pres. pass. infin., “to be shown”)
glossary.paciscitur: pacīscor, pacīscī, pactus sum — bargain, make a compact, agree on (3rd sg. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.pallantias: Pallantias, Pallantiadis, f. — daughter of Pallas, i.e. Aurora, the Dawn (nom. sg.)
glossary.pallidus: pallidus, -a, -um — pale, pallid, blanched (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.parientem: pariō, parere, peperī, partum — give birth to, bring forth (pres. act. part., m./f. acc. sg., “giving birth, in labor”)
glossary.parientibus: pariō, parere, peperī, partum — bring forth, give birth to (pres. act. part., dat./abl. pl.)

glossary.partheniumque: Parthenius, -a, -um + -que — Parthenian, of Mt. Parthenius in Arcadia, and (acc. sg. m./n. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.passam: patior, patī, passus sum — suffer, undergo, allow (perf. part., acc. sg. f.); or pandō, -ere, pandī, passum — spread out, let loose (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f.)
glossary.patior: patior, patī, passus sum — suffer, endure, allow (1st sg. pres. ind. dep.)
glossary.patriis: patrius, -a, -um — of a father, paternal, ancestral (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.paveant: paveō, pavēre, pāvī — be afraid, tremble at (3rd pl. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.pavefacta: pavefaciō, -ere, -fēcī, -factum — terrify, strike with panic (perf. pass. part., nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.peccare: peccō, -āre — do wrong, sin, offend (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.pecoris: pecus, pecoris, n. — herd, flock, cattle (gen. sg.)
glossary.penatibus: Penātēs, -ium, m. pl. — the household gods, and so the home itself (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.peream: pereō, perīre, periī, peritum — perish, die, be lost (1st sg. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.peregrino: peregrīnus, -a, -um — foreign, from abroad, of a stranger (dat./abl. sg. m./n.)
glossary.perpetuumque: perpetuus, -a, -um + -que — unbroken, everlasting, perpetual, and (acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.pestem: pestis, -is, f. — plague, destruction, bane (acc. sg.)
glossary.petet: petō, -ere, petīvī, petītum — seek, make for, ask for, attack (3rd sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.phegeius: Phēgēius, -a, -um — of Phegeus, an Arcadian king of Psophis (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.pietatis: pietās, -ātis, f. — dutifulness, devotion to family and gods (gen. sg.)
glossary.pingues: pinguis, -e — fat, plump, rich (nom./acc. pl. m./f.)
glossary.placida: placidus, -a, -um — calm, gentle, peaceful (nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.poeante: Poeās, -antis, m. — Poeas, father of Philoctetes (abl. sg.)
glossary.pomaque: pōmum, -ī, n. + -que — fruit, apple, and (nom./acc. pl. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.poposcerit: poscō, -ere, poposcī — demand, call for, require (3rd sg. fut. perf. act. ind. or perf. act. subj.)
glossary.populabile: populābilis, -e — able to be ravaged, destructible, consumable (nom./acc. sg. n.)
glossary.porrigeret: porrigō, -ere, porrēxī, porrēctum — stretch out, hold out, offer (3rd sg. impf. act. subj.)
glossary.possint: possum, posse, potuī — be able, can (3rd pl. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.potero: possum, posse, potuī — be able, can (1st sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.potiturque: potior, potīrī, potītus sum + -que — get possession of, obtain (usually + abl.), and (3rd sg. pres. ind. dep. + enclitic “and”)

glossary.premeretur: premō, -ere, pressī, pressum — press, press upon, weigh down, oppress (3rd sg. impf. pass. subj.)
glossary.prensamque: prendō (prehendō), -ere, prendī, prensum + -que — seize, grasp, catch hold of, and (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.priapi: Priāpus, -ī, m. — Priapus, the fertility god of gardens (gen. sg.)
glossary.privignae: prīvigna, -ae, f. — stepdaughter (gen./dat. sg. or nom. pl.)
glossary.probabit: probō, -āre — approve, sanction; prove, test (3rd sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.probatque: probō, -āre + -que — approve, sanction; prove, test, and (3rd sg. pres. act. ind. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.profatur: profor, profārī, profātus sum — speak out, declare (3rd sg. pres. ind. dep.)
glossary.prohibentque: prohibeō, -ēre, -uī, -itum + -que — hold back, hinder, prevent, and (3rd pl. pres. act. ind. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.quadriiugo: quadriiugus, -a, -um — drawn by four horses, four-horse (dat./abl. sg. m./n.)
glossary.quaerentibus: quaerō, -ere, quaesīvī, quaesītum — seek, look for, ask (pres. act. part., dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.quiete: quiēs, quiētis, f. — rest, repose, sleep (abl. sg.); or quiētē, adv. — calmly, quietly
glossary.radiantibus: radiō, -āre — beam, shine, radiate (pres. act. part., dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.ramosque: rāmus, -ī, m. + -que — branch, bough, and (acc. pl. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.raptum: rapiō, -ere, rapuī, raptum — seize, snatch, carry off (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n.; also the supine)
glossary.receperat: recipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — take back, receive, admit (3rd sg. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.recumbis: recumbō, -ere, -cubuī — lie down, recline, sink down (2nd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.redeuntis: redeō, redīre, rediī, reditum — go back, return (pres. act. part., gen. sg. or acc. pl.)
glossary.referunt: referō, referre, rettulī, relātum — bring back; report, relate (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.reformatus: refōrmō, -āre — reshape, remould, transform (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m.)
glossary.refugerit: refugiō, -ere, refūgī — flee back, run away; shrink from, escape (3rd sg. fut. perf. act. ind. or perf. act. subj.)
glossary.regnaque: rēgnum, -ī, n. + -que — kingdom, royal power, realm, and (nom./acc. pl. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.regunt: regō, -ere, rēxī, rēctum — rule, govern, guide (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.reiectura: reiciō, -ere, reiēcī, reiectum — throw back; reject, refuse (fut. act. part., nom. sg. f.)
glossary.relatus: referō, referre, rettulī, relātum — bring back, carry back; report (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m.)
glossary.removete: removeō, -ēre, -mōvī, -mōtum — move away, remove, withdraw (2nd pl. pres. act. imperative)
glossary.repetitque: repetō, -ere, -petīvī, -petītum + -que — seek again, go back over, recall, and (3rd sg. pres. act. ind. + enclitic “and”)

glossary.residentem: resideō, -ēre, -sēdī — sit, remain seated, stay (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m./f.); or resīdō, -ere, -sēdī — settle down, sink, subside (same part. form)
glossary.resisti: resistō, -ere, restitī — stand against, withstand, resist (+ dat.) (pres. pass. inf., used impersonally)
glossary.resumit: resūmō, -ere, -sūmpsī, -sūmptum — take up again, resume, recover (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.retemptantem: retemptō, -āre — try again, make a fresh attempt at (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m./f.)
glossary.rhadamanthon: Rhadamanthus, -ī, m. — Rhadamanthus, son of Jupiter and Europa, a judge of the dead (Greek acc. sg.)
glossary.rhadamanthus: Rhadamanthus, -ī, m. — Rhadamanthus, son of Jupiter and Europa, a judge of the dead (nom. sg.)
glossary.rigescere: rigēscō, -ere, riguī — grow stiff, harden, become rigid (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.rigidos: rigidus, -a, -um — stiff, hard, unbending (acc. pl. m.)
glossary.risisse: rīdeō, -ēre, rīsī, rīsum — laugh, laugh at (perf. act. inf.)
glossary.ritus: rītus, -ūs, m. — rite, religious observance, custom (nom./acc. pl.; also nom. or gen. sg.)
glossary.rotatum: rotō, -āre — whirl round, swing in a circle (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n.)
glossary.ruitis: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — rush, hurry headlong; fall, collapse (2nd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.saevoque: saevus, -a, -um + -que — savage, fierce, cruel, and (dat./abl. sg. m./n. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.salutet: salūtō, -āre — greet, salute, pay respects to (3rd sg. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.scribit: scrībō, -ere, scrīpsī, scrīptum — write (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.scripta: scrībō, -ere, scrīpsī, scrīptum — write (perf. pass. part., nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n.); or scrīptum, -ī, n. — a written thing, writing (nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.securosque: sēcūrus, -a, -um + -que — free from care, untroubled, unconcerned, and (acc. pl. m. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.seditio: sēditiō, -ōnis, f. — dissension, uproar, mutiny (nom. sg.)
glossary.sensurum: sentiō, -īre, sēnsī, sēnsum — feel, perceive, notice (fut. act. part., acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n.)
glossary.sentiet: sentiō, -īre, sēnsī, sēnsum — feel, perceive, notice (3rd sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.seri: sērus, -a, -um — late, coming late (nom. pl. m. or gen. sg. m./n.); or serō, -ere, sēvī, satum — sow, plant, beget (pres. pass. inf.)
glossary.serpit: serpō, -ere, serpsī — creep, crawl, spread gradually (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.servato: servō, -āre — keep, preserve, save, watch over (perf. pass. part., dat./abl. sg. m./n.; or 2nd/3rd sg. fut. act. imperative)
glossary.significant: significō, -āre — signify, indicate, mean (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.sopita: sōpiō, -īre, -īvī, -ītum — put to sleep, lull to rest (perf. pass. part., nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.sorbent: sorbeō, -ēre, sorbuī — suck up, swallow, absorb (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.specta: spectō, -āre — look at, watch, gaze on (2nd sg. pres. act. imperative)
glossary.spectatrix: spectātrīx, -īcis, f. — a woman who looks on, female onlooker (nom. sg.)
glossary.spernite: spernō, -ere, sprēvī, sprētum — scorn, despise, reject (2nd pl. pres. act. imperative)
glossary.squamaque: squāma, -ae, f. + -que — scale, of a snake or fish, and (nom./abl. sg. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.sternentemque: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum + -que — spread out; lay low, strike down, and (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m./f. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.sternis: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum — spread out; lay low, stretch on the ground (2nd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.stheneleius: Sthenelēius, -a, -um — descended from Sthenelus, and so of Eurystheus (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.strenua: strēnuus, -a, -um — brisk, energetic, prompt (nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.strenuitas: strēnuitās, -ātis, f. — briskness, quickness, energy (nom. sg.)
glossary.studeat: studeō, -ēre, studuī — be eager for, favour, support (+ dat.) (3rd sg. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.stymphalides: Stymphalis, -idis, f. — Stymphalian, of Lake Stymphalus in Arcadia (nom. pl. f.)
glossary.subcrescit: subcrēscō (succrēscō), -ere, -crēvī — grow up from below, grow up (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.subductaque: subdūcō, -ere, -dūxī, -ductum + -que — draw away from below, withdraw, remove, and (perf. pass. part., nom./abl. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.sumptas: sūmō, -ere, sūmpsī, sūmptum — take up, take, assume (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. f.)
glossary.superet: superō, -āre — overcome, surpass, get the better of; survive, be left over (3rd sg. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.suscipiunt: suscipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — take up, undertake; of vows, make or offer (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.sustinuit: sustineō, -ēre, -tinuī, -tentum — hold up, support; hold back, endure (3rd sg. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.tabellas: tabella, -ae, f. — small board, writing-tablet; letter (acc. pl.)
glossary.tacitae: tacitus, -a, -um — silent, saying nothing; unspoken (gen./dat. sg. f. or nom. pl. f.)
glossary.tantumne: tantum, adv. + -ne — so much, to such a degree; only (adv., orig. acc. sg. n. of tantus, -a, -um, so great, + enclitic marking a question)

glossary.tardi: tardus, -a, -um — slow, sluggish, late (nom. pl. m. or gen. sg. m./n.)
glossary.temptem: temptō, -āre — try, attempt, test (1st sg. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.tendensque: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum (tēnsum) + -que — stretch, stretch out, strain, and (pres. act. part., nom. sg. + enclitic “and”)
glossary.tenebit: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — hold, keep, hold back (3rd sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.tenuerunt: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — hold, keep, hold back, check (3rd pl. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.tepidique: tepidus, -a, -um + -que — warm, lukewarm, and (gen. sg. m./n. or nom. pl. m. + enclitic “and”)

glossary.thracis: Thrāx, Thrācis — Thracian; a man of Thrace (gen. sg.)
glossary.timeat: timeō, -ēre, timuī — fear, be afraid of (3rd sg. pres. act. subj.)
