glossary.triplex: triplex, triplicis — threefold, triple (nom./acc. sg. m./f./n.)
glossary.tristitiam: trīstitia, -ae, f. — sadness, gloom, grimness (acc. sg.)
glossary.truncum: truncus, -ī, m. — trunk of a tree; trunk of the body (acc. sg.); or truncus, -a, -um — lopped, maimed, mutilated (acc. sg. m. or nom./acc. sg. n.)
glossary.tuli: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — bear, carry, bring; endure (1st sg. perf. act. ind.)

glossary.patetis: pateō, -ēre — to lie open, be accessible, be receptive (2nd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.patietur: patior, patī (deponent) — to suffer, undergo, endure (3rd sg. fut. ind.)
glossary.pendenti: pendeō, -ēre — to hang, be suspended (pres. act. part., f. abl. sg.)
glossary.penduntque: pendō, -ere — to weigh out, pay; with poenās, to pay the penalty (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.) plus enclitic -que
glossary.penetrat: penetrō, -āre — to penetrate, pierce, make its way into (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.peraget: peragō, -ere — to carry through, perform, complete (3rd sg. fut. ind. act.)
glossary.percurrere: percurrō, -ere — to run over, run along, skim across (pres. act. infin.)
glossary.peregrinis: peregrīnus — foreign, from abroad, strange (f. abl. pl.)
glossary.peremptis: perimō, -ere, -ēmī, -ēmptum — to destroy, kill, do away with (perf. pass. part., m. abl. pl., in an ablative absolute)
glossary.periclo: perīculum, -ī (n.), syncopated perīclum — danger, risk, peril (abl. sg.)
glossary.perimunt: perimō, -ere — to destroy, kill, do away with (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.periturus: pereō, -īre — to perish, die (fut. act. part., m. nom. sg.: about to die, doomed to die)
glossary.persephone: Persephonē — Persephone, queen of the underworld, the Roman Proserpina (f. voc. sg., Greek 1st decl.; the vocative is identical in form to the nominative)
glossary.perstrinxerat: perstringō, -ere, -strīnxī — to bind tight, draw close, compress (3rd sg. pluperf. ind. act.)
glossary.pervenerat: perveniō, -īre, -vēnī — to arrive, reach, come through to (3rd sg. pluperf. ind. act.)
glossary.peteret: petō, -ere — to make for, seek, go after (3rd sg. imperf. subj. act., in an indirect question)
glossary.peteretis: petō, -ere — to seek, aim at, strive for (2nd pl. imperf. subj. act., in a subordinate clause within reported speech)
glossary.pharetratus: pharetrātus — quiver-bearing, carrying a quiver (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.pinguntur: pingō, -ere — to paint, depict (3rd pl. pres. ind. pass.)
glossary.piorum: pius — dutiful, righteous, holy (m. gen. pl.; here as a noun, the blessed dead)
glossary.piscosamque: piscōsus — full of fish, teeming with fish (acc. f. sg., with -que)
glossary.plangitur: plangō, -ere — to beat, strike (in grief); in the middle-passive, to beat itself, to flap (3rd sg. pres. ind. pass., middle sense)
glossary.plaustrum: plaustrum, -ī (n.) — wagon, cart; also the constellation of the Wain (acc. sg.)
glossary.poplitibus: poples, -itis (m.) — the back of the knee, the knee (dat. pl.)
glossary.populare: populāris, -e — of the people, native, belonging to the same folk (acc. n. sg., with flūmen; not the verb populārī)
glossary.populusque: populus, -ī (m.) — the people, the crowd (nom. sg., with -que; distinct from pōpulus, -ī f., the poplar tree)
glossary.porrectaque: porrigō, -ere, porrēxī, porrēctum — to stretch out, extend (perf. pass. part., nom. n. pl., with bracchia; + -que)
glossary.portabat: portō, -āre — to carry, bear (3rd sg. impf. ind. act.)
glossary.portat: portō, -āre — to carry, bear (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.potiere: potior, potīrī — to get possession of, win, enjoy (2nd sg. fut. ind., deponent; poetic alternative for potiēris)
glossary.potiuntur: potior, potīrī — to get possession of, gain, reach (3rd pl. pres. ind., deponent; takes the abl.)
glossary.praecedentem: praecēdō, -ere — to go before, walk ahead (pres. act. part., acc. sg.)
glossary.praefertur: praeferō, -ferre — to carry before; to prefer, set above (3rd sg. pres. ind. pass.: is preferred)
glossary.praesuta: praesuō, -ere, -suī, -sūtum — to sew over, cover over in front (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg.; a rare verb)
glossary.praeterit: praetereō, -īre — to go past, pass by, overtake (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.praeterita: praetereō, -īre — to go past, overtake (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg., forming the perf. pass. with est: was overtaken)
glossary.praevius: praevius, -a, -um — going before, leading the way (nom. m. sg.)
glossary.pressitque: premō, -ere, pressī, pressum — to press, press down upon (3rd sg. perf. ind. act., + -que)
glossary.prisci: prīscus, -a, -um — ancient, of former times, of old (nom. m. pl.)
glossary.probro: probrum, -ī (n.) — shameful act, outrage, disgrace (abl. sg.)
glossary.prodesse: prōsum, prōdesse — to be of use, do good, benefit (pres. act. inf.; the d is inserted before the vowel)
glossary.propera: properō, -āre — to hurry, make haste (2nd sg. pres. imper. act.)
glossary.puerili: puerīlis, -e — boyish, of a boy (abl. n. sg., with ōre)
glossary.pullo: pullus, -a, -um — dark-coloured, dusky, mourning-black (abl. sg., with an understood colōre: with dark colour)
glossary.punica: pūnicus, -a, -um — Punic, Carthaginian; pūnica (māla), pomegranates (nom. n. pl., used as a noun)
glossary.putando: putō, -āre — to think, suppose (gerund, abl. sg.: in thinking, by supposing; the same verb also means to prune trees)
glossary.quaerebatque: quaerō, -ere, quaesīvī, quaesītum — to seek, look for (3rd sg. impf. ind. act., + -que)
glossary.quaerensque: quaerō, -ere — to seek, search for (pres. act. part., nom. m. sg., + -que)
glossary.quaesitis: quaerō, -ere, quaesīvī, quaesītum — to seek; to ask, inquire after (perf. pass. part., abl. f. pl., in an abl. abs. with annīs: the years having been asked)
glossary.quale: quālis, -e — of what kind, such as, like (nom./acc. n. sg.; correlative with tālis)
glossary.quando: quandō — ever, at any time; as a conjunction, when, since (indeclinable adv./conj.; after sī it means if ever)
glossary.questaque: queror, querī, questus sum — to complain, lament (perf. part., deponent and so active in sense, nom. f. sg., + -que: having lamented)
glossary.radere: rādō, -ere, rāsī, rāsum — to scrape, graze, skim over (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.raptoresque: raptor, -ōris (m.) — robber, snatcher; used adjectivally, ravening, plundering (acc. m. pl., with lupōs, + -que)
glossary.rastrique: rastrum, -ī (n.), pl. usually rastrī (m.) — rake, mattock, hoe (nom. m. pl., + -que)
glossary.recognoscit: recognōscō, -ere — to recognize, look over again, review (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.recurrunt: recurrō, -ere — to run back, hurry back (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.recuso: recūsō, -āre — to refuse, object to, decline (1st sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.reddunt: reddō, -ere — to give back, render; to utter, give forth (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.rediret: redeō, -īre — to go back, return (3rd sg. impf. subj. act.)
glossary.religione: religiō, -ōnis (f.) — religious awe, sanctity, sacred observance (abl. sg.)
glossary.relinquitur: relinquō, -ere — to leave, leave behind, leave remaining (3rd sg. pres. ind. pass.)
glossary.requiescere: requiēscō, -ere — to rest, take rest (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.respondent: respondeō, -ēre — to answer, reply; of places, to echo back (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.retentis: retineō, -ēre, -tinuī, -tentum — to hold back, check, restrain (perf. pass. part., abl. n. pl., with verbīs)
glossary.retorserunt: retorqueō, -ēre, -torsī, -tortum — to twist back, turn away (3rd pl. perf. ind. act.)
glossary.revocata: revocō, -āre — to call back, recall, summon back (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg., forming the perf. pass. with est)
glossary.rubuerunt: rubeō, -ēre, rubuī — to be red, grow red (3rd pl. perf. ind. act.: turned red)
glossary.ruptosque: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to burst, break, split (perf. pass. part., acc. m. pl., with unguēs, + -que)
glossary.sabaea: Sabaeus, -a, -um — Sabaean, of Saba in southern Arabia, a land of incense (nom. f. sg., with terra)
glossary.sacraria: sacrārium, -ī (n.) — shrine, sanctuary, inner holy place (acc. pl.)
glossary.sacrata: sacrō, -āre — to consecrate, hallow, set among the gods (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg.)
glossary.sacravere: sacrō, -āre — to consecrate, dedicate (3rd pl. perf. ind. act.; poetic -ēre for sacrāvērunt)
glossary.sacrilegae: sacrilegus, -a, -um — sacrilegious, temple-robbing, profaning what is holy (nom. f. pl.)
glossary.saetigerosque: saetiger, -gera, -gerum — bristle-bearing, bristly (acc. m. pl., with suēs, + -que)
glossary.sapiente: sapiēns, -entis — wise, sensible, discerning (abl. f. sg., with puellā)
glossary.sarculaque: sarculum, -ī (n.) — light hoe, garden hoe (nom. pl., + -que)
glossary.saturatos: saturō, -āre — to sate, glut, fill full (perf. pass. part., acc. m. pl., with leōnēs)
glossary.schoeneia: Schoenēius, -a, -um — Schoeneian, daughter of Schoeneus, i.e. Atalanta (nom. f. sg. of the Greek patronymic adjective, used as a name)
glossary.scitanti: scītor, scītārī — to inquire, ask, seek to know (pres. part., deponent and so active in sense, dat. m. sg.: to the one asking)
glossary.scythica: Scythicus, -a, -um — Scythian, of the Scythians, a people famed as archers (abl. f. sg., with sagittā)
glossary.secundi: secundus, -a, -um — second, next; following, favourable (gen. n. sg., with pōmī)
glossary.sederat: sedeō, -ēre, sēdī, sessum — to sit, be seated (3rd sg. pluperf. ind. act.)
glossary.segetis: seges, -etis (f.) — cornfield, standing crop of grain (gen. sg.)
glossary.sensibus: sēnsus, -ūs (m.) — sense, perception, faculty of feeling (dat./abl. pl., 4th decl.)
glossary.sensitque: sentiō, -īre, sēnsī, sēnsum — to feel, perceive, notice (3rd sg. perf. ind. act., + -que)
glossary.setius: sētius — less, to a smaller degree (comparative adv.; in nōn sētius, none the less, no less for that)
glossary.simulamina: simulāmen, -inis (n.) — imitation, semblance, mimicry (acc. pl.; a coinage of Ovid)
glossary.simulatas: simulō, -āre — to imitate, counterfeit, feign (perf. pass. part., acc. f. pl., with umbrās: imitation, seeming)
glossary.sinum: sinus, -ūs (m.) — fold of a garment, lap, bosom, breast (acc. sg., 4th decl.)
glossary.sociantem: sociō, -āre — to join, unite, accompany, set together (pres. act. part., acc. m. sg.)
glossary.sociare: sociō, -āre — to join, share, unite (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.solitos: soleō, -ēre, solitus sum — to be accustomed; the participle solitus as an adj., customary, usual (perf. part., acc. m. pl., with cursūs)
glossary.sontes: sōns, sontis — guilty, criminal; as a noun, the guilty (acc. m. pl.)
glossary.spatiantur: spatior, spatiārī — to walk about, stroll, pace (3rd pl. pres. ind., deponent)
glossary.spectator: spectātor, -ōris (m.) — onlooker, spectator (nom. sg., in apposition)
glossary.spectatosque: spectō, -āre — to look at, gaze upon (perf. pass. part., acc. m. pl., with vultūs, + -que)
glossary.speluncae: spēlunca, -ae (f.) — cave, cavern, grotto (dat. sg., with similis)
glossary.spernenda: spernō, -ere, sprēvī, sprētum — to spurn, scorn, reject (gerundive, nom. f. sg.: to be scorned, deserving contempt)
glossary.spondet: spondeō, -ēre, spopondī, spōnsum — to promise solemnly, pledge, vow (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.stantes: stō, stāre, stetī — to stand, stand upright (pres. act. part., acc. f. pl., with aristās)
glossary.stet: stō, stāre — to stand; with an abl. or gen. of price, to cost (3rd sg. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.stillanti: stīllō, -āre — to drip, trickle, fall in drops (pres. act. part., abl. m. sg., with rōre)
glossary.structoque: struō, -ere, strūxī, structum — to build, pile up, construct (perf. pass. part., abl. n. sg., in an abl. abs. with theātrō, + -que)
glossary.suberant: subsum, subesse — to be underneath, lie beneath (3rd pl. impf. ind.)
glossary.subigebant: subigō, -ere — to drive up; of soil, to turn up, break up, plough (3rd pl. impf. ind. act.)
glossary.sublato: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise, pick up (perf. pass. part., abl. n. sg., in an abl. abs.)
glossary.succiduo: succiduus, -a, -um — sinking, giving way, buckling (abl. m. sg., with poplite)
glossary.suem: sūs, suis (m./f.) — pig, swine; of a wild one, boar (acc. sg.)
glossary.sues: sūs, suis (m./f.) — pig, swine, boar (acc. pl.)
glossary.superando: superō, -āre — to overcome, defeat, surpass (gerund, abl. sg.: by overcoming)
glossary.superari: superō, -āre — to overcome, defeat (pres. pass. inf.: to be beaten)
glossary.superasse: superō, -āre — to overcome, defeat, outrun (perf. act. inf., syncopated for superāvisse)
glossary.supervenit: superveniō, -īre, -vēnī — to come upon, come over, spread over (3rd sg. perf. ind. act.; spelt identically to the present, which differs only in vowel length)
glossary.suras: sūra, -ae (f.) — the calf of the leg (acc. pl.)
glossary.tabula: tabula, -ae (f.) — board, plank; painted panel, picture (abl. sg.)
glossary.tacebitur: taceō, -ēre — to be silent; in the passive, to be passed over in silence, go unmentioned (3rd sg. fut. ind. pass.)
glossary.tacta: tangō, -ere, tetigī, tāctum — to touch, and so to move, affect (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg.)
glossary.tamasenum: Tamasēnus, -a, -um — of Tamasus, a town in Cyprus (acc. m. sg., predicate accusative with ager, used as its name)
glossary.tangor: tangō, -ere — to touch; in the passive, to be touched, moved, affected (1st sg. pres. ind. pass.)
glossary.tardior: tardus, -a, -um — slow, sluggish (comparative, nom. m. sg.: slower)
glossary.tardis: tardus, -a, -um — slow, too slow; as a noun, the slow (dat. m. pl.)
glossary.tectae: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, clothe (perf. pass. part., nom. f. pl., in the middle sense with an acc. of respect: having covered their breasts)
glossary.tegunt: tegō, -ere — to cover, hide, conceal (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.temerat: temerō, -āre — to defile, violate, profane (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.tepidae: tepidus, -a, -um — warm, lukewarm (nom. f. pl., with guttae)
glossary.teretes: teres, -etis — rounded, smooth, shapely, well-turned (acc. f. pl., with surās)
glossary.timeas: timeō, -ēre — to fear, be afraid of (2nd sg. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.tonsa: tondeō, -ēre, totondī, tōnsum — to shear, clip, strip of foliage (perf. pass. part., nom. f. sg., in the middle sense with an acc. of respect: shorn as to her hair)
glossary.torquent: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl, hurl (3rd pl. pres. ind. act.)
glossary.torta: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, wind (perf. pass. part., abl. f. sg., with rādīce: twisted)
glossary.totosque: tōtus, -a, -um (gen. tōtīus) — whole, entire, all of (acc. m. pl., with dentēs, + -que)
glossary.transibant: trānseō, -īre — to cross, pass over, go across (3rd pl. impf. ind. act.)
glossary.transitque: trānseō, -īre — to pass by, go past, overtake (3rd sg. pres. ind. act., + -que)
glossary.traxerat: trahō, -ere, trāxī, tractum — to draw, drag; to draw on, take on (a colour) (3rd sg. pluperf. ind. act.)
glossary.tremulasque: tremulus, -a, -um — trembling, shaking (acc. f. pl., with manūs, + -que)
glossary.trepidans: trepidō, -āre — to be agitated, flutter, struggle in alarm (pres. act. part., nom. sg.)
glossary.tumuli: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, hillock; burial mound, tomb (gen. sg.)
glossary.turritaque: turrītus, -a, -um — turreted, crowned with towers, an epithet of Cybele (nom. f. sg., with Māter, + -que)
glossary.tympanaque: tympanum, -ī (n.) — hand-drum, tambourine, used in the rites of Bacchus and Cybele (nom. pl., + -que)
glossary.ululatus: ululātus, -ūs (m.) — howling, wailing, ritual shrieking (nom. pl., 4th decl.)
glossary.umet: ūmeō, -ēre — to be wet, be moist (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.; also spelt hūmet)
glossary.unxere: unguō (ungō), -ere, ūnxī, ūnctum — to anoint, smear (3rd pl. perf. ind. act.; poetic -ēre for ūnxērunt)
glossary.vacuosque: vacuus, -a, -um — empty, deserted, unoccupied (acc. m. pl., with agrōs, + -que)
glossary.vagata: vagor, vagārī — to wander, roam (perf. part., deponent and so active in sense, nom. f. sg.: having wandered)
glossary.vagitque: vāgiō, -īre — to cry, wail, squall, of an infant (3rd sg. pres. ind. act., + -que; not from vagor, to wander)
glossary.vate: vātēs, -is (m./f.) — bard, poet, seer, prophet (abl. sg.)
glossary.velatae: vēlō, -āre — to veil, cover, drape (perf. pass. part., nom. f. pl., in the middle sense with an acc. of respect: having veiled their bodies)
glossary.veloces: vēlōx, -ōcis — swift, fast, fleet (acc. m. pl., with virōs)
glossary.veloci: vēlōx, -ōcis — swift, fleet; as a noun, the swift one (dat. m. sg.)
glossary.velum: vēlum, -ī (n.) — cloth, awning stretched over a theatre or courtyard; also a sail (nom. sg.)
glossary.venientique: veniō, -īre — to come, approach (pres. act. part., dat. sg., with lignō, + -que)
glossary.verruntur: verrō, -ere — to sweep, brush, skim (3rd pl. pres. ind. pass., in the middle sense: they sweep)
glossary.veterum: vetus, -eris — old, ancient, of long standing (gen. m. pl., with deōrum)
glossary.vetitis: vetō, -āre, vetuī, vetitum — to forbid, prohibit (perf. pass. part., abl. n. pl., used as a noun: forbidden things)
glossary.victo: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, defeat, beat (perf. pass. part., abl. m. sg., in an abl. abs.)
glossary.videnda: videō, -ēre — to see (gerundive, nom. n. pl.: to be seen, visible)
glossary.vincar: vincō, -ere — to conquer, defeat (1st sg. pass.; the form serves as both pres. subj. and fut. ind.: I am, or shall be, beaten)
glossary.vinces: vincō, -ere — to conquer, win, prevail (2nd sg. fut. ind. act.)
glossary.violem: violō, -āre — to violate, dishonour, do outrage to (1st sg. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.virgineosque: virgineus, -a, -um — maidenly, of a maiden, virginal (acc. m. pl., with metūs, + -que)
glossary.virgineus: virgineus, -a, -um — maidenly, of a girl, virginal (nom. m. sg., with vultus)
glossary.vivosque: vīvus, -a, -um — living, alive; as a noun, the living (acc. m. pl., + -que)
glossary.volatilis: volātilis, -e — winged, flying; of time, fleeting, swift-passing (nom. f. sg., with aetās)
glossary.volubile: volūbilis, -e — rolling, spinning, easily turned (acc. n. sg.)
glossary.vomere: vōmer, -eris (m.) — ploughshare (abl. sg.; spelt identically to the pres. act. inf. of vomō, to vomit, which is not the word here)
glossary.acasto: Acastus — Acastus (m. abl./dat. sg.; Greek name, king of Thessalian Iolcos)
glossary.achille: Achillēs — Achilles (m. abl. sg.; Greek name, third-decl. with abl. in -e)
glossary.ademptam: adimō, adimere — taken away, carried off, lost (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.ademptum: adimō, adimere — taken away, carried off, lost (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.adeundi: adeō, adīre — of approaching, of going up to (gerund, gen.; the person approached goes in the gen. with 'copia')
glossary.adicis: adiciō, adicere — you add, you throw in besides (2 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.admissi: admissum — of the thing done, of the offence committed (n. gen. sg.; substantive of the perf. pass. part. of admittō, and so also that participle, m./n. gen. sg. or m. nom. pl.)
glossary.adorandum: adōrō — to be worshipped, that must be revered (gerundive, n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.)
glossary.adpuleram: appellō, appellere (adp-) — I had driven ashore, had brought to land (1 sg. pluperf. act. ind.; ad + pellō, not appellō 'to call'; unassimilated adp-)
glossary.adscendunt: ascendō, ascendere (adsc-) — they climb, they go up (3 pl. pres. act. ind.; unassimilated adsc-)
glossary.adscensu: ascēnsus (adsc-) — climb, rise, slope (m. abl. sg., 4th decl.; unassimilated adsc-)
glossary.adspexerit: aspiciō, aspicere (adsp-) — he has seen, he caught sight of (3 sg. perf. subj. act., as in an indirect question; formally also fut. perf. ind.; unassimilated adsp-)
glossary.adspiciunt: aspiciō, aspicere (adsp-) — they behold, they catch sight of (3 pl. pres. act. ind.; unassimilated adsp-)
glossary.adsuerat: assuēscō, assuēscere (adsu-) — he had grown accustomed, was used (3 sg. pluperf. act. ind., syncopated for 'adsueverat'; + inf.)
glossary.aeacide: Aeacidēs — descendant of Aeacus (m. voc. sg.; Greek patronymic in -idēs, 1st decl.; the same form serves as abl. sg.)
glossary.aeaciden: Aeacidēs — descendant of Aeacus (m. acc. sg. with the Greek ending -ēn)
glossary.aedificat: aedificō — builds, raises (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.aequoreae: aequoreus — of the sea, sea- (f. gen./dat. sg.; also f. nom. pl.)
glossary.aequoreo: aequoreus — of the sea, sea- (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.aequus: aequus — even-tempered, kindly, fair (m. nom. sg.; + dat. of the one treated fairly)
glossary.agrestibus: agrestis, -e — rustic, of the fields (dat./abl. pl.); as a noun, countrymen
glossary.agricolam: agricola — farmer, husbandman (m. acc. sg.; 1st decl. but masculine)
glossary.alcyone: Alcyonē — Alcyone (f. nom. sg.; Greek name, wife of Ceyx; the same form serves as abl. sg.)
glossary.alga: alga — seaweed, wrack (f. nom. or abl. sg.)
glossary.alipedis: ālipēs, ālipedis — wing-footed, swift as wings (adj., gen. sg. of any gender)
glossary.altore: altor, altōris — foster-father, nurturer (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.angustum: angustus — narrow, strait (m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.anhelo: anhēlus — panting, gasping, breathless (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.); the same letters are also anhēlō, 'I pant' (1 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.animasque: anima — lives, souls, breaths (f. acc. pl.; + -que)
glossary.aperti: apertus — open, unclosed, uncovered (perf. pass. part. of aperiō used as adj.; m./n. gen. sg. or m. nom. pl.)
glossary.apollineos: Apollineus — of Apollo, Apolline (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.apollo: Apollō, Apollinis — Apollo (m. nom. sg.; Apollin- is the oblique stem)
glossary.ardentem: ārdeō, ārdēre — burning, blazing, aflame (pres. act. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.arentes: āreō, ārēre — dry, parched, withered (pres. act. part., m./f. nom. or acc. pl.)
glossary.arguitur: arguō, arguere — is faulted, is called in question, is accused (3 sg. pres. pass. ind.)
glossary.artificis: artifex, artificis — of a craftsman, of an artist (m. gen. sg.)
glossary.aselli: asellus — of a donkey, of an ass (m. gen. sg.; diminutive of asinus; also nom. pl.)
glossary.asper: asper — rough, savage, made fierce (m. nom. sg.; + abl. of what makes fierce)
glossary.auderet: audeō, audēre — would dare, dared (3 sg. imperf. subj. act.; semi-deponent)
glossary.auso: ausum — venture, bold attempt, thing dared (n. dat./abl. sg.; + verbs of gaining, which take the abl.); also the perf. part. of audeō, 'having dared' (m./n. dat./abl. sg.)
glossary.autolycus: Autolycus — Autolycus (m. nom. sg.; Greek name, the thief-son of Mercury)
glossary.avarae: avārus — greedy, grasping (f. gen./dat. sg.; also f. nom. pl.)
glossary.bacchaeque: Baccha — Bacchantes, women of Bacchus' band (f. nom. pl.; + -que)
glossary.barbaricoque: barbaricus — foreign, outlandish, barbaric (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.belloque: bellum — war, fighting (n. dat. or abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.berecyntius: Berecyntius — Berecyntian, Phrygian (m. nom. sg.; from Mt Berecyntus in Phrygia, home of Cybele's rites)
glossary.bicoloribus: bicolor, bicolōris — two-coloured, of two hues (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.caeruleam: caeruleus — dark blue, sea-blue (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.candentibus: candeō, candēre — gleaming white, shining (pres. act. part., dat./abl. pl.; as a noun, white things)
glossary.canenti: canō, canere — to one singing, to the player (pres. act. part., m./f. dat. sg.; the -i ending also serves as abl. sg.)
glossary.capessamus: capessō, capessere — let us take up, let us lay hold of (1 pl. pres. subj. act., hortatory)
glossary.carinis: carīna — keels, ships (f. dat./abl. pl.; the keel standing for the whole ship)
glossary.carpathius: Carpathius — Carpathian, of the island Carpathos (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.cecropio: Cecropius — Cecropian, Athenian (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; from Cecrops, first king of Athens)
glossary.celsoque: celsus — high, lofty, upraised (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.cerata: cērātus — waxed, joined with wax (perf. pass. part. of cērō used as adj.; f. nom. or abl. sg., also n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.ceyx: Cēyx, Cēycis — Ceyx (m. nom. sg.; Greek name, king of Trachis)
glossary.chione: Chionē — Chione (f. nom. sg.; Greek name; the same form serves as abl. sg.)
glossary.circumlitus: circumlinō, circumlinere — smeared over, coated all round (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.; + abl. of the coating)
glossary.clivoque: clīvus — slope, hillside (m. dat. or abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.coarguit: coarguō, coarguere — exposes, betrays, proves against; or exposed, betrayed (3 sg. pres. or perf. act. ind.)

glossary.cohors: cohors, cohortis — band, throng, retinue (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.comitantibus: comitor, comitārī — accompanying, attending (pres. part. of the deponent, dat./abl. pl.; with an abl. of number it makes an abl. absolute, 'with few attending')
glossary.commoda: commodum — advantages, benefits, resources (n. nom./acc. pl.); the same letters are also commodus, 'convenient, suitable' (f. nom./abl. sg. or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.complevit: compleō, complēre — filled up; completed, brought to full term (3 sg. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.conantemque: cōnor, cōnārī — trying, attempting (pres. part. of the deponent, m./f. acc. sg.; + inf.; + -que)
glossary.confessam: cōnfiteor, cōnfitērī — having confessed, having owned up (perf. part. of the deponent, active in sense, f. acc. sg.)
glossary.coniugiique: coniugium — of marriage, of wedlock (n. gen. sg.; + -que)
glossary.coniunctaque: coniungō, coniungere — joined, united, brought together (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl. or f. nom./abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.constantia: cōnstantia — steadiness, firmness of purpose (f. nom. or abl. sg.)

glossary.contigero: contingō, contingere — I shall have touched (1 sg. fut. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.crabronum: crābrō, crābrōnis — of hornets (m. gen. pl.)
glossary.creber: crēber — thick, close-set, crowded (m. nom. sg.; + abl. of what it is thick with)
glossary.cruento: cruentus — bloody, blood-stained (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.culpavit: culpō — found fault with, blamed, criticized (3 sg. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.cumulum: cumulus — heap, pile; crowning addition, capstone (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.cylleneo: Cyllēnēus — Cyllenian, of Mt Cyllene in Arcadia (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.daedalion: Daedaliōn, Daedaliōnis — Daedalion (m. nom. sg.; Greek name)
glossary.damna: damnum — losses, harms, damages (n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.damnatur: damnō — is condemned, is sentenced (3 sg. pres. pass. ind.; the part affected in the acc. with 'in')
glossary.decerpsit: dēcerpō, dēcerpere — plucked off, gathered (3 sg. perf. act. ind.)

glossary.delamentatur: dēlāmentor, dēlāmentārī — bewails, laments bitterly (3 sg. pres. ind. of the deponent; a rare compound of lāmentor)
glossary.delenit: dēlēniō (dēliniō), dēlēnīre — soothes, charms, wins over (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.delphine: delphīn, delphīnis — dolphin (m. abl. sg.; Greek third-decl. noun, beside the Latin delphīnus)

glossary.demas: dēmō, dēmere — you take away, you subtract, you leave out of account (2 sg. pres. subj. act.; in an 'if you set aside' condition)

glossary.detraxit: dētrahō, dētrahere — pulled off, drew down, stripped away (3 sg. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.difficili: difficilis, -e — difficult, hard, laborious (dat. or abl. sg. of any gender)
glossary.diramque: dīrus — dreadful, dire, grim (f. acc. sg.; + -que)
glossary.discedit: discēdō, discēdere — departs, goes away (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)

glossary.efferre: efferō, efferre — to carry out, to bring forth into the open (pres. act. inf.; ex + ferō)

glossary.elue: ēluō, ēluere — wash away, wash off (2 sg. pres. act. imper.)
glossary.eumolpo: Eumolpus — Eumolpus (m. dat. or abl. sg.; Greek name)

glossary.exul: exul (exsul), exulis — exile, banished man (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.falcatus: falcātus — sickle-shaped, curved like a hook (m. nom. sg.; from falx, a sickle)
glossary.falsis: falsus — false, lying, deceitful (dat./abl. pl.; perf. part. of fallō used as adj.)
glossary.fameque: famēs, famis — hunger, famine (f. abl. sg., 'famē' with long e; + -que)
glossary.feramus: ferō, ferre — let us bring, let us carry (1 pl. pres. subj. act., hortatory)
glossary.festinus: festīnus — hurrying, in haste (m. nom. sg.; adjective where English would use an adverb)
glossary.fibris: fibra — entrails, inner organs of a victim; fibres (f. dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.fingens: fingō, fingere — shaping, imagining, picturing to oneself (pres. act. part., m./f. nom. sg.)
glossary.finitur: fīniō, fīnīre — is bounded, is bordered; is ended (3 sg. pres. pass. ind.; + abl. of the boundary)
glossary.flavum: flāvus — golden-yellow, blond, tawny (m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.fluitare: fluitō, fluitāre — to flow, to stream, to float along (pres. act. inf.; frequentative of fluō)
glossary.focus: focus — hearth, fireplace; the fire burning on it (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.fragore: fragor — crash, din, roar (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.fratrique: frāter — and to a brother (m. dat. sg.; + -que)
glossary.frenato: frēnō — bridled, reined, curbed (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.)
glossary.freti: fretum — of the sea, of a strait (n. gen. sg.); the same letters also give frētus, relying on (m. nom. pl. or m./n. gen. sg.)
glossary.frugis: frūx, frūgis — of grain, of produce, of the fruits of the earth (f. gen. sg.)
glossary.fulmineus: fulmineus — lightning-like, flashing, destructive as a thunderbolt (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.fulvum: fulvus — tawny, yellow-gold, reddish-yellow (m./n. acc. sg. or n. nom. sg.)
glossary.funesto: fūnestus — deadly, death-dealing, fatal (m./n. abl. sg.)
glossary.fusile: fūsilis — molten, liquefied, poured out (n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.gaudenti: gaudeō — to one rejoicing, glad, delighted (pres. act. part., dat. sg.; also abl. sg. in -i)
glossary.gaudetque: gaudeō — and rejoices, is glad (3 sg. pres. act. ind.; + -que) + abl.
glossary.genialiter: geniāliter — merrily, festively, in holiday style (adv.)
glossary.gentesque: gēns — and peoples, nations, tribes (f. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.; + -que)
glossary.gerenti: gerō — to one bearing, carrying, wearing (pres. act. part., dat. sg.; also abl. sg. in -i)
glossary.glaeba: glaeba — clod, lump of earth (f. nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
glossary.gradientis: gradior — of one stepping, walking, pacing (pres. part. of a deponent, gen. sg.; also acc. pl. in -is for -es)
glossary.gratum: grātus — pleasing, welcome, agreeable (m./n. acc. sg. or n. nom. sg.)
glossary.habitantem: habitō — dwelling, living, inhabiting (pres. act. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
glossary.haerebat: haereō — was clinging, was sticking fast, was caught (3 sg. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.haustae: hauriō — drawn out, dug out, hollowed (perf. pass. part., f. dat./gen. sg. or f. nom. pl.)
glossary.helles: Hellē — of Helle, the daughter of Nephele who fell into the strait named after her (f. gen. sg., Greek genitive in -es)
glossary.hesioneque: Hēsionē — and Hesione, daughter of Laomedon (f. abl. sg., Greek noun; + -que)
glossary.hesperidas: Hesperides — the Hesperides, the nymphs who guarded the golden apples in the far west (f. acc. pl., Greek inflection)
glossary.hesperium: Hesperius — western, of the evening land (m./n. acc. sg. or n. nom. sg.)
glossary.homine: homō — a human being, a man (m. abl. sg.; plus homine: more than human)
glossary.hostiliter: hostīliter — in hostile fashion, like an enemy (adv.)
glossary.humumque: humus — and the ground, the earth, the soil (f. acc. sg.; + -que)
glossary.inclinarat: inclīnō — had bent, had bowed down (3 sg. pluperf. act. ind.; syncopated for 'inclinaverat')
glossary.inclinatoque: inclīnō — and tilted, sloped, bent down (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.inclinavit: inclīnō — bent, turned, drove aside (3 sg. perf. act. ind.)
glossary.inductum: indūcō — drawn over, spread over, laid on top (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.)

glossary.infectum: īnficiō — stained, dyed, tinged (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg.); the same letters also give the adjective īnfectus, unfinished, undone
glossary.infitiatur: īnfitior — denies, disowns, refuses to pay (3 sg. pres. ind., deponent)
glossary.ingeniosus: ingeniōsus — clever, gifted, resourceful (m. nom. sg.) + ad + acc.
glossary.ingentique: ingēns — and huge, mighty, vast (m./f./n. abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.inhaerentem: inhaereō — clinging to, fastened upon (pres. act. part., m./f. acc. sg.) + dat.
glossary.iniusta: iniūstus — unjust, unfair (f. nom. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.innecte: innectō — bind on, entwine, fasten tight (2 sg. pres. act. imper.)
glossary.innectens: innectō — twining round, binding, looping (pres. act. part., nom. sg.)
glossary.insonat: īnsonō — sounds, makes music upon, plays loudly (3 sg. pres. act. ind.) + abl.
glossary.instabilesque: īnstabilis — and unsteady, shifting, not firm (m./f. nom./acc. pl.; + -que)

glossary.inutile: inūtilis — useless, unprofitable, harmful (n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.invaserat: invādō — had seized, had fallen upon, had rushed at (3 sg. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.invidiosus: invidiōsus — envied, arousing envy; grudged (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.inviso: invīsus — hated, hateful, loathed (perf. pass. part. of invideō used as an adjective, m./n. abl. sg.); the same letters also give invīsō, I go to see, I visit (1 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.iudex: iūdex — judge, umpire, arbiter (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.iugulati: iugulō — slain, murdered, cut down (perf. pass. part., m. gen. sg. or m. nom. pl.)
glossary.iunctas: iungō — joined, linked, running one after another (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl.)
glossary.lacerae: lacer — mangled, torn, savaged (f. gen./dat. sg. or f. nom. pl.)
glossary.laomedonta: Lāomedōn — Laomedon, a king of Troy (m. acc. sg., Greek accusative in -a)
glossary.laomedonteis: Lāomedontēus — of Laomedon, Trojan (dat./abl. pl., m./f./n.)
glossary.latarumque: lātus — and of the wide, of the broad, of the far-spread (f. gen. pl.; + -que)
glossary.latoius: Lātōius — the son of Latona, Apollo (m. nom. sg.; a patronymic adjective used as a name)
glossary.lauro: laurus — laurel, bay (f. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.laverat: lavō — had washed, had bathed, had rinsed (3 sg. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.lenaee: Lēnaeus — Lenaean, of the winepress, a cult title of Bacchus (m. voc. sg.)
glossary.leni: lēnis — gentle, soft, mild (m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.liquidumque: liquidus — and clear, limpid, flowing (m./n. acc. sg. or n. nom. sg.; + -que)
glossary.lucus: lūcus — grove, wood, thicket (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.lugebat: lūgeō — was mourning, was grieving for (3 sg. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.lydos: Lȳdus — Lydian, of Lydia (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.maculosae: maculōsus — spotted, dappled, mottled (f. gen./dat. sg. or f. nom. pl.)
glossary.maestus: maestus — sad, sorrowful, in mourning (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.magnetas: Magnētes — the Magnesians, the people of Magnesia in Thessaly (m. acc. pl., Greek inflection)
glossary.maiaque: Māia — and Maia, mother of Mercury (f. abl. sg.; + -que; abl. of origin with a participle such as 'creatus', born of)
glossary.marinae: marīnus — of the sea, sea- (f. gen./dat. sg. or f. nom. pl.)
glossary.maturuit: mātūrēscō — ripened, came to full growth (3 sg. perf. act. ind.; an inceptive verb)
glossary.memorat: memorō — relates, tells, mentions (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.mentiturque: mentior — and lies about, invents falsely, feigns (3 sg. pres. ind., deponent; + -que) + acc.
glossary.meritus: mereor — deservedly, having deserved it (perf. part. of a deponent, m. nom. sg., active in sense)
glossary.meroque: merum — and with unmixed wine, neat wine (n. abl. sg.; + -que)
glossary.messis: messis — harvest, crop, reaping (f. nom. sg.; also gen. sg.)
glossary.midae: Midās — of Midas, a Phrygian king (m. gen. sg.; also dat. sg.)
glossary.midan: Midās — Midas (m. acc. sg., Greek accusative in -n)
glossary.miscuerat: misceō — had mingled, had mixed together (3 sg. pluperf. act. ind.)
glossary.miseratus: miseror — having pitied, taking pity on (perf. part. of a deponent, m. nom. sg., active in sense) + acc.
glossary.miserque: miser — and wretched, and pitiable (m. nom. sg.; + -que)
glossary.mite: mītis — mild, gentle, merciful (n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.mittat: mittō — may send, is to send (3 sg. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.modulatur: modulor — plays, sings in measure, modulates (3 sg. pres. ind., deponent)
glossary.moliri: mōlior — to build, to rear up with effort, to toil at (pres. inf., deponent)
glossary.momento: mōmentum — in a moment, by a movement; by weight, by influence (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.montanis: montānus — mountain-, of the mountains (dat./abl. pl., m./f./n.)
glossary.movebant: moveō — were moving, were stirring, were affecting (3 pl. imperf. act. ind.)
glossary.movente: moveō — moving, stirring, bringing on (pres. act. part., abl. sg.)
glossary.myrtea: myrteus — of myrtle, myrtle- (f. nom./abl. sg. or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.nant: nō, nāre — they swim, they float (3 pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.nascitur: nāscor — is born, is begotten, comes into being (3 sg. pres. ind., deponent)
glossary.negata: negō — denied, refused, withheld (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg. or f. nom. sg. or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.nepheleidos: Nēphelēis — of the daughter of Nephele (f. gen. sg., Greek genitive in -idos; a patronymic)
glossary.nepoti: nepōs — to a grandson, to a descendant (m. dat. sg.)
glossary.nereida: Nērēis — a Nereid, a sea-nymph daughter of Nereus (f. acc. sg., Greek accusative in -a)
glossary.nereis: Nērēis — a Nereid, a sea-nymph (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.nereusque: Nēreus — and Nereus, the old god of the sea and father of the Nereids (m. nom. sg.; + -que)

glossary.nuntius: nūntius — messenger, bringer of news (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.obruit: obruō — buries, covers over, overwhelms (3 sg. pres. act. ind.; identical in form to the perfect, buried, overwhelmed)
glossary.oetaeus: Oetaeus — Oetaean, of Mount Oeta and its region (m. nom. sg.)

glossary.assaracus: Assaracus, -ī, m. — Assaracus, son of Tros and forebear of the Trojan line (nom. sg.)
glossary.athon: Athōs, m. (acc. Athōn) — Mount Athos, the peak of Chalcidice (Greek acc. sg.)
glossary.attonito: attonitus, -a, -um — thunderstruck, stunned (abl. sg. neut. here; the form is also abl. sg. masc./dat.)
glossary.audiri: audiō, audīre — to hear (pres. pass. infinitive)
glossary.audis: audiō, audīre — to hear, hear of (2nd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.augur: augur, auguris, m. — augur, seer, reader of omens (nom. sg.)
glossary.aulam: aula, -ae, f. — hall, palace, court (acc. sg.)
glossary.aulide: Aulis, Aulidis, f. — Aulis, the Boeotian harbour where the Greek fleet mustered (abl. sg.)
glossary.ballistave: ballista, -ae, f. — ballista, a siege engine that hurls stones (nom. sg. + enclitic -ve “or”)
glossary.bellaque: bellum, -ī, n. — war (acc. pl. + -que; not bella, fem. of bellus “pretty”)
glossary.boeotaque: Boeōtus, -a, -um — Boeotian (nom. sg. fem. + -que, with tellūs)
glossary.buxoque: buxum, -ī, n. (also buxus, -ī, f.) — boxwood, and its pale yellow colour (dat. sg. + -que, with simillimus)
glossary.cadensve: cadō, cadere — to fall; of the sun, to set (pres. act. participle, nom. sg. masc. + enclitic -ve “or”)
glossary.cadet: cadō, cadere — to fall, be brought down (3rd sg. fut. indic. act.)
glossary.caelestesque: caelestis, -e — of the sky, heavenly (acc. pl. fem. here + -que; the form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.canibusve: canis, canis, m./f. — dog (abl. pl. + enclitic -ve “or”)
glossary.captae: capiō, capere, captus — to take, capture (perf. pass. participle, gen. sg. fem. here; the form is also nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.captatam: captō, captāre, captātus — to chase after, keep trying to catch, court (perf. pass. participle, acc. sg. fem.)
glossary.carebunt: careō, carēre (+ abl.) — to lack, be free of (3rd pl. fut. indic. act.)
glossary.carpentem: carpō, carpere — to pluck; of a route, to make one's way over, skim (pres. act. participle, acc. sg. masc.)
glossary.castumque: castus, -a, -um — chaste, unstained, innocent (acc. sg. masc. + -que)
glossary.cebrenida: Cebrēnis, Cebrēnidos, f. — daughter of Cebren the river-god, here the nymph Hesperie (patronymic, Greek acc. sg.)
glossary.celeremque: celer, celeris, celere — swift, quick (acc. sg. masc./fem., here fem., + -que)
glossary.ceyca: Cēyx, Cēycis, m. — Ceyx, king of Trachis and husband of Alcyone (Greek acc. sg. in -a)
glossary.ceyce: Cēyx, Cēycis, m. — Ceyx, king of Trachis and husband of Alcyone (abl. sg.)
glossary.ceycis: Cēyx, Cēycis, m. — Ceyx, king of Trachis and husband of Alcyone (gen. sg.)
glossary.cimmerios: Cimmeriī, -ōrum, m. pl. — the Cimmerians, a people placed at the world's edge in unbroken gloom (acc. pl.)
glossary.circumstetit: circumstō, circumstāre, circumstetī — to stand round, ring, close in around (3rd sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.clamatque: clāmō, clāmāre — to shout, cry out (3rd sg. pres. indic. act. + -que)
glossary.clarium: Clarius, -a, -um — of Claros, the Ionian seat of Apollo's oracle (acc. sg. masc., with deum = Apollo)
glossary.cogi: cōgō, cōgere — to compel, force (pres. pass. infinitive)
glossary.coluber: coluber, colubrī, m. — snake, serpent (nom. sg.)
glossary.commenta: commentum, -ī, n. — a fabrication, invented tale (nom. pl. here; the same form is also the perf. participle of comminīscor)
glossary.coniugiale: coniugiālis, -e — of marriage, conjugal (nom. sg. neut. here; the form is also acc. sg. neut.)
glossary.coniurataeque: coniūrātus, -a, -um — bound together by oath, sworn in league (perf. participle of coniūrō; nom. pl. fem. + -que)
glossary.conlapsaque: collābor (conlābor), collābī, collāpsus — to collapse, sink down in a faint (perf. participle, nom. sg. fem., + -que; with est forms the perfect)
glossary.consternatique: consternō, consternāre, consternātus — to throw into panic, dismay (perf. pass. participle, nom. pl. masc., + -que; distinct from consternō, consternere “to strew”)
glossary.consuetissima: consuētus, -a, -um — accustomed, habitual (superlative, acc. pl. neut.: “most familiar”)
glossary.contineat: contineō, continēre — to hold in, keep shut up (3rd sg. pres. subjunctive act.)
glossary.coortis: coorior, coorīrī, coortus — to rise up, break out (perf. participle, abl. pl. masc., in an ablative absolute)
glossary.corripuit: corripiō, corripere, corripuī — to snatch up, seize (3rd sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.credant: crēdō, crēdere — to believe, suppose (3rd pl. pres. subjunctive act.)
glossary.credulitas: crēdulitās, crēdulitātis, f. — credulity, readiness to believe (nom. sg.; here personified)
glossary.crudelior: crūdēlis, -e — cruel, harsh (comparative, nom. sg. masc./fem., here fem.)
glossary.crurum: crūs, crūris, n. — leg, shin (gen. pl.)
glossary.cubat: cubō, cubāre — to lie down, recline, lie asleep (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.cunei: cuneus, -ī, m. — wedge; in a ship, the wedges pinning the planking (nom. pl. here; the form is also gen. sg.)
glossary.curaeque: cūra, -ae, f. — care, anxiety (nom. pl. here + -que; the form is also gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.custodit: custōdiō, custōdīre — to guard, keep watch over, keep shut in (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.danai: Danaī, -ōrum, m. pl. — the Danaans, the Greeks (nom. pl. here; the form is also gen. sg. of Danaus)
glossary.decimae: decimus, -a, -um — tenth (gen. sg. fem. here; the form is also nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.defensae: dēfendō, dēfendere, dēfēnsus — to defend (perf. pass. participle, gen. sg. fem. here; the form is also nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.demissam: dēmittō, dēmittere, dēmissus — to send down, let sink (perf. pass. participle, acc. sg. fem.)
glossary.deposuitque: dēpōnō, dēpōnere, dēposuī — to lay down, set down (3rd sg. perf. indic. act. + -que)
glossary.descendat: dēscendō, dēscendere — to come down, descend (3rd sg. pres. subjunctive act.)
glossary.desideret: dēsīderō, dēsīderāre — to long for, miss (3rd sg. pres. subjunctive act.; not dēsideō “to sit idle”)
glossary.despicere: dēspiciō, dēspicere — to look down, look down upon (pres. act. infinitive)
glossary.digerit: dīgerō, dīgerere — to distribute, apportion, spread out (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.dimittere: dīmittō, dīmittere — to send away, let go, give up (pres. act. infinitive)
glossary.dinumerat: dīnumerō, dīnumerāre — to count out, reckon up one by one (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.discedentem: discēdō, discēdere — to depart, go away (pres. act. participle, acc. sg., here used as a noun)
glossary.discreta: discernō, discernere, discrētus — to separate, keep apart (perf. pass. participle, nom. sg. fem.)
glossary.discutiunt: discutiō, discutere — to shatter, scatter, break apart (3rd pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.distante: dīstō, dīstāre — to be distant, stand apart (pres. act. participle, abl. sg., in an ablative absolute)
glossary.diversae: dīversus, -a, -um — different, of another kind (gen. sg. fem. here; the form is also nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.divinante: dīvīnō, dīvīnāre — to divine, foresee, have a foreboding (pres. act. participle, abl. sg.)
glossary.dolebo: doleō, dolēre — to grieve, feel pain (1st sg. fut. indic. act.)
glossary.dubiaeque: dubius, -a, -um — doubtful, uncertain, dim (gen. sg. fem. here + -que; the form is also nom. pl. fem.)
glossary.dubioque: dubius, -a, -um — doubtful, uncertain (abl. sg. masc./neut. + -que, here masc. in an ablative absolute)
glossary.dubitabat: dubitō, dubitāre — to doubt, be uncertain (3rd sg. imperf. indic. act.)
glossary.ducibusque: dux, ducis, m. — leader, commander (dat. pl. + -que; the form is also abl. pl.)
glossary.duxisses: dūcō, dūcere, dūxī — to lead, take along (2nd sg. pluperf. subjunctive act., here in an unfulfilled wish)
glossary.dymantis: Dymās, Dymantis, m. — Dymas, father of Hecuba (gen. sg.; prōlēs Dymantis is Hecuba, his daughter)
glossary.ebeno: ebenus, -ī, f. (also ebenum, -ī, n.) — ebony (abl. sg., of material)
glossary.edo: ēdō, ēdere, ēdidī — to give out, declare, announce (1st sg. pres. indic. act.; not edō “to eat”, whose 1st sg. is spelled identically)
glossary.eductam: ēdūcō, ēdūcere, ēductus — to lead out, bring out (of a ship from the docks) (perf. pass. participle, acc. sg. fem.; not ēducō, ēducāre “to rear”)
glossary.egissem: agō, agere, ēgī — to do, drive; of time, to spend, pass (1st sg. pluperf. subjunctive act.)
glossary.egressu: ēgressus, -ūs, m. — a going out, way out, egress (abl. sg., of separation)
glossary.eiectas: ēiciō, ēicere, ēiectus — to cast out, throw up (perf. pass. participle, acc. pl. fem.)
glossary.emissi: ēmittō, ēmittere, ēmissus — to send out, let loose (perf. pass. participle, nom. pl. masc.)
glossary.euntque: eō, īre — to go (3rd pl. pres. indic. act. + -que)
glossary.everterit: ēvertō, ēvertere, ēvertī — to overturn, tear up from its place (3rd sg. perf. subjunctive act. here; the form is identical to the fut. perf. indic.)
glossary.evocat: ēvocō, ēvocāre — to call forth, summon out (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.excitat: excitō, excitāre — to rouse, wake, stir up (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.exclamatque: exclāmō, exclāmāre — to cry out, exclaim (3rd sg. pres. indic. act. + -que)
glossary.excutiuntque: excutiō, excutere — to shake out, strike out (of sparks) (3rd pl. pres. indic. act. + -que)
glossary.exhalantur: exhālō, exhālāre — to breathe out, exhale (3rd pl. pres. indic. passive)
glossary.exprimit: exprimō, exprimere — to press out; to reproduce, mimic to the life (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.exstinctique: ex(s)tinguō, exstinguere, exstinctus — to put out, quench, kill (perf. pass. participle, gen. sg. masc. + -que: “of the dead man”)
glossary.extra: extrā — outside, on the outside (adverb here, answering intus; the same form is also a preposition + acc.)
glossary.fallaciter: fallāciter — deceptively, so as to deceive (adverb, from fallāx)
glossary.falso: falsō — falsely, on false grounds (adverb; the same form is also dat./abl. sg. masc./neut. of falsus “false”)
glossary.feremur: ferō, ferre — to bear, carry (1st pl. fut. indic. passive: “we shall be borne”)
glossary.feroces: ferōx, ferōcis — fierce, savage, spirited (nom. pl. masc. here; the form is also acc. pl.)
glossary.ferreus: ferreus, -a, -um — of iron, iron-shod (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.festinat: fēstīnō, fēstīnāre — to hurry; transitive, to hurry on, hasten the making of (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.fingant: fingō, fingere — to shape, mould, feign (3rd pl. pres. subjunctive act.)
glossary.florent: flōreō, flōrēre — to bloom, be in flower (3rd pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.fluctu: fluctus, -ūs, m. — wave, surge, billow (abl. sg.)
glossary.fluere: fluō, fluere — to flow, stream, run down (pres. act. infinitive)
glossary.fluitantia: fluitō, fluitāre — to float, flap loose, stream (pres. act. participle, acc. pl. neut. here; the form is also nom. pl. neut.)
glossary.fluvialis: fluviālis, -e — of a river, river- (nom. sg. fem.)
glossary.fodientibus: fodiō, fodere — to dig, undermine (pres. act. participle, abl. pl. masc., in an ablative absolute)
glossary.frangit: frangō, frangere — to break, shatter (3rd sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.frangitur: frangō, frangere — to break, shatter (3rd sg. pres. indic. passive: “is broken, snaps”)
glossary.fretaque: fretum, -ī, n. — strait, channel; in the plural often simply the sea (acc. pl. + -que)
glossary.fretumque: fretum, -ī, n. — strait, channel; the sea (acc. sg. + -que; the form is also nom. sg.)
glossary.fugeres: fugiō, fugere — to flee, run away from (2nd sg. imperf. subjunctive act.)
glossary.fugientis: fugiō, fugere — to flee (pres. act. participle, gen. sg. fem. here, “of the fleeing girl”; the form is also acc. pl.)
glossary.fulmineis: fulmineus, -a, -um — of lightning, flashing like a thunderbolt (abl. pl. masc.)
glossary.functo: fungor, fungī, functus (+ abl.) — to perform, discharge, undergo; morte functus = one who has met his death (perf. participle, abl. sg. masc., used as a noun)
glossary.fundere: fundō, fundere — to pour, pour out, shed (pres. act. infinitive here; the same form can be 2nd sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.funestas: fūnestus, -a, -um — polluted by death, defiled by a corpse; deadly (acc. pl. fem. here; the same form can be 2nd sg. pres. indic. of fūnestō “to defile with death”)
glossary.ganymedes: Ganymēdēs, -is m. — Ganymede, the Trojan boy carried off by Jupiter (nom. sg., Greek declension)
glossary.geratur: gerō, gerere, gessī, gestum — carry on, be done, go on (pres. pass. subj. 3 sg.; in an indirect question, “what is going on”)
glossary.gerunt: gerō, gerere, gessī, gestum — wage, carry on (pres. act. ind. 3 pl.; with bella, “wage wars”)
glossary.gestumque: gestus, -ūs m. — gesture, bearing, movement (acc. sg. + enclitic -que; not the supine/PPP gestum of gerō)
glossary.granico: Grānīcus, -ī m. — the Granicus, a river of the Troad, here a river-god (abl. sg., of origin with nāta)
glossary.habens: habeō, habēre, habuī, habitum — have, possess (pres. act. part., nom. sg.)
glossary.hector: Hectōr, -oris m. — Hector, eldest son of Priam, chief defender of Troy (nom. sg.)
glossary.hectore: Hectōr, -oris m. — Hector (abl. sg.; here abl. of comparison, “than Hector”)
glossary.herculea: Herculeus, -a, -um — of Hercules, Herculean (abl. sg. fem.; an epithet of places, not the hero's own name)
glossary.hesperien: Hesperiē, -ēs f. — Hesperie, a nymph, daughter of the river Cebren (Greek acc. sg. in -ēn; a person, not the land Hesperia)
glossary.hiberno: hībernus, -a, -um — of winter, wintry (abl. sg. neut.)
glossary.hiemisque: hiems, hiemis f. — winter; storm, tempest (gen. sg. + enclitic -que; “storm” in a sea context)
glossary.hiscere: hīscō, hīscere — open the mouth, gape (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.humanaeve: hūmānus, -a, -um — human (gen. sg. fem. + enclitic -ve “or”; genitive with linguae, not nom. pl.)
glossary.iactabimur: iactō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — toss, buffet (fut. pass. ind. 1 pl., “we shall be tossed”)
glossary.iactatam: iactō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — toss, buffet (PPP, acc. sg. fem., “tossed”)
glossary.iactor: iactō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — toss, buffet (pres. pass. ind. 1 sg., “I am tossed”)
glossary.icelon: Īcelos, -ī m. — Icelos “Likeness”, the dream-god's name among the gods (Greek acc. sg. in -on)
glossary.ida: Īda, -ae f. — Mount Ida, the wooded range above Troy (abl. sg.)
glossary.ignoto: ignōtus, -a, -um — unknown, a stranger (dat. sg. masc. as a noun, “to a stranger”; the form is also abl.)
glossary.iliacos: Īliacus, -a, -um — of Ilium, Trojan (acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.ilus: Īlus, -ī m. — Ilus, son of Tros and founder of Ilium, ancestor of the Trojan kings (nom. sg.)
glossary.imitantia: imitor, imitārī, imitātus sum (dep.) — imitate, copy (pres. part., nom./acc. pl. neut., with somnia)
glossary.imitatur: imitor, imitārī, imitātus sum (dep.) — imitate, copy (pres. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.impleat: impleō, implēre, implēvī, implētum — fill, fill up (pres. act. subj. 3 sg.; with orbem, of the moon filling its disc)
glossary.implerunt: impleō, implēre, implēvī, implētum — fill (perf. act. ind. 3 pl., syncopated for implēvērunt)
glossary.imumque: īmus, -a, -um — lowest, deepest (superl. of īnferus; acc. sg. masc. + enclitic -que)
glossary.inambitiosa: inambitiōsus, -a, -um — unpretentious, free of display (acc. pl. neut., with rūra; a rare word)
glossary.incanduit: incandēscō, -ere, incanduī — grow hot, glow white (perf. act. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.incessus: incessus, -ūs m. — gait, manner of walking (acc. pl.; here object of exprimit, not nom. sg.)
glossary.incommendataque: incommendātus, -a, -um — entrusted to no one's protection, unguarded (nom. sg. fem. + enclitic -que)
glossary.increpuit: increpō, -āre, increpuī — make a din; here transitive, crash upon, thunder at (perf. act. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.indignatur: indignor, indignārī, indignātus sum (dep.) — be indignant at, resent (pres. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.induat: induō, induere, induī, indūtum — put on (clothing) (pres. act. subj. 3 sg., in a relative clause of purpose)
glossary.indue: induō, induere, induī, indūtum — put on (clothing) (pres. act. imper. 2 sg.)
glossary.inferno: īnfernus, -a, -um — of the underworld, lower, infernal (abl. sg. masc., with gurgite)
glossary.iniectos: iniciō, inicere, iniēcī, iniectum — throw on, cast over (PPP, acc. pl. masc., “flung over”)
glossary.inrumpere: inrumpō (irrumpō), -ere, -rūpī, -ruptum — burst in, break in (pres. act. inf.; the edition's inr- for irr-)
glossary.inspicitur: īnspiciō, -ere, -spexī, -spectum — look into, observe, descry (pres. pass. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.insurgens: īnsurgō, -ere, -surrēxī — rise up, swell (pres. act. part., nom. sg.)
glossary.interrumpente: interrumpō, -ere, -rūpī, -ruptum — break off, interrupt (pres. act. part., abl. sg., in an ablative absolute)
glossary.intraque: intrā (prep. + acc.) — within, inside of (+ enclitic -que; not a form of intrō, -āre)
glossary.intulerant: īnferō, īnferre, intulī, illātum — bring in, carry in (pluperf. act. ind. 3 pl.)
glossary.invadere: invādō, -ere, -vāsī, -vāsum — assail, rush upon (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.inveniesque: inveniō, -īre, invēnī, inventum — find (fut. act. ind. 2 sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.invia: invius, -a, -um — pathless, impassable (acc. pl. neut., predicative with a verb of making, “made impassable”)
glossary.invitat: invītō, -āre — invite, woo, entice (pres. act. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.iphigenia: Īphigenīa, -ae f. — Iphigenia, daughter of Agamemnon, offered at Aulis (nom. sg.)
glossary.ipsisque: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — himself, herself, itself; the very (dat. pl. fem. + enclitic -que; dative with the compound verb)
glossary.iri: Īris, Īridis f. — Iris, the rainbow, Juno's messenger (voc. sg., Greek Īri; not a form of eō or of īra)
glossary.iteratque: iterō, -āre — repeat, say again (pres. act. ind. 3 sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.ituras: eō, īre, īvī/iī, itum — go (fut. act. part., acc. pl. fem., “about to go, bound for”)
glossary.iubeatve: iubeō, iubēre, iussī, iussum — order, bid (pres. act. subj. 3 sg. + enclitic -ve “or”)
glossary.iunctim: iūnctim (adv.) — together, side by side, in a pair
glossary.labique: lābor, lābī, lāpsus sum (dep.) — glide, slip, sink (pres. inf. + enclitic -que; from lābor “glide”, not labōr, -ōris “toil”)
glossary.laceras: lacer, lacera, lacerum — mangled, torn, shattered (acc. pl. fem.; the adjective, not 2 sg. of lacerō)
glossary.lacerat: lacerō, -āre — tear, rend (pres. act. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.lacte: lac, lactis n. — milk; the milky juice or sap of a plant (abl. sg.)
glossary.laetitia: laetitia, -ae f. — joy, gladness (nom. sg.; here a personified figure, as the edition's capital shows)
glossary.laniatque: laniō, -āre — tear, rend, mangle (pres. act. ind. 3 sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.laomedonque: Lāomedōn, -ontis m. — Laomedon, king of Troy, father of Priam (nom. sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.lapillis: lapillus, -ī m. — pebble, small stone (dimin. of lapis; abl. pl.)
glossary.largi: largus, -a, -um — abundant, copious (nom. pl. masc.; not gen. sg. and not a form of largior)
glossary.latera: latus, lateris n. — side, flank (acc. pl.; the noun, not the adjective lātus “broad”)
glossary.laudisque: laus, laudis f. — praise, glory (gen. sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.lectusque: lectus, -ī m. — bed, couch (nom. sg. + enclitic -que; not the PPP lectus of legō)
glossary.legi: legō, legere, lēgī, lēctum — read; gather (perf. act. ind. 1 sg., “I read, I have read”; the form is also pres. pass. inf. and dat. sg. of lēx)
glossary.letalibus: lētālis, -e — deadly, lethal (dat. pl. fem.; the form is also abl.)
glossary.lethes: Lēthē, -ēs f. — Lethe, the underworld river of forgetfulness (Greek gen. sg. in -ēs)
glossary.liquebat: liqueō, liquēre, licuī/līquī — be clear, be evident (impf. act. ind. 3 sg., impersonal, “it was clear”)
glossary.locat: locō, -āre — place, set, fix (pres. act. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.locusque: locus, -ī m. — place, spot (nom. sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.lugubriaque: lūgubris, -e — of mourning, mournful (acc. pl. neut. as a noun, “mourning clothes” + enclitic -que)
glossary.madidisque: madidus, -a, -um — wet, soaked, dripping (abl. pl. masc. + enclitic -que)
glossary.maneant: maneō, manēre, mānsī — here transitive, await, be in store for (pres. act. subj. 3 pl.)
glossary.mediusve: medius, -a, -um — middle, midway (nom. sg. masc. + enclitic -ve “or”; of the sun at midday)
glossary.meminitque: meminī, meminisse — remember (defective; perfect in form, present in sense; perf. ind. 3 sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.mergitur: mergō, -ere, mersī, mersum — dip, plunge, sink (pres. pass. ind. 3 sg., “is plunged, dives”)
glossary.mergum: mergus, -ī m. — a diving sea-bird, diver, cormorant (acc. sg.)
glossary.mersum: mergō, -ere, mersī, mersum — dip, plunge, sink (PPP, acc. sg. neut., “sunk, submerged”)
glossary.milia: mīlia, -ium n. pl. — thousands (plural of mīlle; nom. pl. here, with a partitive genitive)
glossary.ministris: minister, ministrī m. — attendant, servant at a rite (abl. pl., in an ablative absolute)
glossary.miscentur: misceō, miscēre, miscuī, mixtum — mix, mingle (pres. pass. ind. 3 pl.)
glossary.misera: miser, misera, miserum — wretched, pitiable (abl. sg. fem.; the form is also nom. sg. fem. and nom./acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.miserande: miserandus, -a, -um — pitiable, to be pitied (gerundive of miseror used as an adjective; voc. sg. masc.)
glossary.miserantibus: miseror, miserārī, miserātus sum (dep.) — pity, take pity on (pres. part., abl. pl. masc., in an ablative absolute)
glossary.mittam: mittō, -ere, mīsī, missum — send (1 sg.; fut. act. ind. or pres. act. subj., identical in form — the relative clause does not settle it)
glossary.mixtae: misceō, miscēre, miscuī, mixtum — mix, mingle (PPP, nom. pl. fem., “mingled”; not gen./dat. sg. here)
glossary.morphea: Morpheus, -eos m. — Morpheus, the dream-god who counterfeits human shape (Greek acc. sg. in -ea)
glossary.morpheus: Morpheus, -eos m. — Morpheus, the dream-god who counterfeits human shape (nom. sg.)
glossary.mortes: mors, mortis f. — death (nom. pl.; subject of the infinitives after videntur)
glossary.moti: moveō, movēre, mōvī, mōtum — move, stir (PPP, nom. pl. masc., “stirred, roused”)
glossary.mulces: mulceō, mulcēre, mulsī, mulsum — soothe, caress, soften (pres. act. ind. 2 sg.)
glossary.multoque: multus, -a, -um — much (abl. sg. neut. used adverbially, of degree of difference: “by much, far” with a comparative; + enclitic -que)
glossary.munire: mūniō, -īre, -īvī, -ītum — fortify, strengthen, shore up (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.murum: mūrus, -ī m. — wall, city wall (acc. sg.)
glossary.mycenida: Mycēnis, -idis f. — the woman of Mycenae, i.e. Iphigenia, daughter of Agamemnon (Greek acc. sg. in -ida)
glossary.nantis: nō, nāre, nāvī — swim, float (pres. act. part., gen. sg., “of the swimmer”; the form is also acc. pl.)
glossary.narrantia: nārrō, -āre — tell, relate (pres. act. part., acc. pl. neut., with somnia)
glossary.narrata: nārrō, -āre — tell, relate (PPP, acc. pl. neut. as a noun, “the things told”)
glossary.natat: natō, -āre — swim, float (pres. act. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.naufraga: naufragus, -a, -um — shipwrecked, of shipwreck (acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.naufragus: naufragus, -a, -um — shipwrecked (nom. sg. masc., often as a noun, “a shipwrecked man”)
glossary.navalibus: nāvāle, -is n., usu. pl. nāvālia — dockyard, ship-shed (abl. pl.; the noun, not the adjective nāvālis here)
glossary.navigii: nāvigium, -ī n. — vessel, ship, craft (gen. sg.)
glossary.neptunum: Neptūnus, -ī m. — Neptune, god of the sea, builder of Troy's walls (acc. sg.)
glossary.nescitve: nesciō, -īre, -īvī — not know, be ignorant of (pres. act. ind. 3 sg. + enclitic -ve “or”)
glossary.nidis: nīdus, -ī m. — nest (dat. pl. with incubat “broods on”; the form is also abl.)
glossary.nidus: nīdus, -ī m. — nest, brood in a nest (nom. sg.)
glossary.nigrior: niger, nigra, nigrum — black, dark (compar., nom. sg. masc./fem., “blacker”)
glossary.nimbosi: nimbōsus, -a, -um — stormy, full of rain-cloud (gen. sg. masc.)
glossary.nitar: nītor, nītī, nīxus/nīsus sum (dep.) — strive, struggle, exert oneself (1 sg.; pres. subj. here, though the form is also fut. ind.)
glossary.nitebat: niteō, nitēre, nituī — shine, be radiant (impf. act. ind. 3 sg.; from niteō “shine”, not the deponent nītor “strive”)
glossary.nitidaque: nitidus, -a, -um — gleaming, sleek, elegant (abl. sg. fem. + enclitic -que)
glossary.noli: nōlō, nōlle, nōluī — be unwilling (imper. 2 sg.; with an infinitive it forms a negative command, “do not …”)
glossary.nosces: nōscō, nōscere, nōvī, nōtum — come to know, recognise (fut. act. ind. 2 sg.)
glossary.notata: notō, -āre — mark, note, take note of (PPP, acc. pl. neut., agreeing with ācta)
glossary.nubilus: nūbilus, -a, -um — cloudy, cloud-bringing (nom. sg. masc.; the adjective, not the neuter noun nūbila “clouds”)
glossary.nudumque: nūdus, -a, -um — naked, bare, stripped (acc. sg. masc. + enclitic -que)
glossary.nullamque: nūllus, -a, -um — no, none, no other (acc. sg. fem. + enclitic -que)
glossary.nuntiat: nūntiō, -āre — announce, report (pres. act. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.nutanti: nūtō, -āre — nod, sway, droop (pres. act. part., abl. sg. neut.)
glossary.obit: obeō, obīre, obiī, obitum — go to meet, come over, overspread (3 sg.; pres. act. ind., or syncopated perf. for obiit — the surrounding perfects leave it open)
glossary.obnoxius: obnoxius, -a, -um — subject to, liable to, at the mercy of (+ dat.) (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.obortas: oborior, oborīrī, obortus sum (dep.) — arise, well up (perf. part., acc. pl. fem., “welling up”)
glossary.obstantia: obstō, obstāre, obstitī — stand in the way, block (pres. act. part., acc. pl. neut.)
glossary.obstarique: obstō, obstāre, obstitī — stand in the way, obstruct (pres. pass. inf., impersonal, “that it is blocked” + enclitic -que)
glossary.occidimus: occidō, -ere, occidī, occāsum — fall, perish, die (perf. act. ind. 1 pl. here, “we are undone”; the form is also pres. 1 pl., and distinct from occīdō “kill”)
glossary.oppugnare: oppugnō, -āre — assault, batter, besiege (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.optabat: optō, -āre — wish for, pray for (impf. act. ind. 3 sg.)
glossary.optatae: optō, -āre — wish for, long for (PPP, gen. sg. fem., “longed-for”; the form is also nom. pl. fem. and dat. sg.)
glossary.ordinibus: ōrdō, ōrdinis m. — row, rank, tier (abl. pl.; of the banks of oars)
glossary.parassent: parō, -āre — prepare, make ready (pluperf. act. subj. 3 pl., syncopated for parāvissent)
glossary.parensque: parēns, parentis m./f. — parent (nom. sg. + enclitic -que; not the participle of pāreō here)
glossary.paridis: Paris, Paridis m. — Paris, son of Priam, who carried off Helen (gen. sg.)
glossary.pelasgae: Pelasgus, -a, -um — Pelasgian, i.e. Greek (gen. sg. fem., with gentis; not nom. pl.)
glossary.pendentes: pendeō, pendēre, pependī — hang, hang down (pres. act. part., acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.peragat: peragō, -ere, perēgī, perāctum — carry through, accomplish (pres. act. subj. 3 sg., in a relative clause of purpose)
glossary.percutiens: percutiō, -ere, -cussī, -cussum — strike, beat (pres. act. part., nom. sg.)
glossary.percutiensque: percutiō, -ere, -cussī, -cussum — strike, beat (pres. act. part., nom. sg. + enclitic -que; common gender, so masc. or fem. as the subject requires)
glossary.perdidimus: perdō, -ere, perdidī, perditum — destroy, ruin, lose (perf. act. ind. 1 pl.)
glossary.pericli: perīculum (syncopated perīclum), -ī n. — danger, peril (gen. sg.)
glossary.perii: pereō, perīre, periī — perish, be lost, be undone (perf. act. ind. 1 sg.)
glossary.perpessae: perpetior, perpetī, perpessus sum (dep.) — endure to the end, suffer through (perf. part., nom. pl. fem., active in sense)
glossary.phantasos: Phantasos, -ī m. — Phantasos, the dream-god who takes the shape of lifeless things (nom. sg., Greek nom. in -os)
glossary.phlegyis: Phlegyae, -ārum m. pl. — the Phlegyans, a lawless Thessalian people (abl. pl., with cum)
glossary.phobetora: Phobētōr, -oris m. — Phobetor “Frightener”, the dream-god's name among mortals (Greek acc. sg. in -a)
glossary.phrygia: Phrygius, -a, -um — Phrygian, Trojan (abl. sg. fem., with harēnā; the adjective, not the place-name Phrygia)
glossary.pias: pius, -a, -um — dutiful, devoted, loving (acc. pl. fem.)
glossary.pietatem: pietās, pietātis f. — dutiful devotion, family loyalty (acc. sg.)
glossary.pignoribus: pignus, pignoris n. — pledge, security; in the plural, children, dear ones (abl. pl.)
glossary.pindumve: Pindus, -ī m. — Pindus, a mountain range of Thessaly (acc. sg. + enclitic -ve “or”)
glossary.piscosa: piscōsus, -a, -um — full of fish, fish-teeming (abl. sg. fem.)
glossary.placandam: plācō, -āre — appease, placate (gerundive, acc. sg. fem., “needing to be appeased”)
glossary.placidissime: placidus, -a, -um — gentle, calm, peaceful (superl., voc. sg. masc., “most gentle”; an adjective addressing a person, not the adverb placidissimē)
glossary.plagas: plaga, -ae f. — region, tract, zone of the sky (acc. pl.); a different word from plaga “net, snare”
glossary.plangor: plangor, -oris m. — beating of the breast, loud lamentation (nom. sg.); the noun, not the 1st sg. passive of plango
glossary.platanum: platanus, -i f. — plane tree (acc. sg.); a Greek loan, feminine despite the -us ending
glossary.plebemque: plebs, plebis f. — the common people, the commons (acc. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.plenumque: plenus, -a, -um — full, filled (acc. sg. m.), regularly governing a genitive of what fills it + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.plumeus: plumeus, -a, -um — of feathers, downy, filled with down (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.portibus: portus, -us m. — harbour, port (4th decl., abl. pl. here of separation; the dat. pl. is identical)
glossary.positisque: pono, ponere, posui, positus — put down, lay aside (perf. pass. part., abl. pl. f.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.praebentque: praebeo, -ere, -ui, -itus — offer, furnish, supply (3rd pl. pres. act.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.praebetque: praebeo, -ere, -ui, -itus — offer, furnish, supply (3rd sg. pres. act.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.praedelassat: praedelasso, -are — wear out beforehand, tire in advance (3rd sg. pres. act.); a rare compound, effectively Ovidian
glossary.praesaga: praesagus, -a, -um — foreboding, prophetic, with a presentiment of (with gen.) (nom. sg. f.; the abl. sg. f. and nom./acc. pl. n. are identical)
glossary.praestatque: praesto, -stare, -stiti, -stitus — provide, guarantee, make good (3rd sg. pres. act.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.precantum: precor, precari (deponent) — pray, entreat (pres. part., gen. pl.; poetic -um for -ium) — “of those praying”
glossary.premitur: premo, -ere, pressi, pressus — press, weigh down, oppress (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
glossary.priamus: Priamus, -i m. — Priam, king of Troy, son of Laomedon, father of Hector, Paris and Aesacus (nom. sg.)
glossary.priamusque: Priamus, -i m. — Priam, king of Troy, son of Laomedon, father of Hector, Paris and Aesacus (nom. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.primas: primus, -a, -um — first, foremost, nearest (acc. pl. f.); not the noun primas, -atis “chief man”
glossary.procellae: procella, -ae f. — violent wind, squall, storm-blast (nom. pl. here; gen./dat. sg. are identical)
glossary.prodigiis: prodigium, -i n. — portent, omen, prodigy (abl. pl.)
glossary.profuso: profundo, -ere, -fudi, -fusus — pour forth, shed (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. m./n.)
glossary.prohibet: prohibeo, -ere, -ui, -itus — hold back, prevent, forbid (3rd sg. pres. act.)
glossary.promittere: promitto, -ere, -misi, -missus — promise, hold out a promise of (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.propius: propius — nearer, closer (comparative adverb of prope; the form is also the neut. nom./acc. sg. of the adj. propior, and with a neuter subject either reading is open)
glossary.propositos: propono, -ere, -posui, -positus — set forth, plan, resolve on (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m.) — of a course “decided on”
glossary.protentaque: protendo, -ere, -tendi, -tentus — stretch out, hold out before one (perf. pass. part., acc./nom. pl. n.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.providus: providus, -a, -um — foreseeing, prescient, prophetic (with gen. of what is foreseen) (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.pugnabo: pugno, -are — fight, do battle, struggle (1st sg. fut. act.)
glossary.pugnem: pugno, -are — fight, struggle (1st sg. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.pulsarunt: pulso, -are — beat, batter, pound (3rd pl. perf. act.; syncopated for pulsaverunt)
glossary.pulsata: pulso, -are — beat, batter, pound (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f. / nom.-acc. pl. n.)
glossary.quaerente: quaero, -ere, quaesivi, quaesitus — seek, look for, try to get (pres. act. part., abl. sg.), commonly in an ablative absolute
glossary.qualemve: qualis, -e — of what sort, such as, of the kind that (acc. sg. m./f.) + enclitic -ve “or”
glossary.quoniamque: quoniam — since, seeing that, because (conjunction, with enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.rapis: rapio, -ere, rapui, raptus — seize, snatch, carry off; with a reflexive object, hurry oneself away (2nd sg. pres. act.)
glossary.raptusque: rapio, -ere, rapui, raptus — seize, carry off, abduct (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m.) + enclitic -que “and”; the same form can be the noun raptus, -us m. “a carrying off”
glossary.rarus: rarus, -a, -um — sparse, thinly scattered, infrequent (nom. sg. m.); predicative with a verb it is best read adverbially, “only rarely”
glossary.ratem: ratis, -is f. — raft, boat, ship (acc. sg.)
glossary.receperunt: recipio, -ere, -cepi, -ceptus — take back, take in, receive (3rd pl. perf. act.)
glossary.redditque: reddo, -ere, reddidi, redditus — give back, return, render (3rd sg. pres. act.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.redis: redeo, redire, redii, reditus — go back, come back, return (2nd sg. pres. act.)
glossary.reditusque: reditus, -us m. — return, homecoming (4th decl., acc. pl. here; nom. sg. and gen. sg. are identical) + enclitic -que “and”; the same form is also the perf. part. of redeo
glossary.reducunt: reduco, -ere, -duxi, -ductus — lead back, draw back, pull back (3rd pl. pres. act.)
glossary.refertque: refero, referre, rettuli, relatus — bring back, report, recall, speak of (3rd sg. pres. act.) + enclitic -que “and”; distinct from the impersonal refert “it matters”, which is a different verb entirely
glossary.refundit: refundo, -ere, -fudi, -fusus — pour back, pour out again (3rd sg. pres. act.)
glossary.regibus: rex, regis m. — king, ruler (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.relabens: relabor, relabi, relapsus (deponent) — glide back, slip back, sink back (pres. part., nom. sg.)
glossary.remeat: remeo, -are — go back, return, travel back (3rd sg. pres. act.)
glossary.remittant: remitto, -ere, -misi, -missus — send back, let go back, release (3rd pl. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.remotus: removeo, -ere, -movi, -motus — remove, withdraw (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m.), used adjectivally “withdrawn, far off (from)”
glossary.renovat: renovo, -are — renew, revive, start afresh (3rd sg. pres. act.)
glossary.reparasque: reparo, -are — restore, renew, repair (2nd sg. pres. act.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.resolutis: resolvo, -ere, -solvi, -solutus — loosen, unbind, dissolve, melt (perf. pass. part., dat./abl. pl.), often in an ablative absolute
glossary.respice: respicio, -ere, -spexi, -spectus — look back at, look round at, regard (2nd sg. pres. act. imperative)
glossary.reversurum: revertor, reverti (semi-deponent) — turn back, return (fut. act. part. reversurus, acc. sg. m.), standard in indirect statement with esse understood
glossary.revulsos: revello, -ere, -velli, -vulsus — tear away, wrench out, uproot (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m.)
glossary.rexque: rex, regis m. — king, ruler (nom. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.rigavit: rigo, -are — wet, moisten, water (3rd sg. perf. act.)
glossary.rogari: rogo, -are — ask, entreat, petition (pres. pass. inf.) — “to be entreated”
glossary.rudentes: rudens, -entis m. — rope, ship's cable, rigging (nom./acc. pl.); the same form can be the pres. part. of rudo “bellow, creak”, but as a plural noun beside sails and yards it is the rigging
glossary.rumoribus: rumor, -oris m. — rumour, hearsay, common talk (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.rumorum: rumor, -oris m. — rumour, hearsay, common talk (gen. pl.)
glossary.rumpunt: rumpo, -ere, rupi, ruptus — break, burst, shatter (3rd pl. pres. act.)
glossary.s: not a Latin word — an editorial abbreviation from Magnus's apparatus (for sive, “or”) marking an alternative reading, which has slipped into the running text of the archived edition; there is nothing for the reader to parse here
glossary.sagacior: sagax, sagacis — keen-scented, keen of sense, shrewd (comparative, nom. sg. m./f.)
glossary.saxumque: saxum, -i n. — rock, stone, boulder (nom./acc. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.sceleratior: sceleratus, -a, -um — wicked, criminal, guilt-stained (comparative, nom. sg. m./f.)
glossary.scindit: scindo, -ere, scidi, scissus — tear, rend, split, cleave (3rd sg. pres. act.)
glossary.secabatur: seco, -are, secui, sectus — cut, cleave, cut through (3rd sg. impf. pass.)
glossary.secretos: secretus, -a, -um — set apart, remote, secluded (acc. pl. m.); originally the perf. part. of secerno “separate”
glossary.secutis: sequor, sequi, secutus (deponent) — follow, come after (perf. part. with active sense, dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.seditioque: seditio, -onis f. — sedition, mutiny, civil discord (nom. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”; capitalised where it stands as a personification
glossary.segnius: segnius — comparative adverb of segniter (from segnis, -e “slow, sluggish”): less sluggishly, more slowly; in a negated comparison it amounts to “no less keenly”
glossary.sensisset: sentio, -ire, sensi, sensus — perceive, feel, experience (3rd sg. pluperf. act. subj.)
glossary.sequerere: sequor, sequi, secutus (deponent) — follow, pursue (2nd sg. impf. subj.; the older ending -re for -reris)
glossary.servatos: servo, -are — keep, preserve, maintain (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m.)
glossary.siccantem: sicco, -are — dry, dry off (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m./f.)
glossary.sidereus: sidereus, -a, -um — of the stars, starry, radiant (nom. sg. m.); of Ceyx it also points to his descent from Lucifer, the Morning Star
glossary.signans: signo, -are — mark, mark out, trace (pres. act. part., nom. sg.)
glossary.simulatoremque: simulator, -oris m. — imitator, counterfeiter, one who feigns a likeness (acc. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.singultuque: singultus, -us m. — sob, sobbing, gasp (4th decl., abl. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.sinuataque: sinuo, -are — bend, curve, arch into a fold (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f. / nom.-acc. pl. n.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.solantia: solor, solari, solatus (deponent) — comfort, console, soothe (pres. part. with active sense, nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.sollertius: sollertius — comparative adverb of sollerter (from sollers, -ertis “skilful, adroit”): more skilfully, more cleverly; the form is also the neut. comparative adjective
glossary.sollicitive: sollicitus, -a, -um — anxious, restless, on the alert (nom. pl. m.) + enclitic -ve “or”
glossary.somne: Somnus, -i m. — Sleep, the god of sleep (voc. sg.); as a common noun, sleep
glossary.somnum: somnus, -i m. — sleep, slumber (acc. sg.); not somnium, -i n. “a dream”, which is a separate word
glossary.sonantibus: sono, -are, sonui — sound, resound, roar, hiss (pres. act. part., dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.soporiferam: soporifer, -fera, -ferum — sleep-bringing, drowsy, soporific (acc. sg. f.)
glossary.soporis: sopor, -oris m. — deep sleep, drowsiness, stupor (gen. sg.)
glossary.sortitus: sortior, sortiri, sortitus (deponent) — obtain by lot, receive as one's allotted portion (perf. part. with active sense, nom. sg. m.); the same form can be the noun sortitus, -us m. “a drawing of lots”
glossary.spatiosum: spatiosus, -a, -um — roomy, wide, long-drawn-out, elongated (acc. sg. m. / nom.-acc. sg. n.)
glossary.specieque: species, -ei f. — appearance, look, outward form (5th decl., abl. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.spectarat: specto, -are — watch, gaze at, look on (3rd sg. pluperf. act.; syncopated for spectaverat)
glossary.spelunca: spelunca, -ae f. — cave, cavern, grotto (nom. sg.; the abl. sg. is identical)
glossary.spirare: spiro, -are — breathe, blow (of winds) (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.spoliataque: spolio, -are — strip, rob, despoil (of something, with abl.) (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f. / nom.-acc. pl. n.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.spoliisque: spolium, -i n. — spoils, plunder, what is stripped from the beaten (dat./abl. pl.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.stantemque: sto, stare, steti, status — stand, stand firm (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m./f.) + enclitic -que “and”
glossary.stratoque: stratum, -i n. — bedding, coverlet, bed (abl./dat. sg.) + enclitic -que “and”; the form is also the perf. part. of sterno “spread out”, from which the noun comes
glossary.stridores: stridor, -oris m. — creaking, grating, harsh shrill sound (nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.stringebat: stringo, -ere, strinxi, strictus — draw tight, graze, skim (3rd sg. impf. act.)
glossary.strinxit: stringo, -ere, strinxi, strictus — graze, nick, just touch (3rd sg. perf. act.)
glossary.subederat: subedo, -esse, -edi, -esus — eat away from beneath, undermine (3rd sg. pluperf. act.)

glossary.virtusque: virtūs, -ūtis f. — valour, prowess, manly excellence (nom. sg.); -que “and”
glossary.vivente: vīvō — living, alive (pres. act. part., m. abl. sg.; 'me vivente', while I am alive, in abl. absolute)
glossary.vixi: vīvō — I have lived (1 sg. perf.)
glossary.volebat: volō, velle — wished, wanted (3 sg. imperf.)
glossary.vomens: vomō — spewing out, vomiting (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.votivi: vōtīvus — votive, offered in fulfilment of a vow (m. gen. sg., with 'cervi')
