glossary.voveas: voveō — you may vow, you would pray for (2 sg. pres. subj., in an indirect question)
glossary.abnuit: abnuō, abnuere, abnuī — refused, shook his head in denial (3 sg. perf. indic. act. here, standing beside the perfect vīdit; the form is also 3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.abstitimus: absistō, absistere, abstitī — we left off, we stood away from (1 pl. perf. indic. act.; taking the inf. exercēre, “we ceased from plying”)
glossary.accubuit: accumbō, accumbere, accubuī, accubitum — lay down, sank down in death (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; some editions print occubuit, the commoner verb for meeting death; not accubō, accubāre “recline at table”, whose perfect is the same)
glossary.achilli: Achillēs, Achillis m. — Achilles, the dead owner of the disputed arms (m. dat. sg. after succēdit “succeeds to”; the Greek-type dative beside Achillī/Achilleī)
glossary.achivis: Achīvus, -a, -um; as noun Achīvī, -ōrum m. — the Achaeans, the Greeks (m. dat. pl., of separation with subdūxit “drew strength away from the Achaeans”; the form is also abl. pl.)
glossary.achivos: Achīvus, -a, -um; as noun Achīvī, -ōrum m. — the Achaeans, the Greeks (m. acc. pl., after per, the rank-and-file Paris shoots at)
glossary.adfixi: adfīgō (affīgō), adfīgere, adfīxī, adfīxum — fastened on, pinned (perf. pass. part., n. gen. sg. with corporis — the body hanging fixed on the arrow; adf- is the edition's unassimilated spelling for aff-; not the 1 sg. perf. act. adfīxī “I fastened”)
glossary.adparet: adpāreō (appāreō), adpārēre, adpāruī — shows, is still visible (3 sg. pres. indic. act., of the scar Nestor is pointing at; adp- is the edition's unassimilated spelling for app-)
glossary.aemulus: aemulus, -ī m. — a rival, a competitor (m. nom. sg., subject of dēmit; also the adj. aemulus, -a, -um “rivalling”)
glossary.aequoreas: aequoreus, -a, -um — of the sea, sea- (f. acc. pl. with undās)
glossary.aggere: agger, aggeris m. — heaped mound, pile (m. abl. sg. with ex; here the heap of trees piled over Caeneus, and the word is also used of a burial mound)
glossary.agimus: agō, agere, ēgī, āctum — we plead, we are pleading (1 pl. pres. indic. act.; causam agere is the courtroom idiom “to plead a case”, and the object causam follows in the next line)
glossary.agnoscit: agnōscō, agnōscere, agnōvī, agnitum — acknowledges, owns as his own (3 sg. pres. indic. act., subject Iuppiter)
glossary.aiaci: Aiāx, Aiācis m. — Ajax, son of Telamon, the speaker of this whole plea (m. dat. sg.; dat. of reference at XIII.17, dat. of purpose at 97, where Aiācī and Aiāx trade places with arma and armīs; the Telamonian, not the lesser Ajax son of Oileus)
glossary.aiax: Aiāx, Aiācis m. — Ajax (m. nom. sg.; at XIII.2 and 28 the Telamonian, the speaker; but Oīleos Aiāx at XII.622 is the other, lesser Ajax, son of Oileus, named there by a Greek genitive)
glossary.ala: āla, -ae f. — wing (f. nom. sg., subject of iungitur; the form is also abl. sg.)
glossary.alae: āla, -ae f. — wing (f. dat. sg. with haeserat, “had stuck fast to the wing”, the poetic dative with haereō; some read it as gen. sg. after quā, “at the point of the wing where”. The form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.alcidae: Alcīdēs, Alcīdae m. — Alcides, that is Hercules, named from his grandfather Alceus (m. gen. sg. with praeteritī, the pair depending on dolōrem: grief at Hercules passed over in the telling; the form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.alesi: Halēsus (Alēsus), -ī m. — Halesus the Emathian, killed earlier by Latreus, whose spoils Latreus now wears (m. gen. sg. with spoliīs; the edition prints the name without the H)
glossary.aliturque: alō, alere, aluī, altum — is fed, is nourished (3 sg. pres. indic. pass., of Philoctetes fed by the birds he shoots; + -que “and”, the second half of the doubled vēlāturque aliturque “both clothed and fed”; not a form of āles “winged, bird”)
glossary.amando: amō, amāre, amāvī, amātum — loving (gerund, abl. sg., one of three parallel ablatives of means, “by loving”; the form is also dat.)
glossary.ampyca: Ampyx, Ampycis m. — Ampyx, the Lapith who drives a pointless cornel shaft into Echeclus' face (Greek acc. sg. for Latin Ampycem; a fighter here — whether or not the same Ampyx who fathered the seer Mopsus at 456 is left open)
glossary.ampyciden: Ampycidēs, Ampycidae m. — son of Ampyx, that is the seer Mopsus, named at once in apposition (Greek patronymic acc. sg. in -en for Latin Ampycidēn/-am)
glossary.animosus: animōsus, -a, -um — high-spirited, full of bravado (m. nom. sg. agreeing with the subject Latreus, doing the work of an adverb with fūdit)
glossary.antimachumque: Antimachus, -ī m. — Antimachus, one of the five centaurs Caeneus had killed (m. acc. sg.; + -que “and”, one link in the epic chain of names; not the Greek poet or the Trojan of the Iliad)
glossary.arboreo: arboreus, -a, -um — of trees, made of timber (n. abl. sg. with pondere, from which it is held apart across the line-end)
glossary.argolicosque: Argolicus, -a, -um — Argive, Greek (m. acc. pl. with ducēs, the accusative subject of considere after iussit; + -que “and”)
glossary.armarat: armō, armāre, armāvī, armātum — had armed, had equipped with armour (3 sg. plup. indic. act., syncopated for armāverat; the subject deus idem is the fire-god who made the armour and now burns the body)
glossary.armatus: armō, armāre, armāvī, armātum — armed, equipped (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg. of Latreus, taking the abl. of means spoliīs “armed with the spoils”)
glossary.arserat: ārdeō, ārdēre, ārsī — had burned, had gone up in flame (3 sg. plup. indic. act.; intransitive, of Achilles burned on the pyre, and the one verb holding four appositions before it)
glossary.artificum: artifex, artificis m. — craftsmen, sculptors (m. gen. pl. with signīs, “the praised statues of craftsmen”)
glossary.atrides: Atrīdēs, Atrīdae m. — son of Atreus (m. nom. sg.; minor Atrīdēs here is Menelaus, the younger brother, set against Agamemnon, the bellō maior et aevō of the next line)
glossary.auresque: auris, auris f. — ears (f. acc. pl., governed by the per carried over from the earlier limbs; + -que “and”; not a form of aura “breeze”)
glossary.avibus: avis, avis f. — birds (f. abl. pl., of the agent or means with vēlātur and alitur, “clothed and fed by birds”; the form is also dat. pl.)
glossary.barbae: barba, -ae f. — beard (f. gen. sg. with color, “the colour of the beard”; the form is also dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.bifurcum: bifurcus, -a, -um — two-pronged, forked (m. acc. sg. with rāmum)
glossary.bipenni: bipennis, bipennis f. — double axe (f. abl. sg. of means with Thermodontiacā, the Amazons' axe; the word is also the adj. bipennis “two-edged”, from which the noun comes)
glossary.bromumque: Bromus, -ī m. — Bromus, one of the five centaurs Caeneus had killed (m. acc. sg.; + -que “and”; not Bromius, the cult-name of Bacchus)
glossary.cadendum: cadō, cadere, cecidī, cāsum — falling, having to fall (gerundive, n. nom. sg., impersonal with fuerat and the dat. tibi: “you had to fall”)
glossary.caecumque: caecus, -a, -um — blind, unseeing (m. acc. sg. with ēnsem, + -que “and”; active in force here — the blade goes in blind, out of sight inside the body, not “invisible”)
glossary.caeneu: Caeneus, Caeneī m. — Caeneus, the Lapith who had been the girl Caenis and was made invulnerable and male (m. voc. sg., the Greek vocative in -eu, held to the very end of Mopsus' greeting to the bird; the man's name, deliberately, and not the woman's)
glossary.caeni: Caenis, Caenidis f. — Caenis, the girl Caeneus had been (f. voc. sg., the Greek vocative; Latreus opens his taunt by refusing the man's name, so this is not a form of Caeneus)
glossary.caesosque: caedō, caedere, cecīdī, caesum — slaughtered, cut down (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl. with frātrēs, + -que “and”; Apollo is speaking to Paris, so the brothers are Paris' own, killed by Achilles)
glossary.calathis: calathus, -ī m. — wool-baskets (m. abl. pl. with cum; with the distaff and the spun thread, the standing Roman signs of a woman's work)
glossary.calcataque: calcō, calcāre, calcāvī, calcātum — trodden on, trampled (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. agreeing with the entrails understood, object of rūpit; + -que “and”, one link in the chain tracta ... calcāta)
glossary.calcavit: calcō, calcāre, calcāvī, calcātum — trod on, trampled (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.callo: callum, -ī n. — hardened skin, callus (n. abl. sg. in the abl. abs. percussō callō, the toughened hide on which the blade breaks; not callis “track, path” and not a form of calleō)
glossary.candentia: candeō, candēre, canduī — gleaming, shining white (pres. act. part. used as an adjective, n. acc. pl. with līlia)
glossary.capienda: capiō, capere, cēpī, captum — to be taken, that had to be taken (gerundive, n. acc. pl. with Pergama after ad: “to Pergama for the taking”)
glossary.capuloque: capulus, -ī m. — hilt, sword-handle (m. abl. sg. with the postposed tenus, “as far as the hilt”; + -que “and”)
glossary.careat: careō, carēre, caruī — let it be free of, let it lack (3 sg. pres. subj. act., jussive, with the abl. invidiā; one of the four jussives that carry the close of the speech)
glossary.castore: Castor, Castoris m. — Castor, the horseman of the twin Dioscuri (m. abl. sg. after dignus; the compliment is that such a body would be worthy to carry the best of riders — Castor the tamer of horses, not Pollux the boxer)
glossary.casuras: cadō, cadere, cecidī, cāsum — about to fall, on the point of falling (fut. act. part., f. acc. pl. with arcēs)
glossary.cecinisse: canō, canere, cecinī, cantum — to have sung, to have prophesied (perf. act. inf. in indirect statement after crēdiderīs; canō is the verb of prophecy as much as of song)
glossary.celsa: celsus, -a, -um — high, raised, standing proud (n. nom. pl. with pectora, predicate with sunt; the form is also f. nom. sg. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.centauros: Centaurus, -ī m. — the Centaurs, the half-human horse-men (m. acc. pl. after inter)
glossary.cerebrum: cerebrum, -ī n. — brain (n. nom. sg., subject of fluit; the form is also acc. sg.)
glossary.cernimus: cernō, cernere, crēvī, crētum — we see, we can see (1 pl. pres. indic. act.; Nestor breaking off to point at Ida, in sight from where he speaks)
glossary.certaque: certus, -a, -um — unerring, sure of their mark (n. acc. pl. with spīcula, + -que “and”; not a form of certō, certāre “contend”)
glossary.certasse: certō, certāre, certāvī, certātum — to have contended, to have fought it out (perf. act. inf., syncopated for certāvisse, a normal verse contraction)
glossary.certumque: certus, -a, -um — fixed, measured (m. acc. sg. with orbem in the phrase certum in orbem “in a measured circle”; + -que “and”)
glossary.chthonius: Chthonius, -ī m. — Chthonius, a centaur killed by Nestor (m. nom. sg., subject of iacent along with Teleboas)
glossary.cicatrix: cicātrīx, cicātrīcis f. — scar (f. nom. sg., subject of adpāret)
glossary.civiliter: cīvīliter — in citizen fashion, as one citizen to another (adv.; with plūs quam — Neptune's anger runs beyond what a fellow-citizen would feel)
glossary.clam: clam — secretly, in stealth (adv. with rem gerit, “does his business in secret”; not the preposition clam “without the knowledge of”)
glossary.clangore: clangor, clangōris m. — clang, harsh clamour (m. abl. sg. of manner, the noise of the bird's cry and wings)
glossary.classemque: classis, classis f. — fleet (f. acc. sg., second object of respexit; + -que “and”)
glossary.classes: classis, classis f. — fleets, the ships (f. acc. pl. after in, “against the Danaan fleet”; the form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.clipeumque: clipeus, -ī m. — shield (m. acc. sg. after post, “behind the shield”; + -que “and”, joining the clauses rather than the nouns)
glossary.clipeus: clipeus, -ī m. — shield (m. nom. sg.; at XII.621 Achilles' shield, subject of movet; at XIII.110 the same shield with the world worked on it; at XIII.118 Ulysses' own undamaged shield, its noun held back a line from iste tuus)
glossary.codice: cōdex (caudex), cōdicis m. — tree-trunk, block of timber (m. abl. sg. in the abl. abs. cōdice missō; the word's later sense “book” has no place here)
glossary.cogis: cōgō, cōgere, coēgī, coāctum — you force, you compel (2 sg. pres. indic. act., governing three infinitives in turn)
glossary.colcha: Colchus, -a, -um — Colchian, of Colchis (n. acc. pl. with lītora, the far shore the Argo reached)
glossary.columque: colus, colūs f. — distaff (acc. sg. colum, object of cape; + -que “and”. Fourth declension, though second-declension forms are also found)
glossary.comitavit: comitō, comitāre, comitāvī — accompanied, went with (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; the active form of a verb normally deponent, comitor, comitārī — both are found and the active suits the verse)
glossary.commissus: committō, committere, commīsī, commissum — joined, fastened together (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg. with vir, forming the plup. pass. commissus erat “had been joined”, of the seam where the man's half meets the horse's)
glossary.commonuit: commoneō, commonēre, commonuī, commonitum — reminded, put in mind (3 sg. perf. indic. act., sharing its one nec with the present subit)
glossary.concedant: concēdō, concēdere, concessī, concessum — yield to, fall short of (3 pl. pres. subj. act. in an indirect question after quantum; concēdō with the dative nostrō ferrō is “to be inferior to”)
glossary.concedimus: concēdō, concēdere, concessī, concessum — we grant, we allow (1 pl. pres. indic. act., with sī modo “provided only that”)
glossary.concipientibus: concipiō, concipere, concēpī, conceptum — catching, taking and holding (pres. act. part., f. abl. pl. with pennīs in an abl. abs., negated by nōn)
glossary.concretum: concrēscō, concrēscere, concrēvī, concrētum — curdled, thickened (perf. part., n. nom. sg. with lac, subject of solet; concrēscō is intransitive, so the participle is “having curdled”, not “having been curdled”)
glossary.concretus: concrēscō, concrēscere, concrēvī, concrētum — formed solid, wrought (perf. part., m. nom. sg. with clipeus, taking the abl. imāgine — the shield made up with the image of the world on it. Same verb as the curdled milk at XII.436, in a very different application)
glossary.concurreret: concurrō, concurrere, concurrī, concursum — might close with, might engage in combat (3 sg. imperf. subj. act. in a relative clause of characteristic after poscentem, “someone with whom he might engage”)
glossary.conexis: cōnectō, cōnectere, cōnexuī, cōnexum — tied together, joined to one another (perf. pass. part., m. abl. pl. with nōdīs, and taking inter sē)
glossary.conferat: cōnferō, cōnferre, contulī, conlātum — let him set beside, let him match (3 sg. pres. subj. act., jussive; cōnferō takes the dat. hīs, “compare with these”)
glossary.confertur: cōnferō, cōnferre, contulī, conlātum — is set beside, is compared (3 sg. pres. indic. pass.)
glossary.coniecta: coniciō, conicere, coniēcī, coniectum — thrown, hurled (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. with vēnābula in the acc. and inf. after meminī; the form is also f. nom. sg. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.conlato: cōnferō, cōnferre, contulī, conlātum — brought together, joined (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg. with Marte in the abl. abs. conlātō Marte “with battle joined”, i.e. at close quarters, set against ēminus; conl- is the edition's unassimilated spelling for coll-)
glossary.conpellat: compellō (conpellō), compellāre, compellāvī, compellātum — accosts, addresses (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; the first-conjugation verb of speaking to someone — not compellō, compellere “drive together, force”, which would give compellit)
glossary.conpleat: compleō (conpleō), complēre, complēvī, complētum — would fill, fills out (3 sg. pres. subj. act. in a relative clause of characteristic, at XII.616 of the urn the ashes would not fill and at 617 of the world his glory does; conp- is the edition's unassimilated spelling for comp-)
glossary.conplexa: complector (conplector), complectī, complexus sum — having embraced (perf. part. of a deponent, active in sense, f. nom. sg. of Hylonome, forming the perf. conplexa est “she embraced”; conp- is the edition's unassimilated spelling for comp-)
glossary.consedere: cōnsīdō, cōnsīdere, cōnsēdī, cōnsessum — sat down, took their seats (3 pl. perf. indic. act. in the poetic -ēre for -ērunt; cōnsīdō is the ordinary word for a council or a court taking its seat)
glossary.conspicuus: cōnspicuus, -a, -um — conspicuous, striking to look at (m. nom. sg. of Latreus, taking the ablatives clipeō, gladiō and sarīsā)
glossary.contende: contendō, contendere, contendī, contentum — contend, fight it out (2 sg. pres. imper. act.; the verb covers a contest at law and a fight in the field alike, and Ajax turns the courtroom sense of line 9 into a challenge to combat here)
glossary.conveniet: conveniō, convenīre, convēnī, conventum — will suit, will be a fit for (3 sg. fut. indic. act. with the dat. sinistrae; not a perfect)
glossary.convicti: convincō, convincere, convīcī, convictum — proved against him, exposed (perf. pass. part., m. gen. sg. with furōris after memor, and qualified by male; not a form of convīcium “abuse” or convīvium “feast”. The form is also m. nom. pl.)
glossary.creato: creō, creāre, creāvī, creātum — begotten, born of (perf. pass. part., m. dat. sg., with Telamōne as abl. of origin; as the edition prints XII.624 it does not agree in number with the dat. pl. sōlīs, and some editions print creātīs. The form is also abl. sg.)
glossary.credideris: crēdō, crēdere, crēdidī, crēditum — believe, suppose (2 sg. perf. subj. act. in the ordinary prohibition nec crēdiderīs “do not believe”; the form is also 2 sg. fut. perf. indic.)
glossary.credita: crēdō, crēdere, crēdidī, crēditum — believed (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. with rēs, forming the perf. pass. crēdita est)
glossary.cremabat: cremō, cremāre, cremāvī, cremātum — was burning, was consuming (3 sg. imperf. indic. act., subject the same fire-god who had armed him; some editions print cremārat, a pluperfect, which loses the contrast of tenses)
glossary.cribri: crībrum, -ī n. — sieve (n. gen. sg. with pondere, “beneath the weight of the loose-woven sieve”)
glossary.cruentatus: cruentō, cruentāre, cruentāvī, cruentātum — unbloodied, unstained by blood (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg. with Caeneus; the printed word is the tail of incruentātus “unbloodied”, split open by tmesis as inque cruentātus with the -que planted inside, so the sense is the negative one — plain cruentātus alone would mean “bloodied”)
glossary.cruentior: cruentus, -a, -um — bloodier, more given to blood (comparative, m. nom. sg. of Achilles, with bellō ipsō as abl. of comparison)
glossary.curvis: curvus, -a, -um — curved, hooked (m. abl. pl. with pedibus, the eagle's talons)
glossary.cyllare: Cyllarus, -ī m. — Cyllarus, the young centaur loved by Hylonome (m. voc. sg.; Nestor breaks off from narrative to address him directly, at XII.393 and again at the moment of the wound at 421)
glossary.cyllaron: Cyllarus, -ī m. — Cyllarus, the young centaur loved by Hylonome (Greek acc. sg. in -on for Latin Cyllarum, object of tenet)
glossary.cymeli: Cymelus, -ī m. — Cymelus, the fighter whose groin the hunting-spears are buried in (m. gen. sg. with inguine; on the Lapith side, since the spears are thrown by the hands of the centaur Nessus)
glossary.danaam: Danaus, -a, -um — Danaan, Greek (f. acc. sg. with rem, “the Danaan cause, the Greek state”, inside the acc. and inf. after fīnxit)
glossary.danaas: Danaus, -a, -um — Danaan, Greek (f. acc. pl. with classēs after in)
glossary.debilitaturum: dēbilitō, dēbilitāre, dēbilitāvī, dēbilitātum — about to cripple, that will weaken (fut. act. part., n. acc. sg. with mūnus and governing tē; Latin uses the future participle where English needs a relative clause)
glossary.deceant: decet, decēre, decuit — suit, become, be fitting for (3 pl. pres. subj. act. in a relative clause of characteristic, “such as would suit her”, with quae — the fleeces — as subject; the verb is usually impersonal but takes a personal subject here)
glossary.decentior: decēns, decentis — more graceful, more comely (comparative, f. nom. sg. with nūlla ... fēmina, and quā as abl. of comparison; from decēns, the participle of decet used as an adjective)
glossary.defendentia: dēfendō, dēfendere, dēfendī, dēfēnsum — defending (pres. act. part., n. acc. pl. with mīlia and governing mūrōs; the thousands are defending and cut down at once)
glossary.deiectam: dēiciō, dēicere, dēiēcī, dēiectum — brought down, felled (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg. with trabem, taking the abl. of means vīribus austrī)
glossary.deiphobum: Dēiphobus, -ī m. — Deiphobus, son of Priam, a leading Trojan (m. acc. sg., with the ordinary Latin ending beside the Greek accusatives Polydamanta and Hectora alongside it)
glossary.demisi: dēmittō, dēmittere, dēmīsī, dēmissum — I sent down, I drove down (1 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.dependebat: dēpendeō, dēpendēre — hung down (3 sg. imperf. indic. act., subject coma; not dēpendō, dēpendere “pay out, weigh out”)
glossary.desertum: dēserō, dēserere, dēseruī, dēsertum — abandoned, deserted (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg. with Nestora in the acc. and inf. after rear: “that Nestor abandoned is no crime”. Not the noun dēsertum “wilderness”)
glossary.deteriorque: dēterior, dēterius — worse, inferior (comparative with no positive in use, f. nom. sg. with faciēs and taking virō as abl. of comparison; + -que “and”)
glossary.detrectavitque: dētrectō, dētrectāre, dētrectāvī, dētrectātum — shirked, declined, refused to take up (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; + -que “and”)
glossary.detrusum: dētrūdō, dētrūdere, dētrūsī, dētrūsum — thrust down, forced down (perf. pass. part., n. acc. sg. with corpus in the acc. and inf. after ferēbant, with esse left out)
glossary.diomede: Diomēdēs, Diomēdis m. — Diomedes, son of Tydeus, the Greek fighter Ulysses' exploits depend on (m. abl. sg. in the abl. abs. Diomēde remōtō; not the Thracian Diomedes of the Hercules story)
glossary.diomedis: Diomēdēs, Diomēdis m. — Diomedes, son of Tydeus, Ulysses' partner on the night raid (m. gen. sg. with pars, “Diomedes' share”)
glossary.diruit: dīruō, dīruere, dīruī, dīrutum — razed, levelled (3 sg. perf. indic. act. here, one of three perfects sharing Hercules as subject; the form is also 3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.dividite: dīvidō, dīvidere, dīvīsī, dīvīsum — divide them, share them out (2 pl. pres. imper. act., addressed to the assembled Greeks)
glossary.doles: doleō, dolēre, doluī — do you grieve for, do you feel the loss of (2 sg. pres. indic. act., taking a plain accusative object here where English needs a preposition)
glossary.dolona: Dolōn, Dolōnis m. — Dolon, the Trojan scout caught and killed by Ulysses and Diomedes on the night raid (Greek acc. sg. in -a for Latin Dolōnem)
glossary.donaverit: dōnō, dōnāre, dōnāvī, dōnātum — shall have granted, shall have made a present of (3 sg. fut. perf. indic. act. in the condition; the form is also 3 sg. perf. subj. act.)
glossary.dubitabilis: dubitābilis, -e — doubtful, open to question (f. nom. sg. with virtūs, in a present contrary-to-fact condition)
glossary.duces: dux, ducis m./f. — leader, chief (m. nom. pl. at XIII.1, subject of consēdēre; m. acc. pl. at XII.627 with Argolicōs, subject of the infinitive considere. Not dūcēs, 2 sg. fut. indic. of dūcō)
glossary.ducum: dux, ducis m./f. — chieftains, leaders (m. gen. pl., partitive with pars ūna, “one of our chieftains”)
glossary.dulci: dulcis, -e — sweet (n. abl. sg. with ōre, an ablative of manner; the form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.dulichius: Dūlichius, -a, -um — Dulichian, of Dulichium, an island of Ulysses' realm, hence “Ulysses'” (m. nom. sg. with vertex; one of the by-names Ajax uses instead of the man's own, like Ithacus at 98)
glossary.echecli: Echeclus, -ī m. — Echeclus, the four-footed centaur into whose face Ampyx drove a pointless cornel shaft (m. gen. sg., with quadrupedantis agreeing, depending on vultū)
glossary.elateius: Elatēius, -a, -um — son of Elatus, Elatus-born (patronymic adjective, m. nom. sg. with Caeneus, whose father was the Lapith Elatus)
glossary.electarumque: ēligō, ēligere, ēlēgī, ēlēctum — chosen, picked out (perf. pass. part., f. gen. pl. with ferārum, depending on vellera; + -que “and”)
glossary.elidite: ēlīdō, ēlīdere, ēlīsī, ēlīsum — crush out, dash out (2 pl. pres. imper. act., with the abl. of means missīs silvīs)
glossary.elimque: Ēlis, Ēlidis f. — Elis, the Peloponnesian city Hercules destroyed (f. acc. sg. Elim, the Greek-type accusative in -im; + -que “and”, paired with Pylumque)
glossary.eloquio: ēloquium, -ī n. — eloquence, power of speech (n. abl. sg. of respect with vincat; the form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.elymumque: Elymus, -ī m. — Elymus, one of the five centaurs Caeneus had killed (m. acc. sg.; + -que “and”; not the Sicilian Elymus of Trojan legend)
glossary.emathii: Ēmathius, -a, -um — Emathian, that is Macedonian or Thessalian (m. gen. sg. with Alesī)
glossary.equitavit: equitō, equitāre, equitāvī — rode, wheeled on horseback (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; of a centaur the verb is grimly literal, since he is his own horse)
glossary.equumque: equus, -ī m. — horse, the horse-half (m. acc. sg., a Greek accusative of respect with prōtēctus, paired with hominemque; + -que “and”)
glossary.erigdupum: Erigdupus, -ī m. — Erigdupus, the centaur laid low by the Lapith Macareus with a bar through the chest (m. acc. sg.; the name is Greek, roughly “thunder-crash”)
glossary.eruit: ēruō, ēruere, ēruī, ērutum — tore open, ripped out (3 sg. perf. indic. act. here, with latus as object; the form is also 3 sg. pres. indic. act., and the historic presents around it leave either reading open)
glossary.evolvere: ēvolvō, ēvolvere, ēvolvī, ēvolūtum — to roll off, to heave away (pres. act. inf., the second of two after cōnātur; the form is also 3 pl. perf. indic. act., which the sentence here does not allow)
glossary.exemplumque: exemplum, -ī n. — precedent, an example for the rest to copy (n. nom. sg., predicate with fuit; + -que “and”. The form is also acc. sg.)
glossary.exercere: exerceō, exercēre, exercuī, exercitum — to ply, to work off, to keep busy at (pres. act. inf. after abstitimus)
glossary.exprimitur: exprimō, exprimere, expressī, expressum — is squeezed out, is pressed through (3 sg. pres. indic. pass.)
glossary.exprobravit: exprobrō, exprobrāre, exprobrāvī, exprobrātum — reproached him with, threw it in his face (3 sg. perf. indic. act., taking the acc. of the thing thrown up, fugam, and the dat. of the person, trepidō amīcō)
glossary.exspectatoque: exspectō, exspectāre, exspectāvī, exspectātum — awaited, long looked for (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg. with sonō, the sound the assembly had been waiting for; + -que “and”)
glossary.extentum: extendō, extendere, extendī, extentum — stretched out, drawn long (perf. pass. part., n. acc. sg. with latus — latus here is the neuter noun “flank”, not lātus “broad” — taking cursū as abl. of cause)
glossary.facundis: fācundus, -a, -um — eloquent, well-spoken (n. dat. pl. with dictīs after abest “is lacking to”; the form is also abl. pl. The narrator means the word in earnest, where Ajax used it sarcastically at 92)
glossary.facundus: fācundus, -a, -um — eloquent, glib (m. nom. sg. with Ulixēs; sarcastic in Ajax's mouth here, and meant straight by the narrator at 127)
glossary.fatiferum: fātifer, fātifera, fātiferum — death-bringing, fate-bearing (m. acc. sg. with ēnsem)
glossary.ferendum: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to be borne, endurable (gerundive, n. nom. sg. in ferendum est, with the acc. and inf. aliōs vincī potuisse as its subject)
glossary.ferentem: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — carrying, holding up (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg. with hunc, the object of ferit, and governing sublīmia membra)
glossary.feretur: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — will be said, will be reported (3 sg. fut. indic. pass., in the sense “is spoken of”; the subject is the man, with the perf. inf. certāsse)
glossary.feriat: feriō, ferīre — should strike, were to strike (3 sg. pres. subj. act., potential, in sīquis ... feriat “if anyone should strike”)
glossary.feroci: ferōx, ferōcis — fierce, savage (m. abl. sg. with Marte, Mars standing for the fighting he presides over)
glossary.feruntque: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — and they drive home, they bring to bear (3 pl. pres. indic. act.; + -que “and”. Set against mittunt, which is the weapon thrown: these are the ones kept in the hand and pushed in)
glossary.fictis: fingō, fingere, fīnxī, fictum — made up, fabricated (perf. pass. part., n. abl. pl. with verbīs; Ajax's charge, not the poem's. Not a form of fīgō “fix, pierce”)
glossary.fictumque: fingō, fingere, fīnxī, fictum — invented, trumped up (perf. pass. part., n. acc. sg. with crīmen; + -que “and”, answering fīnxit in the same line)
glossary.fidum: fīdus, -a, -um — faithful, trusty (m. acc. sg. with Nestora, the standing epithet Ajax allows him)
glossary.fingi: fingō, fingere, fīnxī, fictum — to be invented, to be trumped up (pres. pass. inf. in indirect statement after scit, with mihi as dative of the agent)
glossary.fortissima: fortis, -e — strongest, bravest (superlative fortissimus, -a, -um; n. acc. pl. with animālia, object of iūnxit, and taking rērum as partitive genitive: “the strongest creatures of all”)
glossary.fortunam: fortūna, -ae f. — outcome, upshot, how a thing turned out (f. acc. sg. with pugnae, object of quaeritis in its courtroom sense “inquire into”)
glossary.fracta: frangō, frangere, frēgī, frāctum — shattered, broken open (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. with volūbilitās, with est understood; the form is also n. nom./acc. pl. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.fractaque: frangō, frangere, frēgī, frāctum — broken, shattered (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg., with lammina; + -que “and”)
glossary.fractus: frangō, frangere, frēgī, frāctum — broken, worn down (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., of Philoctetes, with the ablatives morbō and famē)
glossary.fraterna: frāternus, -a, -um — a brother's, belonging to a brother (n. acc. pl. used as a noun, “a brother's things”, object of petō; also f. nom./abl. sg. elsewhere). Ajax uses frāter loosely of a cousin
glossary.fudi: fundō, fundere, fūdī, fūsum — I laid low, brought down, routed (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; the 3rd-conjugation fundō “pour out, rout”, not fundō, fundāre “found, establish”)
glossary.fugavi: fugō, fugāre, fugāvī, fugātum — I put to flight, drove off, routed (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; the 1st-conjugation fugō “put to flight”, transitive — not fugiō “flee”)
glossary.fugienti: fugiō, fugere, fūgī — fleeing, escaping (pres. act. part., f. dat. sg., with animae after obsistere; also abl. sg.)
glossary.fuimus: sum, esse, fuī — we were (1 pl. perf. indic.; Nestor counting his brothers)
glossary.furore: furor, furōris (m.) — madness, frenzy (m. abl. sg., abl. of means with ficto, the feigned madness of Ulysses; the noun, not a form of the verb furō)
glossary.furtis: fūrtum, -ī (n.) — thefts, tricks done by stealth (n. abl. pl., abl. of means; also dat. pl.)
glossary.furtisque: fūrtum, -ī (n.) — thefts, stealth (n. abl. pl., abl. of respect with simillimus; also dat. pl.; + -que “and”)
glossary.genitorem: genitor, genitōris (m.) — father, begetter (m. acc. sg., after in; Tlepolemus' father, Hercules)
glossary.gestet: gestō, gestāre, gestāvī, gestātum — she carries, wears about (3 sg. pres. subj. act. in an ut-clause; frequentative of gerō)
glossary.gestum: gerō, gerere, gessī, gestum — done, carried out (perf. pass. part., n. nom. sg., with est, subject nihil; not the noun gestus, -ūs “gesture”)
glossary.gladioque: gladius, -ī (m.) — sword (m. abl. sg., one of the things Latreus is conspicuous with; also dat. sg.; + -que “and”)
glossary.gladium: gladius, -ī (m.) — sword (m. acc. sg., object of dēmīsī at 441 and of recondere at 482)
glossary.graiae: Grāius, -a, -um — Greek (f. gen. sg. with marītae, the Greek wife carried off, i.e. Helen; also dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.grando: grandō, grandinis (f.) — hail (f. nom. sg., subject of an understood resilit in the comparison)
glossary.gravisque: gravis, -e — heavy, weighty (f. nom. sg. with hasta, predicate after esse; also m. nom. sg. and m./f. acc. pl.; + -que “and”)
glossary.habitavit: habitō, habitāre, habitāvī, habitātum — dwelt, lived (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.hamatisque: hāmātus, -a, -um — hooked, barbed (m. abl. pl. with unguibus, abl. of means; + -que “and”)
glossary.hebes: hebes, hebetis — blunt, dull (adj., m. nom. sg.: of the sword-point mucrō at XII.485, of Ulysses' supposed dullness at XIII.135; the adjective, not a form of hebeō)
glossary.hectoreis: Hectoreus, -a, -um — Hector's, Hectorean (adjective formed from Hector; f. abl. pl. with flammīs, the fires Hector brought against the ships)
glossary.helenum: Helenus, -ī (m.) — Helenus, the seer son of Priam, taken prisoner by Ulysses (m. acc. sg., Latin ending, in apposition to Priamidēn)
glossary.herculeae: Herculeus, -a, -um — of Hercules, Herculean (adjective formed from the name; f. gen. sg. with laudis, separated far from its noun)
glossary.herculeis: Herculeus, -a, -um — of Hercules, Herculean (adjective formed from the name; f. abl. pl. with vīribus at the head of the next line, abl. of means — the strength that killed Nestor's brothers)
glossary.honos: honōs (= honor), honōris (m.) — honour, distinction (m. nom. sg., subject of quaeritur; honōs is the older nominative beside honor)
glossary.hylen: Hylēs, Hylae (m.) — Hyles, a centaur killed at long range in the brawl (Greek m. acc. sg.; the drafter's “Hyle” is the same combatant, not a place-name)
glossary.hylonome: Hylonomē, -ēs (f.) — Hylonome, the female centaur who loves and dies with Cyllarus (f. nom. sg., Greek 1st decl.)
glossary.iactasque: iaciō, iacere, iēcī, iactum — thrown, hurled down (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl., with silvās; from iaciō, not from the frequentative iactō, whose participle would be iactātās; + -que “and”)
glossary.iaculante: iaculor, iaculārī, iaculātus sum — hurling, throwing a javelin (pres. dep. part., m. abl. sg., in the abl. absolute Mopsō iaculante)
glossary.iamiam: iam iam — at this very moment, any moment now (adverb, the doubled iam of imminence, with the future participle cāsūrās)
glossary.icti: īcō (iciō), īcere, īcī, ictum — struck (perf. pass. part., n. gen. sg. with marmoris, “of struck marble”; also m. gen. sg. and m. nom. pl.)
glossary.iliacum: Īliacus, -a, -um — of Ilium, Trojan (adjective formed from Īlium; n. acc. sg. with agmen, after in)
glossary.imbellemque: imbellis, -e — unwarlike, no fighter (m. acc. sg. with Dolōna; Ajax's contemptuous word for the Trojan scout; + -que “and”)
glossary.imbellibus: imbellis, -e — unwarlike, unfit for war (m. dat. pl. with lacertīs, dative after esse; also abl. pl.)
glossary.imploraret: implōrō, implōrāre, implōrāvī, implōrātum — he was begging for help, calling on (3 sg. imperf. subj. act. in a circumstantial cum-clause; object Ulixem)
glossary.improbe: improbus, -a, -um — shameless, without restraint (m. voc. sg., Ajax addressing Ulysses; not the adverb improbē)
glossary.incautum: incautus, -a, -um — unwary, off guard (m. acc. sg. with hostem)
glossary.incipiens: incipiō, incipere, coepī, coeptum — beginning, just starting (pres. act. part., f. nom. sg. with barba, in the periphrasis erat incipiēns — the down of a young beard)
glossary.indulgens: indulgeō, indulgēre, indulsī — indulging, giving way to (pres. act. part., m. nom. sg., of Apollo; takes the dative animō)
glossary.inermis: inermis, -e — unarmed, without weapons (m. nom. sg., of Ulysses in the relative clause)
glossary.inertem: iners, inertis — inactive, spiritless, good for nothing (f. acc. sg. with animam, held back to the line's end; Ajax's verdict on the life he saved)
glossary.ingemis: ingemō, ingemere, ingemuī — you groan, you sigh over it (2 sg. pres. indic. act.; Neptune to Apollo)
glossary.inhaeserat: inhaereō, inhaerēre, inhaesī, inhaesum — had stuck fast, had lodged (3 sg. plup. indic. act.; takes the dative illī)
glossary.inhonorati: inhonōrātus, -a, -um — unhonoured, left without a prize (m. nom. pl., predicate with sīmus; also m. gen. sg. and n. gen. sg.)
glossary.inlaesos: inlaesus (illaesus), -a, -um — unharmed, unhurt (m. acc. pl. with artūs; inl- is the edition's unassimilated spelling of ill-)
glossary.inmani: inmānis (immānis), -e — monstrous, huge (m. abl. sg. with tumulō, abl. of means; inm- is the edition's unassimilated spelling of imm-)
glossary.inmeritas: inmeritus (immeritus), -a, -um — undeserving, that had done no wrong (f. acc. pl. with urbēs; Nestor's verdict, not a neutral epithet; inm- for imm-)
glossary.inpediit: inpediō (impediō), impedīre, impedīvī, impedītum — he entangled, hobbled (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; object crūra, with illīs “with those”, the entrails; inp- for imp-)
glossary.inperfossus: inperfossus (imperfossus), -a, -um — not pierced through, unpunctured (m. nom. sg., of Caeneus; a negative compound of perfodiō; inp- for imp-)
glossary.inplicet: inplicō (implicō), implicāre, implicāvī/-uī, implicātum/-itum — she twines, entwines herself (3 sg. pres. subj. act. in an ut-clause, with reflexive sē; inp- for imp-)
glossary.inpositaque: inpōnō (impōnō), impōnere, imposuī, impositum — laid on, placed upon (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg. with manū in an abl. absolute; inp- for imp-; + -que “and”)
glossary.inpulit: inpellō (impellō), impellere, impulī, impulsum — he drove in, thrust (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; objects ferrum flammamque; inp- for imp-)
glossary.insanis: īnsānus, -a, -um — mad, raving (f. abl. pl. with vīribus, of the south wind's strength; the adjective, not 2 sg. pres. of īnsāniō; also dat. pl.)
glossary.inseris: īnserō, īnserere, īnseruī, īnsertum — you thrust in, insert (2 sg. pres. indic. act.; this is the īnserō “put in among”, not īnserō, -sēvī “sow, graft”)
glossary.insuperabile: īnsuperābilis, -e — unconquerable, not to be overcome (n. nom. sg. with caput, in apposition to Achilles; bellō is abl. of respect)
glossary.interdumque: interdum — sometimes, at times (adverb, third in the interdum ... modo ... interdum series; + -que “and”)
glossary.inutilior: inūtilis, -e — less useful, more of a liability (comparative, m. nom. sg., of Palamedes, with istō as abl. of comparison and sibi “to himself”)
glossary.invidiamque: invidia, -ae (f.) — ill-will, resentment, the odium of the decision (f. acc. sg., object of remōvit; + -que “and”)
glossary.involvite: involvō, involvere, involvī, involūtum — roll on, heap over (2 pl. pres. imper. act.; Monychus to the centaurs)
glossary.iovemque: Iuppiter, Iovis (m.) — Jupiter (m. acc. sg., third in the list of what the Trojans bring against the ships; + -que “and”)
glossary.iphinoum: Iphinous, -ī (m.) — Iphinous, a centaur killed at close quarters (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.isti: iste, ista, istud — that fellow there, that man of yours (m. dat. sg., the contemptuous demonstrative Ajax uses of Ulysses; also m./f./n. gen. sg. and m. nom. pl.)
glossary.ithaco: Ithacus, -ī (m.) — the Ithacan, the man from Ithaca, i.e. Ulysses (m. dat. sg., dative of interest with the understood sunt; also abl. sg.)
glossary.ithacus: Ithacus, -ī (m.) — the Ithacan, i.e. Ulysses (m. nom. sg., subject of the jussive cōnferat; one of Ajax's by-names for the man)
glossary.iubete: iubeō, iubēre, iussī, iussum — order, bid (2 pl. pres. imper. act., with the passive infinitive petī)
glossary.iugulaberis: iugulō, iugulāre, iugulāvī, iugulātum — you will have your throat cut, you will be butchered (2 sg. fut. indic. pass.)
glossary.iuratus: iūrō, iūrāre, iūrāvī, iūrātum — having sworn, sworn in (perf. part. with active force, m. nom. sg., of Philoctetes; in arma is “into the campaign”)
glossary.lacrimantia: lacrimō, lacrimāre, lacrimāvī, lacrimātum — weeping, tearful (pres. act. part., n. acc. pl. with lūmina; also n. nom. pl.)
glossary.laerteque: Lāertēs, -ae (m.) — Laertes, Ulysses' father (m. abl. sg. of origin, paired with Telamōne; + -que “and”)
glossary.laertiadaeque: Lāertiadēs, -ae (m.) — son of Laertes, i.e. Ulysses (Greek patronymic; m. dat. sg., the person prayed about after precāris; also gen. sg. and nom. pl.; + -que “and”)
glossary.laertius: Lāertius, -a, -um — of Laertes, Laertian (adjective from the name; m. nom. sg. with hērōs — Ulysses, named by his father)
glossary.laniaverat: laniō, laniāre, laniāvī, laniātum — had mangled, had torn to pieces (3 sg. plup. indic. act.; subject Periclymenus in eagle-shape)
glossary.lapithaeae: Lapithaeus, -a, -um — Lapith, of the Lapiths (adjective from Lapithae; f. gen. sg. with gentis; also dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.lapithas: Lapithae, -ārum (m. pl.) — the Lapiths, the Thessalian people at war with the Centaurs (m. acc. pl. after inter)
glossary.lapitheia: Lapithēius, -a, -um — Lapith, of the Lapiths (adjective from Lapithae; n. acc. pl. with tēcta, the hall where the wedding brawl breaks out)
glossary.lapsis: lābor, lābī, lāpsus sum — having slipped down, fallen, run down (perf. dep. part. with active sense, m. abl. pl. with fontibus; from lābor “glide, slip”, not labor “toil”; also dat. pl.)
glossary.laterique: latus, lateris (n.) — side, flank (n. dat. sg. with the compound recondere; not later, lateris “brick”, and not the adjective lātus “broad”; + -que “and”)
glossary.latissima: lātus, -a, -um — very broad, widest (superlative, f. nom. sg. with volūbilitās; from lātus “broad”, not latus “side”; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.latreus: Latreus, -eī (m.) — Latreus, the huge centaur who taunts Caeneus and is killed by him (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.laudamus: laudō, laudāre, laudāvī, laudātum — we praise (1 pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.laudaverit: laudō, laudāre, laudāvī, laudātum — would praise (3 sg. perf. subj. act., potential, in the question quis ... laudāverit; identical in form to the fut. perf. indic., which the sense here rules out)
glossary.lavet: lavō, lavāre, lāvī, lautum/lavātum — she washes, bathes (3 sg. pres. subj. act. in an ut-clause; object ōra)
glossary.lemnos: Lēmnos, -ī (f.) — Lemnos, the island where Philoctetes was put ashore (f. nom. sg., Greek nominative; subject of habēret)
glossary.leonum: leō, leōnis (m.) — lions (m. gen. pl. with vellera, the six lion-skins Phaeocomes wore)
glossary.letifera: lētifer, -fera, -ferum — death-bringing, deadly (f. abl. sg. with dextrā, of Apollo's hand; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.linquendus: linquō, linquere, līquī — to be left behind, one who ought to have been abandoned (gerundive, m. nom. sg., with erat; the simple verb beside relinquō just above)
glossary.litis: līs, lītis (f.) — lawsuit, dispute, the contest over the arms (f. gen. sg. with arbitrium; also dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.litoraque: lītus, lītoris (n.) — shores, coasts (n. acc. pl., object of intrāvit; + -que “and”)
glossary.macareus: Macareus, -eī (m.) — Macareus, a Lapith who kills the centaur Erigdupus (m. nom. sg.; not the Macareus who is Ulysses' companion in Book XIV)
glossary.macedoniaque: Macedonius, -a, -um — Macedonian (f. abl. sg. with sarīsā, the long pike — an anachronism Ovid does not disguise; + -que “and”)
glossary.magnus: magnus, -a, -um — great (m. nom. sg. with Achillēs, answering the dative magnō Achillī in the line before)
glossary.malles: mālō, mālle, māluī — you would have preferred, you would rather (2 sg. imperf. subj. act. in an unreal condition; mālō “prefer”, not malus “bad” or mālum “apple”)
glossary.manifestabitque: manifestō, manifestāre, manifestāvī, manifestātum — will show up, will expose (3 sg. fut. indic. act.; subject nitor, the helmet's gleam; + -que “and”)
glossary.maritae: marīta, -ae (f.) — wife (f. gen. sg. with raptōre — the Greek wife Paris carried off, Helen; also dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.marmoris: marmor, marmoris (n.) — marble (n. gen. sg. with corpore, “in a mass of struck marble”)
glossary.meaque: meus, -a, -um — my (f. nom. sg. with facundia; also n. nom./acc. pl.; + -que “and”)
glossary.memoranda: memorō, memorāre, memorāvī, memorātum — needing to be recounted, to be told over (gerundive, n. acc. pl. with facta, subject of esse in indirect statement after reor; also n. nom. pl.)
glossary.mendosa: mendōsus, -a, -um — faulty, flawed (f. nom. sg., predicate with faciēs)
glossary.mentemque: mēns, mentis (f.) — mind (f. acc. sg., object of subit “comes into”; + -que “and”)
glossary.mentoque: mentum, -ī (n.) — chin (n. abl. sg. in the abl. absolute with fīxō; + -que “and”)
glossary.mentum: mentum, -ī (n.) — chin (n. acc. sg. after ad; also nom. sg.)
glossary.messenia: Messēnius, -a, -um — Messenian, of Messene (n. acc. pl. with moenia; also f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.metuaris: metuō, metuere, metuī — you should be feared (2 sg. pres. subj. pass., in the cūr-clause after erit)
glossary.metuendus: metuō, metuere, metuī — to be feared, formidable (gerundive, m. nom. sg., predicate with est; said of Ulysses in sarcasm)
glossary.metuentem: metuō, metuere, metuī — fearing, afraid (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg., object of videō with morte futūrā as abl. of cause)
glossary.militiam: mīlitia, -ae (f.) — military service, soldiering (f. acc. sg., object of dētrectāvit)
glossary.missis: mittō, mittere, mīsī, missum — hurled down, thrown (perf. pass. part., f. abl. pl. with silvīs, abl. of means; also dat. pl.)
glossary.mittantur: mittō, mittere, mīsī, missum — let them be thrown, let them be sent (3 pl. pres. subj. pass., jussive)
glossary.mitti: mittō, mittere, mīsī, missum — to be sent (pres. pass. inf., after debueram)
glossary.mittuntque: mittō, mittere, mīsī, missum — they hurl, they throw (3 pl. pres. indic. act., of the weapon let fly, paired with ferunt of the one driven home; + -que “and”)
glossary.molem: mōlēs, mōlis (f.) — mass, bulk (f. acc. sg., object of opposuī, with clipeī “of my shield”)
glossary.monychus: Mōnychus, -ī (m.) — Monychus, the centaur who cries out the shame of the many losing to one and calls for trees to be piled on Caeneus (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.mopso: Mopsus, -ī (m.) — Mopsus, the Lapith seer, son of Ampyx (m. abl. sg. in the abl. absolute Mopsō iaculante; not Mopsus the son of Manto)
glossary.mopsum: Mopsus, -ī (m.) — Mopsus, the Lapith seer, son of Ampyx (m. acc. sg., in apposition to Ampycidēn, subject of cecinisse)
glossary.mopsus: Mopsus, -ī (m.) — Mopsus, the Lapith seer, son of Ampyx, who greets the transformed Caeneus (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.morari: moror, morārī, morātus sum — to delay, hold back (pres. dep. inf., after poteram; from moror “delay”, not morior “die”, whose infinitive is morī)
glossary.moratos: moror, morārī, morātus sum — having lingered, dwelling (perf. dep. part. with active sense, m. acc. pl. with oculōs; not the adjective mōrātus “mannered” from mōs)
glossary.morboque: morbus, -ī (m.) — disease, sickness (m. abl. sg. with frāctus; + -que “and”)
glossary.morientes: morior, morī, mortuus sum — dying (pres. dep. part., m. acc. pl. with artūs; also m. nom. pl.)
glossary.motumque: mōtus, -ūs (m.) — motion, movement (m. acc. sg., object of negant; the fourth-declension noun, not the perf. part. of moveō; + -que “and”)
glossary.moverent: moveō, movēre, mōvī, mōtum — could move, would shift (3 pl. imperf. subj. act. in a relative clause of characteristic)
glossary.mucro: mucrō, mucrōnis (m.) — point, sword-tip (m. nom. sg.; the point as distinct from the blade's edge)
glossary.nares: nāris, nāris (f.) — nostrils (f. acc. pl. after per, with cava; also nom. pl.)
glossary.naupliades: Naupliadēs, -ae (m.) — son of Nauplius, i.e. Palamedes, who exposed Ulysses' feigned madness (Greek patronymic; m. nom. sg.)
glossary.navibus: nāvis, nāvis (f.) — ships (f. abl. pl. after prō “in return for”; also dat. pl.)
glossary.nebula: nebula, -ae (f.) — cloud, mist (f. abl. sg. with vēlātus, abl. of means; also nom. sg.)
glossary.necopinum: necopīnus, -a, -um — not expecting it, taken unawares (m. acc. sg., object of perde; Achilles at the moment of the shot)
glossary.neganda: negō, negāre, negāvī, negātum — to be denied, to be refused (gerundive, n. nom. pl. with arma, sunt understood; also n. acc. pl.)
glossary.neleius: Nēlēius, -a, -um — Neleian, son of Neleus, i.e. Nestor (adjective from Nēleus used as a noun; m. nom. sg.)
glossary.nelidae: Nēlīdēs, -ae (m.) — sons of Neleus, i.e. Nestor and his eleven brothers (Greek patronymic; m. nom. pl., in apposition to the “we” of fuimus; also gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.nequiret: nequeō, nequīre, nequīvī — he could not, was unable (3 sg. imperf. subj. act. in a circumstantial cum-clause)
glossary.nesseis: Nessēus, -a, -um — of Nessus, Nessus' (adjective from the centaur Nessus' name; f. abl. pl. with manibus, contracted from Nessēīs)
glossary.nestora: Nestōr, Nestoris (m.) — Nestor, the old Pylian, left in the lurch by Ulysses (Greek m. acc. sg. in -a for Latin Nestōrem)
glossary.noluit: nōlō, nōlle, nōluī — he refused, was unwilling (3 sg. perf. indic. act., with the infinitive sūmere)
glossary.nubigenas: nūbigena, -ae (m.) — the cloud-born, i.e. the Centaurs, whose mother was a cloud (m. acc. pl., subject of the infinitive domitōs esse)
glossary.nudare: nūdō, nūdāre, nūdāvī, nūdātum — to strip bare, to strip of (pres. act. inf. after parat, with armīs as abl. of separation)
glossary.nudus: nūdus, -a, -um — bare, stripped (m. nom. sg. with Othrys, the mountain; takes the genitive arboris “of tree”)
glossary.obliquat: oblīquō, oblīquāre, oblīquāvī, oblīquātum — he slants, turns aslant (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; object ēnsem)
glossary.obrutus: obruō, obruere, obruī, obrutum — buried, overwhelmed (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., of Caeneus, with inmānī tumulō as abl. of means)
glossary.obsistere: obsistō, obsistere, obstitī — to stand in the way of, to block (pres. act. inf. after temptat; takes the dative animae fugientī)
glossary.obtulimus: offerō, offerre, obtulī, oblātum — we offered, we exposed (1 pl. perf. indic. act., with nōs as object)
glossary.obversus: obvertō, obvertere, obvertī, obversum — turned towards, facing (perf. pass. part. with middle sense, m. nom. sg., with faciem as Greek acc. of respect)
glossary.occulta: occultus, -a, -um — hidden, unseen (f. abl. sg. with sagittā, abl. of means; not the imperative of occultō, and not n. nom./acc. pl. here)
glossary.offensasque: offēnsa, -ae (f.) — injuries, affronts, grievances (f. acc. pl., object of fatērī; the noun, not the perf. part. of offendō; + -que “and”)
glossary.oileos: Oīleus, -eī (m.) — Oileus (Greek gen. sg.; Oīleos Aiax is the Locrian Ajax, son of Oileus — not the speaker Ajax son of Telamon)
glossary.oleniden: Olenidēs, -ae (m.) — son of Olenus, i.e. the Lapith Tectaphos (Greek patronymic; m. acc. sg.)
glossary.onerosa: onerōsus, -a, -um — burdensome, weighty (f. nom. sg. with hasta, predicate after esse; also n. nom./acc. pl. and f. abl. sg.)
glossary.opposuit: oppōnō, oppōnere, opposuī, oppositum — he set in front, put in the way (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; object dextram, with the dative frontī)
glossary.oppressumque: opprimō, opprimere, oppressī, oppressum — crushed, overwhelmed (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg. with ūnum, in the acc.+inf. after aegrē tulimus with esse understood; + -que “and”)
glossary.ornate: ōrnō, ōrnāre, ōrnāvī, ōrnātum — adorn, deck out (2 pl. pres. imper. act.; not the adverb ōrnātē “elegantly”, nor a vocative of ōrnātus)
glossary.pagasaeae: Pagasaeus, -a, -um — Pagasaean, of Pagasae in Thessaly (f. gen. sg. with silvae; also dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.palamedes: Palamēdēs, -is (m.) — Palamedes, son of Nauplius, framed by Ulysses and put to death (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.parasti: parō, parāre, parāvī, parātum — you got, you procured for yourself (2 sg. perf. indic. act., syncopated for parāvistī)
glossary.parim: Paris, Paridis (m.) — Paris, the Trojan prince whose arrow kills Achilles (Greek m. acc. sg. Parim for Latin Paridem)
glossary.parvam: parvus, -a, -um — small, little (f. acc. sg. with urnam)
glossary.passurae: patior, patī, passus sum — about to suffer, destined to endure (fut. act. part. of the deponent, f. dat. sg. with frontī; also gen. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.patruique: patruus, -ī (m.) — father's brother, uncle (m. gen. sg. with animō; Apollo's uncle is Neptune, Jupiter's brother; + -que “and”)
glossary.pelethronium: Pelethrōnius, -a, -um — Pelethronian, of the Thessalian district the Centaurs come from (n. acc. sg. with pectus, marking the victim Erigdupus as a centaur)
glossary.pelias: Pēlias, -adis — of Mount Pelion, Pelian (Greek f. adjective; f. nom. sg. with hasta, the spear cut from Pelion; not Pelias the king of Iolcus, and not the patronymic Pēlīdēs)
glossary.peliden: Pēlīdēs, -ae (m.) — son of Peleus, i.e. Achilles (Greek patronymic; m. acc. sg. Pēlīdēn, object of ostendēns)
glossary.pelides: Pēlīdēs, -ae (m.) — son of Peleus, i.e. Achilles (Greek patronymic; m. nom. sg.)
glossary.penatis: Penātēs, -ium (m. pl.) — the Penates, the household gods (m. acc. pl. in the older ending -īs for -ēs, after in; also gen. sg. of the rare singular)
glossary.pendentemque: pendeō, pendēre, pependī — hanging, hovering (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg. with hunc, of Periclymenus poised in the air as an eagle; + -que “and”)
glossary.perdis: perdō, perdere, perdidī, perditum — you are wasting, you are throwing away (2 sg. pres. indic. act.; Apollo to Paris)
glossary.peremit: perimō, perimere, perēmī, peremptum — he destroyed, he killed off (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; the present would be perimit)
glossary.pergama: Pergama, -ōrum (n. pl.) — Pergama, the citadel of Troy, Troy itself (n. acc. pl.: after ad at XII.445, after circum at XII.591; also nom. pl.)
glossary.periclymeni: Periclymenus, -ī (m.) — Periclymenus, Nestor's brother, given shape-shifting by Neptune and killed by Hercules (m. gen. sg. with mors)
glossary.periphanta: Periphās, Periphantis — Periphas, the Lapith who overcame the two-formed centaur Pyraethus (Greek acc. sg. in -anta; Latin nom. Periphās)
glossary.perstas: perstō, perstāre, perstitī — you persist, keep on, stand fast (2 sg. pres. indic. act.; with the inf. certare)
glossary.petuntur: petō, petere, petīvī, petītum — are sought, are sought after (3 pl. pres. indic. pass.)
glossary.phaeocomes: Phaeocomēs, -is — Phaeocomes, the centaur clad in six lion-skins (m. nom. sg., Greek nom. in -ēs, in apposition to ille)
glossary.phaethontida: Phaëthontis, -idis — Phaethontian, of Phaethon — of the swan, Phaethon's bird (f. adj., Greek acc. sg. in -ida, agreeing with volucrem; the son turned into it is Cycnus, killed by Achilles)
glossary.phlegraeon: Phlegraeus, -ī — Phlegraeus, one of the centaurs killed at long range before the fighting told here (Greek acc. sg. in -on; Latin nom. Phlegraeus)
glossary.phrygias: Phrygius, -a, -um — Phrygian, Trojan (f. acc. pl. agreeing with arces; Phrygias arces means Troy)
glossary.phrygum: Phryges, Phrygum m. pl. — the Phrygians, i.e. the Trojans (gen. pl., with timor: the terror felt by them)
glossary.phyllei: Phyllēius, -a, -um — of Phyllus, Phyllean (a Thessalian town) — the Phyllean youth is Caeneus (m. gen. sg. agreeing with iuvenis; the form is also m. nom. pl.)
glossary.pice: pix, picis f. — pitch (f. abl. sg., abl. of comparison after nigrior)
glossary.plebis: plēbs, plēbis f. — the common people, the common crowd (gen. sg.; a by-form plēbēs, -ēī also exists)
glossary.poeantia: Poeantius, -a, -um — of Poeas, son of Poeas — the addressee is Philoctetes (f. voc. sg. agreeing with prolēs; the form is also f. nom. sg. and n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.polydamanta: Polydamās, -antis — Polydamas, the Trojan counsellor and comrade of Hector, named with Deiphobus and Hector as an enemy (Greek acc. sg. in -anta)
glossary.populator: populātor, populātōris m. — ravager, devastator (m. nom. sg., in apposition to Achilles; the work ravaged is the walls Neptune built)
glossary.poscentem: poscō, poscere, poposcī — demanding, calling for (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg., of Hector demanding an opponent)
glossary.posuisti: pōnō, pōnere, posuī, positum — you set up, laid, built (2 sg. perf. indic. act., of Apollo raising Troy's walls with Neptune)
glossary.poteremur: potior, potīrī, potītus sum — we would gain possession of, would have (1 pl. imperf. subj. dep., unreal present; here with the acc. te, though potior usually takes the abl. as in tuis armis)
glossary.potiorque: potior, potius — better, preferable, more deserving (comparative adj., m. nom. sg.; + -que “and”). Not the deponent verb potior “gain possession of”, which is the same letters in other forms
glossary.praeconia: praecōnium, -ī n. — a herald's proclamation, formal public praise (n. acc. pl., object of debere; the form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.praefoderat: praefodiō, praefodere, praefōdī, praefossum — had buried beforehand, had dug in in advance (3 sg. plup. indic. act., of the planted gold)
glossary.praetendat: praetendō, praetendere, praetendī, praetentum — holds out in front, drapes over (3 sg. pres. subj. act., in the ut-clause of characteristic)
glossary.praeteriti: praetereō, praeterīre, praeteriī, praeteritum — passed over, left unmentioned (perf. pass. part., m. gen. sg. agreeing with Alcidae, i.e. Hercules passed over in the telling)
glossary.precaris: precor, precārī, precātus sum — you pray for, call down (2 sg. pres. indic. dep.; takes the dat. of the person prayed about, Laertiadae, and the acc. of the thing prayed for)
glossary.premat: premō, premere, pressī, pressum — let it press, weigh down, crush (3 sg. pres. subj. act., jussive)
glossary.priamidenque: Priamidēs, -ae m. — son of Priam, here Helenus, the seer taken with the Palladium (Greek acc. sg. in -en; + -que “and”)
glossary.probavit: probō, probāre, probāvī, probātum — proved, made good, got accepted (3 sg. perf. indic. act., of the fabricated charge)
glossary.prodet: prōdō, prōdere, prōdidī, prōditum — will betray, will give away (3 sg. fut. indic. act.). Not prōdeō “go forth”, whose future is prōdībit
glossary.proditus: prōdō, prōdere, prōdidī, prōditum — betrayed, given up (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., with est: of Nestor abandoned by Ulysses)
glossary.prolemque: prōlēs, prōlis f. — offspring, child (acc. sg., subject of esse in the acc. and inf. after fatetur; + -que “and”)
glossary.prosit: prōsum, prōdesse, prōfuī — let it help, be of use (3 sg. pres. subj. act., jussive/optative; takes the dat., and with in causam “toward the case”)
glossary.protectus: prōtegō, prōtegere, prōtēxī, prōtēctum — covered over, protected (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., with the Greek accusatives of respect hominem ... equum: protected as to man and as to horse)
glossary.protexi: prōtegō, prōtegere, prōtēxī, prōtēctum — I covered, shielded (1 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.provolat: prōvolō, prōvolāre — flies forward, rushes out (3 sg. pres. indic. act., historic present, of the centaur Latreus)
glossary.pugnantem: pugnō, pugnāre — fighting, as he fought (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg. agreeing with te, the centaur Cyllarus addressed)
glossary.pugnare: pugnō, pugnāre — to fight, to do battle (pres. act. inf., set against contendere “to contend in words”)
glossary.pylio: Pȳlius, -a, -um — Pylian, of Pylos; as a noun, the Pylian, i.e. Nestor (m. abl. sg. in the abl. abs. Pylio referente)
glossary.pylumque: Pylus (Pylos), -ī f. — Pylos, Nestor's own city, razed by Hercules (acc. sg. with the Latin ending; + -que “and”)
glossary.pyraechmen: Pyraechmēs, -is — Pyraechmes, the axe-bearing centaur, fifth of those killed by Caeneus (Greek acc. sg. in -en; some editions print the different name Pyracmon)
glossary.pyraethi: Pyraethus, -ī m. — Pyraethus, the two-formed centaur beaten by Periphas (gen. sg. after victorem)
glossary.quadrupedantis: quadrupedāns, quadrupedantis — going on four feet, four-footed (pres. act. part. of quadrupedō used as adj., m. gen. sg. agreeing with Echecli; the form is also acc. pl.)
glossary.quatiatur: quatiō, quatere, quassī, quassum — be shaken (3 sg. pres. subj. pass., in the imagined comparison si ... quatiatur)
glossary.rabidi: rabidus, -a, -um — raging, frenzied (m. nom. pl. agreeing with bimembres, the centaurs). Not rapidus “swift, tearing”
glossary.radiantis: radiō, radiāre — radiant, gleaming (pres. act. part., f. gen. sg. agreeing with galeae; the form is also acc. pl.)
glossary.raptore: raptor, raptōris m. — carrier-off, abductor — here Paris, who carried off Helen (m. abl. sg., agent after a)
glossary.rari: rārus, -a, -um — loose-woven, wide-meshed, open in texture (n. gen. sg. agreeing with cribri, and set against densa foramina; not “rare, few” here, and not the m. nom. pl.)
glossary.raro: rārō — rarely, seldom (adv. from rārus, here with tam and passus; not the abl. sg. of the adjective)
glossary.recondere: recondō, recondere, recondidī, reconditum — to bury, plunge, sink (a blade) out of sight (pres. act. inf. after luctatur)
glossary.recuset: recūsō, recūsāre — let him refuse, decline, turn down (3 sg. pres. subj. act., jussive)
glossary.redeamus: redeō, redīre, rediī, reditum — let us go back, return (1 pl. pres. subj. act., hortatory)
glossary.redemit: redimō, redimere, redēmī, redēmptum — bought back, ransomed, bought off (3 sg. perf. indic. act.). Not redeō “return”, and not the pres. redimit
glossary.reditus: reditus, -ūs m. — return, homecoming (gen. sg. after spem, with vestri; the form is also nom. sg. and acc. pl., and it is not the perf. part. of redeō)
glossary.redunco: reduncus, -a, -um — bent back, hooked (n. abl. sg. agreeing with rostro, of the eagle's beak)
glossary.referentem: referō, referre, rettulī, relātum — bringing back, carrying back (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg., object of ornate)
glossary.refrixit: refrīgēscō, refrīgēscere, refrīxī — grew cold, chilled (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; an inceptive verb, so “went cold”)
glossary.regi: rēx, rēgis m. — king (dat. sg., regi divum “to the king of the gods”, after gratissima). Not a form of regō, whose pres. pass. inf. is the same letters
glossary.rem: rēs, reī f. — thing, affair, cause, state — rem Danaam “the Danaan cause”; rem gerere “conduct the business, carry out the operation” (acc. sg.)
glossary.remoto: removeō, removēre, remōvī, remōtum — removed, taken away, subtracted (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg. in the abl. abs. Diomede remoto)
glossary.repetito: repetō, repetere, repetīvī, repetītum — taken up again, resumed (perf. pass. part., n. abl. sg. in the abl. abs. repetito munere Bacchi)
glossary.reponere: repōnō, repōnere, reposuī, repositum — to put back, lay aside again (pres. act. inf., the second half of Periclymenus' gift: to put off the shape he has taken on)
glossary.resilit: resiliō, resilīre, resiluī — springs back, rebounds (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; the subject is haec, the sarisa)
glossary.respexit: respiciō, respicere, respexī, respectum — looked back at, looked round on (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.respondet: respondeō, respondēre, respondī, respōnsum — corresponds to, matches, is proportionate to (3 sg. pres. indic. act., with the dat. illi ... viro; not “answers a question” here)
glossary.resupinum: resupīnus, -a, -um — bent back, flat on his back (m. acc. sg., proleptic with fudi: the throw put him there)
glossary.retexit: retegō, retegere, retēxī, retēctum — laid bare, uncovered, exposed (3 sg. perf. indic. act.). Not retexō “unweave, undo”, whose pres. is the same letters
glossary.retusa: retundō, retundere, rettudī, retūsum — blunted, dulled (perf. pass. part., n. nom. pl. agreeing with tela)
glossary.rhesum: Rhēsus, -ī m. — Rhesus, the Thracian king killed in his sleep by Ulysses and Diomedes (acc. sg.)
glossary.rhodiae: Rhodius, -a, -um — Rhodian, of Rhodes — the fleet Tlepolemus led (f. gen. sg. agreeing with classis; the form is also dat. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.rosave: rosa, -ae f. — rose (abl. sg. of means; + -ve “or”, the second of the pair -ve ... -ve “either ... or”)
glossary.rostroque: rōstrum, -ī n. — beak, bill (abl. sg. of means, of the eagle; + -que “and”)
glossary.rubefacta: rubefaciō, rubefacere, rubefēcī, rubefactum — reddened, made red (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. agreeing with cornua)
glossary.rupti: rumpō, rumpere, rūpī, ruptum — burst, torn apart (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl. agreeing with nervi)
glossary.saevique: saevus, -a, -um — savage, cruel (n. gen. sg. agreeing with teli, in the idiom vicem praestāre “serve in place of”; + -que “and”, joining the two objects of gerebat)
glossary.saevumque: saevus, -a, -um — savage, cruel (m. acc. sg. agreeing with Achillem, object of perosus; + -que “and”)
glossary.sarisa: sarīsa (sarissa), -ae f. — the long Macedonian pike (abl. sg. at both places, of accompaniment with conspicuus and of means with ferit; the form is also nom. sg.). A deliberate anachronism in a Thessalian battle
glossary.scelerum: scelus, sceleris n. — crime, wicked deed (gen. pl., objective genitive after hortator “urger on to crimes”)
glossary.secumque: sēcum (sē + cum) — with him, with himself (abl. of the reflexive sē with the preposition cum attached behind it; + -que “and”)
glossary.securiferumque: secūrifer, secūrifera, secūriferum — axe-bearing (m. acc. sg. agreeing with Pyraechmen; + -que “and”)
glossary.segnibus: segnis, -e — sluggish, slack, unenterprising (n. abl. pl. agreeing with actis, abl. of cause: “by our sluggish doings”)
glossary.semiferos: sēmifer, sēmifera, sēmiferum — half-beast, half-wild; as a noun, the half-beasts, i.e. the centaurs (m. acc. pl. after inter)
glossary.semihomines: sēmihomō, sēmihominis — half-human, half a man (m. acc. pl. agreeing with Centauros)
glossary.semimari: sēmimās, sēmimaris — half-male, only half a man (m. abl. sg. agreeing with hoste; Monychus' jeer at Caeneus)
glossary.sena: sēnī, sēnae, sēna — six each, six (distributive numeral used in verse for sex; n. acc. pl. agreeing with vellera). Not a form of senex
glossary.senemque: senex, senis m. — an old man (acc. sg. after inter, the second stage of life; + -que “and”)
glossary.septemplicis: septemplex, septemplicis — sevenfold, of seven layers (m. gen. sg. agreeing with clipei, Ajax's shield of seven ox-hides)
glossary.series: seriēs, seriēī f. — line, succession, chain (here of ancestors) (nom. sg.; the 5th-declension form is also nom. pl. and acc. pl.)
glossary.servavique: servō, servāre, servāvī, servātum — I saved, preserved (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; + -que “and”)
glossary.sessile: sessilis, -e — fit to be sat on, that can be sat upon (n. nom. sg. agreeing with tergum, of the centaur's back; a word one would use of furniture)
glossary.sigeia: Sīgēius, -a, -um — Sigean, of Sigeum, the headland by Troy where the Greek ships lay (n. acc. pl. agreeing with litora; the form is also f. nom. sg.)
glossary.silendo: sileō, silēre, siluī — by keeping silent about (abl. gerund of means, and here transitive, governing the acc. fortia facta)
glossary.silentibus: sileō, silēre, siluī — the silent ones, i.e. the dead (pres. act. part. used as a noun, m. dat. pl. after reddit; the form is also abl. pl.)
glossary.silvestribus: silvestris, -e — of the woods, woodland (n. abl. pl. agreeing with antris)
glossary.sisyphio: Sīsyphius, -a, -um — Sisyphian, of Sisyphus — Ajax's charge that Ulysses is Sisyphus' son, not Laertes' (n. abl. sg. agreeing with sanguine, abl. of origin with cretus)
glossary.sminthea: Sminthēus, -eī m. — Smintheus, the Sminthian, a cult title of Apollo in the Troad (Greek acc. sg. in -ea; Latin nom. Sminthēus)
glossary.sollertior: sollers, sollertis — shrewder, more resourceful (comparative, m. nom. sg. agreeing with Naupliades, i.e. Palamedes; isto is abl. of comparison)
glossary.sonantem: sonō, sonāre, sonuī, sonitum — sounding, resounding (pres. act. part., f. acc. sg. agreeing with hanc, the bird)
glossary.spargentem: spargō, spargere, sparsī, sparsum — scattering, sprinkling about (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg. agreeing with Parim, with tela as its object)
glossary.spectemur: spectō, spectāre — let us be looked at, be put on view (1 pl. pres. subj. pass., jussive)
glossary.speravit: spērō, spērāre, spērāvī, spērātum — has hoped for, has set his hopes on (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.spissus: spissus, -a, -um — thick, dense, clotted (m. nom. sg. agreeing with liquor, predicative with exprimitur)
glossary.spoliantis: spoliō, spoliāre — of the man plundering, of the plunderer (pres. act. part. used as a noun, m. gen. sg. depending on ima ilia; the form is also acc. pl.)
glossary.spolieris: spoliō, spoliāre — you should be stripped of it, robbed (2 sg. pres. subj. pass., in the cur clause after erit)
glossary.standi: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — of standing, for standing (gen. gerund depending on vires)
glossary.stante: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — standing (pres. act. part., f. abl. sg. agreeing with corona in the abl. abs. vulgi stante corona)
glossary.sternentem: sternō, sternere, strāvī, strātum — laying low, felling (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg. agreeing with Peliden, with Troica corpora as its object)
glossary.styphelumque: Styphelus, -ī m. — Styphelus, first of the five centaurs killed by Caeneus (acc. sg.; + -que “and”)
glossary.subduxit: subdūcō, subdūcere, subdūxī, subductum — drew away, withdrew, took off (3 sg. perf. indic. act., with Achivis as dat. of separation)
glossary.successore: successor, successōris m. — successor, heir — Philoctetes as heir of Hercules' bow (m. abl. sg., predicative with utuntur, which takes the abl.)
glossary.summus: summus, -a, -um — highest, supreme (m. nom. sg. agreeing with Iuppiter across the line-end)
glossary.superamur: superō, superāre — we are beaten, are overcome (1 pl. pres. indic. pass.)
glossary.taceam: taceō, tacēre, tacuī, tacitum — that I may say nothing of, pass over in silence (1 sg. pres. subj. act. in the aside ut ... taceam; here transitive, with alios as object)
glossary.tantalides: Tantalidēs, -ae m. — descendant of Tantalus — here Agamemnon, named by his line (m. nom. sg., Greek patronymic)
glossary.tardatus: tardō, tardāre, tardāvī, tardātum — slowed, held back (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., with nullo ... vulnere)
glossary.tectaphon: Tectaphos, -ī m. — Tectaphos son of Olenus, the Lapith whose skull the centaur Phaeocomes broke (Greek acc. sg. in -on)
glossary.telamone: Telamōn, Telamōnis m. — Telamon, king of Salamis, father of Ajax and brother of Peleus (abl. sg., abl. of origin with creato, creatus and satus)
glossary.teleboasque: Teleboās, -ae m. — Teleboas, a centaur killed by Nestor (Greek nom. sg. in -ās, subject with Chthonius of iacent; + -que “and”)
glossary.temptaminis: temptāmen, temptāminis n. — attempt, trial, bid (gen. sg. after pretium)
glossary.temptemus: temptō, temptāre, temptāvī, temptātum — let us try, test, make trial of (1 pl. pres. subj. act., hortatory)
glossary.terreris: terreō, terrēre, terruī, territum — you are terrified, are frightened (2 sg. pres. indic. pass.)
glossary.tersit: tergeō (tergō), tergēre, tersī, tersum — wiped, wiped dry (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.texique: tegō, tegere, tēxī, tēctum — I covered, sheltered, shielded (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; + -que “and”). Not texō “weave”, whose perfect is texuī
glossary.thermodontiaca: Thermodontiacus, -a, -um — Thermodontian, of the river Thermodon, hence Amazonian (f. abl. sg. agreeing with bipenni; the form is also n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.timidae: timidus, -a, -um — timid, cowardly (f. dat. sg. agreeing with sinistrae after conveniet; the form is also f. gen. sg. and nom. pl.)
glossary.tingat: tingō, tingere, tīnxī, tīnctum — dips, wets, bathes (3 sg. pres. subj. act., in the ut-clause)
glossary.tlepolemus: Tlēpolemus, -ī m. — Tlepolemus, son of Hercules and leader of the Rhodian contingent, who interrupts Nestor (nom. sg.)
glossary.torque: torqueō, torquēre, torsī, tortum — twist, spin (2 sg. pres. imper. act., of spinning thread). Not torquis (torquēs) “a twisted collar, necklace”, whose abl. sg. is the same letters
glossary.torsi: torqueō, torquēre, torsī, tortum — I hurled, whirled, flung (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; not from torreō)
glossary.trabem: trabs, trabis f. — beam, tree-trunk (acc. sg., object of coniecit)
glossary.trabesque: trabs, trabis f. — beams, tree-trunks (acc. pl., object of involvite; the form is also nom. pl.; + -que “and”)
glossary.tractaque: trahō, trahere, trāxī, tractum — the dragged things, i.e. the entrails already dragged (perf. pass. part. used as a noun, n. acc. pl., object of calcavit; + -que “and”)
glossary.tracti: trahō, trahere, trāxī, tractum — dragged, hauled (perf. pass. part., m. gen. sg. agreeing with Hectoris, dragged round Troy)
glossary.tracto: trahō, trahere, trāxī, tractum — dragged out, drawn out, prolonged (perf. pass. part., n. abl. sg. agreeing with bello in the abl. abs.). Not the verb tractō “handle”
glossary.trahenti: trahō, trahere, trāxī, tractum — dragging, hauling along (pres. act. part., m. dat. sg. agreeing with tibi)
glossary.trementem: tremō, tremere, tremuī — trembling, shaking (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg., object of video)
glossary.troianis: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan (n. dat. pl. agreeing with fatis, “owed to the fates of Troy”; the form is also abl. pl.)
glossary.troica: Trōicus, -a, -um — Trojan (n. acc. pl. agreeing with corpora)
glossary.tulimus: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — we bore, endured — in the idiom aegre tulimus “we took it ill, we resented it” (1 pl. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.tutius: tūtus, -a, -um — safer (comparative, n. nom. sg. as predicate of est with the infinitives; the same form serves as the comparative adverb “more safely”)
glossary.tydides: Tȳdīdēs, -ae m. — son of Tydeus, i.e. Diomedes (m. nom. sg., Greek patronymic; distinct from the Aiax Oileos named beside him at XIII.622)
glossary.ulciscere: ulcīscor, ulcīscī, ultus sum — avenge, take vengeance for (2 sg. pres. imper. dep.; deponent, so this is a command, not a passive infinitive)
glossary.ulixe: Ulixēs, -is (also -ī) m. — Ulysses, Odysseus (m. voc. sg., Ajax turning to address him directly)
glossary.ulixem: Ulixēs, -is (also -ī) m. — Ulysses, Odysseus (m. acc. sg. with the Latin ending, object of imploraret)
glossary.ulixen: Ulixēs, -is (also -ī) m. — Ulysses, Odysseus (m. acc. sg. with the Greek ending -en, like Aeacon and Sisyphon in the same speech)
glossary.ulixes: Ulixēs, -is (also -ī) m. — Ulysses, Odysseus (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.urnam: urna, -ae f. — urn, the jar that holds the ashes (acc. sg., object of conpleat)
glossary.utuntur: ūtor, ūtī, ūsus sum — they make use of, employ (3 pl. pres. indic. dep.; takes the abl., here quo successore “him as their successor”)
glossary.valeo: valeō, valēre, valuī — I am strong, have power, count for something (1 sg. pres. indic. act., with quantum “as much as”)
glossary.valuissent: valeō, valēre, valuī — had prevailed, had been effective (3 pl. plup. subj. act., unreal past)
glossary.vara: vārus, -a, -um — bent outwards, splayed, crooked (n. acc. pl. agreeing with cornua). Not vārius “varied, dappled”
glossary.variabant: variō, variāre, variāvī, variātum — made varied, dappled, streaked (3 pl. imperf. indic. act.; the subject is cani, the grey hairs)
glossary.variatus: variō, variāre, variāvī, variātum — changed, altered — here reflexive in force, “having changed himself” (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg., with est)
glossary.vecte: vectis, vectis m. — bar, lever, crowbar (abl. sg. of means, with adacto). Not a form of vehō
glossary.velaturque: vēlō, vēlāre, vēlāvī, vēlātum — he is clothed, covered, veiled (3 sg. pres. indic. pass.; + -que, here the first of the pair -que ... -que “both ... and”)
glossary.venisset: veniō, venīre, vēnī, ventum — had come (3 sg. plup. subj. act., in the unfulfilled wish after utinam)
glossary.versavitque: versō, versāre, versāvī, versātum — turned, twisted, worked round (3 sg. perf. indic. act., of the blade in the wound; + -que “and”)
glossary.vertex: vertex, verticis m. — the crown of the head, the head (nom. sg.; elsewhere in the poem the same word is “summit” or “whirlpool”)
glossary.vilibus: vīlis, -e — cheap, of small worth (n. dat. pl. agreeing with meritis, dat. with datis; the form is also abl. pl.)
glossary.vinxerat: vinciō, vincīre, vīnxī, vīnctum — had bound, had tied together (3 sg. plup. indic. act.). Not vincō “conquer”, whose pluperfect is vīcerat
glossary.violave: viola, -ae f. — violet (abl. sg. of means; + -ve “or”, first of the pair -ve ... -ve “either ... or”)
glossary.viresque: vīs, pl. vīrēs, vīrium f. — strength, powers (acc. pl., object of negant; + -que “and”). Not vir “man”, and not a form of vireō
glossary.vitataque: vītō, vītāre, vītāvī, vītātum — shunned, avoided (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. agreeing with arma; + -que “and”)
glossary.vivacemque: vīvāx, vīvācis — tenacious of life, long-lived, hard to kill (f. acc. sg. agreeing with animam; + -que “and”)
glossary.viveret: vīvō, vīvere, vīxī, vīctum — he would be alive (3 sg. imperf. subj. act., unreal present)
glossary.vobisque: vōs, vestrum (vestrī) — you (pl.) — here “to you” (dat. pl. after aequa; the form is also abl. pl.; + -que “and”)
glossary.volubilitas: volūbilitās, volūbilitātis f. — roundness, the quality of rolling — here the round of the skull (nom. sg., with fracta and est understood)
glossary.vovistis: voveō, vovēre, vōvī, vōtum — you vowed, prayed for (2 pl. perf. indic. act., of praying that the lot fall to Ajax)
glossary.vulgi: vulgus, -ī n. — the crowd, the common people (gen. sg., with corona “the crowd's ring of onlookers”)
glossary.vulgique: vulgus, -ī n. — the crowd, the common people (gen. sg., with murmur; + -que “and”)
glossary.vulnusque: vulnus, vulneris n. — wound (acc. sg. at both places, object of fecit and of redde; the form is also nom. sg.; + -que “and”)
glossary.acceptior: acceptus, -a, -um — more welcome, more acceptable (comp., nom. sg. m., agreeing with ‘sanguis’: freely given blood is “more welcome”)
glossary.accessisse: accēdō, -ere — to have come to, to have joined (perf. act. inf. in indirect statement, with dat. ‘labori’)
glossary.accusasse: accūsō, -āre — to have accused (syncopated perf. act. inf. = accusavisse)
glossary.accusoque: accūsō, -āre — and I accuse, arraign (1 sg. pres. ind. act. + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.achilleos: Achillēus, -a, -um — of Achilles, Achilles' (acc. pl. m. with ‘manes’, the shade of Achilles demanding Polyxena)
glossary.actorides: Actoridēs, -ae m. — “son of Actor”, i.e. Patroclus, grandson of Actor, who drove the Trojans from the ships wearing Achilles' armour (nom. sg.; Greek patronymic)
glossary.adeam: adeō, adīre — that I may go to, approach (1 sg. pres. subj. act. in a negative purpose clause with ‘ne’)
glossary.adferre: adferō, -ferre — to carry off, bring away (pres. act. inf., of carrying off the Palladium)
glossary.adgrediar: adgredior, -gredī — I shall approach, accost (1 sg. fut. ind.; deponent; future, matching ‘nitar’ in the same line — the form is also pres. subj.)
glossary.adiecisset: adiciō, -ere — had added (3 sg. plupf. subj. act. in a ‘nisi’ clause)
glossary.admiremur: admīror, -ārī — let us be surprised (1 pl. pres. subj.; deponent; jussive under ‘neve’, “let us not be surprised”)
glossary.adspicite: adspiciō, -ere — look! behold! (2 pl. pres. imper. act.)
glossary.adsuetus: adsuēscō, -ere — accustomed, inured (perf. part. used adjectivally, nom. sg. m., with dat. ‘praedae’: Polymestor, used to loot)
glossary.agamemnona: Agamemnōn, -onis m. — Agamemnon, king of Mycenae and commander-in-chief of the Greeks at Troy (Greek acc. sg. in ‑a)
glossary.aiacem: Aiāx, -ācis m. — Ajax, son of Telamon, the strongest Greek fighter after Achilles and Ulysses' rival for the arms (acc. sg.)
glossary.aiacis: Aiāx, -ācis m. — of Ajax, son of Telamon (gen. sg.; ‘Aiacis meritum’ “Ajax's desert”, ‘Aiacis stolidi’ “of dull Ajax”)
glossary.alastoraque: Alastōr, -oris m. — Alastor, a Lycian ally of Troy killed by Ulysses (Greek acc. sg. in ‑a + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.albentes: albeō, -ēre — whitening, white (pres. act. part., acc. pl. f., with ‘comas’: Hecuba's white hair)
