glossary.alcandrumque: Alcandrus, -ī m. — Alcander, a Lycian slain by Ulysses (acc. sg. + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.alendi: alō, -ere — to be fed, nourished (gerundive, nom. pl. m., with ‘simus’ in a passive periphrastic: “by what means we are to be fed”)
glossary.alendum: alō, -ere — to be reared, brought up (gerundive, acc. sg. m., agreeing with ‘te’ and expressing purpose after ‘commisit’)
glossary.aliquem: aliquis, aliqua, aliquid — some, some measure of (masc. acc. sg., used adjectivally with ‘honorem’)
glossary.alumni: alumnus, -ī m. — foster-son, ward (gen. sg.; Polydorus, the boy Polymestor was reared to protect and murdered)
glossary.ambitiosa: ambitiōsus, -a, -um — eagerly canvassing, importunate (nom. sg. f., with ‘mater’ = Thetis, who begged the divine armour for her son)
glossary.amicior: amīcus, -a, -um — more friendly, more favourable (comp., nom. sg. m., with ‘ventus’)
glossary.amissamque: āmittō, -ere — lost (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f., with ‘virtutem’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.amissos: āmittō, -ere — lost ones (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m., used as a noun: “after so many lost”)
glossary.amplexas: amplector, -plectī — having embraced, clasping (perf. part. of a deponent, hence active in sense; acc. pl. f., with ‘matres’)
glossary.andraemone: Andraemōn, -onis m. — Andraemon, father of the Aetolian chief Thoas (abl. sg. of origin with ‘natus’)
glossary.annorum: annus, -ī m. — of years (gen. pl.; ‘tot annorum cura’ “the toil of so many years”, ‘annorum ... suorum’ “of her own years”)
glossary.annosa: annōsus, -a, -um — full of years, aged (nom. sg. f., with ‘senectus’)
glossary.antenora: Antēnōr, -oris m. — Antenor, the Trojan elder who urged giving Helen back, allied with Priam in the debate (Greek acc. sg. in ‑a)
glossary.antistita: antistita, -ae f. — priestess (nom. sg.; feminine of ‘antistes’; here ‘antistita Phoebi’, Cassandra, dragged by the hair)
glossary.arcesius: Arcēsius, -ī m. — Arcesius, son of Jupiter, father of Laertes and grandfather of Ulysses (nom. sg.; the link by which Ulysses claims descent from Jove)
glossary.ardebat: ārdeō, -ēre — was burning, was ablaze (3 sg. imperf. ind. act.; intransitive, of Ilium)
glossary.arguit: arguō, -ere — he charges, accuses (3 sg. pres. ind. act.; the spelling is also the perfect “he charged”, but the present suits the running argument)
glossary.armandique: armō, -āre — to be armed, to be equipped (gerundive, nom. pl. m., with ‘simus’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.arsuris: ārdeō, -ēre — about to burn, doomed to burn (fut. act. part., abl. pl. f., with ‘carinis’)
glossary.asiae: Asia, -ae f. — Asia, i.e. Asia Minor (gen. sg.; ‘Asiae florentis imago’, Hecuba as the image of Asia in flower)
glossary.astyanax: Astyanax, -actis m. — Astyanax, the infant son of Hector and Andromache, flung from the towers of Troy (nom. sg.)
glossary.atridae: Ātrīdēs, -ae m. — “son of Atreus” (gen. sg.; ‘maioris ... Atridae’ is Agamemnon, so the brother meant is Menelaus)
glossary.audistis: audiō, -īre — you heard (2 pl. perf. ind. act., syncopated = audivistis)
glossary.aulidaque: Aulis, -idis f. — Aulis, the Boeotian harbour where the Greek fleet mustered and was becalmed (Greek acc. sg. in ‑a + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.avari: avārus, -a, -um — greedy (gen. sg. m., with ‘animi’: the gold was “a goad to a greedy heart”)
glossary.avitis: avītus, -a, -um — ancestral, of one's forefathers (abl. pl. n., with ‘monumentis’)
glossary.avulsa: āvellō, -ere — torn away (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., of Hecuba, with abl. ‘tumulis’)
glossary.benefacta: benefactum, -ī n. — good deeds, services rendered (acc. pl.; object of ‘detractare’)
glossary.benignior: benīgnus, -a, -um — more generous, kinder (comp., nom. sg. m., with ‘Aiax’)
glossary.bistoniis: Bistonius, -a, -um — Bistonian, i.e. Thracian (abl. pl. m., with ‘viris’; from the Bistones, a people of Thrace)
glossary.blando: blandus, -a, -um — coaxing, flattering (abl. sg. n., with ‘ore’)
glossary.busto: bustum, -ī n. — funeral mound, pyre-tomb (dat. sg. with ‘fit hostia’, “becomes a victim to the grim tomb”; abl. on another construal)
glossary.caderet: cadō, -ere — she was falling (3 sg. imperf. subj. act. in a ‘cum’ clause; of Polyxena sinking as she is struck)
glossary.caelamina: caelāmen, -inis n. — chased relief, embossed work (acc. pl.; the figures worked on Achilles' shield)
glossary.canitiemque: cānitiēs, -ēī f. — grey hair, white hair (acc. sg., 5th decl. + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.captam: capiō, -ere — captured, already taken (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f., with ‘Troiam’)
glossary.captiva: captīvus, -a, -um — a captive woman (nom. sg. f., used as a noun; Polyxena of herself, against ‘Priami ... filia regis’)
glossary.castique: castus, -a, -um — chaste, pure (gen. sg. m., with ‘pudoris’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.casuraque: cadō, -ere — destined to fall (fut. act. part., acc. pl. n., with ‘moenia’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.catulo: catulus, -ī m. — cub, whelp (abl. sg. of separation with ‘orbata’: the lioness “bereft of her suckling cub”)
glossary.cecidisti: cadō, -ere — you fell (2 sg. perf. ind. act.; from ‘cadō’ “fall”, not from ‘caedō’ “cut down”, whose perfect ‘cecīdī’ is spelt the same)
glossary.cernam: cernō, -ere — that I may see (1 sg. pres. subj. act. in a purpose clause with ‘uti’)
glossary.cessante: cessō, -āre — idle, holding back (pres. act. part., abl. sg., in an ablative absolute with ‘pectore’)
glossary.charopem: Charops, -opis m. — Charops, a Trojan slain by Ulysses (Greek third-declension acc. sg. in ‑em)
glossary.chersidamante: Chersidamās, -antis m. — Chersidamas, a Trojan slain by Ulysses (abl. sg. with ‘cum’; Greek ‑ās, ‑antis type)
glossary.chromiumque: Chromius, -ī m. — Chromius, a Lycian slain by Ulysses (acc. sg. + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.chrysenque: Chrȳsē, -ēs f. — Chryse, a town of the Troad sacred to Apollo, taken by the Greeks (Greek acc. sg. in ‑en + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.cillan: Cilla, -ae f. — Cilla, a town of the Troad sacred to Apollo (Greek acc. sg. in ‑an)
glossary.cingo: cingō, -ere — I ring, encircle (1 sg. pres. ind. act.; ‘fossas munimine cingo’, of fortifying the camp)
glossary.claroque: clārus, -a, -um — famous, illustrious (abl. sg. m., with ‘Andraemone’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.classem: classis, -is f. — fleet (acc. sg.; boarded by Hecuba at 422, moored on the Thracian shore at 439)
glossary.classi: classis, -is f. — for the fleet (dat. sg. with ‘contraria’, “winds contrary to the fleet”; the form is also the abl. sg.)
glossary.coeranon: Coerānus, -ī m. — Coeranus son of Iphitus, a Lycian slain by Ulysses (Greek acc. sg. in ‑on)
glossary.cognoram: cognōscō, -ere — I had learned, had found out (1 sg. plupf. ind. act., syncopated = cognoveram)
glossary.combiberat: combibō, -ere — had drunk up, had soaked in (3 sg. plupf. ind. act.; of Jove's altar absorbing Priam's blood)
glossary.communicat: commūnicō, -āre — he shares (3 sg. pres. ind. act.; subject Tydides, i.e. Diomedes, sharing his deeds ‘mecum’)
glossary.comparat: comparō, -āre — he matches, sets side by side (3 sg. pres. ind. act. with reflexive ‘se’: “does Ajax match himself with me?”)
glossary.complerunt: compleō, -ēre — they filled (3 pl. perf. ind. act., syncopated = compleverunt)
glossary.comprendere: comprehendō (comprendō), -ere — to take in, to sum up in words (pres. act. inf.; syncopated form)
glossary.concitat: concitō, -āre — stirs up, drives on (3 sg. pres. ind. act.; subject ‘dementia’)
glossary.concreto: concrēscō, -ere — clotted, congealed (perf. part. used adjectivally, abl. sg. m., with ‘sanguine’)
glossary.concussa: concutiō, -ere — shattered, battered down (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. n., with ‘moenia’ in indirect statement after ‘putate’)
glossary.condeturque: condō, -ere — and will be laid to rest, buried (3 sg. fut. ind. pass. + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.confidit: cōnfīdō, -ere — trusts, relies on (3 sg. pres. ind. act.; semi-deponent, taking the abl. ‘socio ... Ulixe’)
glossary.confiteorque: cōnfiteor, -ērī — and I confess, admit (1 sg. pres. ind.; deponent + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.coniunxque: coniūnx, -iugis f. — wife, consort (nom. sg.; here Juno, ‘Iovis coniunx ... sororque’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.conloquiumque: conloquium, -ī n. — a conversation, an interview (acc. sg., object of ‘petit’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.consederat: cōnsīdō, -ere — had settled, had died down (3 sg. plupf. ind. act.; subject ‘ignis’)
glossary.consensistis: cōnsentiō, -īre — you agreed, you consented (2 pl. perf. ind. act.)
glossary.consolor: cōnsōlor, -ārī — I comfort, console (1 sg. pres. ind.; deponent, so active in sense despite the passive ending)
glossary.consuetaque: cōnsuēscō, -ere — familiar, long known (perf. part. used adjectivally, acc. pl. n., with ‘pectora’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.contingent: contingō, -ere — will fall to (your) lot (3 pl. fut. ind. act.; subjects ‘fletus’ and ‘haustus’, with dat. ‘tibi’)
glossary.continuere: contineō, -ēre — they kept themselves in, confined themselves (3 pl. perf. ind. act. = continuerunt; with reflexive ‘se’)
glossary.correpto: corripiō, -ere — seized, laid hold of (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. m., in an ablative absolute — Polymestor once grasped)
glossary.crudelibus: crūdēlis, -e — cruel (dat. pl. f., with ‘aris’ after ‘admota est’, “brought to the cruel altar”; the form is also the abl. pl.)
glossary.cupiasque: cupiō, -ere — and (though) you desire (2 sg. pres. subj. act., concessive under ‘licet’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.curia: cūria, -ae f. — senate-house, council chamber (nom. sg.; the Trojan council which Ulysses entered as envoy)
glossary.cursuque: cursus, -ūs m. — course, running (abl. sg. governed by ‘in’, 4th decl. + enclitic ‘-que’: her grief is still in mid-course)
glossary.damnasse: damnō, -āre — to have condemned (syncopated perf. act. inf. = damnavisse)
glossary.damnatus: damnō, -āre — condemned, found guilty (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m., predicative with ‘quisquam’)
glossary.danaos: Danaī, -ōrum m. pl. — the Danaans, the Greeks (acc. pl.; Homeric name for the besieging army)
glossary.dardanidas: Dardanis, -idis f. — Dardanian, Trojan (Greek acc. pl. in ‑idas, agreeing with ‘matres’; from Dardanus, founder of the Trojan line)
glossary.dardanio: Dardanius, -a, -um — Dardanian, Trojan (abl. sg. m., with ‘vate’ = the captured seer Helenus)
glossary.datique: dō, dare — given, granted (perf. pass. part., gen. sg. n., with ‘sceptri’ + enclitic ‘-que’: the sway of the sceptre conferred on him)
glossary.deberi: dēbeō, -ēre — to be owed, to be due (pres. pass. inf. in indirect statement, with dat. ‘dextrae’)
glossary.deceperat: dēcipiō, -ere — had deceived (3 sg. plupf. ind. act.; subject ‘fallacia vestis’, the trick of the dress)
glossary.decipienda: dēcipiō, -ere — having to be tricked (gerundive, nom. sg. f., with ‘fuit’ in a passive periphrastic: she “had to be deceived”)
glossary.dederam: dō, dare — I had given (1 sg. plupf. ind. act.; ‘vivo dederam’, “I had given them to him alive”)
glossary.dederit: dō, dare — has given, has yielded (3 sg. perf. subj. act. in an indirect question after ‘quid’; the form is also fut. perf. ind.)
glossary.defensore: dēfēnsor, -ōris m. — defender, champion (abl. sg. with ‘cum’; Patroclus in Achilles' armour)
glossary.delenda: dēleō, -ēre — to be destroyed (gerundive, acc. pl. n., with ‘Pergama’: “for the destruction of Troy”)
glossary.delendaque: dēleō, -ēre — to be destroyed (gerundive, acc. pl. n., with ‘Pergama’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.dementia: dēmentia, -ae f. — madness, folly (nom. sg. with interrogative ‘quae’; not the n. pl. of the adjective ‘demens’, which is spelt the same)
glossary.deploratosque: dēplōrō, -āre — bewailed, mourned over (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m., with ‘Priamidas’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.deprensus: dēprehendō (dēprēndō), -ere — caught out, detected (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m., of Achilles unmasked; syncopated form)
glossary.detractare: dētractō (dētrectō), -āre — to disparage, to belittle (pres. act. inf., subject of ‘meum est’)
glossary.devastata: dēvāstō, -āre — laid waste, cut to pieces (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. n., with ‘agmina’)
glossary.devoveas: dēvoveō, -ēre — (though) you curse, devote to the powers below (2 sg. pres. subj. act., concessive under ‘licet’)
glossary.dicet: dīcō, -ere — she will say (3 sg. fut. ind. act.; subject Penelope, displaying Hecuba to the women of Ithaca)
glossary.differtis: differō, -ferre — you put off, you prolong (2 pl. pres. ind. act.; “why do you keep the long-lived old woman waiting?”)
glossary.diroque: dīrus, -a, -um — dread, grim (dat. sg. n., agreeing with ‘busto’ + enclitic ‘-que’; abl. on another construal of the line)
glossary.diruta: dīruō, -ere — overthrown, demolished (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. n., with ‘Pergama’ after ‘post’)
glossary.disceditis: discēdō, -ere — you are departing, sailing away (2 pl. pres. ind. act.; Achilles' shade to the Greeks)
glossary.disertum: disertus, -a, -um — eloquent (acc. sg. m., predicative after ‘fecerat’: grief “had made him eloquent”)
glossary.disertus: disertus, -a, -um — the eloquent man (nom. sg. m., used as a noun of Ulysses, set against ‘fortis vir’, the brave man Ajax)
glossary.distamus: distō, -āre — we stand apart, are distant (1 pl. pres. ind. act.; with acc. of extent ‘totidem gradus’)
glossary.diversasque: dīversus, -a, -um — scattered, lying apart (acc. pl. f., with ‘urbes’ on the shield + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.divisque: dīvus, -ī m. — god (dat. pl. governed by ‘irascitur’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.doceo: doceō, -ēre — I teach, I show (1 sg. pres. ind. act.; governing the indirect question ‘quo ... modo’)
glossary.dolenti: doleō, -ēre — grieving, in pain (pres. act. part., dat. sg. m., agreeing with ‘tibi’)
glossary.dotabere: dōtō, -āre — you will be dowered, given a dowry (2 sg. fut. ind. pass. = dotaberis; bitter irony, “dowered with funerals”)
glossary.dubitas: dubitō, -āre — you hesitate (2 sg. pres. ind. act., with the inf. ‘evertere’)
glossary.ducar: dūcō, -ere — I shall be led, I shall be guided (1 sg. fut. ind. pass.; “I shall be guided by the order of events”)
glossary.ducumque: dux, ducis m. — leader, chieftain (gen. pl. after ‘oblitus’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.dulichiae: Dulichius, -a, -um — of Dulichium, an island of Ulysses' realm, hence “Ulysses'” (nom. pl. f., with ‘manus’)
glossary.duraeque: dūrus, -a, -um — hard, harsh (nom. pl. f., with ‘sortes’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.dure: dūrus, -a, -um — harsh one, unrelenting (voc. sg. m., addressing ‘Philoctete’; not the adverb ‘dure’ “harshly”, spelt the same)
glossary.edideras: ēdō, -ere — you had brought forth, had borne (2 sg. plupf. ind. act.; ‘partu edideras’, of Hecuba bearing Hector)
glossary.edidici: ēdiscō, -ere — I learned thoroughly, I found out (1 sg. perf. ind. act.)
glossary.eiectum: ēiciō, -ere — cast up, thrown ashore (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. n., with ‘corpus’ of Polydorus)
glossary.eloquioque: ēloquium, -ī n. — eloquence, persuasive speech (abl. sg. of means + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.ennomon: Ennomus, -ī m. — Ennomus, a Trojan ally slain by Ulysses (Greek acc. sg. in ‑on)
glossary.erigor: ērigō, -ere — I raise myself up, I rise (1 sg. pres. ind. pass. used in a middle, reflexive sense)
glossary.eripere: ēripiō, -ere — to snatch away, to tear out (pres. act. inf.; ‘eripere aede deam’, of seizing the Palladium)
glossary.euboicam: Euboicus, -a, -um — Euboean (acc. sg. f., with ‘Aulida’; Aulis lies on the strait facing Euboea)
glossary.eurypylusque: Eurypylus, -ī m. — Eurypylus, a Thessalian Greek chief at Troy, named among those who might have claimed the arms (nom. sg. + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.eventuque: ēventus, -ūs m. — outcome, issue (abl. sg., 4th decl. + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.eventus: ēventus, -ūs m. — outcome, fortune (4th decl.; nom. sg. at 278, “what was the outcome of your fight?”, but acc. pl. at 575, ‘eventus ... illos’ “those fortunes”)
glossary.evertere: ēvertō, -ere — to overthrow, to destroy (pres. act. inf. after ‘dubitas’; the spelling is also 3 pl. perf. ind. = everterunt, which is not the reading here)
glossary.excubias: excubiae, -ārum f. pl. — the watch, the sentry-posts (acc. pl. after ‘per’; plural only)
glossary.exiguumque: exiguus, -a, -um — scanty, thin (acc. sg. m., with ‘cruorem’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.exitioque: exitium, -ī n. — destruction, ruin (dat. sg. of purpose with ‘dedi’ + enclitic ‘-que’: “I gave over to destruction”)
glossary.expellitque: expellō, -ere — and drives out, forces out (3 sg. pres. ind. act. + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.expendite: expendō, -ere — weigh, assess (2 pl. pres. imper. act.; ‘meritis expendite causam’, “weigh the case by merits”)
glossary.exsecrere: exsecror, -ārī — (though) you curse (2 sg. pres. subj. = exsecreris; deponent, concessive under ‘licet’)
glossary.exspectata: exspectō, -āre — awaited, long looked for (perf. pass. part., nom. pl. n., with ‘flamina’)
glossary.externasque: externus, -a, -um — foreign, of a strange land (acc. pl. f., with ‘auras’ + enclitic ‘-que’)
glossary.faciendo: faciō, -ere — by making, by bringing it about (gerund, abl. sg. of means: ‘faciendo posse capi’, “by making it possible for Troy to be taken”)
glossary.facite: faciō, -ere — do (it) (2 pl. pres. imper. act.; ‘ne facite’ is a poetic prohibition, “do not do it!”)
glossary.fassoque: fateor, fassus, -a, -um — (to me) having confessed, having owned up (perf. part. of the deponent ‘fateor’, so active in sense; dat. sg. m., indirect object of ‘ignoscat’) + enclitic -que
glossary.fatisque: fātum, -ī n. — fate, destiny, doom (abl. pl., with ‘inmitibus’, abl. of means/agent: driven by pitiless fates) + enclitic -que
glossary.faveat: faveō, favēre — may she favour, be favourable to (+ dat.) (3 sg. pres. subj. act., optative in the parenthesis ‘faveat Fortuna!’)
glossary.fecimus: faciō, facere — we made, we did (1 pl. perf. indic. act.; here of ancestry — “things we did not make ourselves”)
glossary.ferantur: ferō, ferre — let them be carried, taken (3 pl. pres. subj. pass., jussive; subject ‘haec [arma]’)
glossary.fertis: ferō, ferre — you carry, bring, take home (2 pl. pres. indic. act.; addressed to the fleeing Greeks)
glossary.fidelem: fidēlis, -e — loyal, faithful (acc. sg. m./f., predicate to the infinitive ‘esse’ in ‘cum sit satis esse fidelem’, its subject the indefinite “one”)
glossary.figentem: fīgō, fīgere — fixing, fastening (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m., agreeing with Neoptolemus: fixing his eyes on her face)
glossary.flatuque: flātus, -ūs m. — blast, blowing, breeze (abl. sg., 4th decl., abl. abs. with ‘secundo’: with a following wind) + enclitic -que
glossary.flens: fleō, flēre — weeping (pres. act. part., nom. sg. m., agreeing with ‘sacerdos’)
glossary.fluet: fluō, fluere — will flow (3 sg. fut. indic. act.; of the Simois running backwards in an adynaton)
glossary.foedataque: foedō, foedāre — befouled, defiled (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., agreeing with the subject Hecuba, not with ‘manus’, which as accusative plural would require foedatas) + enclitic -que
glossary.fortemque: fortis, -e — the brave man (acc. sg. m., adjective used as a noun, object of ‘misi’; contrast the neut. pl. ‘fortia’ in the same line) + enclitic -que
glossary.fovebat: foveō, fovēre — she was cherishing, was holding warm (3 sg. impf. indic. act.; subject the mother, object ‘quam’ = Polyxena)
glossary.fueritque: sum, esse — let him have been, granted he was (3 sg. perf. subj. act., concessive/jussive: “and let Ajax have been the more generous”; the same form can be fut. perf., but the jussive suits the surrounding imperative ‘negate’) + enclitic -que
glossary.gemenda: gemō, gemere — to be lamented, needing to be mourned (gerundive, nom. sg. f., agreeing with ‘vita’ in ‘vita gemenda est’)
glossary.genetrici: genetrīx, -īcis f. — to the mother, to her who bore him (dat. sg., indirect object of ‘reddite’; Hecuba)
glossary.geris: gerō, gerere — you bear, carry (2 sg. pres. indic. act.; Ulysses to Ajax, ‘tu vires sine mente geris’)
glossary.gestasset: gestō, gestāre — he would have carried, borne (3 sg. pluperf. subj. act., syncopated from gestavisset; apodosis of a past contrary-to-fact condition after ‘nisi fecissem’)
glossary.graecia: Graecia, -ae f. — Greece, the Greek nation collectively (nom. sg., subject of ‘mandarat’; ‘communis Graecia’, Greece acting as one)
glossary.grai: Grāī, -ōrum m. pl. — the Greeks (nom. pl., subject of ‘trahunt’; poetic byform of Graecī)
glossary.graiorum: Grāī, -ōrum m. pl. — of the Greeks (gen. pl., partitive with ‘unum’: one out of so many thousands of Greeks)
glossary.graios: Grāī, -ōrum m. pl. — the Greeks (acc. pl., object of the preposition ‘ad’: back to the Greek camp)
glossary.graium: Grāī, -ōrum m. pl. — of the Greeks (gen. pl., contracted poetic form for Graiorum, with ‘murus’: Achilles, the wall of the Greeks; not acc. sg. of the adjective Graius here)
glossary.habitata: habitō, habitāre — inhabited, lived in (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., agreeing with ‘tellus’; ‘Bistoniis habitata viris’ = peopled by Thracians)
glossary.haliumque: Halius, -ī m. — Halius, one of the Lycian/Trojan warriors Ulysses claims to have killed (acc. sg., in a list of victims) + enclitic -que
glossary.hastamque: hasta, -ae f. — spear (acc. sg., object of ‘tenenti’, paired with ‘parmam’: the arms Achilles seized among the girls’ wares) + enclitic -que
glossary.haurire: hauriō, haurīre — to drain, drink up, draw off (pres. act. inf., complement of ‘cupiasque’: that you drink our blood)
glossary.hecubam: Hecubē, -ēs f. — Hecuba, queen of Troy, wife of Priam (acc. sg. formed on the Latin 1st-decl. byform Hecuba; subject-accusative of ‘meruisse’)
glossary.hecube: Hecubē, -ēs f. — Hecuba, queen of Troy, wife of Priam and mother of Hector and Polyxena (Greek 1st decl.; nom. sg. at XIII.423 and 549, but vocative sg. at 556 where Polymestor addresses her: ‘tolle moras, Hecube’)
glossary.helenamque: Helena, -ae f. — Helen, wife of Menelaus, carried off by Paris (acc. sg., object of ‘reposco’: Ulysses demands her back on the embassy to Troy) + enclitic -que
glossary.hellespontus: Hellēspontus, -ī m. — the Hellespont, the long narrow strait between Troy’s shore and the Chersonese (nom. sg., subject of ‘clauditur’)
glossary.hortanda: hortor, hortārī — needing to be urged on (gerundive, nom. sg. f., agreeing with the antecedent of ‘quae’ = Achilles’ mother Thetis, with ‘fuit’: she had to be tricked, not exhorted; from a deponent verb, but the gerundive is passive)
glossary.hostesque: hostis, -is m. — enemies (acc. pl., object of ‘moverat’, in apposition to ‘Pelasgos’: her fate moved even her enemies) + enclitic -que
glossary.hostia: hostia, -ae f. — sacrificial victim, offering (nom. sg., predicate nominative with ‘fit’: Polyxena becomes a victim at the tomb)
glossary.hypsipyles: Hypsipylē, -ēs f. — Hypsipyle, queen of Lemnos, daughter of Thoas, who spared her father when the Lemnian women killed their menfolk (gen. sg., Greek 1st decl. in -ēs; ‘Hypsipyles patriam’ = Lemnos)
glossary.ibit: eō, īre — he will go (3 sg. fut. indic. act.; ‘melius Telamonius ibit’, Ulysses’ mock deference to Ajax)
glossary.idomeneus: Idomeneus, -eī m. — Idomeneus, king of Crete and one of the leading Greek commanders at Troy (nom. sg., Greek 2nd decl.; here named among the brave men who did not claim the arms)
glossary.ignoscat: ignōscō, ignōscere — let him pardon, forgive (+ dat. of the person) (3 sg. pres. subj. act., jussive; subject ‘Atrides’, with ‘fassoque’ supplying its dative object)
glossary.iliacas: Īliacus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Ilium (acc. pl. f., agreeing with ‘arces’: to the citadel of Troy)
glossary.immergitque: immergō, immergere — and he/she plunges in, sinks in (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; subject Hecuba, object ‘manus’; note the assimilated spelling here beside the unassimilated inm- of ‘inmiti’ nearby) + enclitic -que
glossary.impendit: impendō, impendere — he expends, lays out, spends (3 sg. pres. indic. act., matching the present ‘habet’ in the next line; the identical form can be 3 sg. perf., “he spent”, and either reading works with ‘per tot … annos’)
glossary.incepti: incipiō, incipere — begun, undertaken (perf. pass. part., gen. sg. n., agreeing with ‘belli’: the war already begun)
glossary.incessere: incessō, incessere — to assail, attack, harry (pres. act. inf., complement of ‘ausus erat’ at XIII.232 and of ‘coepit’ at 566; the same spelling could be a 3 pl. perf. in -ēre, but both occurrences here depend on a governing verb and are infinitives)
glossary.incripta: īnscrībō, īnscrībere — inscribed, written on (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., agreeing with ‘littera’; the archived spelling is defective — it has lost the s of the expected form inscripta and is not a Latin word)
glossary.indomitae: indomitus, -a, -um — untamed, unsubdued (gen. sg. f. with ‘dextrae’, the possessor of the ‘praemia’; the same form can be dat. sg. or nom. pl. f., but ‘praemia indomitae dextrae’ makes it genitive)
glossary.indueret: induō, induere — should put on, should don (3 sg. impf. subj. act., in the indignant purpose clause ‘idcirco … ut … indueret?’)
glossary.inemptum: inēmptus, -a, -um — unbought, not paid for (acc. sg. n., agreeing with ‘corpus’: give her the body without a ransom)
glossary.infestus: īnfestus, -a, -um — hostile, bent on harm (nom. sg. m., predicate with ‘sis licet’: though you be hostile)
glossary.infixum: īnfīgō, īnfīgere — driven in, fixed fast (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. n., agreeing with ‘telum’)
glossary.inhonestaque: inhonestus, -a, -um — dishonourable, shameful (acc. pl. n., agreeing with ‘vela’: the shameful sails of flight) + enclitic -que
glossary.iniecique: iniciō, inicere — and I laid on, threw on (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; ‘iniecique manum’, a legal-sounding phrase for laying claim to Achilles) + enclitic -que
glossary.iniquo: inīquus, -a, -um — unfair, hostile, ill-disposed (abl. sg. m., with ‘iudice’ in the abl. abs. phrase ‘sub iniquo iudice’)
glossary.iniustum: iniūstus, -a, -um — unjust (acc. sg. m., agreeing with ‘Agamemnona’: the day Achilles went for the unjust Agamemnon with his sword)
glossary.inmiti: immītis, -e — pitiless, harsh (3rd-decl. adj.; dat. sg. f. at XIII.449, governed by ‘parentibus’, since the verb pareo takes the dative, and agreeing with ‘umbrae’; abl. sg. m. at XIII.532, agreeing with ‘sanguine’)
glossary.inmunemque: immūnis, -e — having no share in, exempt from (+ gen.) (acc. sg. f., agreeing with ‘arcton’: the Bear that never dips into the sea) + enclitic -que
glossary.insidior: īnsidior, īnsidiārī — I lie in ambush for, set traps for (+ dat.) (1 sg. pres. indic. of a deponent verb, so active in sense despite the passive ending; object ‘hostibus’)
glossary.insons: īnsōns, -ontis — guiltless, innocent (of, + gen.) (nom. sg. m., 3rd decl.; ‘fraterni sanguinis insons’, a jab at Telamon, who killed his brother Phocus)
glossary.intelligit: intellegō, intellegere — he understands (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; the archived spelling with -i- is the later variant of intellegit)
glossary.interimo: interimō, interimere — I kill, do away with (1 sg. pres. indic. act., historic present in Ulysses’ narrative of killing Dolon)
glossary.interritus: interritus, -a, -um — undaunted, unterrified (nom. sg. m., agreeing with the subject of ‘egi’, Ulysses himself)
glossary.intrepidos: intrepidus, -a, -um — unflinching, not trembling (acc. pl. m., agreeing with ‘vultus’: Polyxena kept her looks unflinching to the end)
glossary.introrsus: intrōrsus — inwards, within (adverb; with ‘obortas’, of tears welling up but swallowed inside)
glossary.inventus: inveniō, invenīre — found out, discovered (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m., agreeing with ‘Achilles’: the arms by which Achilles was detected among the girls)
glossary.iphitiden: Īphitidēs, -ae m. — son of Iphitus, patronymic of Coeranus, a Greek killed in Ulysses’ list of victims (acc. sg. in the Greek 1st-decl. ending -en, in apposition to ‘Coeranon’)
glossary.iraque: īra, -ae f. — anger, rage (abl. sg., with ‘morbis’, cause of ‘furentem’: Philoctetes raving from his disease and his anger) + enclitic -que
glossary.irascitur: īrāscor, īrāscī — he grows angry at (+ dat.) (3 sg. pres. indic. of a deponent verb; object ‘divisque … ipsis’)
glossary.ismario: Ismarius, -a, -um — Ismarian, i.e. Thracian, from Mt Ismarus in Thrace (dat. sg. m., agreeing with ‘regi’ = Polymestor, to whom Polydorus was sent)
glossary.ithacis: Ithacus, -a, -um — Ithacan, of Ithaca, Ulysses’ island (dat. pl. f., agreeing with ‘matribus’: the Ithacan mothers to whom Penelope will display her captive)
glossary.ituros: eō, īre — those about to go, men on the point of leaving (fut. act. part. of ‘eo’, acc. pl. m., used as a noun, object of ‘remoratur’)
glossary.iuguloque: iugulum, -ī n. — throat (dat. sg. of the goal with ‘demisit’, a poetic construction where prose would use in + acc.; the form could equally be read as abl. sg.) + enclitic -que
glossary.iugulumque: iugulum, -ī n. — throat (acc. sg., object of ‘retexit’: Polyxena bares throat and breast together) + enclitic -que
glossary.iunctum: iungō, iungere — joined, allied (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. m., agreeing with ‘Antenora’: Antenor, joined to Priam)
glossary.iurantem: iūrō, iūrāre — swearing (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m., agreeing with the understood object Polymestor, with ‘falsaque’ as internal accusative: swearing false oaths)
glossary.laboro: labōrō, labōrāre — I strive, take pains, exert myself (1 sg. pres. indic. act.; ‘ferre laboro’, I struggle to carry — not here “I am ill”)
glossary.lactente: lactēns, -entis — sucking, still at the teat (pres. part. of the verb lacteo used as an adjective, abl. sg. m., agreeing with ‘catulo’ in an abl. of separation with ‘orbata’)
glossary.laertes: Lāertēs, -ae m. — Laertes, father of Ulysses and son of Arcesius (nom. sg., Greek 1st decl.; cited by Ulysses to trace his own descent from Jupiter)
glossary.laniato: laniō, laniāre — torn, mangled (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. n., agreeing with ‘pectore’ in an abl. abs.: with her breast torn in mourning)
glossary.lapidumque: lapis, -idis m. — of stones (gen. pl., with ‘telorum’ depending on ‘iactu’: an assault with a hurling of spears and stones) + enclitic -que
glossary.latravit: lātrō, lātrāre — she barked (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; the moment of Hecuba’s metamorphosis into a dog)
glossary.laudatve: laudō, laudāre — praises (3 sg. pres. indic. act.) + enclitic -ve “or”, paired with ‘petitve’
glossary.letalem: lētālis, -e — deadly, death-dealing (acc. sg. m., agreeing with ‘ensem’: Ajax buries the fatal sword in his breast)
glossary.levabas: levō, levāre — you were relieving, easing (2 sg. impf. indic. act.; Hecuba to Polyxena, ‘quae sola levabas maternos luctus’)
glossary.luctusque: lūctus, -ūs m. — grief, mourning (nom. sg., 4th decl., one of the subjects of ‘tardarunt’ alongside ‘lacrimae’ and ‘timorque’; the form is also gen. sg. and nom./acc. pl., but here it is the nominative singular) + enclitic -que
glossary.lycii: Lycius, -a, -um — Lycian, of Lycia in Asia Minor, allied to Troy (gen. sg. m., agreeing with ‘Sarpedonis’, the Lycian king; not nom. pl. here)
glossary.mactata: mactō, mactāre — sacrificed, slaughtered as an offering (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., agreeing with ‘Polyxena’: let Polyxena, once sacrificed, appease the shade)
glossary.madebit: madeō, madēre — it will be wet, will drip (3 sg. fut. indic. act.; subject the sword, ‘domini nunc caede madebit’)
glossary.maduit: madeō, madēre — it was wet, dripped (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; the sword often soaked with Phrygian blood)
glossary.magnanimo: magnanimus, -a, -um — great-souled, high-hearted (dat. sg. m., agreeing with ‘Achilli’, object of ‘maledicere’)
glossary.maioris: māior, māius — greater, elder (comparative of magnus; gen. sg. m., agreeing with ‘Atridae’ = Agamemnon, the elder son of Atreus, whose ‘frater’ is Menelaus)
glossary.maligne: malignē — grudgingly, stintingly (adverb formed from the adjective malignus, with ‘detractare’: it is not my way to belittle good deeds grudgingly; not a vocative here)
glossary.mandarat: mandō, mandāre — she had entrusted, commissioned (3 sg. pluperf. indic. act., syncopated from mandaverat; subject ‘Graecia’, with double accusative ‘mihi … causam’)
glossary.mandate: mandō, mandāre — entrust, commit (2 pl. pres. imperative act.; with ‘ne’ in ‘ne mandate mihi’, the poetic prohibition by ne + imperative where prose would use nolite + infinitive)
glossary.maneret: maneō, manēre — she remained, were still (3 sg. impf. subj. act., in the unreal comparison ‘tamquam regina maneret’: as though she were still a queen)
glossary.maternos: māternus, -a, -um — of a mother, motherly (acc. pl. m., agreeing with ‘luctus’, 4th-decl. acc. pl.: a mother’s griefs)
glossary.matribus: māter, mātris f. — to the mothers (dat. pl., indirect object of ‘ostendens’, with ‘Ithacis’: showing her off to the mothers of Ithaca)
glossary.maturior: mātūrus, -a, -um — earlier, more timely (comparative, nom. sg. m., predicate with ‘sum’: I came to the war sooner than he did)
glossary.meique: ego — of me (gen. sg. of the personal pronoun, objective genitive with ‘oblitus’, in the series ‘regisque ducumque meique’; not nom. pl. of ‘meus’) + enclitic -que
glossary.menelae: Menelāus, -ī m. — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon and husband of Helen (voc. sg.; Ulysses turns aside to address him as a witness, ‘scis hoc, Menelae’)
glossary.mercibus: merx, mercis f. — wares, goods for sale (abl. pl., with ‘femineis’, place where: Ulysses slipped the weapons in among the women’s wares)
glossary.meriones: Mērionēs, -ae m. — Meriones, Cretan warrior and squire of Idomeneus, one of the foremost Greek fighters (nom. sg., Greek 1st decl. in -ēs; subject with ‘Idomeneus’ of ‘peteret’)
glossary.metuis: metuō, metuere — you are afraid (2 sg. pres. indic. act.; Ulysses taunting Ajax, ‘cur hic metuis?’)
glossary.mihique: ego — to me, for me (dat. sg. of the personal pronoun, with ‘infestus’: hostile to your allies, to the king, and to me) + enclitic -que
glossary.minimus: parvus, -a, -um — youngest, smallest (superlative ‘minimus’, nom. sg. m.; of Polydorus, once the youngest of Priam’s male line)
glossary.minuitque: minuō, minuere — and she lessens, diminishes (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; subject ‘mater’, object ‘gaudia’) + enclitic -que
glossary.mittitur: mittō, mittere — he is sent, is flung (3 sg. pres. indic. pass.; of Astyanax thrown from the towers — the passive is grimly literal here)
glossary.mittor: mittō, mittere — I am sent (1 sg. pres. indic. pass.; the refrain of Ulysses’ catalogue of missions, three times in this speech)
glossary.moderatior: moderātus, -a, -um — more restrained, more self-controlled (comparative, nom. sg. m., agreeing with ‘Aiax’ in the ironic ‘peteret moderatior Aiax’)
glossary.molliet: molliō, mollīre — he will soften, will soothe (3 sg. fut. indic. act.; of talking Philoctetes round)
glossary.monstrare: mōnstrō, mōnstrāre — to point out, to show (pres. act. inf., in indirect statement after ‘se … velle’: that she wanted to show him where the gold was left)
glossary.monstratum: mōnstrō, mōnstrāre — pointed out, shown (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. m., agreeing with ‘patrem’: the father pointed out by his mother; not the supine here)
glossary.monumentis: monumentum, -ī n. — tomb, memorial (abl. pl., with ‘avitis’, place where: your body will be laid in ancestral tombs)
glossary.morbis: morbus, -ī m. — disease, sickness (abl. pl., cause with ‘furentem’: Philoctetes raving from his afflictions)
glossary.murus: mūrus, -ī m. — wall, rampart (nom. sg., in apposition to ‘Achilles’: Achilles, the wall of the Greeks)
glossary.natisque: nātus, -ī m. — sons, children (dat. pl. at XIII.489, with ‘patriae … viroque’ as recipients of ‘dederat’; abl. pl. at XIII.509 in the series with ‘potens’: powerful in her sons) + enclitic -que
glossary.nefandas: nefandus, -a, -um — unspeakable, abominable (acc. pl. f., agreeing with ‘manus’: the wicked hands that Menelaus barely held back)
glossary.negaverit: negō, negāre — would deny, could deny (3 sg. perf. subj. act. in the result clause ‘sic omnes, ut … negaverit’; subject Juno, ‘Iovis coniunxque sororque’; the same form can be fut. perf. indic.)
glossary.neoptolemum: Neoptolemus, -ī m. — Neoptolemus, son of Achilles, who sacrifices Polyxena at his father’s tomb (acc. sg., object of ‘vidit’)
glossary.nequeam: nequeō, nequīre — I am unable, I cannot (1 sg. pres. subj. act. in the conditional ‘si iam nequeam defendere’; irregular verb conjugated like ‘eo’)
glossary.nereia: Nērēius, -a, -um — Nereid, of Nereus, daughter of the sea-god (nom. sg. f., agreeing with ‘genetrix’ = Thetis, mother of Achilles)
glossary.nitidumque: nitidus, -a, -um — shining, bright (acc. sg. m., agreeing with ‘ensem’: the bright sword of Orion figured on Achilles’ shield) + enclitic -que
glossary.nocentem: noceō, nocēre — doing harm, guilty (pres. act. part. used as an adjective, acc. sg. f. here, agreeing with the understood Hecuba: her rage makes her the guilty one)
glossary.noemonaque: Noēmōn, -onis m. — Noemon, one of the warriors Ulysses claims to have killed (acc. sg. in the Greek 3rd-decl. ending -a for Latin -em) + enclitic -que
glossary.nonus: nōnus, -a, -um — ninth (ordinal, nom. sg. m.; Ajax was ninth to come forward for the duel with Hector, and won it only by lot)
glossary.nosti: nōscō, nōscere — you know (2 sg. perf. indic. act., syncopated from novisti; the perfect of this verb, “you have come to know”, has present force)
glossary.nostrique: nōs — of us (gen. pl. of the personal pronoun, objective genitive with ‘orbator’: the man who bereaved us; not a form of the possessive noster here) + enclitic -que
glossary.nostrumque: noster, -tra, -trum — our (acc. sg. m., agreeing with ‘cruorem’; distinct from the identical-looking gen. pl. of nos) + enclitic -que
glossary.nuribusque: nurus, -ūs f. — daughters-in-law (abl. pl., 4th decl., in the series with ‘natisque … viroque’ describing Hecuba’s former power) + enclitic -que
glossary.obiecta: obiciō, obicere — the charges laid against him (perf. pass. part., nom. pl. n., used as a noun and subject of ‘patebant’; the same form can be nom./abl. sg. f.)
glossary.obmutuit: obmūtēscō, obmūtēscere — she fell silent, was struck dumb (3 sg. perf. indic. act. of an inceptive verb: the perfect gives the moment of falling silent)
glossary.obrutaque: obruō, obruere — buried, overwhelmed (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., agreeing with ‘gratia’ in ‘obrutaque est’) + enclitic -que
glossary.occupet: occupō, occupāre — he should seize first, monopolise (3 sg. pres. subj. act. in the negative purpose clause ‘ne communia solus occupet’)
glossary.oceanum: Ōceanus, -ī m. — Ocean, the encircling stream at the rim of the world (acc. sg., object of ‘novit’; one of the figures on Achilles’ shield)
glossary.oebalio: Oebalius, -a, -um — Oebalian, i.e. Spartan, from Oebalus, an early king of Sparta (abl. sg. n., agreeing with ‘vulnere’: the flower born earlier from the Spartan boy Hyacinthus’ wound)
glossary.orantemque: ōrō, ōrāre — pleading, begging (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m., agreeing with the understood Telephus alongside ‘victum’) + enclitic -que
glossary.orator: ōrātor, -ōris m. — spokesman, envoy, ambassador (nom. sg., in apposition to the subject of ‘mittor’; the noun, not a verb form of ‘oro’)
glossary.orbata: orbō, orbāre — bereaved, robbed (of, + abl.) (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., agreeing with ‘leaena’: a lioness robbed of her suckling cub)
glossary.orbator: orbātor, -ōris m. — bereaver, one who robs a parent of children (nom. sg., in apposition to ‘Achilles’; a rare agent noun coined to the verb orbo)
glossary.ostentare: ostentō, ostentāre — to parade, keep displaying (pres. act. inf., complement of ‘desine’; frequentative of ostendo)
glossary.pacatum: pācō, pācāre — calmed, at peace (perf. pass. part. used as an adjective, nom. sg. n., predicate with the understood ‘esset’ and agreeing with ‘mare’)
glossary.palameden: Palamēdēs, -is m. — Palamedes, the Greek who exposed Ulysses’ feigned madness and was destroyed by him on a forged charge of treason (acc. sg. in the Greek ending -en, subject-accusative of ‘accusasse’)
glossary.parares: parō, parāre — you were making ready (2 sg. impf. subj. act. in the ‘cum’ circumstantial clause: when you were rigging the sails of flight)
glossary.parato: parō, parāre — made ready, prepared (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. m., agreeing with ‘rictuque’: her jaws set for words; not the future imperative of the same verb)
glossary.parentibus: pāreō, pārēre — obeying (+ dat.) (pres. act. part., abl. pl. m., agreeing with ‘sociis’ in an ablative absolute: his comrades obeying the pitiless shade; not the noun ‘parens’, parent, which has the same form in the dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.paris: Paris, -idis m. — Paris, son of Priam, whose abduction of Helen caused the war (nom. sg., subject of the clause; not the gen. sg. of the adjective par nor a form of the verb paro)
glossary.paruit: pāreō, pārēre — he obeyed (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; of Philoctetes taking Ulysses’ advice — from pareo, “obey”, not from pario, whose perfect would be peperit)
glossary.passum: patior, patī — having suffered, having endured (perf. part. of a deponent verb, so active in sense; acc. sg. n., agreeing with ‘pectus’ and taking the internal accusative ‘vulnera’: the breast that only now suffered wounds; not from pando, nor the noun passus)
glossary.patebant: pateō, patēre — they lay open, were plain to see (3 pl. impf. indic. act.; subject ‘obiecta’: the charges were exposed by the planted gold)
glossary.patriorum: patrius, -a, -um — ancestral, of the fathers (gen. pl. m., agreeing with ‘deorum’: the emblems of their ancestral gods)
glossary.pelasga: Pelasgus, -a, -um — Pelasgian, i.e. Greek (abl. sg. f., agreeing with ‘classe’: in defence of the Greek fleet)
glossary.pelasgos: Pelasgī, -ōrum m. pl. — the Pelasgians, an old poetic name for the Greeks (acc. pl., in apposition to ‘hostes’: her Trojans and her enemies the Greeks alike)
glossary.penelopae: Pēnelopē, -ēs f. — Penelope, wife of Ulysses, to whom Hecuba is carried off as a prize (dat. sg. of the recipient with ‘munus’, “a gift for Penelope”; the 1st-decl. form is equally possessive gen. sg., “Penelope’s gift”)
glossary.penetrale: penetrālis, -e — of the inner shrine, kept in the sanctuary (acc. sg. n., agreeing with ‘signum’: the Palladium stolen from Minerva’s inmost shrine; here the adjective, not the noun ‘penetrale’, sanctuary)
glossary.pensandum: pēnsō, pēnsāre — to be weighed against, to be paid in return for (gerundive, acc. sg. m., agreeing with ‘titulum’ in ‘reddite’ + predicate gerundive)
glossary.penset: pēnsō, pēnsāre — he may weigh out, pay for (3 sg. pres. subj. act. in the purpose clause ‘ut … penset’: that he buy glory with blood)
glossary.peperi: pariō, parere — I bore, I brought forth (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; Hecuba’s bitter point — she gave birth only to produce offerings for the enemy)
glossary.perdiderim: perdō, perdere — I should have lost, destroyed (1 sg. perf. subj. act. in the negative purpose clause ‘et ne perdiderim quemquam sine caede’)
glossary.peremptam: perimō, perimere — killed, destroyed (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f., agreeing with ‘te’ = Polyxena, object of the following verb)
glossary.petendum: petō, petere — to be sought, needing to be attempted (gerundive, nom. sg. n., agreeing with ‘siquid’ in the impersonal ‘petendum est’)
glossary.petitve: petō, petere — or seeks, or asks for (3 sg. pres. indic. act. + enclitic -ve “or”; XIII.238 ‘quis te laudatve petitve?’, of asking for a man's help)
glossary.philoctete: Philoctētēs, -ae m. — Philoctetes, the archer of Heracles' bow whom the Greeks marooned on Lemnos on Ulysses' advice (Greek voc. sg. in -e; Ulysses addresses him at XIII.329)
glossary.phrygiisque: Phrygius, -a, -um — and from Phrygian, i.e. Trojan (n. abl. pl. agreeing with ‘armis’, + ‘-que’; Phrygian = Trojan throughout these books)
glossary.phthiam: Phthīa, -ae f. — Phthia, Achilles' homeland in Thessaly, seat of his father Peleus (acc. sg.; acc. of place to which, without a preposition)
glossary.piasti: piō, piāre — you appeased, made atonement to (2 sg. perf. indic. act., syncopated from piavisti; Hecuba to the dead Polyxena, whose sacrifice appeased Achilles' pyre)
glossary.placabitis: plācō, plācāre — you will appease, placate (2 pl. fut. indic. act.; Polyxena tells the Greeks no god is appeased by such a rite)
glossary.placare: plācō, plācāre — to appease, placate (pres. inf. act., complementing ‘paratis’)
glossary.plangit: plangō, plangere — beats, strikes in mourning (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; the ritual beating of the breast in grief)
glossary.pleiadasque: Plēiades, -um f. pl. — and the Pleiades, the seven-star cluster shown on Achilles' shield (Greek acc. pl. in -as, + ‘-que’)
glossary.poeantiaden: Poeantiadēs, -ae m. — the son of Poeas, i.e. Philoctetes (Greek patronymic, acc. sg. in -en; object of ‘habet’, the man Lemnos holds)
glossary.polydore: Polydōrus, -ī m. — Polydorus, Priam's youngest son, sent secretly to Thrace for safekeeping and murdered there (voc. sg.; the narrator turns to address him)
glossary.polydori: Polydōrus, -ī m. — of Polydorus (gen. sg., with ‘corpus’: his body cast up on the shore)
glossary.polydorus: Polydōrus, -ī m. — Polydorus (nom. sg.; subject of the clause in which Hecuba names her last surviving son)
glossary.polymestora: Polymēstōr, -oris m. — Polymestor, the Thracian king who took in Polydorus and killed him for his gold (Greek acc. sg. in -a; in apposition, the author of the murder)
glossary.polymestoris: Polymēstōr, -oris m. — of Polymestor (gen. sg., with ‘regia’: his rich palace in Thrace)
glossary.polyxena: Polyxena, -ae f. — Polyxena, daughter of Priam and Hecuba, sacrificed at Achilles' tomb (nom. sg. in both places: subject with ‘mactata’ at XIII.448 and with ‘vellem’ at 460)
glossary.poscat: poscō, poscere — let him demand, may he demand (3 sg. pres. subj. act.; jussive, ironically inviting Ajax to demand Troy's destruction)
glossary.potiar: potior, potīrī — may I gain possession of, win (1 sg. pres. subj. dep., with abl. ‘sagittis’; the deponent regularly takes the ablative)
glossary.potiora: potior, -ius — more powerful, worth more (n. nom. pl. comparative, predicate with ‘pectora’ — heart counts for more than hand)
glossary.praebita: praebeō, praebēre — offered, held out (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. agreeing with ‘praecordia’: the breast Polyxena offered to the knife)
glossary.praecipitique: praeceps, -cipitis — and from the sheer, the headlong, i.e. perilous action (n. abl. sg. of the adjective used as a noun, after ‘ex’, + ‘-que’)
glossary.praedaeque: praeda, -ae f. — and of plunder (gen. sg. with ‘amore’, “by love of plunder”; not dat., though the form is shared)
glossary.praedamque: praeda, -ae f. — and the plunder, the stolen goods (acc. sg. + ‘-que’; the property Paris carried off with Helen)
glossary.praelatus: praeferō, praeferre — preferred, put ahead (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.; Ajax was ninth in line of duty and got his place by the favour of the lot)
glossary.prensantem: prēnsō, prēnsāre — clutching, gripping (pres. act. part., f. acc. sg.; frequentative of prehendō; Hecuba clinging to her sons' tombs, dragged off by Ulysses' men)
glossary.pretioque: pretium, -ī n. — and by the bribe, the price paid (abl. sg. + ‘-que’; the gold that proved the charge against Palamedes)
glossary.priameia: Priamēius, -a, -um — of Priam, Priam's (f. nom. sg. with ‘coniunx’: Hecuba, Priam's wife; a Greek-style patronymic adjective)
glossary.priami: Priamus, -ī m. — of Priam, last king of Troy (gen. sg.; with ‘cruorem’ at XIII.409 and with ‘filia regis’ at 470)
glossary.priamidas: Priamidēs, -ae m. — the sons of Priam (Greek patronymic, acc. pl. in -as; the Trojan women count over the slain princes)
glossary.priamoque: Priamus, -ī m. — and to Priam (dat. sg. + ‘-que’, governed by ‘iunctum’: Antenor, joined to Priam)
glossary.priamum: Priamus, -ī m. — Priam (acc. sg.; object of ‘moveo’ at XIII.201 and subject-accusative of ‘dici’ at 520)
glossary.proavitaque: proavītus, -a, -um — and ancestral, of his forefathers (n. acc. pl. with ‘regna’, + ‘-que’; the realm Hector defended)
glossary.proavos: proavus, -ī m. — forefathers, great-grandfathers (acc. pl.; Ulysses dismisses inherited ancestry as no merit of one's own)
glossary.procubuere: prōcumbō, prōcumbere — they fell, sank down (3 pl. perf. indic. act. with the alternative ending -ēre for -ērunt; of enemies felled by Ulysses' hand)
glossary.procubuisse: prōcumbō, prōcumbere — to have fallen, collapsed (perf. inf. act., with acc. subject ‘moenia’ in indirect statement)
glossary.prodes: prōsum, prōdesse — you are of use, you help (2 sg. pres. indic. act.; irregular compound of ‘sum’, with -d- before a vowel)
glossary.producet: prōdūcō, prōdūcere — he will draw out, bring along (3 sg. fut. indic. act.; ironic — Ajax will coax Philoctetes back by some clever art)
glossary.profecturas: prōficiō, prōficere — going to avail, destined to do good (fut. act. part., f. acc. pl. with ‘palmas’, negated: hands stretched out in vain)
glossary.proiecerat: prōiciō, prōicere — he had thrown off, cast aside (3 sg. pluperf. indic. act.; Achilles had not yet cast off his girl's clothes)
glossary.promittet: prōmittō, prōmittere — will promise (3 sg. fut. indic. act.; in the string of adynata — impossibilities — that must happen first)
glossary.proposita: prōpōnō, prōpōnere — set forth, displayed as a prize (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. with ‘arma’: the arms put up for the contest)
glossary.protervus: protervus, -a, -um — insolent, brazen (m. nom. sg., predicative of Thersites: insolent, and not unpunished, thanks to Ulysses)
glossary.prytanimque: Prytanis, -is m. — and Prytanis, a Lycian killed by Ulysses in the Iliad's night of slaughter (Greek acc. sg. in -im, + ‘-que’)
glossary.puduitque: pudet, pudēre — and it shamed me, and I was ashamed (3 sg. perf. indic. act. of an impersonal verb, + ‘-que’; the person ashamed stands in the acc., here understood)
glossary.pueroque: puer, -ī m. — and to the boy (dat. sg. + ‘-que’, with ‘communis’: the letters AI shared by the boy Hyacinthus and the hero Ajax)
glossary.pugnacem: pugnāx, -ācis — the fighter, the man good at fighting (m. acc. sg. of the adjective used as a noun; subject-accusative of ‘esse’ in indirect statement)
glossary.pugnandi: pugnō, pugnāre — of fighting (gen. sg. of the gerund, with ‘tempora’: the times for fighting)
glossary.pugnavimus: pugnō, pugnāre — we fought (1 pl. perf. indic. act.; the Greeks joined open battle only in the tenth year)
glossary.pugnet: pugnō, pugnāre — let him fight (3 sg. pres. subj. act.; jussive, taunting Ajax to do the one thing he can)
glossary.putate: putō, putāre — reckon, consider (2 pl. pres. imperat. act.; Ulysses tells the chiefs to credit those cities to his hand)
glossary.putatis: putō, putāre — you think, you suppose (2 pl. pres. indic. act., in the protasis ‘si ... putatis’)
glossary.pyrrhus: Pyrrhus, -ī m. — Pyrrhus (Neoptolemus), son of Achilles, who would have the nearer claim to the arms by kinship (nom. sg.)
glossary.quaeratur: quaerō, quaerere — let it be sought, be looked for (3 sg. pres. subj. pass.; jussive: let merit, not blood, be the test)
glossary.quidve: quis, quid — or what (n. acc. sg. of the interrogative + enclitic -ve “or”; XIII.227 “or what do you bring home?”, XIII.517 “or why do I delay?”)
glossary.rapimur: rapiō, rapere — we are carried off, dragged away (1 pl. pres. indic. pass.; the cry of the captive Trojan women as the ships sail)
glossary.rapui: rapiō, rapere — I snatched, seized (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; of stealing the Palladium from the middle of the enemy)
glossary.re: rēs, reī f. — by the event, by the outcome (abl. sg., 5th decl.; XIII.383 ‘re patuit’ “it was plain from the result”, XIII.569 ‘ex re’ “from the event” — the place named for what happened there)
glossary.rebar: reor, rērī — I thought, I supposed (1 sg. imperf. indic. dep.; Hecuba had believed a woman safe from the sword)
glossary.recensent: recēnseō, recēnsēre — they count over, review one by one (3 pl. pres. indic. act.; the Trojan women tally their lamented dead)
glossary.redderet: reddō, reddere — he might give back, hand over (3 sg. imperf. subj. act.; relative clause of purpose — gold for him to pass on to her son)
glossary.reddite: reddō, reddere — give back, restore (2 pl. pres. imperat. act.; XIII.372 of the prize owed to Ulysses, XIII.472 of Polyxena's body owed to her mother)
glossary.redimat: redimō, redimere — let her not buy back, ransom (3 sg. pres. subj. act. in the prohibition ‘neve ... redimat’)
glossary.redimebat: redimō, redimere — she used to ransom, could buy back (3 sg. imperf. indic. act.; once, when she still had gold, Hecuba could pay)
glossary.reduxi: redūcō, redūcere — I brought back, led back (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; Ulysses claims to have turned the fleeing Greeks around)
glossary.refeci: reficiō, reficere — I restored, healed (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; Achilles' spear wounded Telephus and then cured him)
glossary.referrem: referō, referre — that I should carry back (1 sg. imperf. subj. act. in a ‘quin’ clause after a negated verb of hindering)
glossary.regique: rēx, rēgis m. — and to the king, i.e. Agamemnon (dat. sg. + ‘-que’, with ‘infestus’)
glossary.religarat: religō, religāre — he had moored, tied fast (3 sg. pluperf. indic. act., syncopated from religaverat; Agamemnon had beached the fleet on the Thracian shore)
glossary.remigis: rēmex, rēmigis m. — of the oarsman, the rower (gen. sg., with ‘officium’: the helmsman outranks the rower's task)
glossary.remoratur: remoror, remorārī — he holds back, delays (3 sg. pres. indic. dep.; used transitively of the departing men, ‘ituros’)
glossary.reposco: reposcō, reposcere — I demand back, claim as owed (1 sg. pres. indic. act.; three times in Ulysses' speech, of the arms, of Helen, and of the Greeks' lost courage)
glossary.requie: requiēs, -ētis f. — by rest, with rest (abl. sg.; this noun has both requiē and requiēte in the abl.; the means of ending Philoctetes' pain)
glossary.requiritur: requīrō, requīrere — is sought, is looked for (3 sg. pres. indic. pass.; if nearness of kin is what is being asked for)
glossary.reservant: reservō, reservāre — they keep in reserve, save up (3 pl. pres. indic. act.; subject ‘Pergama’, n. pl. — Troy saves itself to perish for Achilles)
glossary.restare: restō, restāre — to remain, be left (pres. inf. act. in indirect statement after ‘putatis’)
glossary.retexi: retegō, retegere — I uncovered, disclosed (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; from retegō “uncover”, not retexō “unweave”, whose perfect is retexui — Ulysses revealed the oracles and Troy's fate)
glossary.retraxi: retrahō, retrahere — I dragged back (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; Ulysses claims he pulled the retreating Ajax back to the fight)
glossary.reus: reus, -ī m. — a defendant, one on trial, guilty party (m. nom. sg., predicative with ‘esse’: Ulysses says he deserves to stand accused over Philoctetes)
glossary.revexit: revehō, revehere — she carried back (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; subject the ship that bore the arms back to the Greeks)
glossary.rhesi: Rhēsus, -ī m. — of Rhesus, the Thracian king killed in his tent by Ulysses and Diomedes on the night raid (gen. sg., with ‘tentoria’)
glossary.rictuque: rictus, -ūs m. — and with jaws, gaping mouth (abl. sg., 4th decl., + ‘-que’; abl. absolute with ‘parato’ — jaws set for words, but a dog's now)
glossary.rsquo: rsquo — not a Latin word: the tail of the HTML entity “’” (a right single quotation mark) left in the archived line XIII.502, where it stands for the closing quote of Hecuba's remembered speech (archive damage; no lemma and no grammatical form)
glossary.rubefactaque: rubefaciō, rubefacere — and reddened, made red (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. agreeing with ‘tellus’, + ‘-que’; the earth reddened by Ajax's blood)
glossary.saevum: saevus, -a, -um — savage, fierce (m. acc. sg. agreeing with the Greek accusative ‘Hectora’ in the next line — savage Hector, not a substantive “the savage one”)
glossary.sapiens: sapiēns, -entis — wise, prudent (n. nom. sg. of the adjective, in apposition to ‘consilium’: a wise plan — the father's secret sending of Polydorus)
glossary.sapienter: sapienter — wisely, prudently (adverb from ‘sapiens’; with the gerundive ‘agendum’)
glossary.sarpedonis: Sarpēdōn, -onis m. — of Sarpedon, the Lycian king and Trojan ally, son of Zeus (gen. sg., with ‘agmina’: his ranks cut down by Ulysses)
glossary.sciret: sciō, scīre — he knew, if he did not know (3 sg. imperf. subj. act. in a past contrary-to-fact protasis, ‘nisi ... sciret’)
glossary.scis: sciō, scīre — you know (2 sg. pres. indic. act.; parenthetical, addressed to Menelaus)
glossary.scyrum: Scyros (Scyrus), -ī f. — Scyros, the Aegean island where Achilles hid among the girls (acc. sg.; Ulysses claims its capture among his deeds)
glossary.scyrumve: Scyros (Scyrus), -ī f. — or Scyros (acc. sg. + enclitic -ve “or”; the arms should go to Phthia or Scyros, to Achilles' father or son)
glossary.sensurus: sentiō, sentīre — going to feel, that will appreciate (fut. act. part., m. nom. sg. agreeing with ‘animus’: a spirit that will know how to value your honours)
glossary.sepulcri: sepulcrum, -ī n. — of burial, of a tomb (gen. sg., with ‘ius’: the grim right of burial, which Hecuba must not have to buy)
glossary.sequatur: sequor, sequī — may follow, would follow (3 sg. pres. subj. dep. in a relative clause of purpose — something for the crowd to follow)
glossary.serum: sērus, -a, -um — late, coming late (m. acc. sg., predicative with the subject-accusative of ‘accessisse’ — that I came late to the work; not the noun ‘serum’ “whey”)
glossary.servas: servō, servāre — you keep, you preserve (2 sg. pres. indic. act., addressed to ‘senectus’ old age; not acc. pl. of the noun serva “slave-woman”)
glossary.servire: serviō, servīre — to be a slave, to serve (pres. inf. act., with the dat. ‘ulli’; Polyxena would be no one's slave)
glossary.simois: Simoīs, -entis m. — the Simois, a river of the Trojan plain (nom. sg.; in the adynaton — sooner will Simois flow backwards)
glossary.simulasse: simulō, simulāre — to have pretended, feigned (perf. inf. act., syncopated from simulavisse; of Achilles' and Ulysses' shared shirking)
glossary.simulavimus: simulō, simulāre — we both pretended (1 pl. perf. indic. act.; Ulysses yokes his own feigned madness to Achilles' disguise)
glossary.siquos: sī + quis, quid — if any men, if any of you (‘si’ + m. acc. pl. of the indefinite ‘quis’, which drops ali- after ‘si’; object of ‘movent’)
glossary.sithonios: Sīthonius, -a, -um — Sithonian, i.e. Thracian (m. acc. pl. agreeing with ‘agros’; the Sithonians were a Thracian people)
glossary.socia: socius, -a, -um — allied, shared (f. abl. sg. agreeing with ‘classe’ — the fleet held in common; not the noun ‘socia’ “female companion”)
glossary.socias: socius, -a, -um — shared, held in common (f. acc. pl. agreeing with ‘spes’; not 2 sg. of the verb ‘socio’)
glossary.sonti: sōns, sontis — guilty (m. abl. sg. agreeing with ‘sanguine’: Polymestor's guilty blood on Hecuba's hands)
glossary.specularer: speculor, speculārī — that I might spy out, scout (1 sg. imperf. subj. dep. in a relative clause of purpose — nothing left to spy on)
glossary.stabit: stō, stāre — will stand (3 sg. fut. indic. act.; subject ‘Ide’, Mount Ida standing leafless — another impossibility)
glossary.stolidae: stolidus, -a, -um — of a stupid, dull (f. gen. sg. agreeing with ‘linguae’: the abuse of a stupid tongue; not dat. sg. or nom. pl. here)
glossary.stolidi: stolidus, -a, -um — of stupid, of dull (m. gen. sg. agreeing with ‘Aiacis’: the cleverness of dull Ajax, said with contempt)
glossary.stygios: Stygius, -a, -um — Stygian, of the Styx, i.e. of the underworld (m. acc. pl. agreeing with ‘manes’: the shades below)
glossary.suasisse: suādeō, suādēre — to have urged, advised (perf. inf. act. in indirect statement after ‘negabo’)
glossary.subtraheret: subtrahō, subtrahere — that he should withdraw himself (3 sg. imperf. subj. act. in a purpose clause, with reflexive ‘se’)
glossary.succensaque: succendō, succendere — and set alight, burning (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl. agreeing with ‘templa’, + ‘-que’)
glossary.sumptae: sūmō, sūmere — of the assumed, of the put-on (perf. pass. part., f. gen. sg. agreeing with ‘vestis’: the trick of the borrowed dress)
glossary.supero: superō, superāre — I surpass, I outdo (1 sg. pres. indic. act.; the verb, not a case-form of the adjective superus — cf. ‘superos’ at XIII.558)
glossary.sustineam: sustineō, sustinēre — I should hold out, keep going (1 sg. pres. subj. act. in an indirect question after ‘cur’ — why I should endure to live a little longer)
glossary.sustollit: sustollō, sustollere — she lifts up, raises (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; Hecuba lifting her grim gaze to heaven)
glossary.tamque: tam — and so, and to such a degree (adverb + ‘-que’; XIII.311 with ‘patens’ “so plain”, XIII.334 as the correlative of ‘quam’ in the next lines; distinct from ‘tamquam’, which occurs at XIII.437)
glossary.tardarunt: tardō, tardāre — they delayed, held back (3 pl. perf. indic. act., syncopated from tardaverunt; grief and fear did not slow Ajax)
glossary.tegendas: tegō, tegere — to be covered, needing covering (gerundive, f. acc. pl. agreeing with ‘partes’: modesty even in falling)
glossary.telamoniades: Telamōniadēs, -ae m. — the son of Telamon, i.e. Ajax (Greek patronymic, nom. sg.; he dared not utter a word when panic struck)
glossary.telamonius: Telamōnius, -a, -um — the Telamonian, Ajax son of Telamon (m. nom. sg. of the adjective used as a name, the standard way this text points at Ajax)
glossary.telephon: Tēlephus, -ī m. — Telephus, the Mysian king whom Achilles' spear wounded and then healed (Greek acc. sg. in -on)
glossary.temptaretque: temptō, temptāre — and that he should try (3 sg. imperf. subj. act. + ‘-que’, second verb of the purpose clause)
glossary.tenedon: Tenedos, -ī f. — Tenedos, the island off Troy where the Greek fleet later hid (Greek acc. sg. in -on)
glossary.tenentes: teneō, tenēre — holding, clinging to (pres. act. part., f. acc. pl. agreeing with ‘matres’, the Trojan mothers dragged off as spoils — accusative, not nominative)
glossary.tergora: tergum (tergus), -oris n. — hides, layers of oxhide (n. acc. pl.; the sevenfold bull's-hide of Ajax's famous shield)
glossary.teucer: Teucer, -crī m. — Teucer, the archer, Ajax's half-brother and likewise a son of Telamon, so equally Achilles' cousin (nom. sg.)
glossary.thersites: Thersītēs, -ae m. — Thersites, the foul-mouthed common soldier whom Ulysses beat down for abusing the kings (Greek nom. sg.)
glossary.thoantis: Thoās, -antis m. — of Thoas, king of Lemnos and father of Hypsipyle (Greek gen. sg.)
glossary.thoona: Thoōn, -ontis m. — Thoon, a Trojan killed by Ulysses (Greek acc. sg. in -a)
glossary.threiciis: Thrēicius, -a, -um — Thracian (n. abl. pl. agreeing with ‘telis’: the Thracian weapons that killed Polydorus)
glossary.timorque: timor, -ōris m. — and fear (m. nom. sg. + ‘-que’; one of the three subjects — tears, grief, fear — that did not slow Ajax)
glossary.tolli: tollō, tollere — to be removed, done away with (pres. pass. inf.; as if the crime could be got rid of along with the body)
glossary.torpet: torpeō, torpēre — she is numb, stiff, frozen (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; Hecuba struck rigid as stone by the sight of Polydorus)
glossary.tracta: trahō, trahere — dragged (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. agreeing with ‘antistita’, with ‘comis’ abl. of means — Cassandra dragged by the hair; most editions print tractaque comis here)
glossary.trahor: trahō, trahere — I am dragged, hauled along (1 sg. pres. indic. pass.; Hecuba, dragged into exile as Ulysses' spoil)
glossary.triumphos: triumphus, -ī m. — triumphs, triumphal processions (acc. pl.; the captured chariot mimics a Roman triumph)
glossary.troada: Trōas, -ados f. — the Trojan woman, i.e. Hecuba (Greek acc. sg. in -a; the feminine noun, distinct from masc. ‘Troas’ “the Trojans” at XIII.274)
glossary.troades: Trōas, -ados f. — the Trojan women (Greek nom. pl. at XIII.421, 481, 538; voc. pl. at XIII.534, where Hecuba calls to them for an urn)
glossary.troas: Trōes, -um m. pl. — the Trojans (Greek masc. acc. pl. in -as; object of an implied verb of driving back from the ships — not the fem. ‘Troas’ “Trojan woman”)
glossary.troasque: Trōes, -um m. pl. — and the Trojans (Greek masc. acc. pl. + ‘-que’: fighting against Trojans and Jove at XIII.269, her own Trojans at XIII.572)
glossary.troiam: Trōia, -ae f. — Troy (acc. sg.; object of ‘evertere’, ‘dimittite’ and ‘capi’ in these lines)
glossary.troianaque: Trōiānus, -a, -um — and Trojan (n. acc. pl. agreeing with ‘fata’, + ‘-que’: the fates of Troy that Ulysses uncovered)
glossary.troum: Trōes, -um m. pl. — of the Trojans (Greek gen. pl.; with ‘moenia’ both times, the walls of the Trojans)
glossary.truculenta: truculentus, -a, -um — grim, savage-eyed (f. nom. sg. agreeing with the unnamed subject Hecuba, predicative with ‘Spectat’ — she watches him grimly; not n. acc. pl.)
glossary.tuentem: tueor, tuērī — guarding, protecting (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg. dep., agreeing with ‘patrem’ — Hector defending his ancestral realm)
glossary.tumidaque: tumidus, -a, -um — and swelling, seething (f. abl. sg. agreeing with ‘ira’, + ‘-que’: she boils with swelling rage)
glossary.tydiden: Tȳdīdēs, -ae m. — the son of Tydeus, i.e. Diomedes, Ulysses' partner on the night raid (Greek patronymic, acc. sg. in -en)
glossary.ulixis: Ulixēs, -is m. — of Ulysses (gen. sg.; Palamedes was caught by Ulysses' cunning)
glossary.ultime: ultimus, -a, -um — last, final (m. voc. sg. agreeing with ‘dolor’: “O last grief of your mother”; the vocative of the adjective, not the adverb)
glossary.utiliter: ūtiliter — usefully, to good purpose (adverb from ‘utilis’; with ‘feci’ — what Ulysses did to good effect during the long war)
glossary.verrens: verrō, verrere — sweeping, dragging through (pres. act. part., f. nom. sg. agreeing with Hecuba, the subject; she sweeps her white hair through the clotted blood)
glossary.vici: vincō, vincere — I conquered, I won (1 sg. perf. indic. act.; from vincō, not the gen. sg. of vīcus “village” — “then I took Troy, when I made it takeable”)
glossary.victores: victor, -ōris m. — victors, conquerors (m. nom. pl., in apposition to the subject ‘Grai’: the victorious Greeks drag off their prizes)
glossary.violatus: violō, violāre — harmed, injured (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg. of Hector, with ‘vulnere nullo’: he walked away hurt by no wound)
glossary.vivacem: vīvāx, -ācis — long-lived, tenacious of life (f. acc. sg. agreeing with ‘anum’: why do the gods put off this stubbornly living old woman?)
glossary.abeuntque: abeō, abīre — go away, depart (3 pl. pres. act. indic. + enclitic -que "and")
glossary.acantho: acanthus — acanthus, bear's-foot (a plant whose curling leaf is a favourite motif in relief work) (m. abl. sg.; Greek 2nd-decl.)
glossary.acerram: acerra — incense box, casket for holding incense (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.achillea: Achillēus, -a, -um — of Achilles, Achillean (f. abl. sg., agreeing with cuspide; not the Greek acc. of the name)
glossary.acidis: Acis, Acidis — Acis, a Sicilian youth, son of Faunus and the nymph Symaethis (m. gen. sg.; Greek 3rd-decl.)
glossary.acin: Acis, Acidis — Acis, a Sicilian youth, son of Faunus and the nymph Symaethis (m. acc. sg.; Greek acc. ending -in)
glossary.acis: Acis, Acidis — Acis, a Sicilian youth, son of Faunus and the nymph Symaethis (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.actiaco: Actiacus, -a, -um — Actian, of Actium (the promontory in Acarnania sacred to Apollo) (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.adeuntque: adeō, adīre — go to, approach, consult (3 pl. pres. act. indic. + enclitic -que "and")
glossary.admiraturque: admīror, admīrārī — wonder at, marvel at (3 sg. pres. indic. of a deponent verb + enclitic -que "and")
glossary.admittite: admittō, admittere — admit, let in, receive (2 pl. pres. act. imperat.)
glossary.admittitur: admittō, admittere — admit, let in (3 sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.adsiduo: adsiduus (assiduus), -a, -um — constant, unceasing (n. abl. sg., agreeing with aequore; unassimilated spelling ads- for ass-)
glossary.adspicias: adspiciō (aspiciō), adspicere — look at, consider, take note of (2 sg. pres. act. subj.; unassimilated spelling ads- for asp-)
glossary.adsumeret: adsūmō (assūmō), adsūmere — take on, take to oneself (3 sg. imperf. act. subj.; unassimilated spelling ads- for ass-)
glossary.aeneae: Aenēās — Aeneas, Trojan prince, son of Anchises and Venus (m. dat. sg.; the form is also gen. sg.)
glossary.aeneas: Aenēās — Aeneas, Trojan prince, son of Anchises and Venus (m. nom. sg.; Greek 1st-decl.)
glossary.aestiva: aestīvus, -a, -um — of summer, summer- (f. abl. sg., agreeing with umbra; abl. of comparison after gratior)
glossary.aestuque: aestus — tide, swell of the sea; heat (m. abl. sg. + enclitic -que "and")
glossary.aetnam: Aetna — Etna, the volcano in eastern Sicily (f. acc. sg.; Latin form)
glossary.aetne: Aetna / Aetnē — Etna, the volcano in eastern Sicily (f. nom. sg.; Greek nom. ending -ē)
glossary.aetnen: Aetna / Aetnē — Etna, the volcano in eastern Sicily (f. acc. sg.; Greek acc. ending -ēn)
glossary.alantque: alō, alere — nourish, rear, feed (3 pl. pres. act. subj. + enclitic -que "and"; subjunctive of indirect command after imperat)
glossary.alcon: Alcōn — Alcon, a craftsman of Hyle, engraver of the mixing-bowl (m. nom. sg.; Greek 3rd-decl.)
glossary.alno: alnus, -ī (f.) — alder tree (f. abl. sg.; abl. of comparison after procerior)
glossary.alteriusque: alter, altera, alterum — the other, a second, another (gen. sg., all genders + enclitic -que "and")
glossary.ambraciam: Ambracia — Ambracia, city of Epirus on the gulf of the same name (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.amissi: āmittō, āmittere — lose (perf. pass. part., m. gen. sg., agreeing with Memnonis)
glossary.amorne: amor — love, desire (m. nom. sg. + enclitic -ne introducing the second limb of a question)
glossary.anchises: Anchīsēs — Anchises, father of Aeneas (m. nom. sg.; Greek 1st-decl.)
glossary.andron: Andros — Andros, island of the Cyclades, ruled by Anius (f. acc. sg.; Greek acc. ending -on)
glossary.angit: angō, angere — distress, torment, choke (3 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.anius: Anius — Anius, king of Andros and priest of Apollo (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.antandro: Antandros — Antandrus, coastal city of the Troad, where Aeneas built his fleet (f. abl. sg.)
glossary.antistite: antistes, antistitis — presiding priest, overseer of a temple (m. abl. sg.; here in an abl. abs. with Phoebus)
glossary.antrorumque: antrum — cave, cavern (n. gen. pl. + enclitic -que "and")
glossary.apertae: aperiō, aperīre — uncover, lay bare (perf. pass. part., f. nom. pl., agreeing with matres; with Greek acc. of respect pectora)
glossary.apicem: apex, apicis — peak, point, summit (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.apollineam: Apollineus, -a, -um — of Apollo, Apollo's (f. acc. sg., agreeing with urbem)
glossary.arbutei: arbuteus, -a, -um — of the arbutus, of the strawberry-tree (m. nom. pl., agreeing with fetus)
glossary.argolicam: Argolicus, -a, -um — Argive, Greek (f. acc. sg., agreeing with classem)
glossary.argumento: argūmentum — subject, theme; a story worked in relief (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.ascaniumque: Ascanius — Ascanius, son of Aeneas (m. acc. sg. + enclitic -que "and")
glossary.ascendit: ascendō, ascendere — climb up, mount (3 sg. perf. act. indic. here, paired with resedit; the form is also 3 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.asperior: asper, aspera, asperum — rough, harsh, savage (compar., nom. sg. m./f.; here f., of Galatea)
glossary.athamantiadesque: Athamantiadēs — son of Athamas, i.e. Palaemon (Melicertes), a sea-god (m. nom. sg.; Greek patronymic + enclitic -que "and")
glossary.augurium: augurium — augury, divination, the reading of omens (n. acc. sg.)
glossary.ausonios: Ausonius, -a, -um — Ausonian, Italian (m. acc. pl., agreeing with portus)
glossary.avitas: avītus, -a, -um — ancestral, inherited from a grandfather (f. acc. pl., agreeing with vires)
glossary.bibenda: bibō, bibere — drink (gerundive, f. nom. sg.: "to be drunk", agreeing with pars)
glossary.bibula: bibulus, -a, -um — absorbent, thirsty, soaking up moisture (f. abl. sg., agreeing with harena)

glossary.linum: līnum, -ī — flax, linen thread; a fishing-line (n. acc. sg.)
glossary.liquidaeque: liquidus, -a, -um — clear, limpid, liquid (f. gen. sg.) + enclitic -que 'and'
glossary.lucidior: lūcidus, -a, -um — brighter, more shining, clearer (comp., f. nom./voc. sg.)
glossary.luctum: lūctus, -ūs — grief, mourning, lamentation (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.lustrant: lustrō, lustrāre — they go round, circle in ritual procession (3 pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.lustror: lustrō, lustrāre — I am purified, I am ritually cleansed (1 sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.madentia: madeō, madēre — dripping, soaking wet (pres. act. part., n. acc. pl.)
glossary.manabat: mānō, mānāre — was flowing, was trickling (3 sg. impf. act. indic.)
glossary.manantem: mānō, mānāre — flowing, dripping, running with (pres. act. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.marinis: marīnus, -a, -um — of the sea, marine (m. dat. pl.)
glossary.memnonides: Memnonis, -idis (pl. Memnonides) — the Memnonides, birds sprung from Memnon's ashes (f. nom. pl., Greek form)
glossary.memnonis: Memnōn, Memnonis — Memnon, son of Aurora, king of the Ethiopians, killed at Troy (m. gen. sg.)
glossary.mensa: mēnsa, -ae — table (f. abl. sg.; noun, not the participle of mētior)
glossary.meritos: mereō, merēre / meritus — deserved, due, earned (perf. part. used as adj., m. acc. pl.)
glossary.mersi: mergō, mergere — I plunged, I sank (something) (1 sg. perf. act. indic.; not the participle mersī)
glossary.miraque: mīrus, -a, -um — wonderful, strange, astonishing (f. nom. sg.) + enclitic -que 'and'
glossary.miro: mīrus, -a, -um — strange, wondrous, extraordinary (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.mirorque: mīror, mīrārī — I wonder, I marvel at (1 sg. pres. indic. of dep. vb.) + enclitic -que 'and'
glossary.moderabar: moderor, moderārī — I was managing, guiding, plying (1 sg. impf. indic. of dep. vb.)
glossary.moli: mōlēs, mōlis — mass, bulk, pile of rock, jetty (f. dat. sg.)
glossary.mollior: mollis, -e — softer, more tender (comp., f. nom./voc. sg.)
glossary.molosso: Molossus — Molossus, king of the Molossi in Epirus (m. abl. sg.; also as adj., Molossian)
glossary.monentem: moneō, monēre — warning, advising, admonishing (pres. act. part., m. acc. sg.)
glossary.monstrumne: monstrum, -ī — monster, portent, prodigy (n. nom. sg.) + enclitic -ne, marking an alternative question ('whether … or')
glossary.morasque: mora, -ae — delay, lingering (f. acc. pl.) + enclitic -que 'and'
glossary.moriturae: morior, morī / moritūrus — about to die, doomed to die (fut. act. part., f. nom. pl.)
glossary.moveris: moveō, movēre — you are moved, you are stirred (2 sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.narrabat: narrō, narrāre — was telling, was recounting (3 sg. impf. act. indic.)
glossary.nequiere: nequeō, nequīre — they were unable, they could not (3 pl. perf. act. indic.; poetic -ēre = -ērunt)
glossary.nerei: Nērēis, Nērēidis — Nereid, daughter of Nereus (voc. sg., Greek form; addressing a sea-nymph)
glossary.neritiasque: Nēritius, -a, -um — Neritian, of Neritos (a peak of Ithaca), hence Ithacan (f. acc. pl.) + enclitic -que 'and'
glossary.nigrique: niger, nigra, nigrum — black, dark, murky (m. gen. sg.) + enclitic -que 'and'
glossary.niti: nītor, nītī — to press, strain, make one's way, push forward (pres. infin. of dep. vb.)
glossary.nobilior: nōbilis, -e — more notable, more renowned, finer (comp., f. nom./voc. sg.)
glossary.noris: nōscō, nōscere / nōvī — you knew, you were acquainted with (2 sg. perf. act. subj., syncopated for nōveris; the perfect of nōscō has present force, 'know')
glossary.novasque: novus, -a, -um — new, fresh (f. acc. pl.) + enclitic -que 'and'
glossary.obumbrat: obumbrō, obumbrāre — overshadows, casts a shade over (3 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.opibus: ops, opis (pl. opēs) — wealth, riches, resources (f. abl. pl.)
glossary.optant: optō, optāre — they wish, they long (3 pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.orione: Ōrīōn, Ōrīonis — Orion (m. abl. sg.; here abl. of origin, 'born of Orion')
glossary.osque: ōs, ōris — mouth, opening, aperture (n. nom. sg.; ōs 'mouth', not os, ossis 'bone') + enclitic -que 'and'
glossary.ovilibus: ovīle, ovīlis — sheepfold, pen (n. abl. pl.)
glossary.pachynos: Pachynos (Pachynum) — Pachynus, the south-eastern cape of Sicily (f. nom. sg., Greek form)
glossary.palaemon: Palaemōn — Palaemon, a sea-god, formerly Melicertes son of Athamas (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.palluerat: palleō, pallēre — had turned pale, had grown wan (3 sg. plupf. act. indic.)
glossary.parabantur: parō, parāre — were being made ready, were being prepared (3 pl. impf. pass. indic.)
glossary.parentali: parentālis, -e — of the rites for dead kin, funerary (f. abl. sg.)
glossary.pariente: pariō, parere — giving birth, bearing (pres. act. part., f. abl. sg.; here in abl. abs.)
glossary.parve: pār, paris — a pair, a couple (n. nom. sg.) + enclitic -ve 'or' (not a form of parvus)
glossary.pateram: patera, -ae — libation bowl, shallow offering dish (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.patientior: patiēns, patientis — more tolerant, better able to endure (comp. adj., m. nom. sg.; here with gen. of the thing borne)
glossary.patrisque: pater, patris — father (m. gen. sg. + enclitic -que 'and')
glossary.pauperis: pauper, pauperis — poor man, poor (m. gen. sg.; predicative gen., 'it is the mark of a poor man')
glossary.pavone: pāvō, pāvōnis — peacock (m. abl. sg.; here abl. of comparison)
glossary.pectendos: pectō, pectere — to be combed (gerundive, m. acc. pl., agreeing with capillos)
glossary.pectis: pectō, pectere — you comb, dress (hair) (2 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.peloros: Pelōrus / Pelōros — Pelorus, the north-eastern headland of Sicily (m. nom. sg., Greek form)
glossary.periturum: pereō, perīre — one about to perish, doomed to die (fut. act. part., m. acc. sg.)
glossary.phaeacum: Phaeāces, Phaeācum — the Phaeacians, the island people of Scheria/Corcyra (m. gen. pl.)
glossary.phrygio: Phrygius — Phrygian, Trojan (adj., m. dat. sg., agreeing with vati; the dat. of the agent with regnata)
glossary.pinnigero: pinniger — fin-bearing, finny (adj., m. abl. sg., agreeing with pisce)
glossary.pinnis: pinna — point, projecting headland (lit. feather, wing) (f. abl. pl.; of Sicily's three promontories)
glossary.placeatque: placeō, placēre — and let him please, be pleasing (3 sg. pres. act. subj. + enclitic -que; concessive with licebit)
glossary.placendi: placeō, placēre — of pleasing, of giving pleasure (gerund, gen. sg.; here with cura)
glossary.placidae: placidus — gentle, quiet (adj., f. nom./voc. pl.; here voc., with oves)
glossary.placidisque: placidus — calm, still (adj., f. abl. pl. + enclitic -que)
glossary.placuitque: placeō, placēre — and it pleased, was pleasing (3 sg. perf. act. indic. + enclitic -que; with dat. of the person pleased)
glossary.platano: platanus — plane tree (f. abl. sg.; here abl. of comparison)
glossary.polydoreo: Polydōrēus — of Polydorus, Polydorean (adj., m. abl. sg.; from Polydōrus, youngest son of Priam)
glossary.polypheme: Polyphēmus — Polyphemus, the Cyclops, son of Neptune (m. voc. sg.)
glossary.polyphemon: Polyphēmus — Polyphemus, the Cyclops, son of Neptune (m. acc. sg., Greek form -on for -um)
glossary.pompam: pompa — procession, funeral procession (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.portubus: portus, portūs — harbour, haven (m. abl. pl.; older/alternative form for portibus)
glossary.praedixerat: praedīcō, praedīcere — he had foretold, predicted (3 sg. plupf. act. indic.)
