glossary.praefersque: praeferō, praeferre — and you prefer, put before (2 sg. pres. act. indic. + enclitic -que; with acc. and dat.)
glossary.praepetibus: praepes, praepetis — swift-flying; (as noun) bird, bird of omen (dat. pl.)
glossary.praestem: praestō, praestāre — I render, perform, am worth (1 sg. pres. act. subj.; in indirect question after quantum)
glossary.pratis: prātum — meadow (n. abl. pl.; here abl. of comparison)
glossary.priamides: Priamidēs — son of Priam (m. nom. sg., Greek patronymic; here of Helenus)
glossary.primisque: prīmus — first, earliest (adj., m. abl. pl. + enclitic -que; here of a man's earliest years)
glossary.procellam: procella — storm, violent blast, squall (f. acc. sg.; figuratively of an onset of rage)
glossary.proceraque: prōcērus — tall, high-grown (adj., f. nom. sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.procerior: prōcērus — taller (comp. adj., f. nom. sg.)
glossary.prodigium: prōdigium — portent, monster, unnatural thing (n. nom. sg.)
glossary.profugaque: profugus — fugitive, exiled, in flight (adj., f. abl. sg. + enclitic -que, agreeing with classe)
glossary.proprior: propior — nearer, closer to home (comp. adj., f. nom. sg., agreeing with cura; printed proprior in this edition)
glossary.prosequitur: prōsequor, prōsequī — he escorts, accompanies, sees off (3 sg. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.pulcher: pulcher — beautiful, handsome (adj., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.pulchrisque: pulcher — fine, splendid (adj., n. abl. pl. + enclitic -que, agreeing with funeribus)
glossary.puniceus: pūniceus — crimson, blood-red (adj., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.purgante: purgō, purgāre — cleansing, purging away (pres. act. part., n. abl. sg., agreeing with carmine)
glossary.purgaturque: purgō, purgāre — and it is cleared, runs clear (3 sg. pres. pass. indic. + enclitic -que)
glossary.quaesieris: quaerō, quaerere — you will have asked, should ask (2 sg. fut. perf. act. indic., or perf. act. subj.; syncopated for quaesīveris)
glossary.quantam: quantus — as great as, how great (rel./interrog. adj., f. acc. sg.; correlative with tanta)
glossary.rapiet: rapiō, rapere — he will snatch away, tear off (3 sg. fut. act. indic.)
glossary.rastris: rastrum (pl. rastrī / rastra) — rake, mattock (n. abl. pl.)
glossary.rebellant: rebellō, rebellāre — they renew the fight, take up war again (3 pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.recenserem: recēnseō, recēnsēre — I might review, count over (1 sg. impf. act. subj.)
glossary.receptos: recipiō, recipere — received, taken in (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.)
glossary.recidere: recīdō, recīdere — to cut off, cut back (pres. act. infin.; from re- + caedō, not recidō 'fall back')
glossary.recordati: recordor, recordārī — remembering, calling to mind (perf. part., deponent, m. nom. pl.; active in sense)
glossary.refrigerat: refrīgerō, refrīgerāre — she cools, refreshes (3 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.regnare: rēgnō, rēgnāre — to reign, be king (pres. act. infin.)
glossary.regnataque: rēgnō, rēgnāre — and ruled over, reigned over (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. + enclitic -que; poetic passive of an intransitive verb)
glossary.reliquerunt: relinquō, relinquere — they left, left behind (3 pl. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.reminiscor: reminīscor, reminīscī — I recall, remember (1 sg. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.remittunt: remittō, remittere — they send back, send in return (3 pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.repulsis: repellō, repellere — driven off, rejected (perf. pass. part., m. abl. pl.; here in an abl. abs. with quibus)
glossary.retentas: retineō, retinēre — held on to, clung to (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl., agreeing with stirpes)
glossary.revomitque: revomō, revomere — and it vomits back up, disgorges (3 sg. pres. act. indic. + enclitic -que)
glossary.revulsam: revellō, revellere — torn away, wrenched off (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.rodunt: rōdō, rōdere — they gnaw, nibble at (3 pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.rogique: rogus — funeral pyre (m. nom. pl. + enclitic -que)
glossary.rorat: rōrō, rōrāre — it drips with dew, sheds moisture (3 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.rostrisque: rōstrum — beak, bill (n. abl. pl. + enclitic -que)
glossary.rubescunt: rubēscō, rubēscere — they redden, grow red (3 pl. pres. act. indic., inceptive)
glossary.sacrificos: sacrificus — sacrificial, used for sacrifice (adj., acc. pl.; printed in the m. form beside f. aras)
glossary.saltibus: saltus, saltūs — woodland pasture, glade, forest ravine (m. abl. pl.; not saltus 'a leap')
glossary.samonque: Samē / Samos — Same (Samos), the island next to Ithaca (f. acc. sg., Greek form + enclitic -que; not the Aegean Samos)
glossary.scindens: scindō, scindere — cleaving, cutting through (pres. act. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.secuere: secō, secāre — they cut, cut off (3 pl. perf. act. indic.; poetic -ēre = -ērunt)
glossary.seductos: sēdūcō, sēdūcere — drawn apart, secluded, remote (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.)
glossary.seducunt: sēdūcō, sēdūcere — they draw apart, separate (3 pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.segetem: seges, segetis — standing corn, grain crop (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.sentitur: sentiō, sentīre — it is felt, is perceived (3 sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.sepulto: sepeliō, sepelīre — buried, entombed (perf. pass. part., m./n. dat. sg., agreeing with cineri)
glossary.servabimus: servō, servāre — we shall keep, save, preserve (1 pl. fut. act. indic.)
glossary.servamus: servō, servāre — we keep, save, reserve (1 pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.servatur: servō, servāre — it is kept, is preserved (3 sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.serviet: serviō, servīre — it will serve, be at the service of (3 sg. fut. act. indic.; with dat.)
glossary.siccatosque: siccō, siccāre — and dried up, drained (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl. + enclitic -que)
glossary.siculam: Siculus — Sicilian, of Sicily (adj., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.signarat: signō, signāre — he had marked, stamped (3 sg. plupf. act. indic.; syncopated for signāverat)
glossary.silvestri: silvester, silvestris — of the woods, woodland (adj., f. abl. sg.)
glossary.simulataque: simulō, simulāre — and imitated, copied, made in likeness (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.sitisque: sitis, sitis — thirst (f. nom. sg. + enclitic -que; here with gen. of the thing thirsted for)
glossary.solata: sōlor, sōlārī — having consoled, comforted (perf. part., deponent, f. nom. sg.; active in sense, with est = perf. indic.)
glossary.soletis: soleō, solēre — you are accustomed, you usually (2 pl. pres. indic., semi-deponent; with infin.)
glossary.soluto: solvō, solvere — loosed, unbound, broken up (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.)
glossary.spargam: spargō, spargere — I shall scatter, strew (1 sg. fut. act. indic.; form also = pres. act. subj.)
glossary.sperno: spernō, spernere — I scorn, despise (1 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.stabulantur: stabulor, stabulārī — they are stabled, are housed, shelter (3 pl. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.stirpes: stirps, stirpis — stem, trunk, tree (f. acc. pl.; nom. pl. has the same form)
glossary.stirpi: stirps, stirpis — stock, offspring, lineage (f. dat. sg.)
glossary.stolidissime: stolidus — most stupid, dullest (superl. adj., m. voc. sg.)
glossary.strophadumque: Strophades, Strophadum — the Strophades, the Ionian islands of the Harpies (f. gen. pl. + enclitic -que)
glossary.succingitur: succingō, succingere — she is girded about, is belted (3 sg. pres. pass. indic., middle in force, with acc. of respect alvum)
glossary.succumbimus: succumbō, succumbere — we yield, give way, submit (1 pl. pres. act. indic.; with dat.)
glossary.sumitque: sūmō, sūmere — and it takes on, assumes (3 sg. pres. act. indic. + enclitic -que)
glossary.superbior: superbus — prouder, more haughty (comp. adj., f. nom. sg.)
glossary.supplicis: supplex, supplicis — suppliant; (as noun) a suppliant (gen. sg.)
glossary.surdior: surdus — deafer, more unhearing (comp. adj., f. nom. sg.)
glossary.symaethide: Symaethis, Symaethidos — Symaethian, of the river Symaethus in Sicily (f. abl. sg., Greek form; here of the nymph)
glossary.symaethius: Symaethius — Symaethian, son of the Symaethian nymph (adj., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.tangeris: tangō, tangere — you are touched, are moved (2 sg. pres. pass. indic.; the form is also fut. pass.)
glossary.tapetibus: tapēs, tapētis — carpet, coverlet, tapestry (m. abl. pl.)
glossary.tege: tegō, tegere — cover, hide, conceal (2 sg. pres. act. imper.)
glossary.tegentem: tegō, tegere — covering, veiling (pres. act. part., f. acc. sg., agreeing with caesariem)
glossary.telemus: Telemus — Telemus, son of Eurymus, a seer among the Cyclopes (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.temploque: templum — temple, shrine (n. abl. sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.teneras: tener — soft, tender, youthful (adj., f. acc. pl.)
glossary.tethynque: Tēthys, Tēthyos — Tethys, sea-goddess, wife of Oceanus (f. acc. sg., Greek form Tēthyn + enclitic -que)
glossary.teucri: Teucer / Teucrī — of Teucer, the first king of Troy (m. gen. sg.); or the Teucrians, the Trojans (m. nom. pl.) — both occur in this batch
glossary.teucros: Teucrī — the Teucrians, the Trojans (m. acc. pl.; from Teucer, Troy's first king)
glossary.therses: Thersēs — Therses, a Theban guest-friend of Anius (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.timentes: timeō, timēre — fearing, dreading (pres. act. part., m. acc. pl.)
glossary.titanidos: Tītānis, Tītānidos — daughter of a Titan, Titaness (f. gen. sg., Greek form; here of Circe, child of the Sun)
glossary.tollentes: tollō, tollere — raising, lifting up (pres. act. part., f. nom. pl.)
glossary.toti: tōtus — whole, entire (adj., m. nom. pl.; the form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.traham: trahō, trahere — I shall drag, tear away (1 sg. fut. act. indic.; form also = pres. act. subj.)
glossary.transformabantur: trānsfōrmō, trānsfōrmāre — they were being transformed, changed (3 pl. impf. pass. indic.)
glossary.translatam: trānsferō, trānsferre — carried across, moved over (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg.)
glossary.tribulis: tribulus — caltrop, thorny burr-plant (m. abl. pl.; abl. of comparison; not tribūlis 'fellow tribesman')
glossary.triton: Trītōn — Triton, a sea-god, son of Neptune (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.troiani: Trōiānus — Trojan; (as noun) the Trojans (m. nom. pl.)
glossary.truculentior: truculentus — fiercer, more savage (comp. adj., f. nom. sg.)
glossary.tulitque: ferō, ferre — and he brought, bore (3 sg. perf. act. indic. + enclitic -que; suppletive perf. tulī)
glossary.tumulique: tumulus — burial mound, tomb (m. nom. pl. + enclitic -que)
glossary.turbati: turbō, turbāre — stirred up, muddied (perf. pass. part., n. gen. sg., agreeing with fluminis)
glossary.uber: ūber, ūberis — udder, teat (n. acc. sg.; not the adj. ūber 'rich')
glossary.ultimaque: ultimus — last, lowest, furthest (adj., n. acc. pl. + enclitic -que, agreeing with inguina)
glossary.urbemque: urbs, urbis — city (f. acc. sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.utilibus: ūtilis — useful, favourable, serviceable (adj., m. abl. pl.)
glossary.validaque: validus — strong, powerful (adj., f. abl. sg. + enclitic -que, agreeing with cupidine, here treated as fem.)
glossary.vatum: vātēs, vātis — seer, prophet, bard (m. gen. pl.)
glossary.velent: vēlō, vēlāre — they should veil, cover (3 pl. pres. act. subj.; in a nisi clause)
glossary.venerabile: venerābilis — worthy of reverence, venerable (adj., n. acc. sg.)
glossary.veneror: veneror, venerārī — I revere, worship, entreat (1 sg. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.venio: veniō, venīre — I come (1 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.verro: verrō, verrere — I sweep, trail, drag along (1 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.versique: vertō, vertere — and turned, transformed (perf. pass. part., m. gen. sg. + enclitic -que, agreeing with iudicis)
glossary.vicino: vīcīnus — neighbouring, near at hand (adj., n. abl. sg., agreeing with aequore)
glossary.videnti: videō, vidēre — seeing, as I looked (pres. act. part., dat. sg., agreeing with mihi)
glossary.villosae: villōsus — shaggy, hairy (adj., f. gen. sg.)
glossary.vocalemque: vōcālis — speaking, utterance-giving, vocal (adj., f. acc. sg. + enclitic -que)
glossary.volucrique: volucer — winged, flying, swift (adj., f. abl. sg. + enclitic -que; abl. of comparison)
glossary.voluistis: volō, velle — you wished, willed (2 pl. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.vorat: vorō, vorāre — she devours, swallows down (3 sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.vulgataque: vulgō, vulgāre — and made common, ordinary, commonplace (perf. pass. part., n. nom. pl. + enclitic -que, agreeing with munera)
glossary.zanclaea: Zanclaeus — of Zancle (Messana in Sicily), Zanclaean (adj., f. abl. sg.)
glossary.zephyris: Zephyrus — Zephyr, the west wind (m. dat. pl.; with expositum, 'exposed to')
glossary.abigitque: abigō + -que — and drives (them) away (3 sg. pres. act. ind. + enclitic -que)
glossary.acceptaque: accipiō — and received (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. f., agreeing with salūte in the ablative absolute dicta acceptaque salute, greeting given and returned)
glossary.accipimus: accipiō — we take, we accept (1 pl. pres. act. ind.; narrative present, since the perfect would be accēpimus)
glossary.acesten: Acestēs — Acestes, the Sicilian king of Trojan descent who hosts Aeneas (Greek acc. sg. of a 1st-decl. masc. name)
glossary.achaemenide: Achaemenidēs — Achaemenides, the companion of Ulysses left behind in the Cyclops' cave (Greek voc. sg., in direct address)
glossary.achaemeniden: Achaemenidēs — Achaemenides, the companion of Ulysses left behind in the Cyclops' cave (Greek acc. sg.)
glossary.achaemenides: Achaemenidēs — Achaemenides, the companion of Ulysses left behind in the Cyclops' cave (nom. sg.)
glossary.acheloiadumque: Achelōias + -que — and of the daughters of Achelous, i.e. the Sirens (gen. pl. f. of a Greek patronymic, with Sīrēnum)
glossary.achivam: Achīvus — Achaean, Greek (acc. sg. f., with gentem)
glossary.adfligi: adflīgō — to be dashed down, be smashed (pres. pass. inf. in indirect statement after vīdī, with corpora as accusative subject; adf- is the unassimilated spelling of aff-)
glossary.adlabimur: adlābor — we glide up to, we drift ashore at (1 pl. pres. ind. of a deponent, with the dative/ablative terrīs; adl- is the unassimilated spelling of all-)
glossary.adsitque: adsum + -que — and let there be, and let it attend (3 sg. pres. act. subj., jussive, with fīdūcia as subject, + -que; some editors instead print absitque, let it be absent)
glossary.adspexi: adspiciō — I caught sight of (1 sg. pf. act. ind.; adsp- is the unassimilated spelling of asp-)
glossary.adspiciam: adspiciō — may I look upon, shall I look upon (1 sg.; the form is both fut. act. ind. and pres. act. subj., and Achaemenides' self-cursing oath reads more naturally as the subjunctive)
glossary.adulantes: adūlor — fawning, cringing (pres. act. part., nom. pl. m., of the beasts that follow; the same form also serves as acc. pl.)
glossary.adulantum: adūlor — of the fawning ones (pres. act. part., gen. pl., with ferārum; -um is the poetic gen. pl. beside the usual -ium)
glossary.advertens: advertō — turning her attention, attending closely (pres. act. part., nom. sg. f.)
glossary.aenean: Aenēās — Aeneas (Greek acc. sg. of a 1st-decl. masc. name; the Latin acc. Aenēam also occurs)
glossary.aeoliique: Aeolius + -que — and of the Aeolian (gen. sg. m., agreeing with tyrannī, the tyrant being Aeolus; the same spelling is also nom. pl. m.)
glossary.aeolon: Aeolus — Aeolus, keeper of the winds (Greek acc. sg.; the Latin acc. Aeolum also exists)
glossary.aequem: aequō — I may match, I may equal (1 sg. pres. act. subj. in a purpose clause)
glossary.aeternamque: aeternus + -que — and everlasting (acc. sg. f., with iuventam, + -que)
glossary.aetnae: Aetna — of Etna (gen. sg. of the Sicilian volcano; the same spelling is also dat. sg.)
glossary.album: albus — white (acc. sg. m., agreeing with flōrem; the identical neuter noun album, a white tablet, is not meant here)
glossary.algae: alga — seaweed (nom. pl., subject of nāscentur; the same spelling is also gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.amata: amō — loved (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., predicative with vidēbor, I shall seem loved; the same spelling is also abl. sg. f. and nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.amissa: āmittō — lost (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. f., with parte in an ablative absolute)
glossary.amplectimur: amplector — we embrace (1 pl. pres. ind. of a deponent)
glossary.anilibus: anīlis — of an old woman (abl. pl. f., with rūgīs, an old woman's wrinkles)
glossary.antiphatae: Antiphatēs — of Antiphates, the Laestrygonian king (gen. sg. of a Greek 1st-decl. masc. name, governed by memorēs; the same spelling is also dat. sg.)
glossary.antiphates: Antiphatēs — Antiphates, king of the man-eating Laestrygonians (nom. sg.)
glossary.aptius: aptus — better suited, more fitting (compar., acc. sg. n., agreeing with ingenium; the identical form aptius also serves as the comparative adverb, more aptly)
glossary.atavosque: atavus + -que — and forefathers, ancestors (acc. pl. + -que; strictly a great-great-great-grandfather, generally an ancestor)
glossary.attigimus: attingō — we reached, we touched (1 pl. pf. act. ind.; the present would be attingimus)
glossary.attrahit: attrahō — draws toward itself, drags along (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.aurato: aurātus — gilded, gold-worked (perf. pass. part. of aurō used as an adjective, abl. sg. m., with amictū)
glossary.ausoniae: Ausonius — Ausonian, Italian (gen. sg. f., agreeing with terrae; the same spelling is also dat. sg. f. and nom. pl. f.)
glossary.ausonium: Ausonius — Ausonian, Italian (nom. sg. n. here, agreeing with lītus, the subject of adesset; the same spelling is also acc. sg. m. and n.)
glossary.averna: Averna — the region of Avernus, the approach to the underworld (acc. pl. n. after per; the adjectival Avernus, -a, -um is a separate use)
glossary.avernae: Avernus — of Avernus, of the underworld (adj., gen. sg. f., with Iūnōnis, the Juno of Avernus being Proserpina)
glossary.avidam: avidus — greedy, ravenous (acc. sg. f., with alvum)
glossary.bifidosque: bifidus + -que — and cloven, split in two (acc. pl. m., with pedēs, + -que)
glossary.blanditiasque: blanditia + -que — and coaxing words, flatteries (acc. pl. + -que)
glossary.bovis: bōs — of an ox (gen. sg., with tergō, an ox's hide; not a plural, since the dat./abl. pl. of this noun is būbus or bōbus, which also appears in this text)
glossary.bubus: bōs — to oxen (dat. pl., a by-form of bōbus, with iūnctīs, yoked oxen)
glossary.caerulaque: caerulus + -que — and dark-blue, sea-blue (acc. pl. n., with vēlāmina in the Greek accusative of respect after the middle induitur, she clothes herself in, + -que)
glossary.calenti: caleō — hot, glowing (pres. act. part., abl. sg. n., with sulphure; the same spelling is also dat. sg.)
glossary.caloris: calor — of heat, of passion (gen. sg., partitive with partem)
glossary.canori: canōrus — of the tuneful, of the melodious one (gen. sg. m., with Aeolidae, the son of Aeolus being the trumpeter Misenus; the same spelling is also nom. pl. m.)
glossary.carituraque: careō + -que — and destined to be without, going to lack (fut. act. part., nom. sg. f., with lūx, governing the abl. fīne, + -que)
glossary.caruisse: careō — to have lacked, to have been without (pf. act. inf. in indirect statement, governing an ablative)
glossary.casusve: cāsus + -ve — or [some] chance, or [some] mischance (nom. sg. m., subject of servat, + enclitic -ve, or; the same spelling cāsus also serves as gen. sg. and nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.caudas: cauda — tails (acc. pl., object of movēre)
glossary.cerbereos: Cerbereus — Cerberus-like, such as Cerberus has (acc. pl. m., with rictūs)
glossary.cercopum: Cercōpes — of the Cercopes, the swindling tribe Jupiter turned into monkeys (gen. pl.)
glossary.certeque: certē + -que — and certainly, and assuredly (adv. + enclitic -que)
glossary.charybdim: Charybdis — Charybdis, the devouring whirlpool of the Sicilian strait (Greek acc. sg.; some editions print Charybdin)
glossary.circaea: Circaeus — of Circe, Circean (acc. pl. n., with moenia)
glossary.circaeo: Circaeus — of Circe, Circean (abl. sg. n., with lītore)
glossary.circe: Circē — Circe, the sorceress daughter of the Sun (nom. sg. of a Greek 1st-decl. name; the same spelling also serves as abl. sg.)
glossary.circen: Circē — Circe, the sorceress daughter of the Sun (Greek acc. sg.)
glossary.circumvelatur: circumvēlō — she veils herself all round, drapes herself (3 sg. pres. pass. ind. with middle, reflexive force)
glossary.claudor: claudō — I am shut in, I am penned (1 sg. pres. pass. ind., with harā, in a sty)
glossary.cognitius: cognitus — better known (compar. of the perf. pass. part. of cognōscō used as an adjective, nom. sg. n., impersonal: to no one is it better known than to me)
glossary.cognosces: cognōscō — you will come to know, you will see for yourself (2 sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.cognoscet: cognōscō — he will recognize (3 sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.cohibentem: cohibeō — confining, keeping penned (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m., with Aeolon)
glossary.coleretur: colō — was worshipped, was honoured (3 sg. impf. pass. subj. in an indirect question)
glossary.colles: collis — hills (acc. pl., object of adiit; the same spelling is also nom. pl.)
glossary.comitant: comitō — they accompany, they attend (3 pl. pres. act. ind.; Ovid uses the rarer active form here, beside the usual deponent comitor)
glossary.concretam: concrēscō — clotted, caked stiff (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f., with barbam)
glossary.condar: condō — let me be buried, I shall be buried (1 sg. pass.; the form is both pres. subj. and fut. ind., and the wish parallel to relinquam favours the subjunctive)
glossary.condebat: condō — he was stowing away, was burying (3 sg. impf. act. ind.)
glossary.coniugii: coniugium — of marriage, of the marriage-union (gen. sg., with dōtem)
glossary.conquesti: conqueror — having complained bitterly, having lamented (perf. part. of a deponent, active in sense, nom. pl. m.)
glossary.conserto: cōnserō — fastened together, stitched (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. n., with tegmine in an ablative absolute; from cōnserō, cōnserere, cōnseruī, cōnsertum, to join, not from the homonymous verb meaning to sow)
glossary.conspexi: cōnspiciō — I caught sight of, I saw (1 sg. pf. act. ind.)
glossary.consumptaque: cōnsūmō + -que — and wasted away, consumed (perf. pass. part., nom. pl. n., with membra, subject of redigentur, + -que)
glossary.contempto: contemnō — scorned, rejected (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. n., with mūnere in an ablative absolute)
glossary.conterit: conterō — grinds up, pounds fine (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.conversae: convertō — turned about, reversed (perf. pass. part., gen. sg. f., with virgae; the same spelling is also dat. sg. f. and nom. pl. f.)
glossary.convexum: convexus — arched, vaulted (acc. sg. n., with iter; the identical neuter noun convexum, a vault, is not meant here)
glossary.cremarat: cremō — had burned (3 sg. plpf. act. ind., syncopated from cremāverat)
glossary.crudelesque: crūdēlis + -que — and cruel (acc. pl. f., with manūs, object of spectantem, + -que; the same spelling is also nom. pl.)
glossary.crurumque: crūs + -que — and of the legs (gen. pl. n. + -que)
glossary.cumaea: Cūmaeus — Cumaean, of Cumae (fem. sg.; abl. with duce, the Cumaean guide, and voc. in address to the Sibyl as virgō Cūmaea, since nom., voc. and abl. sg. f. share this spelling)
glossary.cumarum: Cūmae — of Cumae, the Campanian town of the Sibyl (gen. pl.; the name is plural in form)
glossary.cupidusque: cupidus + -que — and eager, and longing (nom. sg. m., here with the poetic infinitive morīrī rather than a genitive, + -que)
glossary.debentia: dēbeō — owing (pres. act. part., acc. pl. n., with arva)
glossary.deceptaque: dēcipiō + -que — and deceived, tricked (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., of Dido, + -que)
glossary.decurrit: dēcurrō — runs down along, skims (3 sg.; present here, matching the present pōnit alongside it, though the same spelling is also the 3 sg. perfect of this verb)
glossary.deforme: dēfōrmis — misshapen, ugly (acc. sg. n., with animal)
glossary.dempsisse: dēmō — to have taken away, to have removed (pf. act. inf. in indirect statement; from dēmō, dēmere, dēmpsī)
glossary.demurmurat: dēmurmurō — murmurs through, mumbles out from beginning to end (3 sg. pres. act. ind.; a rare compound)
glossary.deprimeret: dēprimō — might sink, might press down (3 sg. impf. act. subj. after a verb of fearing)
glossary.deterruit: dēterreō — frightened off, drove back in fear (3 sg. pf. act. ind.)
glossary.deusve: deus + -ve — or a god (nom. sg. + enclitic -ve, or)
glossary.dextraeque: dextra + -que — and right hands (nom. pl., subject of datae [sunt], the pledging of right hands, + -que; the same spelling is also gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.dignare: dignor — deem worthy, think fit (2 sg. pres. imper. of a deponent, in a prohibition with nec; the same spelling is also an alternative 2 sg. pres. ind., you deem worthy)
glossary.dilexisse: dīligō — to have loved, to have cared for (pf. act. inf. in indirect statement; from dīligō, dīligere, dīlēxī, not from dēligō, to choose)
glossary.disce: discō — learn, come to know (2 sg. pres. act. imper.)
glossary.discidium: discidium — separation, parting (acc. sg. n., object of the future participle lātūra)
glossary.disponunt: dispōnō — they set out in order, they arrange (3 pl. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.dissimiles: dissimilis — unlike, dissimilar (nom. pl. m., predicative with possent vidērī, governing the dat. hominī; the same spelling is also acc. pl.)
glossary.dolosae: dolōsus — deceitful, full of guile (gen. sg. f., with gentis; the same spelling is also dat. sg. f. and nom. pl. f.)
glossary.dominam: domina — mistress, lady of the house (acc. sg.)
glossary.dulichium: Dulichius — Dulichian, i.e. of Ulysses, from the island near Ithaca (acc. sg. m., with ducem)
glossary.eiectantemque: ēiectō + -que — and spewing out, disgorging (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m., of the frequentative of ēiciō, + -que)
glossary.elpenora: Elpēnōr — Elpenor, the comrade of Ulysses undone by wine (Greek acc. sg.)
glossary.elysiasque: Ēlysius + -que — and Elysian, of the blessed dead (acc. pl. f., with domōs, + -que)
glossary.emergit: ēmergō — comes up, emerges (3 sg. pres. act. ind., a historic present; the perfect would be ēmersit)
glossary.erigimur: ērigō — we straighten up, we are raised upright (1 pl. pres. pass. ind., with middle force)
glossary.erres: errō — you may stray, you may be mistaken (2 sg. pres. act. subj., in a negative purpose clause with neu)
glossary.erycis: Eryx — of Eryx, the Sicilian mountain and its eponymous hero (gen. sg.)
glossary.euboicus: Euboicus — Euboean (nom. sg. m., with cultor, of Glaucus of Anthedon on the strait facing Euboea)
glossary.eurylochum: Eurylochus — Eurylochus, the comrade of Ulysses who alone refused Circe's cup (acc. sg.)
glossary.eurylochumque: Eurylochus + -que — and Eurylochus, the comrade of Ulysses who alone refused Circe's cup (acc. sg. + -que)
glossary.evadere: ēvādō — to escape, to get clear of (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.evectus: ēvehō — carried up, having risen (perf. pass. part. with middle force, nom. sg. m.)
glossary.evicere: ēvincō — they overcame, they got past (3 pl. pf. act. ind., the poetic -ēre for -ērunt; the same spelling is also the pres. pass. inf., to be overcome, which is not meant here)
glossary.examinat: exāminō — weighs out, examines (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.experientis: experiēns — of the enterprising, of the much-tried (pres. act. part. of experior used as an adjective, gen. sg. m., with Ulixeī; the same spelling can also stand for the acc. pl. experientēs)
glossary.expugnantior: expugnō — more overpowering, better at storming down resistance (comparative of the pres. part. expugnāns, nom. sg. f., with herba; the reading of the Magnus text, where other editions print expugnācior from expugnāx)
glossary.exsecratur: exsecror — curses, calls down curses on (deponent, 3 sg. pres.)
glossary.exspes: exspēs — without hope, hopeless (indeclinable adj., here nom. sg. m.)
glossary.exstante: exstō — standing out, projecting (pres. part., abl. sg. m. with uterō)
glossary.faucibus: faucēs — throat, jaws, gullet (dat. pl.; the noun is used only in the plural)
glossary.femorum: femur — thigh (n., gen. pl.; the alternative gen. pl. feminum also occurs)
glossary.ferventes: ferveō — boiling, seething (pres. part., acc. pl. f. with undās)
glossary.fineque: fīnis — end, limit; here with opus est, 'there is no need of an end' (abl. sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.fingebam: fingō — I imagined, I pictured to myself (1 sg. impf.)
glossary.finito: fīniō — finished, ended; in abl. absolute with Mārte, 'the war being over' (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. m.)
glossary.flaventi: flāveō — golden-yellow, tawny (pres. part., abl. sg. n. with villō)
glossary.flentem: fleō — weeping (pres. part., acc. sg. m., object of amplectimur)
glossary.fluidos: fluidus — flowing, dripping (acc. pl. m. with rictūs)
glossary.foedari: foedō — to be defiled, be disfigured (pres. pass. inf., in indirect statement after adspicit)
glossary.fugientibus: fugiō — fleeing; those fleeing (pres. part., dat. pl. m. governed by instat)
glossary.fumantes: fūmō — smoking, steaming (pres. part., acc. pl. f. with terrās; some editions print fumantis)
glossary.gemebundus: gemebundus — groaning, moaning (adj., nom. sg. m.)
glossary.gentem: gēns — people, race, nation (f., acc. sg.)
glossary.giganteo: Gigantēus — of the Giants, giant-sized (adj., abl. sg. m. with lacertō)
glossary.glomerata: glomerō — balled together, clotted into lumps (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. n. with frusta)
glossary.grani: grānum — grain, kernel (n., gen. sg. with tostī, 'of roasted grain'; the same form would also be nom. pl. of a masculine grānus, which is not in play here)
glossary.gratos: grātus — grateful, thankful (acc. pl. m.; the commoner sense of this adj. is the opposite direction, 'pleasing, welcome', but here the men are the ones feeling gratitude)
glossary.gurges: gurges — pool, eddying water, whirlpool; here a small sheltered inlet (m., nom. sg.)
glossary.habitantum: habitō — of the inhabitants, of those dwelling there (pres. part. used as a noun, gen. pl.; poetic -um for -ium)
glossary.haeremusque: haereō — we cling, we hang on to (1 pl. pres., with dat.) + -que 'and'
glossary.harenosae: harēnōsus — sandy (gen. sg. f. with terrae; the same form is also nom. pl. f., not the case here)
glossary.hausimus: hauriō — we drained, we drank up (1 pl. pf.)
glossary.hausti: hauriō — scooped up, taken up (perf. pass. part., gen. sg. m. with pulveris)
glossary.haustis: hauriō — drawn deep, drawn up (perf. pass. part., abl. pl. m. with suspīrātibus)
glossary.hecateia: Hecatēius — of Hecate, belonging to the goddess of witchcraft (adj., acc. pl. n. with carmina)
glossary.herbiferos: herbifer — grass-bearing, herb-producing (adj., acc. pl. m. with collēs)
glossary.hippotadae: Hippotadēs — son of Hippotes, i.e. Aeolus, keeper of the winds (Greek patronymic, gen. sg.)
glossary.hippotaden: Hippotadēs — son of Hippotes, i.e. Aeolus, keeper of the winds (Greek patronymic, acc. sg. in -ēn)
glossary.hirsuti: hirsūtus — shaggy, bristly (gen. sg. m. with leōnis; the same form is also nom. pl. m.)
glossary.honorat: honōrō — honours, pays honour to (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.hordea: hordeum — barley (n., acc. pl., poetic pl. for sg.; acc. subject of the passive inf. miscērī)
glossary.horrendis: horrendus — dreadful, to be shuddered at (gerundive of horreō used as an adj., abl. pl. m. with sūcīs)
glossary.horrendum: horrendus — dreadful, terrifying (gerundive of horreō used as an adj., acc. sg. n. with iter)
glossary.iaculantem: iaculor — hurling, flinging (deponent pres. part., acc. sg. m.)
glossary.improvisoque: imprōvīsō — unexpectedly, without warning (adverbial abl. of imprōvīsus 'unforeseen') + -que 'and'; some editions spell it inprovisoque
glossary.inarimen: Inarimē — Inarime, the volcanic island off Campania (mod. Ischia) (f., Greek acc. sg. in -ēn)
glossary.inclamare: inclāmō — to call out, shout aloud (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.inclusos: inclūdō — shut in, penned up (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m. agreeing with quōs, the winds)
glossary.incursat: incursō — runs against, blunders into, keeps colliding with (frequentative of incurrō, 3 sg. pres.)
glossary.iniectam: iniciō — thrown upon, heaped over (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f. with Aetnēn)
glossary.inmansuetique: immānsuētus — untamed, savage (gen. sg. m. with Cyclōpis; spelled inm- here by assimilation) + -que 'and'
glossary.inquinat: inquinō — fouls, taints, poisons (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.inundet: inundō — may flood, may pour over (3 sg. pres. subj., in the wish introduced by ō sī)
glossary.italico: Italicus — Italian, of Italy (adj., abl. sg. n. with lītore)
glossary.ithacique: Ithacus — the man of Ithaca, i.e. Ulysses (m., gen. sg.) + -que 'and'; some editions print Ithaceque, from Ithacē the island
glossary.iustissime: iūstus — most just, most righteous (superlative, voc. sg. m., addressing Aeneas; the identical form iūstissimē is elsewhere the superlative adverb 'most justly', which is not the use here)
glossary.laestrygonis: Laestrȳgōn — Laestrygonian, one of the man-eating people ruled by Antiphates (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.lami: Lāmus — Lamus, legendary founder of the Laestrygonian city (m., gen. sg.)
glossary.laniem: laniō — may I mangle, may I tear to pieces (1 sg. pres. subj., in a wish)
glossary.lassos: lassus — weary, tired out (acc. pl. m. with passūs)
glossary.lateant: lateō — lie hidden, lurk (3 pl. pres. subj., in a relative clause)
glossary.latrantibus: lātrō — barking (pres. part., abl. pl. n. with mōnstrīs)
glossary.ligamina: ligāmen — band, tie, fastening (n., acc. pl.)
glossary.liquerat: linquō — had left, had left behind (3 sg. plupf.; from linquō 'leave', not from liqueō 'be liquid, be clear', whose forms look similar)
glossary.litatis: litō — duly offered with favourable omens (perf. pass. part., abl. pl. n. with sacrīs in an abl. absolute)
glossary.locatas: locō — placed, situated (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. f. with Pithēcūsās)
glossary.lucibus: lūx — day (f., abl. pl. of time; the ordinary sense is 'light', but in the plural with a numeral it means 'days')
glossary.lupis: lupus — wolf (m., dat. pl. with mixtae, 'mingled with wolves'; the form is also the abl. pl.)
glossary.macareu: Macareus — Macareus, the companion of Ulysses who is speaking (m., Greek voc. sg. in -eu)
glossary.madentes: madeō — dripping, wet, soaked (pres. part., acc. pl. m. with vultūs)
glossary.magnanimi: magnanimus — great-souled, high-hearted (gen. sg. m. with Anchīsae; the same form is also nom. pl. m., not the use here)
glossary.mandentemque: mandō, mandere — chewing, champing (pres. part., acc. sg. m.; distinct from mandō, mandāre 'entrust, order', whose forms overlap) + -que 'and'
glossary.manerem: maneō — I would have remained (1 sg. impf. subj., apodosis of a past contrary-to-fact condition)
glossary.medeare: medeor — that you heal, that you cure (deponent, 2 sg. pres. subj., with the poetic ending -re for -ris; takes the dative)
glossary.melioribus: bonus — better (comparative melior, abl. pl. m. with sūcīs)
glossary.mellaque: mel — honey (n., acc. pl., poetic pl. for sg.) + -que 'and'
glossary.memorante: memorō — recounting, telling (pres. part., abl. sg. f. with Sibyllā in an abl. absolute)
glossary.merguntque: mergō — they sink, they send under (3 pl. pres.) + -que 'and'
glossary.mersura: mergō — about to sink, going to send under (fut. act. part., nom. sg. f.; with fuerat it forms 'she would soon have sunk')
glossary.mersurum: mergō — about to plunge, going to bury (fut. act. part., acc. sg. m., in indirect statement after rēbar)
glossary.minimas: parvus — smallest, shortest (superlative minimus, acc. pl. f. with umbrās)
glossary.miratus: mīror — having marvelled, wondering at (deponent perf. part., nom. sg. m.; active in sense and often nearly present in force)
glossary.misceri: misceō — to be mixed, to be blended (pres. pass. inf. after iubet)
glossary.mixtis: misceō — for the things mixed together, for the mixtures (perf. pass. part. used as a noun, dat. pl. n.)
glossary.moly: mōly — moly, the magic white-flowered herb Mercury gave Ulysses against Circe (Greek n., indeclinable, here acc. sg.)
glossary.monitisque: monitum — warning, counsel (n., abl. pl.; originally the perf. pass. part. of moneō used as a noun) + -que 'and'
glossary.moriri: morior — to die (deponent, archaic and poetic pres. inf. formed as if from a 4th-conjugation morīrī, for the usual morī)
glossary.moveret: moveō — was stirring, was rousing herself (3 sg. impf. subj. in a cum-clause; reflexive here with sēsē)
glossary.mulcere: mulceō — to stroke, to touch lightly (pres. act. inf.; not mulgeō 'to milk', which has similar forms)
glossary.multisque: multus — many (abl. pl. f. with corōnīs) + -que 'and'
glossary.musta: mustum — new wine, must; by extension a vintage, a year's pressing (n., acc. pl.)
glossary.mutentur: mūtō — be changed, be altered (3 pl. pres. pass. subj.)
glossary.nascentur: nāscor — will be born, will spring up (deponent, 3 pl. fut.)
glossary.natales: nātālis — birthday, and so a year of life (m. noun, acc. pl.; the same form serves the adj. nātālis 'of birth', but here it is the noun)
glossary.navifragumque: nāvifragus — ship-wrecking, that breaks ships (adj., acc. sg. n. with fretum) + -que 'and'
glossary.negabamus: negō — we refused, we kept saying no (1 pl. impf., with an inf.)
glossary.neritius: Nērītius — of Neritos, the mountain on Ithaca, and so Ithacan (adj., nom. sg. m.)
glossary.nimiique: nimius — excessive, too much of (gen. sg. n. with vīnī, the phrase describing Elpenor as over-fond of wine) + -que 'and'
glossary.nitidi: nitidus — shining, radiant (gen. sg. m. with Sōlis; the same form is also nom. pl. m., not the use here)
glossary.nocenti: noceō — harmful, baneful (pres. part. used as an adj., abl. sg. f. with rādīce)
glossary.nonam: nōnus — ninth (acc. sg. f., with a dawn understood: 'after the ninth')
glossary.noscar: nōscō — I shall be known, I shall be recognized (1 sg. fut. pass.)
glossary.noscit: nōscō — recognizes, comes to know (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.novorum: novus — new, strange, unheard-of (gen. pl. n. with verbōrum)
glossary.occallescere: occallēscō — to grow hard, to harden into a callus (inceptive, pres. act. inf.)
glossary.occursu: occursus — a running to meet, an encounter (m., abl. sg.)
glossary.operosae: operōsus — painstaking, hard-working, and so potent (gen. sg. f. with herbae; the same form is also nom. pl. f., not the use here)
glossary.oppositumque: oppōnō — set opposite, lying over against (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. n. with Rhēgion) + -que 'and'
glossary.optantemque: optō — desiring, wishing for (pres. part., acc. sg. f.) + -que 'and'
glossary.optes: optō — you wish, you choose (2 sg. pres. subj., in an indirect question)
glossary.oravique: ōrō — I begged for, I entreated (1 sg. pf.) + -que 'and'
glossary.orbataque: orbō — bereft, robbed of (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., taking the abl. of what is lost) + -que 'and'
glossary.orci: Orcus — Orcus, the underworld and its god (m., gen. sg.; the same form is also nom. pl., not the use here)
glossary.pacifer: pācifer — peace-bringing (adj., nom. sg. m., an epithet of Mercury and his wand)
glossary.pallamque: palla — palla, the long outer robe of a woman (f., acc. sg., retained as object with the middle-voice participle indūta) + -que 'and'
glossary.parthenopeia: Parthenopēius — of Parthenope, i.e. Neapolitan, of Naples (adj., acc. pl. n. with moenia)
glossary.passo: passum — raisin wine, wine from dried grapes (abl. sg. n.); homograph: identical in form to the perf. part. of patior (having suffered) and of pandō (spread out), and to dat./abl. sg. of passus, a pace — here the noun, the drink Circe mixes with the curds; the wording of the line is textually disputed
glossary.paterer: patior — allow, submit to (1 sg. imperf. subj., deponent)
glossary.patienda: patior — must be endured (gerundive, nom. sg. f., agreeing with senectus)
glossary.patuisset: pateō — lie open, be accessible (3 sg. pluperf. subj.)
glossary.pedumque: pēs — foot (gen. pl.) + -que and; homograph: pedum is also a neuter noun meaning shepherd's crook, but here it is the genitive plural of pēs
glossary.pellens: pellō — drive away, beat off (pres. act. part., nom. sg. m.)
glossary.pensas: pendō — weigh, weigh out (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. f., agreeing with herbas); homograph: also the 2 sg. pres. of pensō, to weigh, but here a participle
glossary.peraravit: perarō — plough through, furrow all over (3 sg. pf.)
glossary.percutimurque: percutiō — strike, smite (1 pl. pres. pass.) + -que and; caput is an accusative of respect, we are struck on the head
glossary.permaneo: permaneō — remain, continue to be (1 sg. pres.)
glossary.pertimui: pertimēscō — grow thoroughly afraid, dread (1 sg. pf.)
glossary.petitam: petō — seek, make for (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f., agreeing with terram: the land they were making for)
glossary.picum: pīcus — woodpecker (acc. sg.); here the bird perched on the statue's head, with an obvious play on Pīcus, the king the statue represents
glossary.pithecusas: Pithēcūsae — Pithecusae, the island off Campania, modern Ischia (acc. pl.)
glossary.politen: Polītēs — Polites, one of Ulysses' companions (acc. sg., Greek form)
glossary.portentificisque: portentificus — monster-making, working prodigies (abl. pl. n., agreeing with venenis) + -que and
glossary.positum: pōnō — place, set up (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. n., agreeing with signum)
glossary.possimne: possum — be able, can (1 sg. pres. subj.) + -ne, the enclitic question particle
glossary.potior: potior, potius — preferable, better, of more account (comparative adj., nom. sg. f., agreeing with domus); homograph and a real trap: identical to the 1 sg. pres. of the deponent verb potior, to gain possession of, which this book uses elsewhere (potiere) — here the adjective
glossary.praecorrumpere: praecorrumpō — bribe beforehand, corrupt in advance (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.praeteriit: praetereō — pass by, go past (3 sg. pf.)
glossary.praevitiat: praevitiō — taint beforehand, spoil in advance (3 sg. pres.); a rare verb, apparently coined here
glossary.prensurum: prendō (prehendō) — seize, grasp (fut. act. part., acc. sg. m., in indirect statement with rebar, with esse understood)
glossary.procedit: prōcēdō — come forward, advance (3 sg. pres.)
glossary.prochytenque: Prochytē — Prochyta, the island off Campania, modern Procida (acc. sg., Greek form) + -que and
glossary.prora: prōra — prow, ship's bow, by extension the ship itself (nom. sg.)
glossary.protendens: prōtendō — stretch out, extend (pres. act. part., nom. sg. m.)
glossary.proterva: protervus — shameless, wanton, savage (acc. pl. n., agreeing with ora, the mouths of the dogs); the form is also nom. sg. f., but not here
glossary.pulchro: pulcher — beautiful, fair (abl. sg. m., agreeing with recessu)
glossary.pyra: pyra — funeral pyre (abl. sg., with in)
glossary.raptus: rapiō — snatch, sweep along (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m.); homograph: also the noun raptus, a carrying off, in the nom./gen. sg. — here the participle, agreeing with Glaucus
glossary.rastra: rastrum — hoe, mattock, drag-rake (acc. pl. n.)
glossary.rati: ratis — raft, boat, ship (dat. sg., governed by nocuit); homograph and a real trap: identical to the perf. part. of reor (nom. pl. m., having thought), which occurs in this same passage as ratos — here the noun
glossary.ratos: reor — think, suppose, believe (perf. part., acc. pl. m.; deponent, so active in sense: thinking it to be gold); homograph: the same form serves the adjective ratus, fixed, valid — not the sense here
glossary.raucum: raucus — hoarse, harsh-sounding (acc. sg. n., agreeing with murmur)
glossary.redigentur: redigō — reduce, bring down to (3 pl. fut. pass.)
glossary.reduxit: redūcō — lead back, bring back (3 sg. pf.)
glossary.regnabat: regnō — reign, be king (3 sg. imperf.)
glossary.relinquent: relinquō — leave, leave behind (3 pl. fut.); note the future, not the present relinquunt, which appears elsewhere in this book
glossary.resimas: resīmus — bent back, turned up, snub (acc. pl. f., agreeing with nares)
glossary.respicio: respiciō — look back at, gaze upon (1 sg. pres.)
glossary.rhegi: Rhēgium — Rhegium, the Italian city on the strait, modern Reggio (gen. sg.)
glossary.rhegion: Rhēgium — Rhegium (acc. sg., Greek form Rhēgion)
glossary.rogaberis: rogō — ask, ask for, court, woo (2 sg. fut. pass.: you will be the one asked)
glossary.rogavi: rogō — ask, ask for, request (1 sg. pf.)
glossary.sacrisque: sacrum — sacred rite, sacrifice (abl. pl. n., in the abl. abs. sacris litatis) + -que and; homograph: the same form serves the adj. sacer (abl./dat. pl.)
glossary.saetaeque: saeta — bristle, coarse hair (nom. pl.) + -que and
glossary.saetigeri: saetiger — bristle-bearing, bristly (gen. sg. n., agreeing with pecoris: of the bristly herd, i.e. swine)
glossary.saeviat: saeviō — rage, be furious (3 sg. pres. subj., in a relative clause of purpose)
glossary.salute: salūs — greeting, salutation (abl. sg., in the abl. abs. dicta acceptaque salute); note the sense: salūs more usually means safety or welfare, but here it is the greeting given and received
glossary.sanesque: sānō — heal, cure (2 sg. pres. subj., in the clause governed by mando) + -que and
glossary.saxeus: saxeus — of stone, stony (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.scyllae: Scylla — Scylla, the nymph turned sea-monster (gen. or dat. sg.; in grata quies Scyllae either reading works, Scylla's welcome rest or rest welcome to Scylla)
glossary.secernunt: sēcernō — separate, sort out (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.semianimesque: sēmianimis — half-alive, half-dead (acc. pl. m., agreeing with artus) + -que and
glossary.senilem: senīlis — of an old man, aged (acc. sg. f., agreeing with umbram)
glossary.sensum: sēnsus — sense, feeling, consciousness (acc. sg.); homograph: identical to the perf. pass. part. of sentiō (acc. sg. m. / nom.-acc. sg. n.) — here the noun, paired with animum
glossary.sese: sē — himself, herself, itself (acc. sg., emphatic reduplicated form of sē; here reflexive with moveret)
glossary.sibylla: Sibylla — the Sibyl, the prophetess of Cumae (abl. sg., in the abl. abs. memorante Sibylla)
glossary.sibyllae: Sibylla — the Sibyl of Cumae (gen. sg.)
glossary.siculaeque: Siculus — Sicilian (gen. sg. f., agreeing with terrae) + -que and
glossary.sidonis: Sīdōnis — the Sidonian woman, i.e. Dido of Carthage, Phoenician by origin (nom. sg. f., Greek-type feminine adjective used as a noun)
glossary.sinuatus: sinuō — bend, curve, wind (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m., agreeing with gurges)
glossary.sitientes: sitiō — be thirsty, thirst (pres. act. part., nom. pl. m.)
glossary.spargimur: spargō — sprinkle, scatter over (1 pl. pres. pass.)
glossary.sparsosque: spargō — scatter, strew (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m., agreeing with flores) + -que and
glossary.spectantem: spectō — look at, gaze on (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m., agreeing with me)
glossary.spernentem: spernō — scorn, reject (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m., used substantivally: the one who scorns you)
glossary.spiro: spīrō — breathe, draw breath (1 sg. pres.)
glossary.spoliavit: spoliō — strip, rob (someone, acc.) of (something, abl.) (3 sg. pf.)
glossary.statuam: statuō — set up, erect, establish (1 sg. fut.); homograph and a real trap: identical to the acc. sg. of statua, a statue — here the verb, with templa as its object, I shall build you temples
glossary.sterilique: sterilis — barren, unfruitful (abl. sg. m., agreeing with colle) + -que and
glossary.stetimusque: stō — stand, halt (1 pl. pf.) + -que and
glossary.subire: subeō — go under, enter, approach (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.substiterat: subsistō — halt, stay behind (3 sg. pluperf.)
glossary.suspiratibus: suspīrātus — a sighing, deep sigh (abl. pl., in the abl. abs. suspiratibus haustis, sighs drawn up from deep)
glossary.temptatis: temptō — try, test, put to the proof (perf. pass. part., abl. pl. f., agreeing with viribus)
glossary.testantia: testor — bear witness to, attest (pres. part., acc. pl. n., agreeing with verba; deponent, so active in sense: words attesting us grateful)
glossary.teucras: Teucrus — Trojan, of Teucer's line (acc. pl. f., agreeing with carinas)
glossary.timenda: timeō — fear (gerundive, nom. sg. f.: none of them was to be feared)
glossary.timetque: timeō — fear, be afraid of (3 sg. pres.) + -que and
glossary.titani: Tītānis — daughter of the Titan, i.e. Circe, child of the Sun (voc. sg. f.); Glaucus is addressing her; the form could also be read as dat. sg. of Tītān, but the vocative is what the sentence needs
glossary.tormenti: tormentum — engine of war, catapult, siege engine (gen. sg.)
glossary.tosti: torreō — parch, roast, scorch (perf. pass. part., gen. sg. n., agreeing with grani)
glossary.transformata: transformō — transform, change in shape (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., with foret forming a pluperf. pass. subj.)
glossary.tremescens: tremēscō — begin to tremble, tremble at (pres. act. part., nom. sg. m.; here with an accusative object, strepitum)
glossary.tremuloque: tremulus — trembling, shaky (abl. sg. m., agreeing with gradu) + -que and
glossary.trepident: trepidō — quiver, twitch, tremble in agitation (3 pl. pres. subj.)
glossary.troianae: Troianus — Trojan (nom. pl. f., agreeing with rates)
glossary.troiane: Troianus — Trojan, a man of Troy (voc. sg. m., the Sibyl addressing Aeneas)
glossary.tumidarum: tumidus — swelling, swollen (gen. pl. f., agreeing with aquarum)
glossary.tusco: Tuscus — Etruscan, Tuscan (abl. sg. n., agreeing with profundo)
glossary.ulixei: Ulixēs — Ulysses, Odysseus (gen. sg., the Greek-flavoured genitive in -ei)
glossary.umbramque: umbra — shade, ghost of the dead (acc. sg.) + -que and; the ordinary sense shadow is not what is meant here
glossary.unoque: ūnus — one, a single (abl. sg. n., agreeing with facto) + -que and
glossary.usae: ūtor — use, employ (perf. part., gen. sg. f., agreeing with Circes; deponent, so active in sense: of Circe, who had used the powers of herbs too cruelly); takes the ablative viribus
glossary.variasque: varius — varied, of many kinds, many-coloured (acc. pl. f., agreeing with herbas) + -que and
glossary.velatos: vēlō — veil, cover, clothe (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m.; corpora is a Greek accusative of respect, covered as to their whole bodies)
glossary.ventusve: ventus — wind (nom. sg.) + -ve or, the enclitic disjunctive
glossary.victos: vincō — conquer, overcome (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. m., agreeing with socios: the comrades overcome by envy and greed)
glossary.videar: videor — seem, appear (1 sg. pres. subj.; formally the passive of videō, but in this middle sense it means seem, not be seen)
glossary.visceraque: viscera — inward parts, flesh, entrails (acc. pl. n.; the noun is used chiefly in the plural) + -que and
glossary.vitale: vītālis — of life, life-giving (acc. sg. n., agreeing with lumen: the light of life)
glossary.vitasset: vītō — avoid, shun (3 sg. pluperf. subj., syncopated for vitavisset)
glossary.viventia: vīvō — live, be alive (pres. act. part., acc. pl. n., agreeing with viscera)
glossary.vocandus: vocō — call, name (gerundive, nom. sg. m.: you are not to be called an enemy)
glossary.vocatus: vocō — call, summon, invite (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m.); homograph: also the noun vocatus, a summons, in the nom. sg. or gen. sg. — here the participle, agreeing with ille
glossary.vomentem: vomō — vomit, spew out (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m.)
glossary.voveo: voveō — vow, pledge oneself (1 sg. pres.)
glossary.zancleia: Zanclēius — of Zancle, Zanclean (acc. pl. n., agreeing with saxa)
glossary.zanclen: Zanclē — Zancle, the old name of Messana in Sicily, modern Messina (acc. sg., Greek form)
glossary.acmon: Acmōn, -onis m. — Acmon, the hot-tempered Pleuronian companion of Diomedes (nom. sg.)
glossary.acmona: Acmōn, -onis m. — Acmon, Diomedes' companion (Greek acc. sg.)
glossary.acris: ācer, ācris, ācre — keen, spirited, fiery (gen. sg. m. here, with equi; the form is also nom. sg. f. and acc. pl. m./f.)
glossary.adhaesi: adhaereō, -ēre — I clung, stuck fast (1st sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.aduncae: aduncus, -a, -um — curved, hooked (nom. pl. f. here, with puppes; also gen.-dat. sg. f.)
glossary.aeneaeque: Aenēās, -ae m. — Aeneas + -que; “and for my Aeneas” (dat. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.aeneia: Aenēius, -a, -um — of Aeneas, Aeneas' (nom. sg. f.)
glossary.aeraque: āēr, āeris m. — the air, the sky + -que (Greek acc. sg. āera + enclitic) / from aes, aeris n., bronze (nom.-acc. pl. n.)
glossary.aetola: Aetōlus, -a, -um — Aetolian, i.e. Diomedes' (acc. pl. n., with arma)
glossary.aetolius: Aetōlius, -a, -um — Aetolian, of Aetolia (nom. sg. m., with heros = Diomedes)
glossary.albula: Albula, -ae f. — the Albula, old name of the Tiber (nom. sg.)
glossary.alcinoi: Alcinous, -ī m. — Alcinous, king of the Phaeacians, whose ship was turned to stone (gen. sg.)
glossary.almo: Almo, -ōnis m. — the Almo, a very short tributary of the Tiber (nom. sg.) / from almus, -a, -um, nourishing, kindly (dat.-abl. sg. m./n.)
glossary.amaris: amārus, -a, -um — bitter (abl. pl. f. here, with bacis) / from amō, you are loved (2nd sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.ambieratque: ambiō, -īre — had gone round, had canvassed, had entreated + -que (3rd sg. pluperf. act. indic. + enclitic)
glossary.ambrosia: ambrosia, -ae f. — ambrosia, the food and unguent of the gods (abl. sg. here, with mixta; nom. sg. is identical)
glossary.ancipitesque: anceps, ancipitis — twofold, double-edged, hazardous + -que (acc. pl. f., with vias, + enclitic)
glossary.anienis: Aniēn (Aniō), Aniēnis m. — the Anio, a tributary of the Tiber (gen. sg.)
glossary.animata: animō, -āre — given life, animated (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. f., with classe in an abl. absolute)
glossary.antemnae: antemna (antenna), -ae f. — yardarm, the spar carrying a sail (nom. pl.)
glossary.apros: aper, aprī m. — wild boar (acc. pl.)
glossary.apulus: Āpulus, -a, -um — Apulian, of Apulia in south-east Italy (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.ardea: Ardea, -ae f. — Ardea, Turnus' Rutulian capital (nom. sg.); Ovid plays on ardea, -ae f., heron, the bird that rises from its ashes
glossary.argolico: Argolicus, -a, -um — Argive, Greek (abl. sg. m., with igne)
glossary.arisque: āra, -ae f. — altar + -que (abl. pl. + enclitic; dat. pl. identical)
glossary.armet: armō, -āre — he may arm, equip (3rd sg. pres. act. subj.)
glossary.armiferae: armifer, -era, -erum — arms-bearing, warlike (gen. sg. f., with Minervae)
glossary.astraei: Astraeus, -ī m. — Astraeus, the Titan father of the winds (gen. sg.; Astraei fratres = the brother winds)
glossary.attactu: attactus, -ūs m. — a touching, contact (abl. sg.)
glossary.ausoniis: Ausonius, -a, -um — Ausonian, Italian (abl. pl. f., with terris)
glossary.caesas: caedō, -ere — cut down, felled (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. f., with pinus)
glossary.caietam: Cāiēta, -ae f. — Caieta, Aeneas' nurse, and the harbour town named for her (acc. sg.)
glossary.calydonia: Calydōnius, -a, -um — of Calydon, the Aetolian city of Diomedes' family (acc. pl. n., with regna)
glossary.camenae: Camēna, -ae f. — a Camena, old Italian goddess of song, identified with the Muses (nom. pl.)
glossary.canens: Canēns, -entis f. — Canens, daughter of Janus and wife of Picus; the name means “singing” (nom. sg.); as an ordinary word, pres. act. part. of canō, “singing”
glossary.canentem: Canēns, -entis f. — Canens, wife of Picus (acc. sg.; at 433 the place named after her) / pres. act. part. of canō, singing (acc. sg.)
glossary.cantato: cantō, -āre — chanted, sung as a spell (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. n., with carmine)
glossary.capherea: Caphēreus, -a, -um — Capherean, of Cape Caphereus, where the returning Greek fleet was wrecked (Greek acc. sg. m., with cumulum)
glossary.caphereus: Caphēreus, -eī m. — Caphereus, the deadly promontory of south-east Euboea (nom. sg.)
glossary.ceperunt: capiō, -ere — they took, they captured (3rd pl. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.chaoque: Chaos n. — Chaos, the primal void of the underworld + -que (abl. sg. + enclitic; the noun has only chaos and chao)
glossary.chlamydis: chlamys, -ydis f. — chlamys, a Greek military cloak (gen. sg.)
glossary.circumfusa: circumfundō, -ere — having wound herself around (+ dat.) (perf. pass. part. in middle sense, nom. sg. f.)
glossary.circumfususque: circumfundō, -ere — thronging around, crowded about + -que (perf. pass. part. in middle sense, nom. sg. m., with satelles, + enclitic)
glossary.columbis: columba, -ae f. — dove, the bird of Venus (abl. pl.)
glossary.concurrit: concurrō, -ere — rushes together, joins battle (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. here; the form is also 3rd sg. perf.)
glossary.confundere: confundō, -ere — to blur, to throw into confusion (pres. act. infin.)
glossary.congerie: congeriēs, -ēī f. — heap, pile — here the burnt mass of the city (abl. sg.)
glossary.contempsere: contemnō, -ere — they scorned, they made light of (3rd pl. perf. act. indic. = contempsērunt)
glossary.continuo: continuō — at once, immediately (adv.) / from continuus, -a, -um, unbroken (dat.-abl. sg. m./n.)
glossary.contractus: contrahō, -ere — drawn together, gathered up (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m., with chlamydem as a Greek acc. of respect) / as a noun, contractus, -ūs m., a drawing together
glossary.corripimus: corripiō, -ere — we round on, seize upon, rebuke (1st pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.cremabit: cremō, -āre — will burn up, will consume (3rd sg. fut. act. indic.)
glossary.cremata: cremō, -āre — burned, burnt up (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f., agreeing with Ilion, which Ovid treats as feminine here)
glossary.cremavit: cremō, -āre — he burned, he cremated (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.crescentis: crescō, -ere — growing, growing up (pres. act. part., gen. sg. m. here, with Iuli; the form is also acc. pl.)
glossary.criminibusque: crīmen, -inis n. — charge, accusation + -que (abl. pl. + enclitic)
glossary.cubitusque: cubitus, -ī m. — elbow, forearm + -que (nom. sg. + enclitic; distinct from cubitus, -ūs m., a lying down)
glossary.cumulumque: cumulus, -ī m. — heap, crowning addition + -que (acc. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.cuperet: cupiō, -ere — she desired, she wanted (3rd sg. imperf. act. subj., in an indirect question)
glossary.dauni: Daunus, -ī m. — Daunus, king of Apulia and Diomedes' father-in-law (gen. sg.)
glossary.dauno: Daunus, -ī m. — Daunus, king of Apulia (abl. sg., governed by sub)
glossary.deplangitur: dēplangō, -ere — is bewailed, is mourned with beating (3rd sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.deponendique: dēpōnō, -ere — of laying down, of giving up + -que (gerund, gen. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.desuetudine: dēsuētūdō, -inis f. — disuse, being out of practice (abl. sg.)
glossary.dicente: dīcō, -ere — speaking (pres. act. part., abl. sg. f., with dea in an abl. absolute)
glossary.dictu: dīcō, -ere — to tell, in the telling (supine in -ū, abl.; mirabile dictu = “wonderful to tell”)
glossary.digessit: dīgerō, -ere — he distributed, he spread (it) out (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.digni: dignus, -a, -um — worthy, deserving (+ abl.) (nom. pl. m.)
glossary.disces: discō, -ere — you will learn (2nd sg. fut. act. indic.)
glossary.discurrunt: discurrō, -ere — they run off in all directions (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.domitis: domō, -āre — tamed, broken (perf. pass. part., abl. pl. m., with leonibus)
glossary.dotalia: dōtālis, -e — of a dowry, given as a dowry (acc. pl. n., with regna)
glossary.dotaliaque: dōtālis, -e — of a dowry, given as a dowry + -que (acc. pl. n., with arva, + enclitic)
glossary.dubiarum: dubius, -a, -um — doubtful, hard to identify (gen. pl. f., with volucrum)
glossary.durisque: dūrus, -a, -um — hard, rugged + -que (abl. pl. m., with montibus, + enclitic)
glossary.ereboque: Erebus, -ī m. — Erebus, the darkness of the underworld + -que (abl. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.ereptam: ēripiō, -ere — snatched away, rescued (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. f.)
glossary.eripiam: ēripiō, -ere — I shall snatch (them) away (1st sg. fut. act. indic. here; the form is also pres. act. subj.)
glossary.estis: sum, esse — you are (2nd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.euandri: Euander, -drī m. — Evander, the Arcadian king settled on the future site of Rome (gen. sg.)
glossary.everberat: ēverberō, -āre — beats hard, thrashes (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.exequialia: exequiālis (exsequiālis), -e — funeral, belonging to obsequies (acc. pl. n., with carmina)
glossary.exhibet: exhibeō, -ēre — displays, presents (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.exsequitur: exsequor, exsequī — carries out, performs (3rd sg. pres. indic., deponent)
glossary.exspectatus: exspectō, -āre — awaited, watched for (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m.; with erat = pluperf. pass.)
glossary.externa: externus, -a, -um — outside, foreign (abl. sg. f. here, with venere; the form is also nom. sg. f. and nom.-acc. pl. n.)
glossary.externo: externus, -a, -um — outside, external (abl. sg. n., with robore)
glossary.farfarus: Farfarus, -ī m. — the Farfar (Fabaris), a Sabine tributary of the Tiber (nom. sg.)
glossary.fassura: fateor, fatērī — about to confess, on the point of admitting (fut. act. part., nom. sg. f.)
glossary.faunigenaeque: Faunigena, -ae m. — the Faunus-born one, son of Faunus, i.e. Latinus + -que (gen. sg. + enclitic)
glossary.fecundis: fēcundus, -a, -um — fruitful, rich (abl. pl. m., with collibus)
glossary.feminea: fēmineus, -a, -um — womanly, of a woman (abl. sg. f., with voce)
glossary.ferentes: ferō, ferre — bringing, carrying (pres. act. part., nom. pl. m.)
glossary.fervidus: fervidus, -a, -um — burning, hot-headed, impetuous (nom. sg. m.)
glossary.fictaque: fingō, -ere — shaped, fashioned, made up + -que (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. f., with imagine, + enclitic)
glossary.finitimosque: finitimus, -a, -um — “neighboring, adjoining” (acc. pl. m. with lacūs, + enclitic -que “and”)
glossary.flammaque: flamma, -ae f. — “flame, fire” (nom. sg. + enclitic -que; here the fire of love running through the marrow)
glossary.flenda: fleō, flēre — “I weep, lament” (gerundive, nom. sg. f. with Graecia: “to be wept for”)
glossary.flumineis: flūmineus, -a, -um — “of a river, river-” (abl. pl. f. with undīs)
glossary.fontana: fontānus, -a, -um — “of a spring, of the fountains” (nom. pl. n. with nūmina)
glossary.fretoque: fretum, -ī n. — “strait, open sea” (abl. sg. + enclitic -que; not the adjective frētus “relying on”, which the unmacronned spelling matches)
glossary.fugatas: fugō, -āre — “I put to flight, drive off” (perf. pass. part., acc. pl. f. with hās, the nymphs; from fugō, not from fugiō “flee”)
glossary.fundatis: fundō, -āre — “I found, establish” (perf. pass. part., abl. pl. f. with opibus in an abl. abs.; not from fundō, -ere “pour”, and not the 2nd pl. pres. here)
glossary.funis: fūnis, -is m. — “rope, mooring-cable” (nom. sg., subject of solvitur)
glossary.graia: Grāius, -a, -um — “Greek” (abl. sg. f. with Ēlide, the Elis of the Olympic games)
glossary.gratesque: grātēs f. pl. — “thanks” (acc. pl.; the word exists only in the plural; + enclitic -que)
glossary.habetque: habeō, -ēre — “I have, hold” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. + enclitic -que)
glossary.hecaten: Hecatē, -ēs f. — Hecate, goddess of the crossroads, night and witchcraft, patroness of Circe (Greek acc. sg.)
glossary.herboso: herbōsus, -a, -um — “grassy, overgrown with grass” (abl. sg. m. with aggere)
glossary.ianigenam: Iānigena, -ae — “child of Janus” (acc. sg. f. with Canentem; Canens is the daughter of Janus and Venilia)
glossary.iano: Iānus, -ī m. — Janus, the two-faced god of doorways and beginnings (dat. sg., “to Janus”, with peperisse)
glossary.iapyge: Iāpyx, -ygis — “Iapygian, Apulian” (abl. sg. m. with Daunō; Iapygia is the heel of Italy, Apulia)
glossary.iapygis: Iāpyx, -ygis — “Iapygian, Apulian” (gen. sg. m. with Daunī)
glossary.idaeo: Īdaeus, -a, -um — “of Mount Ida” (abl. sg. m. with vertice; the Trojan Ida, whose pines built Aeneas' fleet)
glossary.ignotosque: ignōtus, -a, -um — “unknown, strange” (acc. pl. m. with deōs + enclitic -que)
glossary.immotos: immōtus, -a, -um — “unmoved, unchanging” (acc. pl. m. with vultūs)
glossary.importunusque: importūnus, -a, -um — “relentless, pitiless” (nom. sg. m. with Caphēreus + enclitic -que)
glossary.improbat: improbō, -āre — “I disapprove of, jeer at” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.incurvae: incurvus, -a, -um — “curved, bent” (gen. sg. f. with carīnae)
glossary.indigenas: indigena, -ae — “native, native-born” (acc. pl. m. with aprōs; a 1st-decl. noun used adjectivally)
glossary.indigetem: Indiges, -getis m. — Indiges, the cult-title of Aeneas once deified, a native ancestral god (acc. sg.)
glossary.indurata: indūrō, -āre — “I harden” (perf. pass. part., nom. pl. n. with ōra)
glossary.infamataeque: īnfāmō, -āre — “I defame, give an evil name to” (perf. pass. part., gen. sg. f. with deae, i.e. Circe + enclitic -que)
glossary.inflati: īnflō, -āre — “I blow into” (perf. pass. part., gen. sg. n. with buxī, the blown boxwood pipe)
glossary.ingemuitque: ingemō, -ere — “I groan, give a groan” (3rd sg. perf. act. indic. + enclitic -que)
glossary.inire: ineō, inīre — “I enter, set out upon” (pres. act. infin., depending on iubēmur)
glossary.instimulat: īnstimulō, -āre — “I goad on, incite” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.intonuit: intonō, -āre — “I thunder” (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.iratam: īrātus, -a, -um — “angry, enraged” (acc. sg. f. with Venerem; originally the perf. part. of īrāscor)
glossary.iuli: Iūlus, -ī m. — Iulus (Ascanius), son of Aeneas and claimed ancestor of the Julian house (gen. sg.)
glossary.laedam: laedō, -ere — “I injure, violate” (1st sg.; future act. indic. here, “I will not violate”; the form is identical to the pres. act. subj.)
glossary.latini: Latīnus, -ī m. — Latinus, king of Latium and father of Lavinia (gen. sg.)
glossary.latio: Latium, -ī n. — Latium, the region of Italy around Rome (dat. sg. with concurrit, “clashes with Latium”; the form is also abl.)
glossary.latios: Latius, -a, -um — “Latian, of Latium” (acc. pl. m. with agrōs)
glossary.latuerunt: lateō, -ēre — “I lie hidden, am buried out of sight” (3rd pl. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.laurens: Laurēns, -entis — “Laurentine, of Laurentum” (acc. sg. n. with lītus; Laurentum is the coastal town of Latinus' kingdom)
glossary.laurentes: Laurēns, -entis — “Laurentine, of Laurentum” (acc. pl. m. with agrōs)
glossary.laurenti: Laurēns, -entis — “Laurentine, of Laurentum” (dat. sg. m. with Pīcō)
glossary.lavinia: Lāvīnia, -ae f. — Lavinia, daughter of Latinus, promised to Turnus and married to Aeneas (voc. sg., with virgō)
glossary.legati: lēgātus, -ī m. — “envoy, ambassador” (nom. pl., subject of rediēre; the form is also the perf. pass. part. of lēgō, -āre “depute”)
glossary.legerat: legō, -ere — “I gather, pick” (3rd sg. pluperf. act. indic.; the same verb also means “read”, but here Circe is picking herbs)
glossary.lusibus: lūsus, -ūs m. — “play, sport” (abl. pl., of means)
glossary.lustratum: lūstrō, -āre — “I purify by ritual” (perf. pass. part., acc. sg. n. with corpus; the same verb elsewhere means “traverse, survey”)
glossary.lycus: Lycus, -ī m. — Lycus, one of Diomedes' comrades turned into a bird (nom. sg.)
glossary.maduerunt: madeō, -ēre — “I am wet, am soaked” (3rd pl. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.manantia: mānō, -āre — “I flow, run, drip” (pres. act. part., acc. pl. n. with antra)
glossary.marinas: marīnus, -a, -um — “of the sea, sea-” (acc. pl. f. with nymphās)
glossary.mediisque: medius, -a, -um — “middle, the middle of” (dat. pl. n. with nāvigiīs after subdita + enclitic -que; the form is also abl.)
glossary.messapiaque: Messāpius, -a, -um — “Messapian”, of Messapia in Apulia (acc. pl. n. with arva + enclitic -que)
glossary.mitissimus: mītis, -e — “mild, gentle” (superl. mītissimus, nom. sg. m., predicate of sīs)
glossary.modulata: modulor, -ārī — “I sing, shape in measured song” (deponent perf. part., nom. sg. f., active in sense: “having sung”)
glossary.mollito: molliō, -īre — “I soften” (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. n. with rōbore in an abl. abs.)
glossary.momorderat: mordeō, -ēre — “I bite, grip fast” (3rd sg. pluperf. act. indic.; reduplicated perf. momordī)
glossary.multumque: multus, -a, -um — “much” (nom. sg. n. used as a noun with the partitive gen. cruōris + enclitic -que; the same form also serves as the adverb “much, greatly”)
glossary.naiades: Nāias, -adis f. — “Naiad, water-nymph” (Greek nom. pl., in apposition to nūmina)
glossary.narve: Nār, Nāris m. — the Nar (modern Nera), a sulphurous river of Umbria flowing into the Tiber (nom. sg. + enclitic -ve “or”)
glossary.natantia: natō, -āre — “I swim, float” (pres. act. part., acc. pl. n. with crūra after in)
glossary.nataque: nāta, -ae f. — “daughter” (abl. sg. governed by potītur, which takes the abl., + enclitic -que; not nom. or voc. here)
glossary.navigiis: nāvigium, -ī n. — “ship, vessel” (dat. pl. after subdita; the form is also abl.)
glossary.neritiaeque: Nēritius, -a, -um — “Neritian”, of Mt. Neritos on Ithaca, so “Ithacan, Ulysses'” (gen. sg. f. with ratis + enclitic -que)
glossary.novam: novus, -a, -um — “new, strange” (acc. sg. f. with avem, in the acc.-and-infin. after indignātus)
glossary.nubilibus: nūbilis, -e — “of marriageable age, ripe for marriage” (abl. pl. m. with annīs; from nūbō “marry”, not from nūbilum “cloud”)
glossary.numeri: numerus, -ī m. — “number” (gen. sg. of description: numerī māiōris amīcī, “the friends of the larger number”, the majority)
glossary.numici: Numīcius (Numīcus), -ī m. — the Numicius, a small river of Latium sacred to Aeneas (gen. sg., with aquae)
glossary.numicius: Numīcius, -ī m. — the Numicius, the Latian river in which Aeneas' mortal part is washed away (nom. sg.)
glossary.nuncupat: nuncupō, -āre — “I name, call by name” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.nycteus: Nycteus, -eī m. — Nycteus, a comrade of Diomedes turned into a bird (nom. sg.)
glossary.nymphen: nymphē, -ēs f. — “nymph” (Greek acc. sg.; the Latin form nympha, -ae also occurs)
glossary.oblitae: oblīvīscor, -ī — “I forget” (deponent perf. part., nom. pl. f. with nāides, active in sense; not from oblinō “smear”, whose part. is oblitus)
glossary.obscenis: obscēnus, -a, -um — “foul, obscene” (dat. pl. n. with dictīs after addidit; the form is also abl.)
glossary.occasum: occāsus, -ūs m. — “setting of the sun, the west” (acc. sg. after ad)
glossary.occiduus: occiduus, -a, -um — “setting, sinking westward” (nom. sg. m. with Phoebus)
glossary.oderit: ōdī, ōdisse — “I hate” (3rd sg. perf. subj. act. but present in sense, concessive after licet; the form is also fut. perf. indic.)
glossary.oenides: Oenīdēs, -ae m. — “son of Oeneus”, i.e. Diomedes (nom. sg.)
glossary.ortae: orior, -īrī — “I rise, spring up, am born” (deponent perf. part., nom. pl. f. with nāides, active in sense: “sprung from”)
glossary.pactaque: pacīscor, -ī — “I bargain for, contract for” (deponent perf. part. used passively, abl. sg. f. with coniuge: “betrothed, promised”, + enclitic -que)
glossary.palati: Palātium, -ī n. — the Palatine, the hill of Rome (gen. sg. with colle; not palātum “palate”)
glossary.parant: parō, -āre — “I prepare, make ready” (3rd pl. pres. act. indic., with the infin. incessere)
glossary.passaque: patior, patī — “I suffer, allow” (deponent perf. part., nom. sg. f., active in sense; with erat it forms “she had allowed”; + enclitic -que; not from pandō “spread open”)
glossary.passi: patior, patī — “I suffer, endure” (deponent perf. part., nom. pl. m. with comitēs, active in sense: “having endured”)
glossary.patiente: patiens, -entis (pres. act. part. of patior) — “allowing, permitting” (abl. sg. m. with mē in an abl. abs.; also used as an adjective, “enduring, patient”)
glossary.paventis: paveō, -ēre — “I am terrified, tremble” (pres. act. part.; gen. sg. with the collective vulgus, “of the panicking crowd”; the spelling is also the older acc. pl. paventēs)
glossary.paverunt: pāscō, -ere — “I feed, give food to” (3rd pl. perf. act. indic., with flammās as object: Pergamum fed the Greek flames; identical in form to the perf. of paveō, “they feared”)
glossary.pellor: pellō, -ere — “I drive out, expel” (1st sg. pres. pass. indic.: “I am driven out”)
glossary.perpetimur: perpetior, -petī — “I endure to the end” (deponent, 1st pl. pres. indic.)
glossary.pertulerint: perferō, -ferre — “I bear through, endure to the end” (3rd pl. perf. subj. act., in the indirect question after quam multa; the form is also fut. perf. indic.)
glossary.pervidet: pervideō, -ēre — “I see through, survey all things” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.pessima: malus, -a, -um — “bad”, superl. pessimus “worst” (nom. sg. f. with sors)
glossary.petebant: petō, -ere — “I seek, make for, court” (3rd pl. imperf. act. indic.)
glossary.peucetiosque: Peucetius, -a, -um — “Peucetian”, of Peucetia in Apulia (acc. pl. m. with sinūs + enclitic -que)
glossary.picem: pix, picis f. — “pitch, tar” (acc. sg.; from pix, not from Pīcus the king)
glossary.pico: Pīcus, -ī m. — Picus, king of Latium, son of Saturn, changed by Circe into a woodpecker (dat. sg. at 336 and 396; abl. sg. in the abl. abs. at 398; not from pix “pitch”)
glossary.picus: Pīcus, -ī m. — Picus, king of Latium, son of Saturn, whom Circe turns into a woodpecker (nom. sg.); the common noun pīcus “woodpecker” is the same word, and the pun is the point of the tale
glossary.pinea: pīneus, -a, -um — “of pine, pinewood” (acc. pl. n. with texta, “the pine-woven [ships]”; the same form can also be nom./abl. sg. f.)
glossary.placatoque: plācātus, -a, -um — “calmed, appeased, serene” (perf. pass. part. of plācō; abl. sg. n. with ōre, + -que “and”)
glossary.plausis: plaudō, plaudere, plausī, plausum — “beat, flap, clap” (perf. pass. part., abl. pl. f. with ālīs: “with beating wings”)
glossary.pleuronius: Pleurōnius, -a, -um — “of Pleuron,” a town in Aetolia (nom. sg. m., describing Acmon)
glossary.poeniceam: poenīceus (pūnīceus), -a, -um — “crimson, purple-red” (acc. sg. f. with chlamydem)
glossary.portant: portō, portāre — “carry, bear along” (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.praecingitur: praecingō, praecingere — “gird about, encircle” (3rd sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.praeposito: praepōnō, praepōnere, praeposuī, praepositum — “set before, prefer” (perf. pass. part., dat. sg. m. with Pīcō: “preferred to all”)
glossary.priamo: Priamus, -ī m. — Priam, last king of Troy (dat. sg.; dative of agent with the gerundive flenda, “to be wept over even by Priam”)
glossary.probes: probō, probāre — “approve, judge genuine, take as proven” (2nd sg. pres. act. subj., after licet: “you may judge”)
glossary.pronas: prōnus, -a, -um — “tipped forward, headlong, face-down” (acc. pl. f. with ratēs)
glossary.proripit: prōripiō, prōripere — “drag forth”; with sē, “rush out, tear oneself away” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.prorumpit: prōrumpō, prōrumpere — “burst forth, break out” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.pulsi: pellō, pellere, pepulī, pulsum — “strike, beat” (perf. pass. part., gen. sg. n. with aeris: “of struck bronze”; the same form is also nom. pl. m.)
glossary.puppem: puppis, -is f. — “stern, poop”; by extension “ship” (acc. sg.)
glossary.quinquennem: quīnquennis, -e — “five-yearly,” of the Olympic contest, counted inclusively though held every fourth year (acc. sg. f. with pugnam)
glossary.quirini: Quirīnus, -ī m. — Quirinus, the deified Romulus (gen. sg.; turba Quirīnī = the Roman people)
glossary.rapiare: rapiō, rapere — “snatch, sweep away” (2nd sg. pres. pass. subj., older form of rapiāris: “though you be carried off”)
glossary.rapti: rapiō, rapere, rapuī, raptum — “snatch, sweep away” (perf. pass. part., nom. pl. m., of the Greeks driven over the sea; the same form is also gen. sg. m./n.)
glossary.rarior: rārus, -a, -um — “rare, uncommon, exceptional” (comparative, nom. sg. f.)
glossary.raucos: raucus, -a, -um — “hoarse, harsh-sounding” (acc. pl. m. with mūgītūs)
glossary.recludi: reclūdō, reclūdere — “open up, unclose, disperse” (pres. pass. infin., after passa erat)
glossary.redeuntia: redeō, redīre — “return, come back” (pres. act. part., nom. pl. n. with lūmina: “the returning lights of the sun”)
glossary.religatus: religō, religāre — “bind fast, moor” (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m. with fūnis)
glossary.remi: rēmus, -ī m. — “oar” (nom. pl.; the identical form is also gen. sg., and Remus is the name of Romulus’ brother)
glossary.renoventur: renovō, renovāre — “renew, make fresh again” (3rd pl. pres. pass. subj., concessive after quamquam)
glossary.reperto: reperiō, reperīre, repperī, repertum — “find, discover” (perf. pass. part., abl. sg. m. with Pīcō in an ablative absolute)
glossary.reposcunt: reposcō, reposcere — “demand back, call for the return of” (3rd pl. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.repurgat: repurgō, repurgāre — “cleanse away, wash out” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.resides: reses, residis (adj.) — “inactive, slack, grown idle” (nom. pl. m.; distinct from residēs, 2nd sg. of resideō “sit back”)
glossary.respergit: respergō, respergere — “sprinkle, besprinkle” (3rd sg. pres. act. indic.)
glossary.respondere: respondeō, respondēre — “answer, reply” (pres. act. infin. with volentī; the identical respondēre can also be 3rd pl. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.retemptatis: retemptō (retentō), retemptāre — “try again, renew the attempt” (perf. pass. part., abl. pl. f. with precibus in an ablative absolute)
glossary.rhexenore: Rhēxēnōr, -oris m. — Rhexenor, one of Diomedes’ companions (abl. sg., after cum)
glossary.rutuli: Rutulus, -ī m. — a Rutulian, one of Turnus’ people in Latium (nom. pl.; the same form serves the adjective Rutulus, -a, -um)
glossary.rutulos: Rutulus, -ī m. — a Rutulian, one of Turnus’ Latin people (acc. pl.)
glossary.rutulum: Rutulus, -ī m. — “the Rutulian,” i.e. Turnus (acc. sg., subject of the infinitive dēsistere; the form can also be an older gen. pl. = Rutulōrum)
glossary.sacrilega: sacrilegus, -a, -um — “sacrilegious, impious” (abl. sg. f. with dextrā)
glossary.saevisque: saevus, -a, -um — “savage, cruel” (abl. pl. n. with tēlīs, + -que “and”)
glossary.saliente: saliō, salīre — “leap, bound” (pres. act. part., abl. sg. f. with grandine: “with bounding hail”)
glossary.saltuque: saltus, -ūs m. — “leap, bound; dancing step” (abl. sg. + -que “and”; the identical noun saltus also means “woodland glade,” not the sense here)
glossary.sancta: sānctus, -a, -um — “holy, hallowed” (nom. sg. f. with genetrīx, of Cybele; the same form can be nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.sanguineis: sanguineus, -a, -um — “bloody, blood-red” (abl. pl. f. with guttīs)
glossary.satelles: satelles, -itis m./f. — “attendant, escort,” here collectively the king’s retinue (nom. sg.)
glossary.scythicae: Scythicus, -a, -um — “Scythian, Tauric,” of the Diana whose cult came from the Tauric land to Aricia (gen. sg. f. with Diānae)
glossary.securaque: sēcūrus, -a, -um — “free from care, untroubled” (nom. sg. f. with summa, + -que “and”)
glossary.sequentem: sequor, sequī — “follow, pursue” (pres. act. part., acc. sg. m.: “the one chasing them”)
glossary.servabunt: servō, servāre — “keep, preserve, guard” (3rd pl. fut. act. indic.)
glossary.signata: signō, signāre — “mark, set a mark upon” (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. f. with fāma; the same form can be nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.socialia: sociālis, -e — “of alliance; conjugal, marriage-” (acc. pl. n. with foedera)
glossary.sollicitis: sollicitus, -a, -um — “anxious, restless, hard-pressed” (abl. pl. n. with armīs)
glossary.solvitur: solvō, solvere — “loosen, untie, cast off” (3rd sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.somnique: somnus, -ī m. — “sleep” (gen. sg. + -que “and”; genitive of want with inopem)
glossary.spectasse: spectō, spectāre — “watch, look on at” (syncopated perf. act. infin. = spectāvisse)
