glossary.spumantia: spūmō, spūmāre — “foam, be flecked with foam” (pres. act. part., acc. pl. n. with terga)
glossary.squalere: squāleō, squālēre — “be rough, bristle, be foul with” (pres. act. infin., with humus as subject)
glossary.stuppea: stuppeus, -a, -um — “of tow, hempen” (acc. pl. n. with retinācula)
glossary.subtexere: subtexō, subtexere — “weave beneath, spread over, veil” (pres. act. infin. with solet; the identical subtexēre can also be 3rd pl. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.sucosque: sūcus, -ī m. — “juice; distilled essence, potion” (acc. pl. + -que “and”)
glossary.supposuere: suppōnō, suppōnere, supposuī, suppositum — “put under, set beneath” (3rd pl. perf. act. indic. = supposuērunt)
glossary.suscipitur: suscipiō, suscipere — “take up, undertake” (3rd sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.tantosque: tantus, -a, -um — “so great, so many” (acc. pl. m. with labōrēs, + -que “and”)
glossary.tartessia: Tartēssius, -a, -um — “of Tartessus,” a city of southern Spain, hence “western” (acc. pl. n. with lītora)
glossary.teguntur: tegō, tegere — “cover, clothe” (3rd pl. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.tempestivus: tempestīvus, -a, -um — “timely, ripe, ready” (nom. sg. m.; here “ripe for heaven,” with caelō)
glossary.tenuaverat: tenuō, tenuāre — “make thin, thin out” (3rd sg. pluperf. act. indic.)
glossary.terrestribus: terrester (terrestris), -tris, -tre — “on land, of the land” (abl. pl. n. with armīs)
glossary.tetidem: totidem — “just as many” (indeclinable; the archived text prints tetidem, which is not a Latin word — read totidem, answering sex noctēs)
glossary.thybris: Thybris, -idis m. — the Tiber, and the river’s god (nom. sg.; Greek-declension form of Tiberis)
glossary.timebant: timeō, timēre — “fear, be afraid of” (3rd pl. imperf. act. indic.)
glossary.timentur: timeō, timēre — “fear” (3rd pl. pres. pass. indic.: “are feared”)
glossary.transcurrere: trānscurrō, trānscurrere — “run across, dash past” (pres. act. infin. in indirect command after iussit; the identical trānscurrēre can also be 3rd pl. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.transtra: trānstrum, -ī n. — “thwart, rower’s cross-bench” (nom. pl., subject of fūmābant)
glossary.turne: Turnus, -ī m. — Turnus, king of the Rutulians and Aeneas’ rival for Lavinia (voc. sg.)
glossary.turni: Turnus, -ī m. — Turnus, king of the Rutulians (gen. sg.)
glossary.turno: Turnus, -ī m. — Turnus (abl. sg., in the ablative absolute Turnō sōspite “while Turnus was safe”; the form is also dat. sg.)
glossary.turnus: Turnus, -ī m. — Turnus, Rutulian king, Aeneas’ rival for Lavinia (nom. sg.)
glossary.tyrrhenia: Tyrrhēnia, -ae f. — Etruria, the Etruscan country north of Latium (nom. sg.)
glossary.unxit: unguō (ungō), unguere, ūnxī, ūnctum — “anoint, smear” (3rd sg. perf. act. indic.)
glossary.urebat: ūrō, ūrere — “burn, consume with fire” (3rd sg. imperf. act. indic.)
glossary.urnaque: urna, -ae f. — “urn,” here the funerary urn (abl. sg. + -que “and”)
glossary.utilium: ūtilis, -e — “useful, serviceable” (gen. pl. m. with equōrum; bellō “for war”)
glossary.vagas: vagus, -a, -um — “wandering, roving” (acc. pl. f. with volucrēs)
glossary.vanam: vānus, -a, -um — “empty, illusory, false” (acc. sg. f. with spem)
glossary.vellemque: volō, velle — “wish, want” (1st sg. imperf. act. subj. + -que “and”; unfulfilled wish: “and I could wish that…”)
glossary.venenata: venēnātus, -a, -um — “drugged, enchanted, charged with poison” (abl. sg. f. with virgā; the same form can be nom. sg. f. or nom./acc. pl. n.)
glossary.venilia: Venīlia, -ae f. — Venilia, a nymph, by Janus the mother of Canens (nom. sg.)
glossary.venulus: Venulus, -ī m. — Venulus, the envoy Turnus sends to Diomedes to ask for help (nom. sg.)
glossary.verterat: vertō, vertere, vertī, versum — “turn, turn toward, change” (3rd sg. pluperf. act. indic.)
glossary.vesana: vēsānus, -a, -um — “frenzied, out of her senses” (nom. sg. f.)
glossary.virgineis: virgineus, -a, -um — “maidenly, of maidens” (abl. pl. m. with lūsibus)
glossary.virgultis: virgultum, -ī n. — “thicket, brushwood” (abl. pl.; the noun is normally plural)
glossary.vocati: vocō, vocāre — “call, name” (perf. pass. part., nom. pl. m. with illī: “those often called [happy]”; the same form is also gen. sg.)
glossary.volitare: volitō, volitāre — “flit about, fly to and fro” (pres. act. infin.)
glossary.abanteis: Abantēus, -a, -um — of Abas, Abantean, and so Argive (dat./abl. pl., m./f./n.)
glossary.ablatum: auferō, auferre, abstulī, ablātum — carried off, taken away, swept up (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg.; also the supine)
glossary.absolvere: absolvō, absolvere, absolvī, absolūtum — to acquit, to release, to set free of (pres. act. inf.; + abl. of the charge; the same letters can also be 3 pl. perf. absolvēre for absolvērunt)
glossary.abstulerit: auferō, auferre, abstulī, ablātum — shall have carried off, has taken away (3 sg. fut. perf. indic. act. or 3 sg. perf. subj. act.)
glossary.acceptissimus: acceptus, -a, -um — most welcome, best beloved, most acceptable (superl., m. nom. sg.; properly the perf. part. of accipiō; + dat. of the person pleased)
glossary.accessus: accessus, accessūs — approach, coming near, means of access (m. acc. pl. or nom. sg.; the same letters are also the perf. part. of accēdō, “having approached”)
glossary.acclinata: acclīnō, acclīnāre, acclīnāvī, acclīnātum — leaned against, propped on, resting on (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg. or n. nom./acc. pl.; + dat.)
glossary.acrota: Acrota, Acrotae — Acrota, an Alban king, son of Tiberinus and brother of Remulus (m. nom. sg., a Greek-type first-declension masculine; the abl. sg. Acrotā is spelt alike)
glossary.adero: adsum, adesse, adfuī — I shall be present, I shall be there (1 sg. fut. indic.)
glossary.aditum: aditus, aditūs — approach, way in, access (m. acc. sg.; the same letters are also the perf. part. and supine of adeō, “gone to”)
glossary.adsimulavit: adsimulō, adsimulāre, adsimulāvī, adsimulātum — made himself like, took on the likeness of, counterfeited (3 sg. perf. indic. act.; the edition's spelling for assimulāvit)
glossary.aequata: aequō, aequāre, aequāvī, aequātum — made equal, levelled, dealt out even-handedly (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl. or f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.aesarei: Aesarēus, -a, -um — of the Aesar, the river at Croton (m./n. gen. sg. or m. nom. pl.)
glossary.aesaris: Aesar, Aesaris — the Aesar, a river of Bruttium beside Croton (m. gen. sg.)
glossary.aetheris: aethēr, aetheris — the upper air, the clear sky, heaven (m. gen. sg.; a Greek noun, acc. sg. aethera)
glossary.agrestum: agrestis, agreste — of the fields, rustic; as a noun, countrymen, farm folk (gen. pl., syncopated for agrestium)
glossary.albanos: Albānus, -a, -um — Alban, of Alba Longa (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.alemone: Alemōn, Alemonis — Alemon, an Argive, father of Myscelus (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.alemoniden: Alemonidēs, Alemonidae — the son of Alemon, i.e. Myscelus (m. acc. sg. in the Greek form -ēn)
glossary.alemonides: Alemonidēs, Alemonidae — the son of Alemon, i.e. Myscelus (m. nom. sg.; a Greek patronymic)
glossary.alieno: aliēnus, -a, -um — another's, belonging to someone else, not one's own (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.alpino: Alpīnus, -a, -um — Alpine, of the Alps (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.amatis: amō, amāre, amāvī, amātum — you love, you are in love with (2 pl. pres. indic. act.; the same letters are also amātus, “loved”, dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.amissum: āmittō, āmittere, āmīsī, āmissum — lost, let go, taken away (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.amphitryoniadae: Amphitryōniadēs, Amphitryōniadae — the son of Amphitryon, i.e. Hercules (m. dat. sg.; also gen. sg.; a Greek patronymic)
glossary.amuli: Amūlius, Amūliī — Amulius, the Alban king who drove out his brother Numitor (m. gen. sg., the contracted -ī of -ius nouns)
glossary.anaxaretae: Anaxaretē, Anaxaretēs — Anaxarete, a girl of Cyprus who scorned Iphis (f. dat. sg.; Greek first declension, nom. -ē, acc. -ēn)
glossary.anaxarete: Anaxaretē, Anaxaretēs — Anaxarete, a girl of Cyprus who scorned Iphis (f. voc. sg.; the nom. sg. is spelt alike)
glossary.anaxareten: Anaxaretē, Anaxaretēs — Anaxarete, a girl of Cyprus who scorned Iphis (f. acc. sg. in the Greek form -ēn)
glossary.anilia: anīlis, anīle — of an old woman, an old woman's (n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.animantem: animāns, animantis — a living creature, an animal (acc. sg., m./f./n.; properly the pres. part. of animō, “breathing, alive”)
glossary.animantis: animāns, animantis — of a living creature, of an animal (gen. sg.; also acc. pl. animantīs for animantēs)
glossary.anumque: anus, anūs — old woman (f. acc. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.aptus: aptus, -a, -um — fitted to, suited to, adapted (m. nom. sg.; + dat.; properly the perf. part. of the obsolete apiō, and used as an adjective)
glossary.arcisque: arx, arcis — citadel, stronghold, the height of a city (f. gen. sg.; also acc. pl. arcīs for arcēs; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.ardentis: ārdeō, ārdēre, ārsī — burning, on fire, aflame with love (pres. act. part., gen. sg.; also acc. pl. ardentīs for ardentēs)
glossary.argis: Argī, Argōrum — Argos, the Argive city of Juno (m. dat./abl. pl.; the place is also called Argos, n. indeclinable)
glossary.arsuro: ārdeō, ārdēre, ārsī, ārsūrus — about to burn, that will be set alight (fut. act. part., m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.ascanii: Ascanius, Ascaniī — Ascanius, son of Aeneas, also called Iulus (m. gen. sg.)
glossary.atrisque: āter, ātra, ātrum — black, dark, unlucky (m./n. dat. or abl. pl.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.audebatis: audeō, audēre, ausus sum — you were daring, you had the boldness to (2 pl. imperf. indic.; semi-deponent, perfect ausus sum)
glossary.audetis: audeō, audēre, ausus sum — you dare, you bring yourselves to (2 pl. pres. indic.; semi-deponent)
glossary.augustae: augustus, -a, -um — venerable, majestic, hallowed (f. gen. or dat. sg., or f. nom. pl.; not the proper name Augustus)
glossary.aventino: Aventīnus, Aventīnī — Aventinus, an Alban king buried on the hill that took his name (m. dat. or abl. sg.; the same letters serve the adjective Aventīnus, of the Aventine)
glossary.averserisque: āversor, āversārī, āversātus sum — you turn away from, you spurn, you refuse to face (2 sg. pres. subj. of a deponent; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.bibulaeque: bibulus, -a, -um — ever-drinking, thirsty, soaking up moisture (f. gen. or dat. sg., or f. nom. pl.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.binominis: binōminis, binōmine — of two names, twice-named (gen. sg., m./f./n.)
glossary.bitumine: bitūmen, bitūminis — bitumen, pitch, mineral tar (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.blanditus: blandior, blandīrī, blandītus sum — having coaxed, having spoken caressingly, having wheedled (perf. part. of a deponent and so active in sense, m. nom. sg.; + dat.)
glossary.caesorum: caedō, caedere, cecīdī, caesum — slaughtered, cut down, killed (perf. pass. part., m./n. gen. pl.)
glossary.calidusque: calidus, -a, -um — warm, hot (m. nom. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.candidaque: candidus, -a, -um — shining white, bright; of a voting-pebble or a verdict, white, and so acquitting (f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.capaci: capāx, capācis — roomy, capacious, able to take in much (dat. or abl. sg., m./f./n.)
glossary.capetusque: Capetus, Capetī — Capetus, one of the Alban kings (m. nom. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.capys: Capys, Capyis — Capys, one of the Alban kings (m. nom. sg., a Greek-type nominative in -ys)
glossary.capysque: Capys, Capyis — Capys, one of the Alban kings (m. nom. sg., Greek-type nom. in -ys; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.carendum: careō, carēre, caruī — must be gone without, has to be done without (gerundive, n. nom./acc. sg.; impersonal in mihi carendum est, “I must do without”, + abl.)
glossary.carent: careō, carēre, caruī — they lack, they are without, they are free of (3 pl. pres. indic. act.; + abl.)
glossary.ceditis: cēdō, cēdere, cessī, cessum — you yield, you give way (2 pl. pres. indic. act.; + dat.)
glossary.ciborum: cibus, cibī — food, fare, a dish (m. gen. pl.)
glossary.clausura: claudō, claudere, clausī, clausum — about to shut, on the point of closing (fut. act. part., f. nom. sg. or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.claviger: clāviger, clāvigerī — the club-bearer, i.e. Hercules (m. nom. sg.; a distinct clāviger, from clāvis, means “key-bearer” and belongs to Janus)
glossary.coetusque: coetus, coetūs — a gathering, an assembly, a throng (m. acc. pl.; also nom. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.cogeris: cōgō, cōgere, coēgī, coāctum — you are compelled, you are forced (2 sg. pres. pass. indic.; the fut. pass. cōgēris is spelt alike)
glossary.cognatas: cognātus, -a, -um — related by blood, kindred, of the same stock (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.coluit: colō, colere, coluī, cultum — tilled, tended, cared for; also dwelt in, honoured, worshipped (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.coluntur: colō, colere, coluī, cultum — they are tended, they are cultivated (3 pl. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.compescit: compescō, compescere, compescuī — checks, restrains, cuts back (3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.complexaque: complector, complectī, complexus sum — having embraced, having clasped (perf. part. of a deponent and so active in sense, f. nom. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.concubitusque: concubitus, concubitūs — a lying together, sexual union (m. acc. pl.; also nom. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.conditur: condō, condere, condidī, conditum — is hidden away, is laid to rest, is buried; of the sun, sinks out of sight (3 sg. pres. pass. indic.; the verb also means to found and to store up, and the letters equally fit condiō, “is seasoned, is preserved”)
glossary.conduntur: condō, condere, condidī, conditum — are founded, are built, are laid down (3 pl. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.congestis: congerō, congerere, congessī, congestum — heaped up, piled together (perf. pass. part., m./n. dat. or abl. pl.)
glossary.congestoque: congerō, congerere, congessī, congestum — heaped up, crammed in, piled on (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.contrahit: contrahō, contrahere, contrāxī, contractum — draws together, narrows, shrinks (3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.corbe: corbis, corbis — basket, wicker hamper (m./f. abl. sg.)
glossary.corporeasque: corporeus, -a, -um — of the body, made of flesh, bodily (f. acc. pl.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.crimisenque: Crimīsē, Crimīsēs — Crimise, a point on the south-Italian coast passed on the voyage to Croton; the name belongs elsewhere to a Sicilian river (f. acc. sg. in the Greek form -ēn; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.crotonis: Crotōn, Crotōnis — Croton, the Italian host of Hercules, from whom the city Croton took its name (m. gen. sg.)
glossary.cultosque: colō, colere, coluī, cultum — tended, cultivated, well-kept (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.curibus: Curēs, Curium — Cures, the Sabine town of Tatius and Numa (f. dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.curibusque: Curēs, Curium — Cures, the Sabine town of Tatius and Numa (f. dat./abl. pl.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.dabas: dō, dare, dedī, datum — you were giving, you kept giving (2 sg. imperf. indic. act.; iūra dare, to dispense law)
glossary.decertare: dēcertō, dēcertāre, dēcertāvī, dēcertātum — to fight it out, to contend to a finish (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.deducentia: dēdūcō, dēdūcere, dēdūxī, dēductum — drawing down, bending down, leading away (pres. act. part., n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.delphosque: Delphī, Delphōrum — Delphi, the oracular seat of Apollo (m. acc. pl.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.demersit: dēmergō, dēmergere, dēmersī, dēmersum — plunged, sank, thrust down (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.demersus: dēmergō, dēmergere, dēmersī, dēmersum — sunk, plunged under, drowned (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.demittitur: dēmittō, dēmittere, dēmīsī, dēmissum — is dropped in, is let down, is sent down (3 sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.dempsistis: dēmō, dēmere, dēmpsī, dēmptum — you have taken away, you have subtracted (2 pl. perf. indic. act.; + dat. of what is robbed)
glossary.deperit: dēpereō, dēperīre, dēperiī — perishes utterly, is wholly lost (3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.desectum: dēsecō, dēsecāre, dēsecuī, dēsectum — cut off, mown, reaped (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.)
glossary.desiderat: dēsīderō, dēsīderāre, dēsīderāvī, dēsīderātum — longs for, misses, wants (3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.despectare: dēspectō, dēspectāre — to look down upon, to gaze down at (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.dicione: diciō, diciōnis — sway, dominion, authority (f. abl. sg.; a noun used almost only in the oblique cases)
glossary.dignam: dignus, -a, -um — worthy, deserving (f. acc. sg.; + abl. of what is deserved)
glossary.dignoque: dignus, -a, -um — worthy, deserving (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.dilapsum: dīlābor, dīlābī, dīlāpsus sum — melted away, dissolved, slipped apart (perf. part. of a deponent and so active in sense, n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.)
glossary.discenda: discō, discere, didicī — things to be learned, matter for learning (gerundive, n. nom./acc. pl.; also f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.discussa: discutiō, discutere, discussī, discussum — shattered, broken apart, scattered (perf. pass. part., f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.disiunxisse: disiungō, disiungere, disiūnxī, disiūnctum — to have unyoked, to have separated (perf. act. inf.)
glossary.divitias: dīvitiae, dīvitiārum — riches, wealth, abundance (f. acc. pl.; a plural-only noun)
glossary.divumque: dīvus, dīvī — a god (m. gen. pl., syncopated for dīvōrum; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.dixisti: dīcō, dīcere, dīxī, dictum — you said, you have said (2 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.docebat: doceō, docēre, docuī, doctum — was teaching, used to teach (3 sg. imperf. indic. act.)
glossary.dolisque: dolus, dolī — trick, guile, deceit (m. dat./abl. pl.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.domibus: domus, domūs — house, home, dwelling (f. dat./abl. pl.; the noun is mixed second and fourth declension)
glossary.duc: dūcō, dūcere, dūxī, ductum — lead! bring! take! (2 sg. pres. act. imperat., the shortened form without -e)
glossary.eademque: īdem, eadem, idem — the same (n. nom./acc. pl.; also f. nom. sg. and, with long ā, f. abl. sg. eādem; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.elicuere: ēliciō, ēlicere, ēlicuī, ēlicitum — they drew forth, they lured out, they called up (3 pl. perf. indic. act., the poetic -ēre for -ērunt)
glossary.emensas: ēmētior, ēmētīrī, ēmēnsus sum — measured out, run to the end, passed through (perf. part. of a deponent, f. acc. pl.; used of time completed, often with passive force)
glossary.epulanda: epulor, epulārī, epulātus sum — to be feasted on, fit to be eaten (gerundive, n. nom./acc. pl.; also f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.epytus: Epytus, Epytī — Epytus, one of the Alban kings (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.ereptas: ēripiō, ēripere, ēripuī, ēreptum — snatched away, torn out, wrenched free (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl.)
glossary.errante: errō, errāre, errāvī, errātum — wandering, straying, roaming (pres. act. part., abl. sg., m./f./n.)
glossary.eruerit: ēruō, ēruere, ēruī, ērutum — has rooted up, has dug out (3 sg. perf. subj. act. or fut. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.etenim: etenim — for indeed, and in fact, the truth is (conj., introducing a reason)
glossary.euphorbus: Euphorbus, Euphorbī — Euphorbus, the Trojan son of Panthous, killed by Menelaus (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.evicit: ēvincō, ēvincere, ēvīcī, ēvictum — overcame, broke through, prevailed over (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.excoquit: excoquō, excoquere, excoxī, excoctum — smelts, refines by fire, boils out (3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.excutiant: excutiō, excutere, excussī, excussum — may shake off, may strike down (3 pl. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.exhortari: exhortor, exhortārī, exhortātus sum — to urge on, to encourage (pres. inf. of a deponent, active in sense)
glossary.exturbare: exturbō, exturbāre, exturbāvī, exturbātum — to drive out, to thrust forth (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.facile: facile — easily, readily, without effort (adv.; the same letters are also facilis, facile, “easy”, n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.facilis: facilis, facile — easy, pliant, yielding to the hand (m./f. nom. sg.; also gen. sg. and acc. pl. facilīs for facilēs)
glossary.factisque: factum, factī — deed, act, thing done (n. dat./abl. pl., with enclitic -que, “and”; the same letters are also the perf. pass. part. of faciō, facere, fēcī, factum, “done, made”)
glossary.faeno: faenum, faenī — hay, dry grass (n. abl. or dat. sg.)
glossary.falsique: falsus, -a, -um — false, feigned, unreal (m./n. gen. sg. or m. nom. pl.; properly the perf. part. of fallō, fallere, fefellī, falsum; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.fastus: fastus, fastūs — haughtiness, disdain, cold pride (m. acc. pl.; also nom. sg.; distinct from the adj. fāstus, of days when court may sit)
glossary.fatebere: fateor, fatērī, fassus sum — you will admit, you will confess (2 sg. fut. indic. of a deponent, the poetic -re for -ris)
glossary.fauce: faux, faucis — throat, gullet, windpipe (f. abl. sg.; the noun is usually plural, faucēs)
glossary.faventibus: faveō, favēre, fāvī, fautum — favouring, blowing fair, being kind (pres. act. part., dat./abl. pl.; + dat.)
glossary.favorem: favor, favōris — favour, goodwill, support (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.fenestris: fenestra, fenestrae — window, opening in a wall (f. dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.ferenda: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to be carried, to be borne, needing to be endured (gerundive, n. nom./acc. pl.; also f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.feretro: feretrum, feretrī — bier, litter for carrying a corpse (n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.fingetur: fingō, fingere, fīnxī, fictum — will be shaped, will be moulded, will be fashioned (3 sg. fut. pass. indic.)
glossary.firmo: firmus, -a, -um — strong, firm, unyielding (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.; the same letters are also firmō, firmāre, “I make firm, I strengthen”, 1 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.fisso: findō, findere, fidī, fissum — split, cleft, cut open (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.)
glossary.flagrans: flagrō, flagrāre, flagrāvī — blazing, burning, ablaze (pres. act. part., nom. sg., m./f./n.)
glossary.flammifera: flammifer, flammifera, flammiferum — flame-bearing, fiery (f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.flebilis: flēbilis, flēbile — tearful, mournful, to be wept over (m./f. nom. sg.; also gen. sg.)
glossary.formatur: fōrmō, fōrmāre, fōrmāvī, fōrmātum — is shaped, is given form (3 sg. pres. pass. indic.)
glossary.fraudat: fraudō, fraudāre, fraudāvī, fraudātum — cheats, defrauds, robs of (3 sg. pres. indic. act.; + abl. of the thing withheld)
glossary.frondator: frondātor, frondātōris — a pruner of leaves, one who strips foliage (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.fuisse: sum, esse, fuī — to have been (perf. act. inf.)
glossary.fulgure: fulgur, fulguris — lightning, a flash of lightning (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.fulmineo: fulmineus, -a, -um — of the thunderbolt, like lightning, destroying as lightning does (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.fumante: fūmō, fūmāre, fūmāvī — smoking, steaming, giving off fumes (pres. act. part., abl. sg., m./f./n.)
glossary.fundamine: fundāmen, fundāminis — foundation, groundwork (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.fures: fūr, fūris — thief, robber (m. acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
glossary.gelidae: gelidus, -a, -um — icy, chill, freezing (f. gen. or dat. sg., or f. nom. pl.)
glossary.generatus: generō, generāre, generāvī, generātum — begotten, fathered, sprung from (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.; + abl. of the parent)
glossary.generique: gener, generī — son-in-law (m. gen. sg., with enclitic -que, “and”; the same letters are also genus, generis, “race, kind”, n. dat. sg.)
glossary.generosam: generōsus, -a, -um — of noble birth, high-born, of good stock (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.glaebaque: glaeba, glaebae — clod of earth, lump of soil (f. abl. sg.; also nom. sg.; with enclitic -que, “and”)
glossary.glans: glāns, glandis — acorn, mast; and a leaden sling-bullet of that shape (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.gradivus: Grādīvus, Grādīvī (m.) — Gradivus, cult-title of Mars, the strider or marcher (nom. sg.)
glossary.graviora: gravis, grave — heavier, graver, more serious (comparative gravior, n. nom./acc. pl.: heavier things)
glossary.habitantque: habitō, habitāre, habitāvī, habitātum — they dwell, they live in, they inhabit (3 pl. pres. indic. act. + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.habitu: habitus, habitūs (m.) — dress, garb, outward guise; bearing (abl. sg.)
glossary.haedis: haedus, haedī (m.) — kid, young goat; capitalized, the Haedi, the Kids, the stormy stars in Auriga (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.helene: Helenē, Helenēs (f.) — Helen of Sparta, wooed by many suitors (nom. sg., Greek 1st-decl. form)
glossary.herculei: Herculeus, -a, -um — of Hercules, Herculean (m./n. gen. sg., or m. nom. pl.)
glossary.herculeo: Herculeus, -a, -um — of Hercules, Herculean (m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.hersiliam: Hersilia, Hersiliae (f.) — Hersilia, wife of Romulus, taken up as the goddess Hora (acc. sg., Latin 1st-decl. form)
glossary.hersilie: Hersiliē, Hersiliēs (f.) — Hersilia, wife of Romulus (nom. sg., Greek form beside the Latin Hersilia)
glossary.hersilien: Hersiliē, Hersiliēs (f.) — Hersilia, wife of Romulus (acc. sg., Greek -ēn ending)
glossary.hiberis: Hibērus, -a, -um — Iberian, Spanish (dat./abl. pl.; the noun Hibērī, the Spaniards, has the same form)
glossary.hodierna: hodiernus, -a, -um — of today, today's, present (f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.iani: Iānus, Iānī (m.) — Janus, god of doorways and beginnings; his gateway at Rome (gen. sg.; the form is also nom. pl.)
glossary.idalien: Idaliē, Idaliēs (f.) — the Idalian goddess, Venus, named from Idalium in Cyprus (acc. sg., Greek -ēn ending)
glossary.iliades: Īliadēs, Īliadae (m.) — son of Ilia, i.e. Romulus (nom. sg., Greek patronymic; the identical Īliades is also nom./acc. pl. of Īlias, a Trojan woman)
glossary.imitator: imitātor, imitātōris (m.) — imitator, one who copies or mimics (nom. sg.)
glossary.impavidus: impavidus, -a, -um — fearless, undaunted, unafraid (m. nom. sg.; printed inpavidus in some witnesses)
glossary.impellitur: impellō, impellere, impulī, impulsum — is driven on, is pushed forward, is urged (3 sg. pres. indic. pass.)
glossary.imponi: impōnō, impōnere, imposuī, impositum — to be placed upon, to be set on (pres. pass. infin.)
glossary.imponique: impōnō, impōnere, imposuī, impositum — to be placed upon, to be set on (pres. pass. infin. + enclitic -que, and; printed inponi- in some witnesses)
glossary.incaluisse: incalēscō, incalēscere, incaluī — to have grown hot, to have become heated (perf. act. infin.)
glossary.incenduntque: incendō, incendere, incendī, incēnsum — they set alight, they kindle, they inflame (3 pl. pres. indic. act. + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.incingere: incingō, incingere, incīnxī, incīnctum — gird yourself, wreathe yourself about (2 sg. pres. pass. imperative in middle sense; the same form is also the pres. act. infin., to gird about)
glossary.incurva: incurvus, -a, -um — bent, stooped, curved over (f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.indigenis: indigena, indigenae (m./f.) — native, native-born inhabitant (dat./abl. pl.; also used adjectivally, native, home-born)
glossary.inducto: indūcō, indūcere, indūxī, inductum — drawn over, spread on, put on as a covering (perf. pass. part., m./n. dat. or abl. sg.)
glossary.induerat: induō, induere, induī, indūtum — he had put on, he had donned, he had clothed himself in (3 sg. pluperf. indic. act.)
glossary.iniit: ineō, inīre, iniī, initum — he entered, he went into (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.inmansuetumque: immānsuētus, -a, -um (printed inmansuetum) — untamed, unsoftened, savage (n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg., + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.innixusque: innītor, innītī, innīxus sum — leaning on, propped upon, resting against (+ dat. or abl.) (perf. dep. part., m. nom. sg., active in sense, + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.innocuum: innocuus, -a, -um — harmless, doing no injury, blameless (n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.)
glossary.inrigat: irrigō, irrigāre, irrigāvī, irrigātum (printed inrigat) — waters, irrigates, floods over (3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.inscripsere: īnscrībō, īnscrībere, īnscrīpsī, īnscrīptum — they wrote in, they entered as responsible, they charged with (3 pl. perf. indic. act., poetic -ēre for īnscrīpsērunt)
glossary.inseruitque: īnserō, īnserere, īnseruī, īnsertum — he thrust in, he inserted, he put through (3 sg. perf. indic. act. + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.insidiis: īnsidiae, īnsidiārum (f. pl.) — ambush, treachery, plot (dat./abl. pl.; the noun is used only in the plural)
glossary.inspiciunt: īnspiciō, īnspicere, īnspexī, īnspectum — they look into, they examine, they inspect (3 pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.interceperit: intercipiō, intercipere, intercēpī, interceptum — has cut off, has intercepted, has snatched away (3 sg. perf. subj. act. or fut. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.interit: intereō, interīre, interiī, interitum — perishes, is destroyed, passes out of being (3 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.intrasse: intrō, intrāre, intrāvī, intrātum — to have entered, to have gone in (perf. act. infin., syncopated for intrāvisse)
glossary.invadunt: invādō, invādere, invāsī, invāsum — they rush in, they fall upon, they invade (3 pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.investigata: investīgō, investīgāre, investīgāvī, investīgātum — tracked out, searched out, discovered by inquiry (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl. or f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.ionium: Ionius, -a, -um — Ionian; as a noun Ionium, the Ionian Sea (n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.)
glossary.iphin: Īphis, Īphidis — Iphis, a personal name borne both by a man and by a woman (acc. sg., Greek -in ending)
glossary.iracundique: īrācundus, -a, -um — quick to anger, hot-tempered, wrathful (m. nom. pl., or m./n. gen. sg., + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.irin: Īris, Īridis (f.) — Iris, the rainbow, messenger of the gods (acc. sg., Greek -in ending)
glossary.italis: Italus, -a, -um — Italian, of Italy (dat./abl. pl.; the noun Italī, the Italians, has the same form)
glossary.iubeas: iubeō, iubēre, iussī, iussum — you may bid, you should order, you were to command (2 sg. pres. subj. act.)
glossary.iurasses: iūrō, iūrāre, iūrāvī, iūrātum — you would have sworn (2 sg. pluperf. subj. act., syncopated for iūrāvissēs)
glossary.iuvatis: iuvō, iuvāre, iūvī, iūtum — you help, you benefit, you give pleasure (2 pl. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.iuvenalior: iuvenālis, iuvenāle — more youthful, younger in look than his years (comparative iuvenālior, m./f. nom. sg.)
glossary.lacedaemoniumque: Lacedaemonius, -a, -um — Spartan, Lacedaemonian, of Spartan foundation (m. or n. acc. sg., + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.lacinia: Lacinius, -a, -um — Lacinian, of the Lacinium promontory beside Croton (n. nom./acc. pl.); the identical lacinia is also the noun lacinia, a hem or flap of a garment (f. nom./abl. sg.)
glossary.lacrimosa: lacrimōsus, -a, -um — tearful, weeping; causing tears (f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.laetaque: laetus, -a, -um — glad, joyful; rich, flourishing (f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl., + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.laevae: laevus, -a, -um — left, on the left (f. gen. or dat. sg., or f. nom. pl.; as a noun laeva, the left hand)
glossary.lapidosas: lapidōsus, -a, -um — full of stones, stony (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.latina: Latīnus, -a, -um — Latin, of Latium (f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.latinas: Latīnus, -a, -um — Latin, of Latium (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.latinum: Latīnus, Latīnī (m.) — Latinus, name of a king of the Latins (acc. sg.); the same spelling serves the adjective Latīnus, -a, -um, Latin (m./n. acc. sg.)
glossary.latinus: Latīnus, Latīnī (m.) — Latinus, name of a king of the Latins (nom. sg.); the same spelling serves the adjective Latīnus, -a, -um, Latin (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.laudatae: laudō, laudāre, laudāvī, laudātum — praised, commended (perf. pass. part., f. gen. or dat. sg., or f. nom. pl.)
glossary.lauru: laurus, laurī (f.) — laurel, bay-tree, laurel wreath (abl. sg., in the 4th-declension form laurū)
glossary.lecturum: legō, legere, lēgī, lēctum — about to pick, going to gather (fut. act. part., m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg.; legō means gather, pick, and also read)
glossary.legum: lēx, lēgis (f.) — law, statute, ordinance (gen. pl.)
glossary.lentos: lentus, -a, -um — slow, lingering; pliant, tough; unmoved, unyielding (m. acc. pl.)
glossary.lepus: lepus, leporis (m.) — hare (nom. sg.; not to be confused with lepōs, charm)
glossary.levatum: levō, levāre, levāvī, levātum — lifted, raised up; relieved, lightened (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg. or n. nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.liquet: liqueō, liquēre, licuī — it is clear, it is plain, it is evident (3 sg. pres. indic. act., used impersonally)
glossary.luctatusque: luctor, luctārī, luctātus sum — having struggled, having wrestled (perf. dep. part., m. nom. sg., active in sense, + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.luridaque: lūridus, -a, -um — sallow, ghastly pale, wan (n. nom./acc. pl., or f. nom./abl. sg., + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.luxuriem: luxuriēs, luxuriēī (f.) — rank growth, exuberance, excess (acc. sg.; 5th-decl. by-form of luxuria)
glossary.mactatus: mactō, mactāre, mactāvī, mactātum — slaughtered, sacrificed (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
glossary.maculatum: maculō, maculāre, maculāvī, maculātum — stained, spotted, defiled (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. sg. or m. acc. sg.)
glossary.madidas: madidus, -a, -um — wet, soaked, drenched (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.mandere: mandō, mandere, mandī, mānsum — to chew, to champ, to devour (pres. act. infin.; distinct from mandō, mandāre, to entrust or enjoin)
glossary.materiem: materiēs, materiēī (f.) — matter, stuff, material; subject-matter (acc. sg.; 5th-decl. by-form of māteria)
glossary.mearent: meō, meāre, meāvī, meātum — they moved along, they passed, they travelled their course (3 pl. imperf. subj. act.)
glossary.memento: meminī, meminisse — remember, bear in mind (2 sg. future imperative of the defective verb meminī)
glossary.memoremque: memor, memoris — mindful, remembering, unforgetting (adj., m./f. acc. sg., + enclitic -que, and; the identical memorem is also 1 sg. pres. subj. act. of memorō, I would recount)
glossary.memoro: memorō, memorāre, memorāvī, memorātum — I recount, I relate, I call to mind (1 sg. pres. indic. act.)
glossary.mentesque: mēns, mentis (f.) — mind, thought, intention, purpose (nom. or acc. pl. + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.meruistis: mereō, merēre, meruī, meritum — you have deserved, you have earned (2 pl. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.migrare: migrō, migrāre, migrāvī, migrātum — to move house, to migrate, to pass over into (pres. act. infin.)
glossary.minoris: minor, minus — smaller, lesser, younger (comparative of parvus; gen. sg., any gender)
glossary.mirantum: mīror, mīrārī, mīrātus sum — of those wondering, of the marvelling (pres. dep. part., gen. pl., contracted for mīrantium)
glossary.mitescere: mītēscō, mītēscere — to grow mild, to soften, to become ripe or tender (pres. act. infin.)
glossary.mitibus: mītis, mīte — mild, mellow, ripe; gentle (dat./abl. pl.)
glossary.mitra: mitra, mitrae (f.) — mitra, an Eastern headband or turban-like cap (abl. sg.; also nom. sg.)
glossary.monere: moneō, monēre, monuī, monitum — to warn, to advise, to remind (pres. act. infin.; the form is also 2 sg. pres. pass. imperative, be warned)
glossary.moriorque: morior, morī, mortuus sum — I die, I am dying (1 sg. pres. indic. dep. + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.morsa: mordeō, mordēre, momordī, morsum — bitten, gnawed, nibbled (perf. pass. part., f. nom. or abl. sg., or n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.mos: mōs, mōris (m.) — custom, usage, established practice; in the plural, character or morals (nom. sg.)
glossary.myscelos: Myscelos, Myscelī (m.) — Myscelus, the Argive founder of Croton (nom. sg., Greek -os ending; also spelled Myscelus)
glossary.narremur: nārrō, nārrāre, nārrāvī, nārrātum — that we be told of, that we be spoken about (1 pl. pres. subj. pass.)
glossary.nascentia: nāscor, nāscī, nātus sum — being born, springing up, budding (pres. dep. part., n. nom./acc. pl.)
glossary.nemorosi: nemorōsus, -a, -um — woody, thickly wooded, full of groves (m./n. gen. sg., or m. nom. pl.)
glossary.neretum: Nēretum, Nēretī (n.) — Neretum, a town of the Sallentines in Calabria (acc. sg.)
glossary.nitentibus: niteō, nitēre, nituī — shining, gleaming, glossy (pres. act. part., dat./abl. pl.; the identical form also serves nītor, nītī, to lean or strive, straining)
glossary.nocturnae: nocturnus, -a, -um — of the night, nocturnal, by night (f. gen. or dat. sg., or f. nom. pl.)
glossary.noricus: Nōricus, -a, -um — Norican, of Noricum, the Alpine region famed for its steel (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.notior: nōtus, -a, -um — better known, more familiar (comparative nōtior, m./f. nom. sg.)
glossary.novantur: novō, novāre, novāvī, novātum — they are made new, they are renewed, they are altered (3 pl. pres. indic. pass.)
glossary.numam: Numa, Numae (m.) — Numa Pompilius, second king of Rome (acc. sg.)
glossary.numenque: nūmen, nūminis (n.) — divine will, divine power; a divinity (nom. or acc. sg. + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.numerandos: numerō, numerāre, numerāvī, numerātum — to be counted, for counting (gerundive, m. acc. pl.)
glossary.numitorque: Numitor, Numitōris (m.) — Numitor, king of Alba, grandfather of Romulus and Remus (nom. sg. + enclitic -que, and)
glossary.obitumque: obitus, obitūs (m.) — death, passing away; the setting of a star (acc. sg. + enclitic -que, and; the same spelling serves obitum, perf. pass. part. of obeō, gone to meet or encountered)
glossary.obstante: obstō, obstāre, obstitī — standing in the way, blocking, hindering (pres. act. part., abl. sg.)
glossary.obtulit: offerō, offerre, obtulī, oblātum — he offered, he presented, he brought before (3 sg. perf. indic. act.)
glossary.odioque: odium, odiī (n.) — hatred, loathing, disgust (dat. or abl. sg. + enclitic -que, and)
